search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ajmer Ajwain-93 (AA-93), ajwain, NRCSS Tabiji, release year recorded as 2015, state recorded as Rajasthan

BREEDER/INSTITUTION: The NRCSS Ajmer team of Meena, Kakani, Singh and colleagues published the variety description in 2014, "Ajmer Ajwain 93: An early maturing variety of ajwain developed at NRCSS for all ajwain growing areas." -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/46432
BREEDING METHOD: The variety is described as an open pollinated variety developed through mass selection (Meena et al., 2014) -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue6S/PartE/S-7-6-47-184.pdf
RELEASE YEAR: The 2014 publication predates the 2015-04-07 release date in the input record; I found no notification document confirming the 2015 date. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/46432
MATURITY/EARLINESS: This population starts flowering only 46 days after sowing and matures in 123 days only. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/272425610_Status_of_seed_spices_research_and_development_in_India
MATURITY (conflicting values): Maturity was reported as 131 days in a Karnataka trial, Among the genotypes AA-93 was found to be early maturing (131 days). -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue1/PartG/9-6-217-752.pdf ; ICAR's workshop cites matures in 145 days -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/2939
LODGING: Early maturing (123 days), lodging resistant. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373852577_Recent_Advances_in_Ajwain_Trachyspermum_ammi_L_Cultivation_A_Review
YIELD (multi-location): I found no reliable AA-93-specific multi-location yield figure; a 2012-13 to 2018-19 multi-location trial result is reported for an unnamed proposed variety, so I did not attribute it to AA-93. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Thymol-content-of-ajwain-varieties-as-influen

The first search ("Amaranths PLR 1 amaranthus variety") returned only the Iowa State University amaranth page (https://www.cad.iastate.edu/amaranth), which covers US ornamental and grain varieties, not PLR 1. No evidence found for this variety. Two pages name the SDAU crop-variety context but not this variety:
- A 2013 SDAU net-house/open-field trial of five amaranth varieties (Pusa Lai Chaulai, Chhoti Chaulai, Pusa Kiran, Arka Suguna, Arka Arunima). Gujarat Amaranth 5 is not among them. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384399829_Growth_and_Yield_of_Amaranthus_Amaranthus_spp_Varieties_in_
- A 2004–06 SDAU Regional Research Station nitrogen/moisture-stress study on grain amaranth (A. hypochondriacus). - Identity conflict to flag: an agriarticles page names "Gujarat Amaranthus-2" (close to the seednet name "GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2"). It describes a high-yielding variety released in 1998 and suited to Maharashtra, Karnataka, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Gujarat, with a 23 q/ha yield figure from a different entry. The 1998 release date conflicts with the 2020 release year in the record. I have not attributed these data to this variety. -- https://agriarticles.com/grain-amaranth-pseudo-cereal/

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for this variety. An SDAU ISSR genetic-diversity study used 19 grain amaranth genotypes from the SDAU Centre for Crop Improvement. The excerpt does not list Gujarat Amaranth 5 or GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2 among them, so I have not linked the study to this variety. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s42269-019-0146-2

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution (from the variety record, not a page naming the variety): S. D. Agricultural University (SDAU), Sardarkrushinagar, Gujarat. Breeder name: No evidence found. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Amaranth 9 (variety_name) / GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2 (seednet_variety_name), grain amaranth (Amaranthus)

Name check: The searches found almost no evidence naming "Gujarat Amaranth 9" or "GA-9". The only items that match the variety code "SKNA-1701" are a table entry in one research note. The Seednet name "GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2" matches sources about Gujarat Amaranth-2 (GA-2), a different variety released in 1998. Under each heading below, I state which name the evidence refers to.

STRESS TOLERANCE
variety_name (GA-9): No evidence found. Searches returned only general statements about grain amaranth as a crop (drought, salinity, frost tolerance) and no variety-specific data. -- https://journaljsrr.com/index.php/JSRR/article/view/3463 (crop-level only, discarded)
seednet_variety_name (GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2): No evidence found. No stress-tolerance statement for GA-2 was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
variety_name (GA-9): No evidence found.
seednet_variety_name (GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2): No evidence found. One source says Gujarat Amaranth-1 was not affected by disease or insects, but that refers to GA-1, not GA-2 or GA-9. -- https://eng.kisanofindia.com/latest-news/amaranth-cultivation-10-advanced-varieties-give-good-yield-rich-in-many-nutrients (discarded for this heading)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
variety_name (GA-9): No evidence found for yield, maturity, or trial results.
seednet_variety_name (GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2): One popular article says GA-2 is early relative to GA-1, suited to plains, matures in about 90 days, and yields about 23 q/ha. This is unreplicated and not from a research source. -- https://eng.kisanofindia.com/latest-news/amaranth-cultivation-10-advanced-varieties-give-good-yield-rich-in-many-nutrients
seednet_variety_name (GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2): Gujarat Amaranthus-2 was released in 1998 for general cultivation, according to a review. -- https://agriarticles.com/grain-amaranth-pseudo-cereal/
variety_name (GA-9): Field trial at SDAU Regional Research Station (Sardarkrushinagar) on nitrogen and moisture stress exists, but the paper does not name the variety, so it is not attributed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344327393_Growth_and_yield_of_grain_amaranth_Amaranthus_hypochondriacus_L_as_influenced_by_nitrogen_management_under_different_moisture_stress (discarded)

GENETICS AND QTL
variety_name (GA-9): No evidence found. No QTL, marker, or genetic-parameter study naming GA-9 was found. The SKNA-1701 code appears only in a genotype table (see PUBLICATIONS).
seednet_variety_name (GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2): No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
variety_name (GA-9): No evidence found for breeder name(s). The input record gives the institution as ICAR-AICRN on Potential Crops, Centre for Crop Improvement, S.D. Agricultural University; I could not confirm this from search results.
seednet_variety_name (GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2): A review co-authored by SDAU scientists (R. S. Solanki, N. M. Bhut, D. P. Joshi, C. D. Prajapati) describes the GA-1 and GA-2 releases, but it does not state who bred GA-2. Attribution to these authors is not confirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/362761716_Agri_Articles_e-Magazine_for_Agricultural_Articles_Grain_Amaranth_Amaranthus_hypochondriacus_L_A_New_Millennium_Crop_of_Pseudo-Cereals
Institution context only: a genetic-diversity study used grain amaranth germplasm from the Centre for Crop Improvement, SDAU, Sardarkrushinagar. It does not name GA-9 or GA-2. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s42269-019-0146-2

CONTACT DETAILS
variety_name (GA-9): No breeder contact found. Institute-level details only:
Institution: Sardarkrushinagar Dantiwada Agricultural University (SDAU), Sardarkrushinagar, Gujarat 385506, India. Address from the author affiliations in the Springer study and Solanki et al. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s42269-019-0146-2
Website: www.sdau.edu.in -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardarkrushinagar_Dantiwada_Agricultural_University
Email and phone: not found.
seednet_variety_name (GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2): Same institute-level details as above. No breeder contact found.

PUBLICATIONS

Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding 9(4): 1484-1496. -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00184.9 (Code match only: SKNA-1701 is in the study's genotype list in the table. The snippet did not show GA-9 or the trait data for SKNA-1701, so this is not confirmed as the same material.)

Names GA-2 only. Relevant to the seednet name only.)

SEED AVAILABILITY
variety_name (GA-9): No evidence found. Results were generic rajgira/amaranth grain traders (IndiaMART, TradeIndia, and others) that do not name any variety. Discarded. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rajgira-seed-14484000562.html
seednet_variety_name (GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2): No evidence found. No NSC, state corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sale listing was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
variety_name (GA-9): No independent evidence found. The only source for the state list is the input record: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha. This needs verification against the CSC release minutes.
seednet_variety_name (GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2): No state list found for GA-2 in the search results. The popular article gives plains suitability only. -- https://eng.kisanofindia.com/latest-news/amaranth-cultivation-10-advanced-varieties-give-good-yield-rich-in-many-nutrients

Gaps to resolve: Confirm the release notification for GA-9 (CSC minutes) and check whether "GUJARAT AMARANTHS-2" on Seednet is a separate entry or a mislabel of GA-2. Seek the SDAU Centre for Crop Improvement or AICRN on Potential Crops (Grain Amaranth) annual reports and KrishiKosh for GA-9 data.

drought.details: No variety-specific drought evidence for KBGA-4 was found in the provided sources. The CABI review notes that water stress is associated with increased ambient temperature in the crop context, and that drought and heat stress at the terminal stage are high in northern regions, but these statements are not attributed to KBGA-4. The CABI and ICAR-type sources describe grain amaranth as generally rainfed.

heat.details: No KBGA-4-specific heat tolerance data was found. The CABI sources discuss higher temperatures and unpredictable rainfall as challenges for the crop in general, and the CABI review states that the crop may encounter extreme weather events such as drought, flood, heat and cold during its life cycle. These are crop-level statements only.

salinity.details: No salinity evidence for KBGA-4 was found in the provided search results.

flood.details: Crop-level evidence only: grain amaranth is generally grown as a rainfed crop and does not withstand waterlogging. No KBGA-4-specific flood data was found. The rating reflects the crop-level statement, not a variety-level test.

disease_resistance.summary: Root-knot nematode: CISH pathologist P.K. Shukla's studies report that Lalit, along with Dhawal, Lalima and Shweta, shows greater tolerance than foreign varieties, which are highly susceptible. This is a press report, not a peer-reviewed trial; no resistance level or quantitative data given. Wilt: No evidence found for Lalit. The CISH wilt-resistance work concerns P. molle x P. guajava rootstocks, not the Lalit scion. Generic 'tolerant to major pests and diseases' claim appears only on a commercial nursery listing and is unverified.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-specific resistance evidence found in the digest. The only pest-related statement ('tolerant to major pests and diseases') comes from a commercial nursery listing and is unverified; no pest is named.

agronomic_details.yield: CISH states about 100 kg/plant at about 6 years, higher than other commercial varieties (CISH claim). Bengaluru (Regional Horticultural Research Station, UHS): at 6 x 6 m spacing, 12.63 kg/tree; fertilizer/vermicompost treatment reached 33.43 t/ha (treatment effect, varietal attribution not explicit in digest). Meerut (SVPUAT, 2021-23): best nano urea/chelated zinc treatment gave 18.53 kg/tree and 205.90 q/ha (treatment effect, not a varietal baseline). Marathwada trial: Lalit gave the lowest yield among five cultivars (21.34 kg/tree, 51.29 q/ha), contradicting the CISH claim. Nursery listing claims 35-40 kg/plant; unverified and conflicts with CISH figures.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Yield results differ across the Marathwada trial (lowest among five cultivars) and CISH claim (higher than other commercial varieties); no multi-environment stability analysis found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Tested under Western Uttar Pradesh conditions (Meerut, SVPUAT, 2021-23) and in Bengaluru (Karnataka) research station trials and Marathwada (Maharashtra) trial. CISH developing institution is in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. No formal agro-climatic adaptation statement found in digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CISH states high responsiveness to pruning. Fruit is 185-200 g, with firm pink pulp, about 250 mg/100 g vitamin C, suited to table and processing use. CISH demonstrations used a planting density of 555 plants/ha (3 x 6 m) with paclobutrazol for regular flowering.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) CISH demonstrations: planting density 555 plants/ha (3 x 6 m) with paclobutrazol for regular flowering. (2) Bengaluru (Regional Horticultural Research Station, UHS): 6 x 6 m spacing gave 12.63 kg/tree; fertilizer/vermicompost treatment reached 33.43 t/ha. (3) Meerut (SVPUAT, 2021-23): best nano urea/chelated zinc treatment gave 18.53 kg/tree and 205.90 q/ha. (4) Marathwada trial: Lalit lowest yield among five cultivars (21.34 kg/tree, 51.29 q/ha). (5) Foliar micronutrient trial (Sonkar et al., 2024) is listed in the digest publications; results not summarised in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Root-knot nematode: CISH pathologist P.K. Shukla's studies report that Lalit, along with Dhawal, Lalima and Shweta, shows greater tolerance than foreign varieties, which are highly susceptible. This is a press report, not a peer-reviewed trial; no resistance level or quantitative data given. Wilt: No evidence found for Lalit. The CISH wilt-resistance work concerns P. molle x P. guajava rootstocks, not the Lalit scion. Generic 'tolerant to major pests and diseases' claim appears only on a commercial nursery listing and is unverified.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-specific resistance evidence found in the digest. The only pest-related statement ('tolerant to major pests and diseases') comes from a commercial nursery listing and is unverified; no pest is named.

genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: Anthocyanin QTL map (Allahabad Safeda x Purple guava): Lalit not included. Guava fruit-quality QTL map (PAU, Punjab): Lalit not confirmed as a mapping parent. No QTL effects attributable to Lalit found.

agronomic_performance.yield: CISH states about 100 kg/plant at about 6 years, higher than other commercial varieties (CISH claim). Bengaluru (Regional Horticultural Research Station, UHS): at 6 x 6 m spacing, 12.63 kg/tree; fertilizer/vermicompost treatment reached 33.43 t/ha (treatment effect, varietal attribution not explicit in digest). Meerut (SVPUAT, 2021-23): best nano urea/chelated zinc treatment gave 18.53 kg/tree and 205.90 q/ha (treatment effect, not a varietal baseline). Marathwada trial: Lalit gave the lowest yield among five cultivars (21.34 kg/tree, 51.29 q/ha), contradicting the CISH claim. Nursery listing claims 35-40 kg/plant; unverified and conflicts with CISH figures.
agronomic_performance.stability: Not found in searched sources. Yield results differ across the Marathwada trial (lowest among five cultivars) and CISH claim (higher than other commercial varieties); no multi-environment stability analysis found.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Tested under Western Uttar Pradesh conditions (Meerut, SVPUAT, 2021-23) and in Bengaluru (Karnataka) research station trials and Marathwada (Maharashtra) trial. CISH developing institution is in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. No formal agro-climatic adaptation statement found in digest.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: CISH states high responsiveness to pruning. Fruit is 185-200 g, with firm pink pulp, about 250 mg/100 g vitamin C, suited to table and processing use. CISH demonstrations used a planting density of 555 plants/ha (3 x 6 m) with paclobutrazol for regular flowering.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) CISH demonstrations: planting density 555 plants/ha (3 x 6 m) with paclobutrazol for regular flowering. (2) Bengaluru (Regional Horticultural Research Station, UHS): 6 x 6 m spacing gave 12.63 kg/tree; fertilizer/vermicompost treatment reached 33.43 t/ha. (3) Meerut (SVPUAT, 2021-23): best nano urea/chelated zinc treatment gave 18.53 kg/tree and 205.90 q/ha. (4) Marathwada trial: Lalit lowest yield among five cultivars (21.34 kg/tree, 51.29 q/ha). (5) Foliar micronutrient trial (Sonkar et al., 2024) is listed in the digest publications; results not summarised in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. -- https://cish.icar.gov.in/lalit.php (checked; no stress data)
- Root-knot nematode: CISH pathologist P.K. Shukla's studies report that Lalit, along with Dhawal, Lalima and Shweta, shows greater tolerance than foreign varieties, which are highly susceptible. Press report, not a peer-reviewed trial. -- https://thelucknowtribune.org/guava-the-poor-mans-apple-under-major-threat/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt: No evidence found for Lalit. The CISH wilt-resistance work concerns P. molle x P. guajava rootstocks, not the Lalit scion. -- https://www.nhb.gov.in/Training/Brochure/Guava_Central_Institute.pdf ; https://agriculture.institute/production-tech-fruit-crops/innovative-guava-hybrids-india/
- Generic "tolerant to major pests and diseases" claim: found only on a commercial nursery listing, unverified. -- https://plantparadise.in/products/lalit-guava-buy-lalit-guava-plant-online

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CISH states yield of about 100 kg/plant at about 6 years, higher than other commercial varieties, and high responsiveness to pruning. -- https://cish.icar.gov.in/lalit.php
- Fruit is 185-200 g, firm pink pulp, about 250 mg/100 g vitamin C, suited to table and processing use. -- https://cish.icar.gov.in/lalit.php
- Planting density of 555 plants/ha (3 x 6 m) with paclobutrazol for regular flowering, in CISH demonstrations. -- https://www.nhb.gov.in/Training/Brochure/Guava_Central_Institute.pdf
- Bengaluru (Regional Horticultural Research Station, UHS): at 6 x 6 m spacing, 12.63 kg/tree; fertilizer/vermicompost treatment reached 33.43 t/ha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353558516_Guava_Psidium_guajava_L
- Meerut (SVPUAT, 2021-23): best nano urea/chelated zinc treatment gave 18.53 kg/tree and 205.90 q/ha; this is a treatment effect, not a varietal baseline. -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/Enhancement-in-Yield-Parameters-of-Guava-(Psidium-guajava-L.)-cv.-Lalit-through-Foliar-Application-of-Nano-Urea-and-chelated-Zinc-under-Western-Uttar-Pradesh-conditions-Shalini-Singh-65.pdf
- Marathwada trial: Lalit gave the lowest yield among five cultivars (21.34 kg/tree, 51.29 q/ha), which contradicts the CISH claim. -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue10/PartM/8-10-152-997.pdf
- Nursery listing claims 35-40 kg/plant; unverified commercial source, conflicts with CISH figures. -- https://plantparadise.in/products/lalit-guava-buy-lalit-guava-plant-online

GENETICS AND QTL
- Origin: CISH describes Lalit as a superior seedling selection from Apple guava. -- https://cish.icar.gov.in/lalit.php ; the selection came from a half-sib population of Apple guava. -- https://agriculture.institute/production-tech-fruit-crops/innovative-guava-hybrids-india/
- Conflicting parentage: a nursery page says Allahabad Safeda x Chinese guava and calls it a hybrid. Not supported by CISH; treat as unverified. -- https://plantparadise.in/products/lalit-guava-buy-lalit-guava-plant-online
- Original selection: 631 open-pollinated seedlings of red-fleshed guava were evaluated at CISH, and Lalit was released on that basis (CISH 1999). -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304423813005438
- Anthocyanin QTL map (Allahabad Safeda x Purple guava): Lalit not included. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9370526/
- Guava fruit-quality QTL map (PAU, Punjab): Lalit not confirmed as a mapping parent. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10324979/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture (CISH), Lucknow. -- https://cish.icar.gov.in/lalit.php
- Lead breeder or scientist name for Lalit: No evidence found in the search results. CISH Director Shailendra Rajan is named in a 2020-era news item, not as breeder. -- https://www.thehawk.in/news/health/cish-ready-with-grafted-plants-rich-in-immunity-boosting
- Release year conflict: CISH's variety page lists 2024 (SVRC) and 2024 (CVRC). The ScienceDirect review cites a CISH 1999 release. The UP government announced the Lalit release for a 2024 ceremony. -- https://www.cish.org.in/varieties ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304423813005438 ; https://x.com/UPGovt/status/1822122743120142840
- Institute station: Rehmankhera, Lucknow. -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/39256324/HD-MO-Guava

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
- Institute address: Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture, Rehmankhera, Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh). Postal code, phone and email: No evidence found. -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/39256324/HD-MO-Guava
- Institute web pages: https://cish.icar.gov.in/lalit.php ; https://www.cish.org.in/varieties
- Institute scientist names (not breeders): Dr P.K. Shukla (pathology), Dr Prabhat Kumar (nematode prevention technology). -- https://thelucknowtribune.org/guava-the-poor-mans-apple-under-major-threat/

drought.details: Not found in searched sources. Drought tolerance of RMA 7 is unverified. The general grain amaranth drought review retrieved does not name RMA 7.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. Heat tolerance of RMA 7 is unverified.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. Salinity tolerance of RMA 7 is unverified. The general salinity review retrieved does not name RMA 7.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. Flood tolerance of RMA 7 is unverified.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Field-tolerance statements in the Raiger et al. package-of-practices review refer to other varieties (for example PRA and Durga) and are excluded as not relating to RMA 7.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest reaction for RMA 7 was located.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 14.32 q/ha (under normal condition). No trial yield figure for RMA 7 was found in the searched sources. The Odisha trial reports Suvarna as the highest-yielding entry at 11.23 q/ha; this is not a yield for RMA 7.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No location-by-location yield data for RMA 7 were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: plain areas for Rabi season. Institutional attribution places development at Mandor, Rajasthan. No agro-climatic validation from trial data was found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: CSC record: Not specified. Odisha trial (kharif 2019-2020, College of Agriculture, OUAT Bhubaneswar): RMA 7 matured in about 102.5 days, against about 104.2 days for Suvarna.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Odisha trial (kharif 2019-2020): RMA 7 had the longest panicle (38.9 cm) among the four varieties tested. CSC record morphological characteristics: Not specified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RECORD: Rajasthan Mandor Amarnath 7 (CSC name) / Rajasthan Mandor Amarnath 7 (RMA 7) (Seednet name). Crop: grain amaranth. Four web searches were run. None returned a page that uses the full CSC or Seednet name. Every relevant hit uses the short form "RMA 7" or "RMA-7" for grain amaranth, so the findings below refer to that short form.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned general grain amaranth drought and salinity reviews, and a Southern Italy trial of A. hypochondriacus, but none of these name RMA 7. Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance for RMA 7 remain unverified. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44279-024-00057-8 (general review, not RMA 7)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The field-tolerance statements located in the Raiger et al. package-of-practices review refer to other varieties (for example PRA and Durga), not RMA 7. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372162569_Traditional_to_Modern_Era_of_Grain_Amaranth_Amaranthus_Spp_Cultivation_Package_and_Practices

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In a kharif 2019–2020 trial at the College of Agriculture, Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology, Bhubaneswar, RMA 7 matured in about 102.5 days, against about 104.2 days for Suvarna, and it had the longest panicle (38.9 cm) among the four varieties tested. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/134764
- RMA 7 was one of four check varieties (with Suvarna, BGA-2 and GA-5) in an augmented-design evaluation of 59 grain amaranth genotypes, which the abstract attributes to the Agricultural Research Station, Tornala. The same record also gives a Bagalkot (University of Horticultural Sciences) field location and a 2016 date, so the site and season details are inconsistent. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/326717552_Genetic_Variability_Heritability_and_Genetic_Advance_in_Grain_Amaranth_Amaranthus_spp
- Yield (q/ha), trial location-by-location yield and seed quality for RMA 7 were not found. The Odisha trial reports Suvarna as the highest-yielding entry (11.23 q/ha) and does not give a yield figure for RMA 7 in the retrieved text. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/134764

GENETICS AND QTL
- An ISSR marker study of grain amaranth genotypes from India lists "RMA-7" as one of the genotypes in its gel figure, with an average polymorphism of 87.15%. RMA 7 was not analysed individually and no marker or QTL result is attributed to it. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s42269-019-0146-2
- No QTL or marker-trait study for RMA 7 was found. -- No further URL

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (institutional attribution only): Agricultural Research Station, Mandor, Jodhpur, Rajasthan, which is part of Agriculture University, Jodhpur (formerly Rajasthan Agricultural University). A grain amaranth list gives "RMA-4 (2) RMA 7" with the location "Mandor, Rajasthan". -- https://agriarticles.com/grain-amaranth-pseudo-cereal/
- The Agriculture University, Jodhpur profile lists "RMA 4, RMA 7" under grain amaranth at Mandor, Jodhpur. -- https://www.aujodhpur.ac.in/public/pdf/Agriculture-University-profile-Document.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
- Year of release (2010-12-23 in the CSC record) and parentage: No evidence found. The "selection from IC 35647" parentage in the review refers to RMA 4, not RMA 7. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372162569_Traditional_to_Modern_Era_of_Grain_Amaranth_Amaranthus_Spp_Cultivation_Package_and_Practices

A figure caption describes it as suited to rainfed organic conditions in the Uttarakhand hills, which is an adaptation note, not tolerance data. VL Chua 110: for rainfed organic ecology. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/314%20GENETIC-RESOURCES,-VARIETAL-AND-VALUE-ADDED-DEVELOPMENT-OF-GRAIN-AMARANTH-IN-INDIA-STATUS-AND-PROSPECTS.pdf

IPU 17-2 is not among them -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/blackgram-and-greengram?lgn=en

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

GENETICS AND QTL

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found naming the lead breeder or developing scientists for Dristi/Drishti or IPU 17-2. The only institutional reference located was a general review that cites the Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur, in pulse breeding work, not in connection with this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/46194378_Role_of_classical_breeding_in_improvement_of_pulse_crops

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute-division email, phone, postal address, or contact page for this variety was returned by the searches.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for a Dristi or Drishti (IPU 17-2) publication, report, thesis, or DOI. The closest hit was an unrelated blackgram variability study on PU-19 and other cultivars: Authors not verified (Year not verified). Genetic variability studies for yield, its attributes and quality traits in blackgram [Vigna mungo (L.)]. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368351348_GENETIC_VARIABILITY_STUDIES_FOR_YIELD_ITS_ATTRIBUTES_AND_QUALITY_TRAITS_IN_BLACKGRAM_Vigna_mungo_L

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for Dristi or Drishti seed from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales, or private dealers. The seed-availability query returned only general Vikaspedia blackgram content.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found that Dristi or Drishti is recommended for Madhya Pradesh or any other state. The input record gives Madhya Pradesh, but no source confirms it.

NOTES ON THE RECORD
- Name mismatch: CSC minutes use "Dristi" and Seednet uses "Drishti". Neither spelling produced variety-specific results, so this cannot be resolved from the evidence.
- Crop mismatch: the Seednet crop field reads "ASH GOURD (PETHA)", but the variety is recorded as blackgram. This should be checked against Seednet before the record is used.
- Search limit: the search tool's usage cap was reached after four queries, so the planned verification searches (for example, KrishiKosh, IIPR release notifications, and seed-agency listings) could not be run. Coverage is therefore incomplete, and the absence of evidence above reflects the searches run, not confirmed absence of data.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: RECOMMENDED FOR RELEASE AND CULTIVATION IN THE STATES OF PUNDICHERRY, TAMILNADU, KERALA AND TRIPURA IN SUMMER AND KHARIF SEASON.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: SUITABLE FOR BOTH SUMMER AND RAINY SEASONS I BOTH IN SOUTH AND NORTH INDIA. IT RESPONSES WELL TO OPTIMUM DOSES OF NITROGENOUS FERTILIZERS. IT REQUIRES MORE MOISTURE FOR RAPID DEVELOPMENT AT EARLY STAGE OF CROP GROWTH.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 6.0 M ; PLANT TYPE : VINES ARE LARGE, HAIRY AND SPREADING ; LEAF CHARACTERS : LARGE, SILVERY GREEN, HAIRY AND LOBED LEAVES WITH LONG PETIOLES ; FRUIT CHARACTERS : THE FRUITS ARE GREEN IN IMMATURE STAGE AND WHITE IN FULL MATURE STAGE. THEY ARE CYLINDRICAL, RIND COLOUR GREEN, IMMATURE FRUITS ARE PUBESCENT, CYLINDRICAL . MATURE FRUITS HAVE A DENSE PELT OF MINUTE HAIRS AND COVERED WITH A WHITE WAXY BLOOM. THE AV. FRUITS WT. IS 7 KG AND AV. NUMBER OF FRUITS PER PLANT IS 3.10. THE FRUIT FLESH IS WHITE AND SEEDS ARE CREAMY WHITE IN COLOUR.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: AS OTHER LINES OF ASH GOURD.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: IT IS ALSO RESISTANT TO CUCUMBER MOSAIC VIRUS AND WATER MELON MOSAIC VIRUS AND OTHER MAJOR DISEASES AND INSECTS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: AS IN OTHER LINES OF ASH GOURD.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Apple-1 (apple, SKUAST-K)

Name note: The CSC name is "Shalimar Apple-1" and the Seednet name is also "Shalimar Apple-1". Sources use "Shalimar Apple 1" (no hyphen) and "Shalimar Apple-1". All findings below refer to Shalimar Apple-1 unless marked otherwise. No Seednet record was retrieved, so I could not confirm the variety code H0611001 or the 2012 release date from a primary source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No stress-tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) evidence found for Shalimar Apple-1 specifically. Searches covered this topic. -- No URL
- A 2024 storage study describes the 'Shalimar' apple as a relatively new cultivar known for resistance to apple scab and powdery mildew. Its variety number is not given, so this may or may not refer to Shalimar Apple-1. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11009402/ ; https://link.springer.com/10.1038/s41598-024-57688-6

DISEASE AND PEST
- Breeding summaries list Shalimar Apple-1 as bred for scab resistance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353038434_Apple_Breeding
- Breeding summaries list Shalimar Apple-2 as tolerant to scab and Alternaria leaf spot, a different cultivar. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353038434_Apple_Breeding
- No pest-specific (insect or mite) resistance data for Shalimar Apple-1 was found. -- No URL

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A breeding table gives Shalimar Apple-1 a yield of about 95 kg per tree (about 23.75 t/ha), though the table does not say under which trial conditions this was measured. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353038434_Apple_Breeding
- A storage study on 'Shalimar' apples found controlled atmosphere at 1 °C effective for long-term storage, and dynamic CA with CO2 monitoring a good option for quality and aroma. Cultivar number is not stated. -- https://link.springer.com/10.1038/s41598-024-57688-6
- A SKUAST-K trial at the Pomology experimental field, Srinagar, evaluated fruit traits of Shalimar Apple-2 and other cultivars on MM-106 rootstock, and reported Shalimar Apple-2 as the lowest-yield-efficiency cultivar. This is not Shalimar Apple-1. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10361390
- A SKUAST-K bloom and fruit-set study included Shalimar among early-blooming selections with good pollen compatibility, without separating the numbered Shalimar selections. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Apple-cultivars-grown-in-the-Kashmir-Valley_tbl3_339521395

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL or marker studies for Shalimar Apple-1 were found. -- No URL
- Parentage: the breeding table lists Shalimar Apple-1 as Sunhari x Prima. The input record says "Not specified", so this conflicts with the record and should be checked. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353038434_Apple_Breeding ; https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/advances-in-apple-breeding-sanjay-chetrypptx/259080077
- Shalimar Apple-2 is listed as Red Delicious x Ambri in the same table. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353038434_Apple_Breeding

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The breeding table credits SKUAST (K), Srinagar, J&K as the developing institution for Shalimar Apple-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353038434_Apple_Breeding
- A breeding overview credits hybridization work to the Regional Fruit Research Station, Mashobra, FRS Shalimar (J&K), and the Chaubattia station, and lists Shalimar Apple 1 as Sunheri x Prima. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/advances-in-apple-breeding-sanjay-chetrypptx/259080077
- No lead breeder or scientist name for Shalimar Apple-1 was found. -- No URL
- Institution background: SKUAST-K has its main campus and Faculty of Horticulture at Shalimar, Srinagar. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sher-e-Kashmir_University_of_Agricultural_Sciences_and_Technology_of_Kashmir

CONTACT DETAILS

agronomic_details.yield: Reported green fodder yield is about 877 quintal per acre. In two kharif seasons (2018 and 2019) at the PAU forage research farm, Ludhiana, PBN 342 gave the highest green fodder and dry matter yields among the bajra napier hybrids tested.

agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Hybrid napier bajra (pearl millet x napier grass forage hybrid). Sprouts early in spring and stays vegetative until winter onset. Leafy hybrid with smooth, non-hairy, broad leaves. Forage quality was reported as superior among hybrids tested. Nitrogen trial: 120 kg N/ha/cut gave the highest yield, statistically similar to 75 kg N/ha/cut; higher N reduced stump mortality.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Two kharif seasons (2018 and 2019), PAU forage research farm, Ludhiana: PBN 342 gave the highest green fodder and dry matter yields among the bajra napier hybrids tested, with superior quality. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PBN 342 -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

NOTE: Both name fields read "PBN 342", so variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical. The Seednet crop name is "BAJRA NAPIER HYBRID", a pearl millet × napier grass forage hybrid, not a grain millet. All evidence below refers to that forage hybrid. Searches ran 4 times (fodder/variety, breeder, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for PBN 342. The search returned stress-tolerance statements for other napier-type grasses (Co 4, Super Napier), which were discarded. -- https://uknowledge.uky.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=6529&context=igc (discarded: different variety)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for PBN 342 appeared in any search result.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
PBN 342 is a hybrid napier bajra that sprouts early in spring and stays vegetative until winter onset. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intEventID=4179
PBN 342 is described as a leafy hybrid with smooth, non-hairy, broad leaves. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344124034_Bajra_Napier_Hybrid_An_Ideal_Crop_for_Round_the_Year_Green_Fodder_Production
Reported green fodder yield is about 877 quintal per acre. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intEventID=4179 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344124034_Bajra_Napier_Hybrid_An_Ideal_Crop_for_Round_the_Year_Green_Fodder_Production
In two kharif seasons (2018 and 2019) at the PAU forage research farm, Ludhiana, PBN 342 gave the highest green fodder and dry matter yields among the bajra napier hybrids tested, and its quality was also superior. -- https://rmaj.in/rma/article/view/649
Nitrogen response trial: 120 kg N/ha/cut gave the highest yield, statistically similar to 75 kg N/ha/cut; higher N reduced stump mortality. This trial covered the bajra napier varieties in the PAU study, including PBN 342. -- https://rmaj.in/rma/article/view/649

GENETICS AND QTL
PBN 342 is listed as one of 34 napier grass genotypes from the PAU Forage Research Farm in an SSR-based diversity study of napier grass. This is a diversity study, not a QTL or mapping study. -- https://publications.rmsi.in/index.php/rma/article/download/1375/811/3163
Parentage: No PBN 342-specific parentage found. Bajra napier hybrids in general are bajra × napier crosses, but this is not confirmed for PBN 342. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344124034_Bajra_Napier_Hybrid_An_Ideal_Crop_for_Round_the_Year_Green_Fodder_Production (general, not variety-specific; treat as unverified)
QTL / marker data specific to PBN 342: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Notified by Rahul Kapoor and R. S. Sohu (2018) as "Bajra Napier Hybrid-PBN 342". -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=0&intFacultyID=475&intLinkID=9&strDepTitle=
Rahul Kapoor's profile lists the role "Assistant Forage Breeder (Forage and Millets Section)" from 1 December 2009, with a mandate covering napier bajra hybrids. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=0&intFacultyID=475&intLinkID=9&strDepTitle=
Developing institution: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana. Station: Forage and Millets Section, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics (forage farm). -- https://publications.rmsi.in/index.php/rma/article/download/1375/811/3163 ; https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=0&intFacultyID=475&intLinkID=9&strDepTitle=

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder name and role: Rahul Kapoor, Assistant Forage Breeder (Forage and Millets Section), PAU. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=0&intFacultyID=475&intLinkID=9&strDepTitle=
Breeder email, phone and postal address: No evidence found in retrieved text. Use the PAU College of Agriculture faculty page above to look these up.
Institute: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, Punjab, India. Institute-level page: https://pau.edu (no phone or email found in retrieved text).

PUBLICATIONS
Kapoor, R. and Sohu, R. S. (2018). Notification of crop varieties and registration of germplasm: Bajra Napier Hybrid-PBN 342. Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding 78(2): 283. -- URL/DOI not found in retrieved text; citation appears at https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=0&intFacultyID=475&intLinkID=9&strDepTitle= and https://pau.edu/content/downloads/icar/icar_1.pdf
Authors not shown (approx. 2019-2020 publication). Fodder productivity and quality assessment of bajra napier hybrid varieties under different nitrogen levels. Journal not confirmed (page hosted on rmaj.in). -- https://rmaj.in/rma/article/view/649
Authors not shown (year not shown). Hybrid napier and napier genotype diversity study including PBN 342 (SSR-based). Journal: Range Management and Agroforestry (publications.rmsi.in). -- https://publications.rmsi.in/index.php/rma/article/download/1375/811/3163
Other PAU-related titles found but not PBN 342: Sidhu and Mehndiratta (1986), PBN-83, and Sidhu et al. (2001), PBN-233 -- discarded as different varieties.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned only unrelated pages (native seed strategy, pesticide labels, a Buffalo property grant). No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, PAU seed sales or dealer listing for PBN 342 appeared.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Record states (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Odisha, Assam, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka) are not confirmed by any retrieved page. A Karnataka bajra napier trial snippet was found but does not name PBN 342, so it was discarded. -- No evidence found for PBN 342. The PAU ICAR ranking page confirms only a gazette entry for PBN 342 under Bajra Napier, not the state list. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/icar/icar_1.pdf

Gazette reference (release): "Bajra Napier · PBN 342 · S.O.1379(E)/27.3.2018", consistent with the 2018-01-20 release year in the record. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/icar/icar_1.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The variety-specific searches returned no page on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for Phule Priya (fieldpea). Results about the ICAR-IIPR fieldpea lines IPF 16-13, IPFD 12-8 and IPFD 9-2 were discarded as other varieties. -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page recorded disease or pest reaction for Phule Priya. The IIPR varieties page describes powdery mildew and rust resistance for other fieldpea lines, which does not apply to this variety. -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. No yield, maturity or multi-location trial record for Phule Priya was returned. The only Phule Priya entry is the state-wise recommendation list (see RECOMMENDED STATES). The 2015-16 NEH pulses report covers DPL 15 and was discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308680263_Annual_Report_2015-16_on_Promotion_of_Pulses_in_NEH_Region

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No QTL, marker or pedigree study for Phule Priya was returned. The "variant from Giant Cavendish group" parentage in the input is a banana-type description and was not supported by any fieldpea source. -- https://www.itfnet.org/v1/tag/phule-pride/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. No page named a lead breeder or scientist for Phule Priya, and none linked Phule Priya to MPKV fieldpea breeding. The institution given in the input (Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth) is not confirmed by any fieldpea source. The Phule Pride banana pages name MPKV's Banana Research Station, Jalgaon, but that is a different crop and was excluded. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue12/PartAP/11-12-584-403.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone or postal address for Phule Priya or MPKV fieldpea was returned. The ICAR-IIPR crop improvement page lists fieldpea in its mandate, but it gives no contact details in the retrieved text and does not name this variety, so it is not used here. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/cimprovment/

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, thesis or conference item on Phule Priya was returned. The papers that came up cover other fieldpea varieties or other crops and were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for Phule Priya (fieldpea). Name mismatch: the Seednet name "Phule Pride" with crop "BANANA" is a banana record. Under the strict-relevance rule these banana pages were excluded from the fieldpea record:
- Phule Pride is a banana (AAA) clone released from the Banana Research Station, Jalgaon, MPKV. It is a natural mutant of Grand Naine, which fits the "Giant Cavendish group" parentage in the input, so the Seednet record and parentage appear to describe the banana, not the fieldpea. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue12/PartAP/11-12-584-403.pdf
- A 2024 paper on plant spacing in banana cv. Phule Pride (AAA) is also a banana source. -- https://download.sdiarticle5.com/2024/Aug/09-Aug-24/2024_JEAI_121287/Rev_JEAI_121287_Dia_A.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
Maharashtra. The DPD (GoI) state-wise pulses list gives Phule Priya (RHRP-87) under fieldpea for Maharashtra, with year 2015. The name is printed as "Phule Priva" in the scanned text, which appears to be an OCR error for Phule Priya. The input release date is 2014-01-13, which does not match this 2015 listing; the discrepancy is unresolved. -- https://dpd.gov.in/1.%20Final%20State-wise%20within%2010%20Yrs.%20Pulses%20(Compile).pdf

Additional note: a PPV&FRA annual report (2015-16) lists Phule Priya in a variety list that sits near the fieldpea entries. The crop heading is not clear in the retrieved text, so this is recorded as unconfirmed. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/eannual-report-15-16.pdf

drought.details: The variety is tolerant to drought and can withstand water stress. It is also described as resistant to water stress.

heat.details: While planting practices may offer protection against heat stress for Phule Pride (e.g., specific planting distances), the inherent heat tolerance of the variety is not explicitly stated in the provided results.

salinity.details: Phule Pride can withstand salinity and is described as salt tolerant, including maintaining normal bunch mass even under marginal conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: The variety is generally described as disease resistant. It was developed utilizing an ITC accession, which is linked to disease-resistant breeding. No specific diseases are named for resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: Phule Pride is described as pest tolerant.

agronomic_details.yield: The variety promises almost 100% yield, attributed to its resistance to lodging. Bunch weight varies between 26-28 kg. It is generally considered superior to Grand Naine in terms of reliability.
agronomic_details.stability: Information on stability across diverse environments is not explicitly detailed, but its multiple stress tolerances suggest adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Western Maharashtra, Kerala, and particularly suitable for North and Central India.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Phule Pride is a natural dwarf variety with early maturity, bearing fruit about two months earlier than Grand Naine. Its plant architecture is dwarf and slender, unlike the tapering top of Grand Naine. It is resistant to lodging, pseudostem breaking, and bunch breaking. It is also tolerant to high wind velocity (> 20 km/hr). Fruits are thick-skinned. They can be stored for two weeks in a cold store at 6-8°C. Recommended spacing is 1.5 x 1.5 m with specific fertilizer recommendations (10 kg FYM + 25 g Azospirillum + 25 g PSB + 150:60:150 g N:P2O5:K2O/plant) through fertigation in 44 weeks. Planting seasons are June, October, and February.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Studies have been conducted to evaluate the effect of different planting distances on growth, durational, bunch, and yield parameters, as well as disease resistance.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Phule Pride is categorized as a Musa (AAA) variety. It is described as a variant from the Giant Cavendish group and a natural dwarf mutant of Grand Naine, developed utilizing an ITC accession.

drought.details: No drought test specific to BH 885 was found in the digest. The nitrogen-level trial (CCSHAU, rabi 2019-20) reported BH 885 with higher effective tillers and 1000-grain weight than other tested cultivars under irrigated conditions, which does not address drought.

heat.details: BH 885 recorded the highest accumulated growing degree days and heat-unit values in the late-sown (2nd fortnight December) treatment, which indicates a thermal response rather than heat tolerance. The input record states minimum yield reduction under terminal heat stress, but the digest contains no independent BH 885 heat-stress trial to confirm this.

salinity.details: The Hisar barley programme description lists salinity and brackish-water resistance as breeding targets for the centre, but the source does not attribute this to BH 885. The input record states BH 885 performed better under salinity-alkalinity stress, but the digest has no independent BH 885 salinity data to verify this.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: No BH 885-specific rust, smut, stripe or other disease reaction was found. The stripe-disease study used BH-393 (not BH 885) as the susceptible check. The only disease-related content is general seed-treatment advice for covered smut, which is not variety-specific.

pest_resistance.summary: No BH 885-specific pest reaction was found. The only pest-related content is general seed-treatment advice for termites, which is not variety-specific.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources for BH 885. The digest gives BH 946 at about 33.11 q/ha in the 2019-20 nitrogen trial, and BH 885 gave lower grain yield than BH 946 and BH 393 in that trial, but no BH 885 value is stated. The input record gives the average yield unit only (Kg/Ha) with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. BH 885 appeared in trials at Hisar over rabi 2016-17 and 2017-18 and in the 2019-20 nitrogen trial, but no cross-environment stability analysis was reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Timely-sown, irrigated conditions (input record). Input record recommends sowing 10th to 25th November at 37.5 kg/acre seed rate. The digest's trials were conducted in Hisar, Haryana (semi-arid region).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Input record: tolerant to lodging, resistant to shattering, responsive to recommended doses of fertilizers and irrigation, very high biomass, bold grains, suitable for malting. Digest: two-row type with higher effective tillers and 1000-grain weight than other tested cultivars in the Hisar nitrogen trial. Input record morphological characteristics: Not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Nitrogen-level trial, CCSHAU Wheat and Barley Section, rabi 2019-20: BH 885 gave lower grain yield than BH 946 (about 33.11 q/ha) and BH 393; it had higher effective tillers and 1000-grain weight than other tested cultivars. (2) Growing-environment trial, Hisar, rabi 2016-17 and 2017-18, sowing dates 3 Nov to 19 Dec: BH 885 (V4) was one of four varieties; late-sown BH 885 had the highest GDD, HTU and PTU values. (3) Sowing-date and plant growth regulator trial at CCSHAU, rabi 2017-18: barley varieties were included but BH 885 inclusion was not confirmed. (4) Fodder-yield and growing-environment study (Forage Research, Vol. 50 No. 2, 2024): reports BH885 under sowing-date treatments; no results were extracted. (5) Morphological response to sowing dates: BH 885 inclusion not confirmed. (6) Stripe-disease study: BH-393 was the check; BH 885 was not confirmed as a tested entry.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME/CROP CHECK: The input record says "BH-85" / cashew nut, but the Seednet name "BH 885" is listed under BARLEY (JAU), and the institution (CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar), parentage (BH 563 two-row male-sterile line, RD 2508, PL 419) and notification data all describe a barley variety. The cashew hits found for "BH-85" refer to a different cashew germplasm/hybrid. The findings below are for barley BH 885. The year of release in the input (2008-10-07) does not match the notification date found (10.09.2012).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Two-row BH 885 showed higher effective tillers and 1000-grain weight than other tested cultivars in a Hisar nitrogen trial, but no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence test specific to BH 885 was found. -- https://scialert.net/fulltext/?doi=ijar.2022.1.4
- BH 885 recorded accumulated growing degree days and heat-unit values that were highest in the late-sown (2nd fortnight December) treatment, indicating its thermal response, not heat tolerance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344596811_RESPONSE_OF_BARLEY_GENOTYPES_TO_DIFFERENT_NITROGEN_LEVELS_UNDER_IRRIGATED_TIMELY_SOWN_CONDITIONS
- Hisar barley programme description lists salinity and brackish-water resistance as breeding targets for the centre, but this is not attributed to BH 885 in the source. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-48-Barley-Varieties-and-Genetic-Stocks-A-Compendium.pdf
- No evidence found for flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No BH 885-specific rust, smut, stripe or pest reaction found. The stripe-disease study used BH-393 (not BH 885) as the susceptible check. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-5-2019/Satish%20Kumar%20and%20S.S.%20Karwasra.pdf
- General seed-treatment advice for covered smut and termites (not variety-specific). -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/barley?lgn=en

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Nitrogen-level trial, CCSHAU Wheat and Barley Section, rabi 2019-20: BH 885 gave lower grain yield than BH 946 and BH 393 (BH 946 ~33.11 q/ha). -- https://scialert.net/fulltext/?doi=ijar.2022.1.4
- Growing-environment trial, Hisar, rabi 2016-17 and 2017-18 (sowing dates 3 Nov to 19 Dec): BH 885 (V4) among four varieties; highest GDD/HTU/PTU in late-sown BH 885. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341321791_Analysis_and_Correlation_among_Agronomic_and_Weather_Parameters_in_Barley_Hordeum_vulgare_L_Cultivars_under_Semi-Arid_Regions_of_Haryana_India
- Sowing-date and plant growth regulator trials at CCSHAU (rabi 2017-18) included barley varieties, but BH 885 inclusion was not confirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344229153_PERFORMANCE_OF_BARLEY_VARIETIES_AS_INFLUENCED_BY_THE_APPLICATION_OF_DIFFERENT_PLANT_GROWTH_REGULATORS
- Fodder-yield and growing-environment study (Forage Research, Vol. 50 No. 2, 2024) reports BH885 under sowing-date treatments. -- https://forageresearch.in/category/vol-50-2/

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found (no QTL, marker or pedigree-genetics study for BH 885 was retrieved). Parentage data are from the notification listing only. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf (not confirmed for BH 885 parentage; the parentage string is from the input record and https://hau.ac.in/page/achievements-36)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. Breeder names for BH 885 were not retrieved.
- Developing institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar (CCSHAU), Wheat and Barley section, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding. -- https://hau.ac.in/page/achievements-36 ; https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/varieties-of-barley/
- Cereal-breeding network record lists the variety as a two-row CCSHAU, Hisar release of 2012 (SVRC). -- https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/varieties-of-barley/

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Department of Genetics & Plant breeding, CCS HAU, Hisar.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Punjab, Haryana, Western Uttar Pradesh (excluding Jhansi division), Delhi, Rajasthan (excluding Kota AND Udaipur divisions), Uttarakhand, Jammu & Kathua districts of J&K under timely sown irrigated conditions.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Tolerant to lodging; resistant to shattering, responsive to recommended doses of fertilizers and irrigations; suitable for timely sown with a seed rate of 35-37.5 kg/acre
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
BH 946 is having semi erect growth habit at boot stage with profuse tillering and medium size dark green leaves.
ii) BH 946 has very strong stem and club shaped dense ear heads.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: BH 946 gave compatible yield performance to check NDB 1173 in salinity alkali trials. The variety also showed minimum reduction in grain yield under terminal heat stress conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: It exhibited excellent degree of resistance to yellow rust and leaf rusts, leaf blight, covered smut and powdery mildew.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: It showed at par reaction to checks against aphid attack.

drought.details: No direct drought tolerance rating for BH 946 was found in the search results. It appears as a check or comparison genotype in AICRP NWPZ trials under rising temperature and water stress. The 2022 Wheat and Barley Newsletter reports that BH 946 produced significantly higher yield than DWRB 160 overall, but the snippet does not say whether this was under drought. A drought screening symposium abstract names BH-946 with RD-2907 for biological yield per plant, which is not a tolerance rating.

heat.details: The original variety data states that BH 946 showed minimum reduction in grain yield under terminal heat stress. The search results do not give a heat susceptibility index for BH 946. The newsletter heat-stress indices (TOL and HSI) named other genotypes: DBW107, HD3118 and Raj3765. The rating is therefore based mainly on the supplied variety data and is graded medium.

salinity.details: The original data states that BH 946 gave yield compatible with check NDB 1173 in salinity/alkali trials. Barley is generally described as inherently tolerant of salinity and alkalinity. The compendium and pocket guide list BH 946 as a feed barley for irrigated, timely sown conditions. The salt-tolerant varieties highlighted in the sources are others, such as KRL 210 and NDB 1173. BH 946 is therefore comparable to a tolerant check rather than a dedicated salt-tolerant variety.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data for BH 946 was found. A general source states that barley cannot tolerate waterlogging.

disease_resistance.summary: Not specified in the original data. A ResearchGate snippet (Pesticide Resistance and its Management in Insect Pests) mentions rust and leaf blight in a list that includes BH 946, but the context is truncated, so specific resistance cannot be confirmed.

pest_resistance.summary: No resistance was documented. The IIWBR Annual Report 2017-18 lists a study on grain borer on variety BH 946, which suggests storage pest susceptibility was studied, but no result is given in the snippet.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield is 51.96 q/ha under irrigated timely sown NWPZ conditions, with a potential of 66.32 q/ha (NSAI Seed Times table; IIWBR pocket guide gives 51.96 q/ha, feed). It recorded 63.02 q/ha at Chomu (Jaipur) in NWPZ trials (IIWBR Annual Report 2017-18). A ResearchGate snippet mentions an average yield of 21 (truncated, unit unclear).
agronomic_details.stability: BH 946 has been used as a check in recent AICRP NWPZ trials (2024) and performed at par with or better than DWRB 160 in 2020 and 2022 reports. This indicates sustained relevance and reasonably stable performance.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated, timely sown conditions in the North Western Plains Zone. It is a six-row hulled feed barley. Recommended states are Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh (western), Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir (Jammu and Kathua districts).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: nan. Original data: tolerant to lodging, resistant to shattering, responsive to recommended fertilizer and irrigation, seed rate 35-37.5 kg/acre for timely sowing.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Tested in AICRP NWPZ irrigated timely sown trials and used as a check. Reported yields include 63.02 q/ha at Chomu. In the 2020 report it was at par with DWRB 160, and in the 2022 newsletter it yielded significantly more than DWRB 160. Salinity/alkali trials gave yields comparable to check NDB 1173.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I could not complete the required search plan. The tool hit its server-side use limit after only two successful searches, so the digest below covers only what those two returned. Several headings have no evidence because those topics were never searched, not because nothing exists.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Central Barley DWRB 137 (barley)
Name note: The CSC name is "Central Barley DWRB 137" and the Seednet name is "Central Barley DWRB-137". The IIWBR variety list spells it "Central Barley (DWRB 137)". I did not reach Seednet, so no evidence specific to the Seednet record was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- DWRB137 is described as a six-row, high-yielding barley for irrigated, timely-sown conditions; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were retrieved. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/84065
DISEASE AND PEST -- Stripe rust resistance is reported for DWRB137 in the same article. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/84065

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Over central-zone check varieties, DWRB137 reportedly out-yielded BH959 by 10.67%, PL751 by 9.01% and RD2786 by 5.46%. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/84065
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- In the North Eastern Plains Zone, DWRB137 had a mean grain yield of 37.93 q/ha. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/84065
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Listed as a central-zone six-row variety released in 2018 by CVRC, under ICAR-IIWBR Karnal. -- https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/varieties-of-barley/
MATURITY -- No evidence found (search not completed).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found (search not completed).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution listed as ICAR-IIWBR, Karnal, with release year 2018. -- https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/varieties-of-barley/
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder name(s) not found in retrieved evidence. -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder or institute contact details were retrieved from the search results. An IIWBR contact page would need to be checked directly at https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/. -- No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS -- The JWR article on DWRB137 is found, but its authors, year and volume were not in the retrieved snippet. Entry: [Authors not retrieved] ([Year not retrieved]). DWRB137: Six row, high yielding and stripe rust resistant feed barley for irrigated timely sown conditions of north eastern plains zone and central zone. Journal of Wheat Research -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/84065
PUBLICATIONS -- No KrishiKosh theses, AICRP reports or other papers were searched. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found (search not completed).

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Supplied in the record: Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Kota and Udaipur division of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand, West Bengal (excluding hills), Odisha, Assam and plains of NE states. The retrieved evidence confirms the central and NE plains zones only; it does not independently verify the full list. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/view/84065

Suggested next steps: rerun the seed availability search, the breeder/contact search (IIWBR site and Seednet), and the research/QTL search (KrishiKosh, AICRP reports) in a new session.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DARL-70 (CSC name) / DL-70 (Seednet name)

Name and crop check: No search result mentions "DARL-70" under chili or any other crop. All barley evidence concerns "DL-70" under BARLEY (JAU), so the findings below refer to the Seednet name DL-70, not the CSC name. The record's crop ("chili") conflicts with the Seednet crop ("BARLEY (JAU)"), and the search turned up no chili evidence. The record's 2014 release year, DIBER/DRDO institution, and BG-1 x M-5-13 parentage were not corroborated. The only notification found is dated 1977 (see below).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for DL-70 specifically. A general AICRPW&B compendium states that its barley releases include drought- and salinity-tolerant types, but it does not name DL-70 for either trait -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-48-Barley-Varieties-and-Genetic-Stocks-A-Compendium.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for DL-70. The same compendium mentions disease- and insect-resistant releases in general terms only -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-48-Barley-Varieties-and-Genetic-Stocks-A-Compendium.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No multi-location or field-trial results for DL-70 were found. A 1985 study reports that DL-70, a six-row barley, was gamma-irradiated at 0 to 250 krad and malted with and without gibberellic acid, with malting quality as the outcome -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/j.2050-0416.1985.tb04335.x

GENETICS AND QTL -- No QTL or marker study on DL-70 was found. The compendium lists "RANJIT (DL 70)" among released varieties and gives pedigree entries that include DL70 (e.g., RD2615/DL70/BG105), which suggests DL-70 is a parent in other crosses -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-48-Barley-Varieties-and-Genetic-Stocks-A-Compendium.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder name was found for DL-70. A DRDO DIBER document describes the institute's hydroponic fodder work, including barley, but does not mention DL-70 or any barley variety release -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/352827398_Role_of_DIBER_DRDO_Technologies_in_Improving_Livelihood_Opportunities_and_Curtailing_Migration_in_Uttarakhand

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, postal address, or contact page appeared in any result.

PUBLICATIONS --
Avtar (1985). Effect of irradiation on the malting quality of barley. Journal of the Institute of Brewing -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/j.2050-0416.1985.tb04335.x (DOI: 10.1002/j.2050-0416.1985.tb04335.x). Only the first author name appears in the result; co-authors were not visible.
No other DL-70 publication, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for DL-70 or DARL-70 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record's "Not specified" stands. The only related item is the 2015 Bihar list of notified varieties, which records DL-70 under BARLEY (JAU) with a notification date of 29/09/1977 and does not list states -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

Recommended action: Verify the crop (barley, not chili) and the release history against the CSC minutes and the Seednet entry. The 1977 notification date conflicts with the 2014 release date in the record.

drought.details: Specific drought tolerance details for DWRB-223 are not available in the provided search results. Barley generally is known for drought resistance (RESULT_6, RESULT_19, RESULT_29). Other DWRB varieties, such as DWRB 92, have been identified as drought tolerant (RESULT_1, RESULT_5, RESULT_38). Challenges related to increasing water stress on barley productivity are noted (RESULT_4, RESULT_8).

heat.details: Specific heat tolerance details for DWRB-223 are not available in the provided search results. General barley research focuses on enhancing heat tolerance due to rising temperatures (RESULT_4, RESULT_8, RESULT_16). Some barley lines were found to be less tolerant to heat stress (RESULT_15). Other varieties like DWRB 92 have been identified as potentially heat stress tolerant (RESULT_17) or mentioned in the context of breeding for heat tolerance (RESULT_14, RESULT_50).

salinity.details: Specific salinity tolerance details for DWRB-223 are not available in the provided search results. Barley is inherently tolerant to salinity and alkalinity (RESULT_23, RESULT_29). Other DWRB varieties like DWRB 92 are described as salinity tolerant (RESULT_1, RESULT_11). Barley is evaluated under salinity conditions as part of trials (RESULT_27), and huskless barley with salt tolerance is a research objective (RESULT_30).

flood.details: Specific flood tolerance details for DWRB-223 are not available in the provided search results. Waterlogging tolerance is a research focus in barley (RESULT_34, RESULT_39), and some other sugarcane varieties are tolerant to water-logging (RESULT_10).

disease_resistance.summary: Specific disease resistance information for DWRB-223 is not available in the provided search results. General barley breeding efforts target disease resistance, including for rusts (RESULT_1, RESULT_25, RESULT_47, RESULT_49), spot blotch (RESULT_30, RESULT_34), and white rust (RESULT_19). Other varieties, like HUB-113, show tolerance to major diseases (RESULT_37).

pest_resistance.summary: Specific pest resistance information for DWRB-223 is not available in the provided search results. General insect resistance is mentioned for some barley genetic stocks (RESULT_1, RESULT_11) and combating insect pests is a research focus for wheat (RESULT_16, RESULT_20).

agronomic_details.yield: Not specified for DWRB-223 in the provided search results. Average yield for other barley varieties like DWRB 92 is available (e.g., 49.81 for malt in RESULT_21; ranges from 56.5 to 67.1 across environments in RESULT_38).
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified for DWRB-223 in the provided search results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation in Rajasthan (excluding Kota and Udaipur), Western Uttar Pradesh (except Jhansi), Jammu and Kathua district of Jammu and Kashmir, Paonta Valley (Himachal Pradesh), Una district of Himachal Pradesh, and Tarai region of Uttarakhand.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified in the provided search results. Other DWRB varieties are described, such as DWRB 92 being a two-row malt barley (RESULT_1, RESULT_23, RESULT_49).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Evaluation of 'AVT-II year entries' of wheat and barley under different growing conditions including timely, late, restricted irrigation, salinity, and high yield potential trials (HYPT) is conducted (RESULT_27). Given DWRB-223's release year of 2025, it is expected to have undergone such trials, but specific trial results for this variety are not detailed.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not specified directly for DWRB-223 in the provided search results. General QTL information related to Na content has been identified in other barley varieties like DWRB 64, DWRB 73, DWRB 92, DWRB 101, and DWRB 123 (RESULT_28).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not specified directly for DWRB-223 in the provided search results. QTLs related to Na content were located in other DWRB barley varieties (RESULT_28).
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not specified directly for DWRB-223 in the provided search results. Drought stress tolerant genotypes, like DBW 110, showed highest up-regulation of specific genes (RESULT_5), but no such details are given for DWRB-223.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for timely sown conditions, having good culm strength, seed rate-100 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: DWRB101 is two-row malt barley having erect flag leaf, green spikes (tapering type and intermediate density) with rudimentary lateral florets.  The peduncle is highly waxy.  Grains are yellow, bold with narrow crease width and rachilla hairs are scars type.

salinity.details: DWRB 101 was included in a nitrogen-response trial under saline-water irrigation (ResearchGate). That trial reports nitrogen optima for this condition only (economic optimum 67.7 kg/ha) and gives no tolerance rating. Salinity tolerance is therefore not established.

disease_resistance.summary: No evidence found that DWRB 101 has resistance to any disease. IIWBR pages mention rust and leaf blight screening of breeding material in general but do not name this variety. pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The CSC record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified', and no pest resistance evidence for DWRB 101 was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Not stated directly in the sources. The nitrogen-response trial reports that BH 946 was the top yielder, 5.1% above DWRB 101. This implies DWRB 101 yielded about 4,900 kg/ha, a figure derived from the reported percentage and not stated in the source.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated, timely-sown conditions in the North Western Plains Zone (IIWBR listing). The CSC record describes it as suitable for timely sown conditions. agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Two-rowed (IIWBR listing). Good culm strength and seed rate of 100 kg/ha (CSC agronomic features). Other morphological characteristics: Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Nitrogen-response trial under irrigated, timely-sown conditions: optimum N dose of 69.2 kg/ha; economic optimum of 67.7 kg/ha under saline-water irrigation. (2) In the same trial, DWRB 101 ranked second in harvest index (39.3), behind RD-2849. BH 946 was the top yielder, 5.1% above DWRB 101. (3) Malting evaluation (JWR): DWRB 101 was among genotypes meeting the malting standard for hot water extract and was rated suitable for two-row malt. (4) Grain beta-amylase of DWRB 101 was reported at 13.2 units (JWR, Barley beta-Amylase study). No other trial results were found.
