search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DWRB 101 (barley)

Name note: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "DWRB 101". No Seednet page for this variety came up in the four searches, so every finding below comes from non-Seednet sources (IIWBR, DWR bulletins, JWR journal, a ResearchGate paper). Searches run: (1) variety/release, (2) breeder/institution, (3) research, (4) seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to DWRB 101. A ResearchGate nitrogen trial included DWRB 101 under saline-water irrigation, but it reports only nitrogen optima for that condition, not a tolerance rating. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344596811_RESPONSE_OF_BARLEY_GENOTYPES_TO_DIFFERENT_NITROGEN_LEVELS_UNDER_IRRIGATED_TIMELY_SOWN_CONDITIONS

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for DWRB 101. IIWBR pages mention rust and leaf blight screening of breeding material in general, but do not name this variety. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/achievements/
- Seed-treatment and fungicide advice in the IIWBR pocket guide is general and does not name DWRB 101 as resistant. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- DWRB 101 was included in a nitrogen-response trial under irrigated, timely-sown conditions. It had the optimum N dose of 69.2 kg/ha, and the economic optimum was 67.7 kg/ha under saline-water irrigation. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344596811_RESPONSE_OF_BARLEY_GENOTYPES_TO_DIFFERENT_NITROGEN_LEVELS_UNDER_IRRIGATED_TIMELY_SOWN_CONDITIONS
- In that trial, DWRB 101 ranked second in harvest index (39.3), behind RD-2849. BH 946 was the top yielder, 5.1% above DWRB 101, which implies DWRB 101 yielded about 4,900 kg/ha (derived from the reported percentage, not stated directly). -- same URL
- Maturity: no evidence found.
- Seed rate and sowing guidance for barley in general (100 kg/ha, 5-7 cm depth) is not variety-specific. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/achievements/

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genotyping study naming DWRB 101 turned up in the searches.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR), Karnal, formerly the Directorate of Wheat Research. -- https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/varieties-of-barley/ ; https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-48-Barley-Varieties-and-Genetic-Stocks-A-Compendium.pdf
- Release: listed as DWRB 101, ICAR-IIWBR Karnal, 2015, CVRC, two-rowed. The input record gives a release date of 2014-10-20; the listing says 2015. -- https://iiwbr.icar.gov.in/varieties-of-barley/
- Parentage: a JWR paper's table gives DWR 28/BH 581, which differs from the input's DWR29/BH581 (the input bracket reads DWR28). Treat as a discrepancy to verify. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/171911/63098/496671
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level address (from the IIWBR seed portal footer, shown on a DWRB 137 page; applies to the institute, not to DWRB 101 specifically): "IIWBR, ICAR, PO Box - 158, Agrasain Marg, Karnal - 132001, Haryana, India." -- https://iiwbrseed.in/seed-details.aspx?id=20
- Breeder email and phone: No evidence found.
- Institute contact page: no URL retrieved in these searches. The institute site is https://iiwbr.org.in/ (domain only; not a verified contact page).

PUBLICATIONS
- Verma RPS, Kumar V, Sarkar B, Kharub AS, Kumar D, Selvakumar R, Malik R, Sharma I (2012). Barley cultivars released in India: Names, parentages, origins and adaptations. Research Bulletin No. 29, Directorate of Wheat Research, Karnal -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-29-Barley-cultivars-released-in-India-Names-parentages-origins-adaptations.pdf (this bulletin is the national release compendium; I did not verify a DWRB 101 entry inside it).
- Authors not shown in snippet (year not shown). Industrial evaluation for malting quality of Indian barley. Journal of Wheat Research (JWR), ICAR e-pubs -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/119498/46151/314330 (DWRB 101 was among genotypes meeting the malting standard for hot water extract and was rated suitable for two-row malt).
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Barley β-Amylase: Effect of Genotype and Growing Location. Journal of Wheat Research (JWR), ICAR e-pubs -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/171911/63098/496671 (grain β-amylase of DWRB 101 reported at 13.2 units).
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Response of barley genotypes to different nitrogen levels under irrigated timely sown conditions. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344596811_RESPONSE_OF_BARLEY_GENOTYPES_TO_DIFFERENT_NITROGEN_LEVELS_UNDER_IRRIGATED_TIMELY_SOWN_CONDITIONS
- KrishiKosh theses and AICRP annual reports naming DWRB 101: No evidence found in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- DWRB 101 is listed among ICAR-IIWBR wheat and barley varieties under the 2024-25 seed production programme. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/technology-developed/
- IIWBR seed portal lists DWRB 101 among its barley varieties, but no seed-details page or price/quantity was retrieved for it. -- https://iiwbrseed.in/seed-details.aspx?id=20
- Seednet listing: No evidence found.
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK and SAU seed sales: No evidence found.
- Excluded: "101 Balwan Research Barley Seed" (Keya Agri Seeds, Jaipur) is a different product with a name resemblance, so it is not attributed to DWRB 101. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/101-balwan-research-barley-seed-2854114026497.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- IIWBR lists DWRB 101 as a two-rowed malt barley for irrigated, timely-sown conditions in the North Western Plains Zone. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/bn/ ; https://iiwbr.org.in/technology-developed/
- The state list in the input record (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Western UP, Rajasthan excluding Kota and Udaipur) is not confirmed for DWRB 101. The only state-level zone description found (Tribune article) refers to DWRB-219, so I excluded it. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/haryana/karnal-scientists-behind-barley-variant/
- The technology page's header lists NWPZ, NEPZ and CZ. It is unclear whether those zones apply to DWRB 101 or to the page as a whole, so I have not treated them as confirmed. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/technology-developed/

agronomic_details.yield: Yield potential for DWRB 182 not found in searched sources. The AICRP 2021-22 multi-location table records values of 39.5 to 49.25 for DWRB 182 at Ludhiana, Mansa, Muktsar, Bathinda, Rewari, Bhiwani and Karnal, against check varieties PL 426 and BH 393. The digest does not confirm the measured trait or the units, so these values must not be quoted as kg/ha yield until the source table is checked.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The multi-location values above span seven sites, but no stability analysis was retrieved.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Sources describe DWRB 182 as an NWPZ, irrigated, timely-sown malt barley. The input lists Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Western Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan (except Kota and Udaipur divisions); the digest states this state-level list was not confirmed by any retrieved source. The release year is 2020 in the CVRC listing and 2021 on the IIWBR technology page; the input gives 2020-11-09, and the discrepancy is unresolved.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Two-rowed barley, malt type (CVRC listing). Morphology values were not retrieved.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP 2021-22 Social Sciences progress report: DWRB 182 was grown in farmer-field demonstrations, including at Bhiwani (Haryana) through KVK Bhiwani, alongside DWRB 137. (2) AICRP 2021-22 multi-location table: DWRB 182 recorded values of 39.5 to 49.25 at Ludhiana, Mansa, Muktsar, Bathinda, Rewari, Bhiwani and Karnal against checks PL 426 and BH 393; units and trait not confirmed in extracted text. (3) AICRP Barley technical programme, Rabi 2022-23: DWRB 182 is a check entry in quality and yield nurseries. (4) IIWBR Annual Report 2019: DWRB 182 was promoted to the All India Varietal Trial (AVT) on the basis of superiority over checks. No quantitative yield summary was retrieved.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: QTL or marker studies specific to DWRB 182: No evidence found. Pedigree (not stated on the variety record): DWRUB 52/DWRB 78. No SSR, SNP or positional marker data found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No evidence found for QTLs specific to DWRB 182. Malting quality: the IIWBR compendium reports low beta-glucan in grain, malt and wort for DWRB 182. EVIDENCE DIGEST: DWRB 182 (barley)
Name checked: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "DWRB 182". Evidence refers to this name, and the crop is barley. No seednet.gov.in page was retrieved; the seed-portal evidence comes from iiwbrseed.in.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to DWRB 182. The search returned only general barley pages. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drought_tolerance_in_barley (general barley, not this variety; discarded)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to DWRB 182. A 2022 RAC proceedings document lists DWRB 182 among varieties in the institute's work but gives no resistance data for it. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/RAC-Proceedings-IIWBR-for-ICAR-29032022.pdf

Units are not shown in the extracted text, so the table should be checked before quoting numbers. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363257945_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2021-22_Social_Sciences

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE [names: DWRB 73 / DWRB-73]
- Resistant to both leaf rust and yellow rust, per the IIWBR FAQ on a malt barley page -- https://www.academia.edu/49057570/Widening_the_malt_barley_cultivation_in_north_western_plains_of_India
- Described as a semi-dwarf, lodging-resistant plant type with erect leaves and stiff straw, in the DWR Vision 2030 document -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Vision-2030.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to DWRB 73. The search returned only general barley statements.

DISEASE AND PEST [names: DWRB 73 / DWRB-73]
- Listed among varieties to grow as resistant or tolerant, in the IIWBR barley cultivation pocket guide -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
- Seed treatment and fungicide spray recommendations in the same guide are general, not variety-specific -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
- No evidence found for loose smut, insect or other pest reactions specific to DWRB 73.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS [names: DWRB 73 / DWRB-73]
- Early maturing, with a duration of about 113 days (range 110-118), in the IIWBR malt barley paper -- https://www.academia.edu/49057570/Widening_the_malt_barley_cultivation_in_north_western_plains_of_India
- Averaged 3871 kg/ha and exceeded existing checks by up to 17.3% in grain yield, in the same paper -- https://www.academia.edu/49057570/Widening_the_malt_barley_cultivation_in_north_western_plains_of_India
- Listed at 38.70 for irrigated, late-sown conditions in the pocket guide's yield table; the unit is as printed, not converted -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
- Malting quality score of 15/27, comparable to the best check DWRUB 52 -- https://www.academia.edu/49057570/Widening_the_malt_barley_cultivation_in_north_western_plains_of_India
- Late-sown quality data: test weight 62.1, protein 12.3%, malt yield 85%, and friability 67% -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-varietes/malt-barley-variety/ (values from the DWRB 91 comparison table) and https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/41939/18644
- Used as a zonal check (two-row) in coordinated evaluation of DWRB 91 at 23 locations -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-varietes/malt-barley-variety/
- Gives good yield with acceptable malting quality under late sowing up to mid-December -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/41939/18644

GENETICS AND QTL [names: DWRB 73 / DWRB-73]
- Developed through a two-row by six-row hybridization, per the DWR Vision 2030 document -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/DWR-Vision-2030.pdf (this text names "DWRUB73", which is probably a typo for DWRB 73; treat as unconfirmed)
- Parentage PL 710/DWR 17 (from the input record) is NOT verified by any search result. The only pedigree found, "DWRB 62/DWRB 73", is the parentage of a different line, DWRB-160, and is excluded for this variety.
- No QTL or marker study specific to DWRB 73 found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION [names: DWRB 73 / DWRB-73]
- Developed by DWR, Karnal (Barley Network), listed with year 2011 and CVRC release, in the IIWBR barley varieties table -- https://iiwbr.org.in/varieties-of-barley/
- The Karnal institute is now ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research, which hosts the AICRP on Wheat and Barley -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-48-Barley-Varieties-and-Genetic-Stocks-A-Compendium.pdf
- No individual breeder or lead scientist name for DWRB 73 found. Names on the Beta-amylase paper (Dinesh Kumar, OP Gupta, Ram Pal, RPS Verma, GP Singh) are IIWBR authors on an unrelated study and are not attributed to this variety -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/171911/63098/496671

CONTACT DETAILS [names: DWRB 73 / DWRB-73]
- Institute-level only: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research, Karnal – 132001, India -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/171911/63098/496671
- Institute website: https://iiwbr.org.in/ (the Barley Improvement page, https://iiwbr.org.in/bn/, is also in the results)
- Genetic Resources Unit of IIWBR manages the notified-varieties database and supplies seed of notified varieties -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf
- No email, phone, or breeder contact found in any result.

PUBLICATIONS [names: DWRB 73 / DWRB-73]
- Authors not shown in the retrieved text (2025 or earlier). Widening the malt barley cultivation in north western plains of India. IIWBR malt barley paper (no journal or report name in retrieved text) -- https://www.academia.edu/49057570/Widening_the_malt_barley_cultivation_in_north_western_plains_of_India
- Authors not shown in the retrieved text. Barley research in India: Retrospect & prospects. Journal of Wheat Research -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/41939/18644
- ICAR-IIWBR (2017-18). Annual Report 2017-18 (lists DWRB 73 among released barley varieties). ICAR-IIWBR Karnal -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sendhil-Ramadas/publication/334083251_ICAR-IIWBR_Annual_Report_2017-18/links/5d15b62e92851cf440518d6f/ICAR-IIWBR-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- ICAR-IIWBR. Barley Varieties and Genetic Stocks: A Compendium (RB-48, 2024) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-48-Barley-Varieties-and-Genetic-Stocks-A-Compendium.pdf
- ICAR-IIWBR. Barley Cultivation in India, pocket guide (EB-53, 2023) -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or AICRP report specific to DWRB 73 was retrieved. The Academia.edu paper above cites AICRP Barley progress reports for 2005-06 and 2006-07, but these are references, not confirmed sources for DWRB 73.

SEED AVAILABILITY [names: DWRB 73 / DWRB-73]
- No Seednet portal page, NSC/state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or private dealer listing for DWRB 73 found.
- Breeder seed of seven barley varieties in the list including DWRB 73 was produced at the IIWBR farm, per the 2017-18 annual report -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Sendhil-Ramadas/publication/334083251_ICAR-IIWBR_Annual_Report_2017-18/links/5d15b62e92851cf440518d6f/ICAR-IIWBR-Annual-Report-2017-18.pdf
- Contract-farming companies in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and western UP supply two-row barley seed to farmers, but no named company is linked to DWRB 73 -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES [names: DWRB 73 / DWRB-73]
- Recommended for irrigated, late-sown conditions in the NWPZ, per the IIWBR barley page -- https://iiwbr.org.in/bn/
- Listed under NWPZ for late-sown conditions, in the IIWBR research review -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/41939/18644
- Late-sown malt barley for the northern plains in rotation with cotton, pearl millet, sorghum, maize and sugarcane -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-48-Barley-Varieties-and-Genetic-Stocks-A-Compendium.pdf
- The specific states in the input (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP, Delhi, Rajasthan except Kota and Udaipur) were NOT confirmed by any result. Only the zone and sowing condition are confirmed.

RELEASE RECORD (for reconciliation)
- The Bihar notified-variety list gives DWRB-73, notified 25/03/2011, S.O. 632(E) -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- The input's release date is 2010-12-23, which differs from the notification date above. The IIWBR table gives 2011. Confirm against the CSC minutes.
- Seednet portal page not retrieved, so the "DWRB 73" spelling is unverified on Seednet.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to DWRB 91. The institute page lists programme-level goals (drought, salinity and sowing-date adaptation) that are not tied to this variety. The only variety-specific description is that DWRB 91 was developed for irrigated late-sown conditions.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to DWRB 91. Programme-level goals on the institute page are not linked to this variety.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to DWRB 91. Salinity appears only as a programme-level goal on the institute page, not as a variety attribute.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to DWRB 91.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance or tolerance evidence found for DWRB 91 (rust, leaf blight and other diseases). The Karnal pocket guide's list of recommended resistant or tolerant varieties names DWRUB52, DWRB73, DWRUB64 and RD2552 and omits DWRB 91.

pest_resistance.summary: No aphid or other pest resistance evidence found for DWRB 91.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of 40.62 q/ha (equivalent to 4,062 kg/ha) under irrigated late-sown conditions, as listed in the Karnal pocket guide table. No other quantitative yield data found.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location or across-environment yield data beyond the single average-yield table value.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated late-sown conditions in the North Western Plain Zone (NWPZ) profile, per the Journal of Wheat Research retrospective. Recommended states as listed in the variety data: Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and Rajasthan (the source excludes Kota and Udaipur Division of Rajasthan). The MDPI study attributes excellent malt quality to on-time sowing, which is consistent with late-sown release.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Two-row malt barley (per the IIWBR page). Test weight of 64.5 recorded for the late-sown trial in the Journal of Wheat Research retrospective (column labels not fully legible in the extract). Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Karnal pocket guide: listed under irrigated late-sown conditions with an average yield of 40.62 q/ha and malt end use. (2) Journal of Wheat Research retrospective: 2013 release year, irrigated late-sown NWPZ profile, test weight 64.5 for the late-sown trial. (3) MDPI malting-quality evaluation (Foods 2022): hot water extract 81.0%, at or above the 80% benchmark, with differences among genotypes not statistically significant; malt homogeneity 95.9%, the highest in the set; filtration rate 226.1 mL/h, below the 250 mL/h desirable level; authors conclude excellent malt quality when sown on time. (4) Journal of Cereal Research malting study: one of four genotypes meeting international malting standards, with filtration rate falling short. Farmers' field trials and multi-location yield trials: Not found in searched sources.

agronomic_performance.adaptation: Irrigated late-sown conditions in the North Western Plain Zone (NWPZ) profile, per the Journal of Wheat Research retrospective. Recommended states as listed in the variety data: Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and Rajasthan (the source excludes Kota and Udaipur Division of Rajasthan). The MDPI study attributes excellent malt quality to on-time sowing, which is consistent with late-sown release.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Two-row malt barley (per the IIWBR page). Test weight of 64.5 recorded for the late-sown trial in the Journal of Wheat Research retrospective (column labels not fully legible in the extract). Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) Karnal pocket guide: listed under irrigated late-sown conditions with an average yield of 40.62 q/ha and malt end use. (2) Journal of Wheat Research retrospective: 2013 release year, irrigated late-sown NWPZ profile, test weight 64.5 for the late-sown trial. (3) MDPI malting-quality evaluation (Foods 2022): hot water extract 81.0%, at or above the 80% benchmark, with differences among genotypes not statistically significant; malt homogeneity 95.9%, the highest in the set; filtration rate 226.1 mL/h, below the 250 mL/h desirable level; authors conclude excellent malt quality when sown on time. (4) Journal of Cereal Research malting study: one of four genotypes meeting international malting standards, with filtration rate falling short. Farmers' field trials and multi-location yield trials: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DWRB 91 barley digest

Name note: the CSC minutes name and the Seednet name are both "DWRB 91" in the brief. Every source I found uses "DWRB 91" (sometimes "DWRB91"), so all evidence below refers to that one name. The Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) was not reached by any search, so no Seednet-specific evidence exists here.

STRESS TOLERANCE
DWRB 91 is a two-row malt barley developed by IIWBR, Karnal, for irrigated late-sown conditions. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/bn/
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance specific to DWRB 91: No evidence found. The programme-level goals (drought, salinity and sowing-date adaptation) are listed on the institute page but are not tied to this variety. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/bn/

DISEASE AND PEST
The pocket guide's list of recommended resistant or tolerant varieties names DWRUB52, DWRB73, DWRUB64 and RD2552, and omits DWRB 91. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
Rust, leaf blight, aphid or other disease/pest reaction specific to DWRB 91: No evidence found. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/bn/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
DWRB 91 is listed in the Karnal pocket guide's table under irrigated, late-sown conditions with an average yield of 40.62 q/ha and a malt end use. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/EB-53-Barley-Cultivation-in-India-Pocket-Guide.pdf
The Journal of Wheat Research retrospective gives a 2013 release year and an irrigated late-sown NWPZ profile for DWRB 91, with a test-weight entry of 64.5 for the late-sown trial (column labels are not fully legible in the extract). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/41939/18644
A malting-quality evaluation reports DWRB 91 among genotypes whose hot water extract is at or above the 80% benchmark; the reported value is 81.0%, and the authors state that the differences among genotypes were not statistically significant. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2304-8158/11/21/3403
The same study reports DWRB 91 at 95.9% malt homogeneity, which is the highest value in the set, and 226.1 mL/h filtration rate, which is below the 250 mL/h desirable level. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2304-8158/11/21/3403
The MDPI paper concludes that DWRB 91 (late-sown release) shows excellent malt quality when sown on time. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2304-8158/11/21/3403
A second malting study in the Journal of Cereal Research reports DWRB 91 as one of four genotypes meeting international malting standards, with a filtration rate that falls short. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/119498/46151/314330
Field-trial results in farmers' fields, multi-location yield data and maturity: No evidence found beyond the average-yield table value above.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage is recorded as DWR 46/RD 2552 in a barley beta-amylase study, though the brief lists parentage as "Not specified." -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JWR/article/download/171911/63098/496671
QTL, marker or molecular-diversity studies specific to DWRB 91: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Named lead breeder(s) for DWRB 91: No evidence found. The IIWBR page lists staff names, but none is linked to this variety. -- https://researchgate.net/institution/Directorate-Of-Wheat-Research
Developing institution: the variety is attributed to the Directorate of Wheat Research (DWR), Karnal, and the institute's 2013 bulletin credits DWR. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-29-Barley-cultivars-released-in-India-Names-parentages-origins-adaptations.pdf
The Directorate was elevated to ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research in 2014, per the institute's About page. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/about/
Station: Karnal, Haryana. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/about/

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. Institute-level contacts only:
Institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (formerly DWR), Karnal, Haryana. Website: http://www.iiwbr.org/ -- https://researchgate.net/institution/Directorate-Of-Wheat-Research
Postal address (per the bulletin, Project Director, DWR): Karnal - 132001, Haryana, India. -- https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-29-Barley-cultivars-released-in-India-Names-parentages-origins-adaptations.pdf
Official email: No evidence found. Phone: No evidence found.

drought.details: DWRUB64 is characterized as drought stress tolerant with a Drought Susceptibility Index (DSI) of 0.81. It is also described as highly tolerant to water stress conditions.

heat.details: The variety exhibits heat stress tolerance with a Heat Susceptibility Index (HSI) of 0.77. DWRUB64 is noted as heat tolerant, and its derivative, DWRB 137, is reported to escape terminal heat stress.

salinity.details: DWRUB64 is described as salinity tolerant and salt resistant. It is considered a suitable option for cultivation in sodic (salt-affected) soils. The variety has also been evaluated in Salinity/Alkalinity Barley tolerance Trials.

flood.details: No specific information is available regarding DWRUB64's direct tolerance to flood or waterlogging. General information about barley indicates that it "cannot tolerate waterlogging". However, a derivative variety, DWRB 137 (which has DWRUB64 as a parent), is reported to give higher grain yield under waterlogging conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: DWRUB64 is broadly described as disease resistant. More specifically, it is reported to be highly resistant to yellow rust and brown rust. It is also listed among varieties resistant/tolerant to various diseases and insect pests.

pest_resistance.summary: DWRUB64 is identified as a resistant/tolerant variety against aphids.

agronomic_details.yield: The average yield reported is 40.5 quintal/ha. Specific yields recorded include 37.9 quintal/ha in the North Eastern Plains Zone (NEPZ) and 42.5 quintal/ha in the Central Zone (CZ) under irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety demonstrates adaptation and yield performance across different zones including NEPZ and CZ under irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: DWRUB64 is adapted for cultivation under irrigated late sown conditions in the North Western Plains Zone (NWPZ). It is suitable for regions requiring cold temperatures during vegetative growth and warm temperatures at maturity.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: DWRUB64 is a six-row malt barley with good malting and brewing quality.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Yield data from trials in NEPZ and CZ under irrigated conditions are available. The variety has also been evaluated for drought, heat, and salinity tolerance, indicating its performance under various stress conditions.

drought.details: One ICAR-linked secondary summary describes Co 0239 as performing well under drought conditions; this is not a trial report. An ICAR-SBI review table lists Co 0239 among NW-zone varieties tolerant to drought (DR) and waterlogging (WL), but the table layout is ambiguous about which row each tag belongs to. The described early maturity may also contribute to stress escape, but the digest does not state this as a mechanism. Evidence is limited and indirect; no drought trial data for Co 0239 was found.

heat.details: No heat stress data for Co 0239 was found in the digest.

salinity.details: No salinity data for Co 0239 was found in the digest.

flood.details: Under waterlogging, Co 0239 showed a drop in pol % in cane compared with normal conditions, indicating a quality penalty under waterlogging. The magnitude of the drop is not reported. This conflicts with the ambiguous ICAR-SBI review table, which lists Co 0239 among varieties tolerant to waterlogging (WL). The level is provisional because the table tag is ambiguous and the study quantifies only pol % change.

disease_resistance.summary: Red rot: Co 0239 is described as moderately resistant to the prevalent races of red rot (secondary blog source, no trial reference given). A release-era ICAR summary notes Co 0239 for the North-West Zone with no specific disease rating in the snippet. No other disease resistance data for Co 0239 was found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No insect-pest data (top borer, early shoot borer) for Co 0239 was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Cane yield of about 79.23 t/ha and sugar yield of about 9.88 t/ha in AICRP NW-zone trials (secondary blog source). The CSC record gives an average yield of 79.23 T/Ha of canes and 10.37 Tons of sugar, which conflicts with the 9.88 t/ha sugar figure from the blog; the CSC record is used as ground truth. Sucrose is reported as 18.45% in one source and 18.58% in another.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond zonal listings. Co 0239 appears in NW-zone AICRP listings for 2009 and 2010 as an early variety. No multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: North-West zone of India (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Central and Western Uttar Pradesh). Described as an early variety in the NW zone, including the early-group listing for Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan (the digest's NW listing is truncated).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Early group, about 10-12 months (reported in months; no day count was found in the digest).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Fibre content about 12.79%; fair ratooning ability. Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP NW-zone trial (blog source): Co 0239 recorded about 79.23 t/ha cane yield, 9.88 t/ha sugar yield and 18.45% sucrose, against CoJ 64 at 67.59 t/ha and CoPant 84211 at 66.84 t/ha. (2) The same source reports about 17% higher cane yield, 21% higher sugar yield and 3.8% higher sucrose % than the CoJ 64 check, and ranks Co 0239 1st for sugar yield and 2nd for cane yield in the zone. (3) A separate AICRP-linked table gives 79.23 t/ha cane yield, 18.58% sucrose and 12.0% recovery. (4) Zonal trial history: identified as an early variety in the NW zone in the 2009 and 2010 AICRP listings. (5) Waterlogging study: drop in pol % in cane under waterlogging compared with normal conditions. No trial-level data on drought or heat was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Co 0239 (Karan 6) is described as a fairly early-maturing variety that performed well under drought conditions in one ICAR-linked summary; this is a secondary source, not a trial report -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
Under waterlogging, Co 0239 showed a drop in pol % in cane compared with normal conditions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309135876_Impact_of_sugarcane_varieties_Co_0238_Co_0118_Co_0239_and_Co_98014_on_yield_and_sugar_recovery
An ICAR-SBI review table lists Co 0239 among NW-zone varieties tolerant to drought (DR) and waterlogging (WL), but the table layout is ambiguous about which row each tag belongs to -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345662120_Advance_Production_Technologies_of_Sugarcane_A_Step_Towards_Higher_Productivity
Name note: all of the above refer to Co 0239 (Karan 6). No heat, salinity, or submergence data for this variety was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
Co 0239 is described as moderately resistant to the prevalent races of red rot -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
A release-era ICAR summary notes Co 0239 for North-West Zone with no specific disease rating in the snippet; no insect-pest (top borer, early shoot borer) data was found for Co 0239 -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/recent-plant-breeding
Name note: refers to Co 0239 (Karan 6). The Seednet name "KARAN - 16" is a different variety (see BREEDER section).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
In AICRP NW-zone trials, Co 0239 recorded about 79.23 t/ha cane yield, 9.88 t/ha sugar yield and 18.45% sucrose, against CoJ 64 at 67.59 t/ha and CoPant 84211 at 66.84 t/ha -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
The same source reports about 17% higher cane yield, 21% higher sugar yield and 3.8% higher sucrose % than the CoJ 64 check, ranking it 1st for sugar yield and 2nd for cane yield in the zone -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
A separate AICRP-linked table gives 79.23 t/ha cane yield, 18.58% sucrose and 12.0% recovery for Co 0239 -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/coimbatore.htm
Fibre content of about 12.79% and fair ratooning are reported -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
Early maturity: the variety is described as early (about 10-12 months, as an early group in NW India) -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ICAR-SBI_Newsletter_2025_Vol-474.pdf
Zonal varietal trial history: Co 0239 was identified as an early variety in the NW zone in 2009 and 2010 AICRP listings -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
Name note: all trial data above refer to Co 0239 (Karan 6). The Co 0239 vs Co 0238 labelling conflict is covered under BREEDER AND INSTITUTION.

GENETICS AND QTL
Co 0239 is a selection from the progeny of the general cross Co 93016 GC -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309135876_Impact_of_sugarcane_varieties_Co_0238_Co_0118_Co_0239_and_Co_98014_on_yield_and_sugar_recovery
No QTL, marker, or molecular fingerprinting study specific to Co 0239 was found -- searched; none located.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore, through its Regional Centre, Karnal (Haryana) -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/recent-plant-breeding
Breeders named in the release-era paper: Bakshi Ram and Karuppaiyan Ramaiyan (SBI Karnal) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309135876_Impact_of_sugarcane_varieties_Co_0238_Co_0118_Co_0239_and_Co_98014_on_yield_and_sugar_recovery
Release timeline: Co 0239 was released by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release in 2010 for the North West Zone; some sources give 2009 -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/ and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309135876_Impact_of_sugarcane_varieties_Co_0238_Co_0118_Co_0239_and_Co_98014_on_yield_and_sugar_recovery
Name note: the Seednet entry "KARAN - 16" (crop listed as "BARLEY (JAU)") does not match Karan 6. Karan-16 is Co 16030, a sugarcane variety identified at the AICRP meeting in Lucknow in 2022 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JSR/article/view/150455. The Seednet record appears to be a data-entry error and should not be used for Karan 6.
Name note: ICAR-SBI's "Varieties" page lists "Co 0238 (Karan-6)", which conflicts with other sources that give Co 0238 as Karan 4 and Co 0239 as Karan 6 -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/component/content/article?id=171. The majority of sources identify Karan 6 as Co 0239.
Current SBI director (Coimbatore) named in a 2026 news item: Dr. P. Govindaraj -- https://global-agriculture.com/ag-tech-research-news/icar-sbi-breeds-three-disease-resistant-sugarcane-varieties-for-indias-cane-belt/ (not specific to Karan 6)
Karnal Regional Centre director named in a news item: Dr. M.L. Chhabra -- https://www.chinimandi.com/karnal-co-operative-sugar-mill-explores-advanced-sugarcane-varieties-to-support-farmers/

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder email, phone, or direct contact was found in any search result. Institute-level contacts only:
ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Coimbatore -- official site: https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in (a "Contact Address" heading exists but no address text was captured in the snippet)
ICAR-SBI Regional Centre, Karnal -- site: https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=5563 (no address or phone text captured in the snippet)
Name and role in news item: Dr. M.L. Chhabra, Director (Karnal), as named in the ChiniMandi article.
Please verify phone and email directly on the institute site before use.

PUBLICATIONS
Ram B, Karuppaiyan R (2010). Impact of sugarcane varieties Co 0238, Co 0118, Co 0239 and Co 98014 on yield and sugar recovery. Conference paper, National Seminar on Sugarcane, VAMNICOM Pune (3 Sept 2010) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309135876_Impact_of_sugarcane_varieties_Co_0238_Co_0118_Co_0239_and_Co_98014_on_yield_and_sugar_recovery
AICRP on Sugarcane (2016). Forty Five Years of All India Coordinated Research Project on Sugarcane. Project report (ICAR-IISR, Lucknow); author names not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
ICAR-SBI (undated). Vision 2050 document; mentions Co 0239 among subtropical varieties; author names not captured -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/ICAR-SBIVision2050.pdf
Authors not verified (2019+). Advance Production Technologies of Sugarcane: A Step Towards Higher Productivity. Book chapter/report; Table 9 lists abiotic-stress-tolerant AICRP varieties including Co 0239 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345662120_Advance_Production_Technologies_of_Sugarcane_A_Step_Towards_Higher_Productivity
No DOI-indexed journal paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or Journal of Sugarcane Research article specific to Co 0239 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
ICAR-SBI Regional Centre Karnal seed is sold in October and again in February-March -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=5563
The Karnal centre runs participatory seed production with progressive farmers and supplies quality seed to sugar mills and public firms; MoUs were signed with Sugarfed Haryana, Sugarfed Punjab, Mawana Sugars and Avadh Sugar -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ICAR-SBI_Newsletter_2025_Vol-474.pdf
A Karnal mill sought seed of several ICAR varieties, but Karan 6 (Co 0239) was not named in that request -- https://www.chinimandi.com/karnal-co-operative-sugar-mill-explores-advanced-sugarcane-varieties-to-support-farmers/
Recent SBIRC settlement sales list Co 0118 and Co 0238 but do not mention Co 0239 -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ICAR-SBI_Newsletter_2025_Vol-474.pdf
No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, or private dealer listing specific to Karan 6 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Recommended for North West Zone: Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, and Central and Western Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.nitiforstates.gov.in/public-assets/Policy/policy_files/TNG1660A000065.pdf

drought.details: No drought data were found for this variety in the evidence digest.

heat.details: No heat stress data were found for this variety in the evidence digest.

salinity.details: No salinity data were found for this variety in the evidence digest.

flood.details: No flood data were found for this variety in the evidence digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Red rot: tolerance reported by the developer and linked to release approval (ThePrint, 2024). A 2025 ICAR/IISR announcement lists the variety among seven red-rot-resistant varieties approved by CVRC; the item names it 'CoS 17018 (Karan-17)', which the digest accepts as the same variety. AgriInsite describes the variety as disease-resistant. No other disease data were found.

pest_resistance.summary: Top borer: tolerance reported by the developer and linked to release approval (ThePrint, 2024). No pest data beyond top borer tolerance were found.

agronomic_details.yield: Trial cane yield of about 91.48 t/ha, 13.1% above CO-767 and 14.2% above CoPant 97222. Official yield potential of 914.8 q/ha, consistent with the trial figure.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Karan 17 (CSC name) / KARAN - 16 (Seednet name), sugarcane, variety code Co 17018

Name check: The Seednet entry "KARAN - 16" sits under BARLEY (JAU) in the notified list (https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf). It is a barley record and is discarded. Sugarcane "Karan-16" is a different variety (Co 16030) and is also discarded. Every finding below refers to Karan 17 / Co 17018 / CO-17018 (also written CoS 17018 in one article), and to no other entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Reported tolerance to red rot and top borer, which the developer links to the release approval (ThePrint, 2024) -- https://theprint.in/agriculture/pathogen-tolerance-better-yield-haryana-scientists-new-sugarcane-variety-awaits-release/1972752/
A published account describes the variety as disease-resistant and suited to ratoon crops (AgriInsite) -- https://agriinsite.com/sugarcane-breakthrough-new-variety-promises-higher-yields/
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Red rot and top borer tolerance, as stated above -- https://theprint.in/agriculture/pathogen-tolerance-better-yield-haryana-scientists-new-sugarcane-variety-awaits-release/1972752/
A 2025 ICAR/IISR announcement lists the variety among seven red-rot-resistant varieties approved by CVRC, though the same item gives the name as "CoS 17018 (Karan-17)" -- https://www.cmv360.com/tractors/news/7-new-red-rot-resistant-sugarcane-varieties-approved
No pest data beyond top borer tolerance were found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Trial cane yield of about 91.48 t/ha, 13.1% above CO-767 and 14.2% above CoPant 97222 -- https://www.chinimandi.com/sugarcane-breakthrough-new-variety-promises-higher-yields/
Juice sugar of 18.38%, 5.12% above COA 767 -- https://www.chinimandi.com/sugarcane-breakthrough-new-variety-promises-higher-yields/
Official yield potential of 914.8 q/ha (consistent with the trial figure) -- https://www.chinimandi.com/high-yielding-climate-resilient-and-biofortified-varieties-know-about-the-four-sugarcane-varieties-released-by-pm-modi/
Mid-late maturity group, intended as a replacement for the early Co 0238 -- https://theprint.in/agriculture/pathogen-tolerance-better-yield-haryana-scientists-new-sugarcane-variety-awaits-release/1972752/
Multi-location trials were run before the varietal identification committee approved it (ThePrint, as above). No individual trial-site data were found.
Release date: the Seednet/CSC value of 2024-08-02 could not be confirmed. Sources report CVRC approval and a PM-led release event but give no notification date.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Searches returned no parentage, marker or QTL study for Co 17018. The parentage field is "Not specified" in the input record and no source supplied it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Team listed as Dr Ravindra Kumar, Dr M.R. Meena, Dr R. Karupeyan, Dr Bakshi Ram, Dr G. Hemaprabha, Dr M.L. Chhabra, Dr Pooja and Dr B. Parameshwari -- https://www.chinimandi.com/sugarcane-breakthrough-new-variety-promises-higher-yields/
Dr Ravindra Kumar is named as Senior Scientist at the Regional Centre, Karnal (ChiniMandi, same URL, second article: https://www.chinimandi.com/sugarcane-breakthrough-new-variety-promises-higher-yields/)
A ThePrint report names Ravinder Kumar Yadav, a senior scientist, as the developer. This conflicts with the team list above, so both names are kept -- https://theprint.in/agriculture/pathogen-tolerance-better-yield-haryana-scientists-new-sugarcane-variety-awaits-release/1972752/
Developing institution: ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Regional Centre, Karnal, which is part of the Coimbatore headquarters -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=5563
The Regional Centre was set up in 1932 as a liaison with the Coimbatore headquarters -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=11140 (see also https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=5563)

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level contact for ICAR-SBI Regional Centre, Karnal (no individual breeder contact was found):
Address: P.B. 52, Near Parnami Mandir, Model Town, Karnal-132001 -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=2088
Email: mlchhabrasbik@gmail.com -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=2088
Phone: 0184-2268096 -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=2088
Caution: the email uses a gmail.com domain rather than an official institute domain. Verify it before use.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Search returned papers on other varieties (Co 12029, Co 15002, CoPant 97222) and on red rot in general. These were discarded. A 2005 Indian Journal of Genetics paper by Bakshi Ram, N. Singh and B.K. Sahi concerns red rot combining ability and is not about this variety. It is discarded.
AICRP/ICAR annual reports and KrishiKosh theses were not returned by the search.

SEED AVAILABILITY
The ICAR-SBI seed portal lists Co 17018 in its seed chain -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=11140
The seed production and sale licence for Co 17018 went to six sugar mills, including Mawana Sugars (Meerut) and Uttam Sugars (Bijnor) -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ICAR-SBI_Newsletter_2025_Vol-474.pdf
Reported sales include 338,999 single-bud setts of Co 17018 and 9,203 tissue-culture plantlets (ICAR-SBI newsletter, same URL)
Tissue-culture plantlets are produced at the Karnal Regional Centre's 50,000 plantlet/year facility -- https://sugarcane.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/ICAR-SBI_Newsletter_2025_Vol-474.pdf
No state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Haryana, Punjab, western and central Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand, with the same yield potential noted above -- https://www.chinimandi.com/high-yielding-climate-resilient-and-biofortified-varieties-know-about-the-four-sugarcane-varieties-released-by-pm-modi/
This matches the input recommended_states_raw. The Karnal Regional Centre page also names these states as its target sub-tropical zone -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=11140

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PBHL-56 (brinjal)

Name note: Searches used "PBHL-56" (CSC/variety_name) and "PL-56" (Seednet name). The PL-56 search returned no Seednet record, so every finding below refers to PBHL-56 or PBHL 56. The Seednet crop label "BARLEY (JAU)" conflicts with brinjal and could not be verified. Year of release is NaT in the input and no release year was found in the sources, so none is given.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for PBHL-56 under drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence. Other brinjal varieties appear in the results, but none are PBHL-56. -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for PBHL-56 disease or pest resistance. The results mention resistance for other PAU crops and varieties, which I excluded. -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- PBHL-56 is a long-fruited hybrid of brinjal having purple-black fruits and gave an average yield of 274 quintals per acre, per PAU's Department of Vegetable Science head. -- https://farmingcosmos.com/3-pau-vegetable-varieties-identified-for-cultivation-at-national-level/
- PBHL-56 is an early-maturing hybrid of long fruit group of brinjal and is characterized by medium-statured, compact and thornless plants. -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
- The varieties were identified at the 39th Annual Meeting of the All India Coordinated Research Project for Vegetable Crops (AICRP-Vegetable Crops). The meeting report itself was not retrieved. -- https://farmingcosmos.com/3-pau-vegetable-varieties-identified-for-cultivation-at-national-level/
- No multi-location trial data for PBHL-56 found. -- (searched)

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for PBHL-56 parentage, marker, or QTL studies. The parentage field is "Not specified" and no source named parents. The heterosis and genetic-divergence papers that surfaced cover other brinjal genotypes and were excluded. -- (searched)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana. -- https://pau.cyberframe.in/pau/public/newsdetail/10140
- Dr TS Dhillon, Head, Department of Vegetable Science, PAU, spoke about PBHL-56 in press coverage. -- https://farmingcosmos.com/3-pau-vegetable-varieties-identified-for-cultivation-at-national-level/
- A PAU vegetable breeder named Dr Dhatt is credited with developing PBHL-56 among several brinjal hybrids. The page does not give a first name or station. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=secondLink&_act=manageLink&intLinkID=132&intSubID=21
- Station: Department of Vegetable Science, PAU Ludhiana. This is inferred from the department named above, not from a station record.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone, or direct contact found for Dr TS Dhillon or Dr Dhatt.
- The only PAU contact data in the results belongs to Dr B S Gill (Principal Soybean Breeder, office phone 0161-2401960-443, email gillbs@pau.edu). This is a different crop and person, so I have not treated it as a PBHL-56 contact. -- https://pau.cyberframe.in/pau-new/public/college/coa/departments/Plant%20Breeding%20&%20Genetics/Faculty/B%20S%20Gill
- Institute-level address and phone for PAU Vegetable Science: not found in the results. Verify at pau.edu.

PUBLICATIONS
- Punjab Agricultural University (2022). Annual Report 2022 (PAU). Punjab Agricultural University annual report -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses, or conference papers specifically on PBHL-56 were found. -- (searched)

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for PBHL-56 seed from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, PAU seed sales, or private dealers. The seed-shop results were for other or unnamed brinjal varieties and were excluded. -- (searched)

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICRP identification assigns PBHL-56 to Zone IV (Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand) and Zone VI (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana and Delhi). -- https://farmingcosmos.com/3-pau-vegetable-varieties-identified-for-cultivation-at-national-level/
- PAU's annual report lists Zone IV as Punjab, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand-Terai, and Zone VI as Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana and Delhi. The Jharkhand/Uttarakhand-Terai difference should be resolved against the CSC minutes. -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
- PAU's news item (30-12-2024) lists PBHL 56 (brinjal) among its recent varieties. -- https://pau.cyberframe.in/pau/public/newsdetail/10140

disease_resistance.summary: PL 807 is resistant to common barley diseases across seasons and locations. It shows moderate resistance to white rust and high resistance to stem rot disease.

agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PL 807 is a six-rowed, feed barley variety. It features medium broad and upright leaves and is highly resistant to lodging.
agronomic_details.field_trials: PL 807 has been utilized as a check variety in the All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Wheat and Barley trials. Its yield performance and ancillary characters (e.g., Leaf Blight resistance) have been evaluated against check varieties like PL426 over multiple years in various locations, including Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs) at farmers' fields.

drought.details: Tolerant to combined stress of drought and salinity. As a drought resistant barley variety, it suits areas with scanty rainfall.

heat.details: Listed among salinity/heat tolerant modern cultivars.

salinity.details: Tolerant to combined stress of drought and salinity. Listed among salinity/heat tolerant modern cultivars. QTLs related to Na content have been located.

flood.details: Tolerant to waterlogging.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to pathotype 24. Highly resistant to stem rot disease. Exhibits multiple disease resistance, including White rust and powdery mildew.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to aphids and stem borer. Resistant to shoot fly and stored grain insect-pest infestation. It showed significant performance in hulless barley trials related to host plant resistance against insect pests.

agronomic_details.yield: In hulless barley trials, the test entry PL 891 recorded significantly, implying a positive yield performance.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly stated, but its inclusion in various regional trials suggests adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: A hulless food barley variety suitable for timely sown irrigated conditions. It has been evaluated in AICRP huskless barley trials in the North Western Plains Zone (NWPZ) and Advanced Varietal Trials (AVT) under irrigated (IR) and rainfed (RF) conditions in the North Eastern Plains Zone (NEPZ), as well as in the Tropical-Subtropical MB (TS-MB) zone.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: It is a two-rowed, hulless/huskless food barley variety. It can be processed into sattu, flakes, dalia, and flour. It is described as 'peel-free'. Specific nutrient content information is incomplete (e.g., 'contains 4...').
agronomic_details.field_trials: Participated in AICRP (All India Coordinated Research Project) huskless barley trials in 2019-20 in NWPZ. Also listed in Advanced Varietal Trials (AVT-IR-NEPZ, AVT-RF-NEPZ, AVT-TS-MB).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The four searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for VLB 94 or VLB94.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page on disease or pest resistance for VLB 94 or VLB94 was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield or multi-location trial data for VLB 94 or VLB94 was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage "DL 2 7/VLB 58" did not appear in any result. Two other pages were returned: a barley GWAS on Siberian spring barley (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10295979/) and a Korean barley breeding paper (https://www.koreabreedjournal.org/journal/view.php?doi=10.9787%2FKJBS.2022.54.4.488). Neither names VLB 94, so I have excluded them.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial. The only institutional link is a barley seed-production slide deck listing "VLB94" against VPKAS, Almora, in a varietal table with a release-type entry of "SVRC" and a six-rowed type (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/seed-production-technology-in-barley-pptx/282691818). The slide deck does not name a breeder. No breeder name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, email, phone or address for VPKAS (ICAR-Vivekanand Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan) was returned. The only institutional reference is the Almora location given in the slide deck above. I did not find an institute contact page in the results.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The search returned no paper, thesis, AICRP report or KrishiKosh record for VLB 94 or VLB94. A related compendium lists the variety names and their centres but gives no bibliographic details (https://iiwbr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/RB-48-Barley-Varieties-and-Genetic-Stocks-A-Compendium.pdf). It lists VLB94 under the Almora (VPKAS) centre symbol table, but I did not find a standalone publication for the variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No Seednet listing, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer page for VLB 94 or VLB94 was returned. The seed-standard content on the slide deck is generic to barley and does not name this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record's "Not specified in table" entry was not resolved by any result. The slide deck links VLB94 to Almora, which indicates an institute location but not a recommended state or zone.

Notes on the run:
- Name variants: "VLB 94" (CSC release minutes, per the record) and "VLB94" (the spelling used on the slide deck and compendium). Both were searched. The Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) did not appear in any result, so the Seednet listing for "BARLEY (JAU)" could not be checked.
- Four searches were run: variety, breeder/institute, research, and seed availability. The results were dominated by unrelated pages (Berlin brewing institute VLB, US seed sellers, and other barley studies).
- The evidence base for this record is very thin. The most useful next steps are the Seednet variety page, the VPKAS (Almora) website, and the CSC/AICRP barley annual reports, none of which were reachable in this search.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BDNGK 798 (chickpea)

Name check: "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" are both "BDNGK 798" in the input, so every heading below refers to that single name. No Seednet portal page was retrieved; the evidence comes from the sources listed. Spelling variants (BDNGK-798, BDNG 798) appear in the sources and are treated as the same variety only where the page context supports it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as moderately resistant to wilt and stunt, with an irrigated growing condition and 16-18 q/ha yield potential. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-bdngk-798/
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to BDNGK 798. The DPD listing gives only "Irrigated" as the agronomic feature. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderately resistant to wilt and stunt. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-bdngk-798/
Moderately resistant (DPD table row for BDNGK 798) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Greenhouse Trichoderma biocontrol work on BDNGK-798 against Fusarium wilt: a pot culture experiment was carried out under greenhouse conditions during the rabi season of 2024 using chickpea cultivar BDNGK-798 (sourced from Agricultural Research Station, Badnapur, Maharashtra). This tests biocontrol, not inherent resistance. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5579
Trichoderma seed and soil treatment study on BDNGK-798 with pathogen inoculation, measuring wilt incidence at 65 days after sowing. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361032295_Exploring_potential_of_Trichoderma_spp_against_Fusarium_oxysporum_fsp_ciceris_and_their_growth_promotion_activity

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Release and origin: Year of release 2016 (SVRC), originating centre ARS, Jalna, yield 16-18 q/ha, 120-135 days to maturity, kabuli type with white grain of about 29 g/100 seed. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-bdngk-798/
Maturity and grain (DPD table): BDNGK 798, 2016, ARS, Badnapur, Jalna (MH), 16-18 q/ha, 120-135 days, Maharashtra, irrigated, kabuli type with white colour grain (29 g/100 seed), moderately resistant. Note: this source says ARS Badnapur; the other says ARS Jalna. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Conflicting record: the Mahabeej listing gives BDNGK-798 as released from VNMKV Parbhani in 2013, with 75 days maturity, 110-115 days duration and 16-18 yield. This conflicts with the SVRC 2016 record and is not used for the release fields. -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/cereals?id=20

drought.details: BGD-103 is moderately resistant to drought. It has been studied for water use and tolerance to heat and drought, and was included in trials in environments experiencing drought stress. Research has also focused on its drought tolerance at seed, seedling, and whole plant levels.

heat.details: The variety BGD-103 shows tolerance to heat and has been studied for performance under terminal heat stress. It was grown in environments that coincided with high terminal heat stress.

salinity.details: While BGD-103 is listed as an abiotic stress-tolerant variety, no specific evidence or details regarding its salinity tolerance are provided in the search results.

flood.details: BGD-103 was part of studies in environments experiencing flash floods, but no specific tolerance level or mechanisms for flood tolerance are stated.

disease_resistance.summary: BGD-103 is resistant to Fusarium Wilt and moderately resistant against soil borne diseases. It has been evaluated as a promising entry in studies related to chickpea wilt complex.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance details are specified for BGD-103.

agronomic_details.stability: BGD-103 has been sown and studied across four different growing environments, including those experiencing heat and drought stress, indicating evaluation for yield stability; however, specific stability results are not provided.
agronomic_details.adaptation: This variety is suitable for rainfed conditions, particularly demonstrating higher grain yield in rainfed black soils.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-spreading habit, broader leaflets, attractive bold seed size, and white extra large seeds.
agronomic_details.field_trials: BGD-103 was included in the All India Coordinated Research Project on Agrometeorology (AICRPAM) trials, sown in four distinct growing environments to study water use and tolerance to heat and drought. A study on rainfed black soils reported a significantly higher grain yield of 14.28 q/ha. It was also identified as a promising entry in studies concerning chickpea wilt complex and dry root rot. Specific trials were conducted at the College of Agriculture, Vijayapur, during Rabi 2018.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to wilt disease, per the DPD central/state release table (listed as a 2015 SVRC release, Jharkhand, normal sown condition). The same salient-features text describes the variety as resistant to wilt. The digest notes that this attribution rests only on these table entries, and no field screening data was found. Lodging and shattering resistance are agronomic traits, not disease resistance, and are reported under agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant of gram pod borer (Helicoverpa), per the salient-features entry on Global Agriculture. No other pest reaction data was found. The CSC record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'. The digest does not state whether this is resistance or tolerance beyond the wording 'tolerant'.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 18.00 to 20.00 Kg/Ha. The SVRC table, as summarised in the digest, gives 18-20 q/ha. These units conflict and should be checked against the primary source. Performance stability trial in Jharkhand: 1461 kg/ha for Birsa Chana 3 versus 1303 kg/ha for check KWR108.
agronomic_details.stability: Judged stable with wide adaptability in the Jharkhand performance stability trial (ResearchGate source).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Jharkhand, normal sown condition (CSC record; SVRC table).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Resistant to lodging and shattering; suitable for normal sown condition; seed rate 65-70 Kg/ha (CSC record agronomic features). Morphological characteristics: Not specified. The trial source gives maturity of 120 days, which differs from the 115-118 day range.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Performance stability trial in Jharkhand (ResearchGate source): Birsa Chana 3 gave the highest grain yield at 1461 kg/ha against check KWR108 at 1303 kg/ha, a 12% advantage. It was judged stable with wide adaptability. Recorded maturity was 120 days. The trial table lists pedigree as ICCV2 / Bhawani Patna local and the institute as BAU, Ranchi. The same source lists release year as 2013, which conflicts with the 2015 SVRC year in the DPD and trade sources and the 2014 CSC year. The ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea 2021-22 report lists 'Birsa Chana 3', but the retrieved text gives no agronomic data for it.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Birsa Chana-3 (Desi), chickpea

Name note: Every finding below refers to "Birsa Chana 3" (CSC-style name, no hyphen). No search result used the Seednet form "Birsa Chana - 3 (Desi)", so no evidence was found under that name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as resistant to lodging and shattering and as tolerant of wilt disease (listed as 2015 SVRC release, Jharkhand, normal sown condition) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
Same salient-features text (resistant to lodging, shattering, wilt; tolerant to gram pod borer) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-birsa-chana-3/
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found for this variety -- searched under topic 1 and 3 results; none named it.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to wilt disease (dpd central/state release table) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Tolerant of gram pod borer (Helicoverpa) per the same salient-features entry -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-birsa-chana-3/
Wilt-resistance attribution for this variety is limited to these table entries; no field screening data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yield 18-20 q/ha; 115-118 days to maturity; normal sown condition (SVRC table) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
Same yield, maturity and area data -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-birsa-chana-3/
Performance stability trial in Jharkhand: Birsa Chana 3 gave the highest grain yield (1461 kg/ha) against check KWR108 (1303 kg/ha), a 12% advantage, and was judged stable with wide adaptability; 120 days maturity, pedigree ICCV2 / Bhawani Patna local, BAU Ranchi -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327931315_Performance_stability_of_promising_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_cultivars_in_Jharkhand
Listed in the ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea 2021-22 report as "Birsa Chana 3", but the retrieved text gives no agronomic data for it -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Searched under topic 3; the only marker-related hits (Pusa Chickpea 20211 and Fusarium-pyramiding work at PMC9388742) concern other varieties and were discarded. Parentage recorded in the input (ICCV-2 / Bhawanipatna) is supported only by the ResearchGate trial table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327931315_Performance_stability_of_promising_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_cultivars_in_Jharkhand

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Originating centre given as BAO (Birsa Agricultural University), Jharkhand -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
Trial table lists the institute as BAU, Ranchi -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327931315_Performance_stability_of_promising_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_cultivars_in_Jharkhand
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The Krishi Jagran SVRC article mentions unnamed "breeders of the variety" but covers four BAU varieties collectively and does not name Birsa Chana 3, so no name is attributed -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/16-all-new-high-yielding-varieties-of-crops-developed-by-this-agri-research-institution/
Institution background: Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, established 1981 -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birsa_Agricultural_University

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level only (no breeder contact found): Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, Jharkhand; website www.bauranchi.org -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birsa_Agricultural_University
Official email, phone and postal address for the BAU Department of Plant Breeding or the chickpea programme: No evidence found.
Director of Research named in a news item (A. Wadood) is not tied to this variety and is not listed as a contact -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/birsa-agricultural-university

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Performance stability of promising chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) cultivars in Jharkhand. ResearchGate PDF (genotype table includes Birsa Chana 3, release 2013, BAU Ranchi) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327931315_Performance_stability_of_promising_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_cultivars_in_Jharkhand
Note: this paper lists release year 2013, which conflicts with the 2015 SVRC year in the DPD and trade sources.
ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea Progress Report 2021-22 (lists Birsa Chana 3 in a variety table; no details retrieved) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
No KrishiKosh theses, journal papers or conference papers specific to this variety were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY

GENETICS AND QTL

CONTACT DETAILS

RECOMMENDED STATES

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GM-2 (Seednet name: GBM 2), fenugreek, Gujarat Methi-2

Search coverage: four web_search queries were run: "GM-2 fenugreek variety", "GM-2 fenugreek breeder institute", "GM-2 fenugreek research paper", and "GBM 2 fenugreek seed availability". None returned a page about this variety, under either name, so every heading below reports no evidence.

Name and record notes:
- The CSC minutes name is GM-2 and the Seednet name is GBM 2. The searches used both names and neither returned variety-specific results.
- The Seednet crop field reads "BENGAL GRAM (GRAM/CHICK PEA/KABULI/CHANA)", but the variety is fenugreek. This looks like a crop-mapping error in the Seednet record and should be checked on the portal.
- The parentage field contains corrupted characters ("Physical mutation of Annigeri" followed by unreadable text). The parent name is recorded as Annigeri, and the rest could not be recovered.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found
DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found
GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a breeder or lead scientist of GM-2 or GBM 2. The institution named in the record is S.D. Agricultural University; no SDAU variety page or release notice was retrieved.
CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No SDAU, Sardarkrushinagar station, or ICAR contact details were retrieved, so none are given here.
PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The results that came back concerned fenugreek in general, not this variety: a PMC systematic review on fenugreek and type 2 diabetes (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10531284/) and a ResearchGate review of fenugreek biology and cultivation (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/266879404_A_Review_on_Biology_Cultivation_and_Biotechnology_of_Fenugreek_Trigonella_foenum-graecum_L._as_a_Valuable_Medicinal_Plant_and_Multipurpose). Neither mentions GM-2 or GBM 2, so neither is listed as a publication for this variety.
SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Only commercial retail seed listings appeared (for example https://territorialseed.com/products/fenugreek), and none refer to this variety. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing was found.
RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The CSC record lists KARNATAKA, but no independent source was retrieved to confirm it.

Suggested next steps: check seednet.gov.in directly under GBM 2 and correct the crop field, search SDAU's site (sdau.edu.in) and Gujarat state notification records for GM-2 / Gujarat Methi-2, and search KrishiKosh for fenugreek release reports.

drought.details: Drought tolerance of GNG-1969: No evidence found in the digest. The only related finding is under irrigated late-sown conditions, where GNG-1969 was a low performer for productivity and profitability compared with GNG-469 and GNG-1958. This is not a drought assessment.

heat.details: Under heat stress, GNG-1969 maintained pollen viability, pollen germination and pod set and showed low membrane damage. It was rated heat tolerant and proposed as a donor for heat tolerance. A meta-QTL study (Devi et al., 2022) cites GNG 1969 as a heat-tolerance donor. Level assigned as high based on the source rating; the digest does not give a quantitative scale.

salinity.details: Salinity tolerance of GNG-1969: No evidence found in the digest.

flood.details: Flood and waterlogging tolerance of GNG-1969: No evidence found in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Botrytis grey mould: highly resistant, rated by lab and field marker-based screening. Dry root rot: rated resistant in a blotter-paper in-vitro screen (14 kabuli lines), in which GNG-1969 was among the resistant entries. Wilt, Ascochyta blight and dry root rot official resistance status from a release notification: No evidence found. Other diseases: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod borer: official resistance status from a release notification: No evidence found. Root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne incognita): No evidence found. No pest resistance evidence found in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Original CSC record: 2500.00 to 3000.00 Kg/Ha. DPD sources list about 22-23 q/ha (approximately 2200-2300 kg/ha) for GNG 1969 and 22 q/ha in a second DPD table. A conflicting record gives 7.3 q/acre (approximately 1800 kg/ha). The sources disagree and the CSC figure is retained as the ground truth.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources (multi-location trial results: No evidence found beyond the trials listed in field_trials).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Listed as suitable for irrigated normal-sown conditions (DPD). ARS Sriganganagar includes GNG 1969 (Triveni, timely sown) in its zone package of practices. The development station is in Zone 1b, Irrigated North West Plain Zone. The original record recommends Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan (excluding southern part), western Uttar Pradesh, Delhi and Uttarakhand. The digest does not provide evidence for the excluded southern part of Rajasthan. Under irrigated late-sown conditions, performance was low relative to GNG-469 and GNG-1958.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified in the original record. Not found in searched sources for GNG-1969. (The tall plant type in the IIPR report refers to GNG 16, not GNG-1969.) Seed description from DPD: creamy beige seed, about 26.2 g/100 seeds. A conflicting record gives 33.6 g/100 grain.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Heat stress trial: GNG-1969 kept pollen viability, pollen germination and pod set and had low membrane damage, and was rated heat tolerant. (2) Irrigated late-sown trial: GNG-1969 was a low performer for productivity and profitability compared with GNG-469 and GNG-1958. (3) IIPR ERA genetic-gain trial (2019-20 and 2020-21): GNG 1969 was one of 30 varieties tested; numeric results were not captured. (4) DPD variety data: about 22-23 q/ha yield and 146-150 days maturity; ARS Sriganganagar release in 2013. (5) Conflicting record: release in 2011, 157 days maturity, 7.3 q/acre. Multi-location trial results beyond these: No evidence found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Marker-assisted or QTL mapping specific to GNG-1969: No evidence found. Lab and field marker-based screening was used for botrytis resistance (see disease_resistance); marker names and positions: Not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: GNG 1969 is used as a donor source in a meta-QTL analysis for heat tolerance in chickpea. QTL details, positions and effects were not captured in the digest. Parentage was not verified: the digest states that the GNG-1969 entries do not report a parentage, and the S 26 x GNR 14 parentage in the original record matches GNG 16 in the IIPR report. Parentage from a primary source for GNG-1969: No evidence found.
