search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNG-1969 (CSC release minutes name) / GNG-16 (Seednet portal name), chickpea

Name check: The Seednet name GNG-16 does not refer to the same line as GNG-1969 in the sources. The AICRP/IIPR report lists GNG 16 as a separate 1982 release from Sriganganagar with the parentage S 26 x GNR 14, which is the parentage given in the record for GNG-1969. The GNG-1969 entries in the sources do not report a parentage. Treat the parentage and the Seednet name as unverified until checked against the CVRC notification.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under heat stress, GNG-1969 kept pollen viability, pollen germination and pod set well and had low membrane damage, so it was rated heat tolerant and proposed as a donor for heat tolerance -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2022.880519/full
- A meta-QTL study on heat tolerance cites GNG 1969 as a heat-tolerance donor (Devi et al., 2022) -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1274759/full
- Under irrigated late-sown conditions, GNG-1969 was a low performer for productivity and profitability compared with GNG-469 and GNG-1958 -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/e6bbf4ad-03de-4363-9b40-3886f9efb7b4/content
- Drought, flood/waterlogging and salinity tolerance of GNG-1969: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Lab and field marker-based screening rated GNG-1969 highly resistant to botrytis grey mould -- http://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/arcc/Final-attachment-published-LR-3925.pdf
- In a blotter-paper in-vitro screen for dry root rot, GNG-1969 was among the entries rated resistant (14 kabuli lines) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/special/7/Akhilesh%20Jagre,%20et%20al.pdf
- Official resistance status for wilt, Ascochyta blight, dry root rot and pod borer from a release notification: No evidence found
- Root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne incognita) reaction of GNG-1969: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- GNG 1969 is listed as released in 2013 by ARS Sriganganagar, with about 22-23 q/ha yield, 146-150 days maturity, irrigated normal-sown suitability, and creamy beige seed of about 26.2 g/100 seeds -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The DPD table gives 22 q/ha yield and 146 days maturity, with the same creamy beige seed description -- http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
- A conflicting record gives release in 2011, 157 days maturity, 7.3 q/acre and 33.6 g/100 grain -- https://mapmycrop.com/gram-chickpea-crop-guideindia/
- ARS Sriganganagar includes GNG 1969 (Triveni, timely sown) in the zone package of practices -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/themes/theme2/PDF/Ganganagar.pdf
- Under an IIPR ERA genetic-gain trial (2019-20, 2020-21), GNG 1969 was one of 30 varieties tested; numeric results not captured -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Multi-location trial results for GNG-1969: No evidence found beyond the above

GENETICS AND QTL
- Meta-QTL analysis for heat tolerance in chickpea; GNG 1969 used as a donor source, with QTL details not captured -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1274759/full
- Marker-assisted or QTL mapping specific to GNG-1969: No evidence found
- Parentage of GNG-1969 from a primary source: No evidence found (the S 26 x GNR 14 parentage matches GNG 16 in the IIPR report, see BREEDER AND INSTITUTION)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Agricultural Research Station, Sriganganagar, Rajasthan Agricultural University (AICRP on Chickpea site; established April 1976; Zone 1b, Irrigated North West Plain Zone) -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf
- Principal breeder or lead scientist name for GNG-1969: No evidence found
- Name and parentage conflict for GNG 16 (Seednet name): the AICRP report lists GNG 16 as a 1982 Sriganganagar release, S 26 x GNR 14, tall plant type, rainfed NWPZ -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Release notification number and gazette date for GNG-1969: No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute website found on ARS documents: raubikaner.org (Rajasthan Agricultural University, Bikaner, domain as found) -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf
- Breeder name, role, official email, phone and postal address of ARS Sriganganagar or the chickpea breeder: No evidence found
- Institute-level contact page URL: No evidence found

drought.details: GNG 2461 is identified as a rainfed desi line in the North-West Plain Zone after three years of multi-location testing and is listed among promising rainfed desi genotypes in the AICRP report. Rainfed adaptation is not the same as demonstrated drought tolerance. Drought-specific tolerance (terminal drought mechanisms) for GNG 2461 was not found. The drought-tolerance statement in the cited report applies to a different line derived from ICC 4958.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GNG 2461 (Moomal), chickpea (desi, Cicer arietinum)

Name check: The CSC release name and the Seednet name both read "GNG 2461", so every finding below refers to GNG 2461. I did not search seednet.gov.in directly, so Seednet-side fields (crop code, parentage, release date) are unverified. The release-minutes field gives 2023-05-02, but the sources give notification 4222(E) dated 25.09.2023. I have treated 25.09.2023 as the notification date and flagged the mismatch.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Identified as a rainfed desi line in the North-West Plain Zone after three years of multi-location testing; the AICRP report lists it among the promising rainfed desi genotypes. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Drought-specific tolerance (e.g., terminal drought, heat, salinity, flooding, submergence) for GNG 2461 was not found. The drought-tolerance statement in that report applies to a different line derived from ICC 4958. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- GNG 2461 is listed among entries found moderately resistant to dry root rot (DRR) in multi-location testing. The entry appears more than once in the table, so the exact trial count is unclear. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Resistance to wilt, Botrytis blight, pod borer or other pests was not found for GNG 2461 specifically. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed NWPZ yield table, AICRP Chickpea 2021-22 (kg/ha): AVT-2 (2020-21) 2217 from 5 trials; AVT-1 (2020-21) 1698 from 2 trials; IVT (2019-20) 2390 from 2 trials; weighted mean 2140 from 9 trials. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Average rainfed yield of 2140 kg/ha, reported as better than the older check RSG. -- https://raubikaner.org/directorate-of-research/
- Maturity duration, seed size and plant-type data for GNG 2461 were not found. -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: developed by pedigree selection from a dual hybridization, combining a single cross of KWR-108 × GNG 1861 with a single cross of Pant G-186 × GNG 1958. This answers the "Not specified" parentage field. -- https://raubikaner.org/directorate-of-research/
- QTL, marker or genomic studies on GNG 2461 were not found. -- No evidence found

- Developing institution: AICRP on Chickpea at the Agricultural Research Station (ARS), Sriganganagar, under Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University (SKRAU), Bikaner. basic_info.institution: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana (the source data lists Himachal Pradesh, but the DPD variety lists and the PAU compendium attribute release to PAU)

drought.details: No direct drought tolerance rating for GPF 2 was found in the results. The only drought-related items are a rhizobacteria study that used GPF-2 under water stress (an ACC-deaminase rhizobacteria effect, not a varietal tolerance trait) and a heat/drought QTL study (see heat).

heat.details: The snippets name GPF 2 as a parent of a mapping population with ILWC 292 used for QTL mapping of heat stress tolerance (PLoS One 2021;16(8):e0254957). One ResearchGate snippet describes GPF 2 as a tolerant genotype, but the surrounding text is truncated and it is unclear whether the trait is heat or drought. This rating is provisional.

salinity.details: No salinity data for GPF 2 were found.

flood.details: No flooding data for GPF 2 were found. The CRIDA package advises surface drainage in high-rainfall and deep black soils to avoid waterlogging, which is generic advice for chickpea.

disease_resistance.summary: GPF 2 is listed as wilt resistant (HC 1, GPF 2, JG 315, KWR 108 and others). It is also reported resistant to both Ascochyta blight and the wilt complex, together with PBG 1. It is used in fusarium wilt screening panels (KWR 108, GPF 2, IPC lines). The DPD lists describe the variety as erect with a thick stem resistant to lodging.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance specific to GPF 2 was found. The IPM package lists it only among recommended varieties for Rajasthan, and the CRIDA package lists it with a seed treatment recommendation.

agronomic_details.yield: The DPD list gives 22-25 q/ha for GPF-2 (GF 89-36) in the North West Plains Zone. In NWPZ agronomy trials in rabi 1993-94, GF 89-36 yielded 2018 kg/ha against 1718 kg/ha for PBG 1 under normal sown, irrigated conditions (from the original record). The recommended seed rate is 45 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability analysis was found. A cold stress study classed GPF 2 as cold-sensitive, which suggests a risk at the reproductive stage under low temperatures.
agronomic_details.adaptation: North West Plains Zone (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, North Rajasthan, West Uttar Pradesh). It is also grown in the mid hills of Himachal Pradesh, where it recorded significantly higher growth characters than other cultivars across sowing dates. It is listed in ICAR rabi advisories for Himachal Pradesh and in a Gujarat seed list.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 134-163 per the DPD list, which conflicts with the 150-155 days shown for the neighbouring entry. The original record has no value (nan).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plants grow erect with a thick stem and resist lodging (DPD). It is a desi type with a high crude fiber content in biochemical comparisons. The parentage is given as GL 769 crossed with a variety from HAU.
agronomic_details.field_trials: NWPZ agronomy trials in rabi 1993-94 (see yield). A mid-hills Himachal Pradesh sowing-date trial (2024) found GPF 2 superior in growth traits. A cold stress trial with sowing in early November classed GPF 2 as cold-sensitive.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No marker data for GPF 2 itself were found. It is a parent of a mapping population (GPF 2 x ILWC 292) used for heat stress QTL mapping. The snippets give no marker types or positions.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTLs for heat stress tolerance were identified in the GPF 2 x ILWC 292 population (PLoS One 2021;16(8):e0254957). Effect sizes are not given in the snippets. The review notes that such QTLs can be used in genomics-assisted breeding.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not described in the results.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: No specific seed corporation listing was found. The variety appears in government recommended-variety lists and a Parliament (sansad.in) document that lists it for Gujarat.
commercial_info.availability_status: limited (an older variety, still recommended in advisories and used in research, but no current seed source was identified)

drought.details: No drought evidence found for this variety in the searched sources. Trials were reported under irrigated conditions only (Gujarat, 2015-16 and later), so drought performance is not established.

heat.details: No heat evidence found for this variety in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No salinity evidence found for this variety in the searched sources.

flood.details: No flood evidence found for this variety in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: resistant (DPD release table; 2022 seed-industry notice; JAU variety proposal). Stunt: resistant (same three sources). Root rot: tolerant (DPD release table; 2022 seed-industry notice). Ascochyta blight: tolerant (DPD release table; 2022 seed-industry notice). Wilt, Ascochyta blight, stunt, root rot and BGM: rated moderately resistant in a commercial seller listing (GG-5), treated as lower confidence. No Ascochyta, BGM or insect-specific trial data beyond these listings.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance evidence found. A commercial listing (GG-5) reports low pod borer infestation; this is an observation in a seller listing, not a resistance trial result. No insect-specific trial data found.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 2115 kg/ha against potential 4306 kg/ha (JAU proposal, GG 5). Average yield 16 q/ha (DPD release table; ICAR-IIPR AICRP 2021-22 entry; Agricultural Science Digest citing an anonymous 2023 report). Under irrigated Gujarat trials, about 27.6% higher seed yield than Dahod Yellow and about 12.3% higher than Gujarat Gram 1.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources (no multi-environment stability analysis in the digest; AICRP 2021-22 entry lists irrigated, NHZ conditions only)
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated conditions in Gujarat; the release proposal title identifies the North Hill Zone (NHZ) as the target zone. No rainfed, drought-prone or other agro-climatic adaptation evidence found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Conflicting: 157 days (DPD and CVRC table; ICAR-IIPR AICRP 2021-22 entry; the figure shared by the national table); 98 days (JAU proposal sheet, early group); 103 days (seller listing). The 157-day figure is the one shared by the national table.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 168.1 cm; indeterminate habit; 10.6 branches/plant; 220.5 pods/plant (JAU proposal). Medium brown seed; 21.5 g/100 seeds (DPD table). 100-seed weight 21.37 g (seller listing). Seed rate 24 kg/acre and spacing 18 inches (seller listing).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Sixty front-line demonstrations under irrigated conditions in Gujarat during 2015-16 (GG 5). (2) Irrigated Gujarat trials: about 27.6% higher seed yield than Dahod Yellow and about 12.3% higher than Gujarat Gram 1 (GG 5). (3) Average yield 2115 kg/ha against potential 4306 kg/ha, with plant height, habit, branching and pod data from the JAU proposal (GG 5). (4) Average yield 16 q/ha and 157 days to maturity (GJG 0809, DPD). (5) Phosphorus study, rabi 2015-16, calcareous soil, South Saurashtra, with GJG 0809 as test variety: 40 kg P2O5/ha gave highest seed yield (1507 kg/ha) and best B:C ratio (2.40). (6) Entry in the ICAR-IIPR AICRP chickpea 2021-22 report: 16.0 q/ha, 157 days, irrigated, NHZ. (7) Breeder-seed programme of about 1200 kg planned for 2015-16.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No SSR, SNP or other marker data found in searched sources. Parentage: GJG 9707 x IPC 97-7 (pedigree JND 2001-02-02-01-05-01-5B), developed by hybridization followed by pedigree selection. Germplasm accession IC:598345 deposited with NBPGR.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL, marker or genomic study specific to GJG 0809 found. A 2022 chickpea genome-variation paper lists co-author M. S. Pithia but gives no GJG 0809 data in the retrieved text.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant to wilt and stunt, with tolerance to root rot and Ascochyta blight, per the DPD release table (name in evidence: GJG 0809) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Wilt and stunt resistance, root rot resistance and Ascochyta blight tolerance, per a 2022 seed-industry notice (name in evidence: GJG 0809) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-gjg-0809/
Wilt and stunt resistance per the JAU variety proposal (name in evidence: Gujarat Gram 5 / GG 5) -- https://aau.in/sites/default/files/X%20Agresco%20proceedings.pdf
Rated moderately resistant to wilt, Ascochyta blight, stunt, root rot and BGM (commercial seller listing, name in evidence: Gujarat Gram 5 / GG-5; treat as lower confidence) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gg-5/
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found for this variety

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to wilt and stunt (see above) -- https://aau.in/sites/default/files/X%20Agresco%20proceedings.pdf
Low pod borer infestation (commercial listing, GG-5) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gg-5/
No Ascochyta, BGM or insect-specific trial data beyond the listings above

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Sixty front-line demonstrations under irrigated conditions in Gujarat during 2015-16 (GG 5) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265
Under irrigated Gujarat trials, about 27.6% higher seed yield than Dahod Yellow and about 12.3% higher than Gujarat Gram 1 (GG 5) -- https://aau.in/sites/default/files/X%20Agresco%20proceedings.pdf
Average yield 2115 kg/ha against potential 4306 kg/ha; plant height 168.1 cm, indeterminate habit, 10.6 branches/plant, 220.5 pods/plant (GG 5) -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
Average yield 16 q/ha and 157 days to maturity, medium brown seed, 21.5 g/100 seeds (GJG 0809) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
Maturity conflict: 98 days (JAU proposal sheet, early group) and 103 days (seller listing) versus 157 days (DPD and CVRC table); the 157-day figure is the one shared by the national table -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf ; https://fuleseeds.com/products/gg-5/
Phosphorus study, rabi 2015-16, calcareous soil, South Saurashtra: 40 kg P2O5/ha gave highest seed yield (1507 kg/ha) and best B:C ratio (2.40) (GJG 0809 used as the test variety) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323553069_Chickpea_Cultivation_Governing_By_Phosphorus_Application_in_Calcareous_Soil
Seed rate 24 kg/acre, spacing 18 inches, 100-seed weight 21.37 g (commercial listing, GG-5) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gg-5/
Breeder-seed programme of about 1200 kg planned for 2015-16 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265
Entry in the ICAR-IIPR AICRP chickpea 2021-22 report: 16.0 q/ha, 157 days, irrigated, NHZ -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage GJG 9707 x IPC 97-7 (pedigree JND 2001-02-02-01-05-01-5B), breeding by hybridization followed by pedigree selection -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
Parentage GJG 9707 x IPC 97-7 (JAU Pulses Research Station table) -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
Germplasm accession IC:598345 deposited with NBPGR -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
No QTL, marker or genomic study specific to GJG 0809 found (a 2022 chickpea genome-variation paper lists co-author M. S. Pithia but gives no GJG 0809 data in the retrieved text) -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9007733/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed and evaluated by Main Pulses Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323553069_Chickpea_Cultivation_Governing_By_Phosphorus_Application_in_Calcareous_Soil
Lead scientist: M. S. Pithia, Research Scientist (Chickpea), Pulses Research Station, JAU, Junagadh; presented the release proposal as convener -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265 ; https://aau.in/sites/default/files/X%20Agresco%20proceedings.pdf

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: moderately resistant (ICAR-IIPR AICRP Chickpea 2021-22); resistant per DPD listing. Stunt: moderately resistant (ICAR-IIPR 2021-22); resistant per DPD listing. Root rot: resistant (ICAR-IIPR 2021-22; DPD listing). Ascochyta blight: tolerant (ICAR-IIPR 2021-22; DPD listing; Current Science review 2019 names GJG 0809 among Ascochyta-tolerant lines; dealer listing reports moderate resistance). BGM (Botrytis grey mould): moderate resistance per dealer listing only (dealer data, not an official source). The DPD varietal table attributes wilt and stunt tolerance to the JAU Gram 3/6 series, not explicitly to this variety.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance was established for Gujarat Gram 5. A dealer listing reports low pod borer infestation (dealer data, not an official source), which is an observation of infestation level rather than a documented resistance mechanism. No separate pest data for this variety was found in the DPD varietal table.

agronomic_details.yield: Dang district (KVK Dang, NAU) front-line demonstrations 2018-19 to 2020-21: 1102 kg/ha versus 825 kg/ha under farmer practice. agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Yield data come from different zones and years and were not analysed for stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recorded in North Hill Zone and Saurashtra kharif entries (JAU list). Demonstrated under irrigated conditions in Gujarat (2015-16 FLDs) and on calcareous soil in South Saurashtra (irrigated phosphorus trial). Dang district FLD reports seed yield gains against farmer practice. No explicit agro-climatic recommendation statement was found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 157-160 days (DPD listing); 176 days, medium group (JAU listing). A dealer listing gives 103 days, which the digest flags as unreliable and which is not used here.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Gujarat, 2015-16: 60 front-line demonstrations under irrigated conditions (Indian Farming, 2018); breeder seed production of about 1200 kg was planned for 2015-16. (2) Dang district, KVK Dang (NAU), 2018-19 to 2020-21: FLD seed yield 1102 kg/ha versus 825 kg/ha under farmer practice. (3) South Saurashtra calcareous soil, irrigated phosphorus trial: 40 kg P2O5/ha was most effective, giving yield 11.62% above control. (4) JAU variety list: North Hill Zone entry, potential 3392 kg/ha, average 2510 kg/ha; Saurashtra kharif entry, potential 4306 kg/ha, average 2115 kg/ha. Trial sites, replication and statistical details were not found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME NOTE: Evidence for "Gujarat Gram 5" (CSC name, also GG 5 / GJG 0809) and "Gujarat Gram 8" (Seednet name) describes two different varieties. Each heading below states which name the evidence refers to. Searches run: 4 (no Seednet portal page surfaced in any of them).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Gujarat Gram 5 (GG 5, GJG 0809): DPD listing records resistance to wilt and stunt, root rot, and tolerance to Ascochyta blight; the same listing also tags a drought-tolerance note to a MABB-derived variety, which I could not confirm is this variety -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 5: the ICAR-IIPR AICRP chickpea report (2021-22) lists GJG 0809 as moderately resistant to wilt and stunt, resistant to root rot, and tolerant to Ascochyta blight -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 5: a Current Science review (2019) names GJG 0809 among chickpea lines tolerant to Ascochyta blight -- https://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/116/02/0239.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 8 (Seednet name): JAU's notice describes it as selected for machine harvest suitability, with resistance to diseases and pests claimed generally -- https://asthafoundation.in/img/02-Gujarat%20Gram%208%20-%20A%20Chickpea%20Variety%20High%20Yielding%20and%20Suitable%20for%20Machine%20Harvest.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance specific to Gujarat Gram 5 beyond the single ambiguous DPD drought note.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Gujarat Gram 5: dealer listing describes moderate resistance to wilt, Ascochyta blight, stunt, root rot and BGM, with low pod borer infestation (dealer data, not an official source) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gg-5/
- Gujarat Gram 5: DPD varietal table notes tolerance to wilt and stunt for the JAU Gram 3/6 series; no separate pest data for GG 5 -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 8 (Seednet name): JAU-linked notice says it was tested against checks and found to show resistance to diseases and pests -- https://asthafoundation.in/img/02-Gujarat%20Gram%208%20-%20A%20Chickpea%20Variety%20High%20Yielding%20and%20Suitable%20for%20Machine%20Harvest.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Gujarat Gram 5: Indian Farming (2018) reports 60 front-line demonstrations in Gujarat in 2015-16 under irrigated conditions, and breeder seed production of about 1200 kg planned for 2015-16 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265
- Gujarat Gram 5: KVK Dang (NAU) front-line demonstrations, 2018-19 to 2020-21, report seed yield of 1102 kg/ha against 825 kg/ha under farmer practice -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378078345_Evaluation_of_frontline_demonstration_of_new_technology_on_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_in_Dang_district_of_Gujarat
- Gujarat Gram 5: phosphorus trial on calcareous soil (South Saurashtra, irrigated) found 40 kg P2O5/ha most effective, with yield 11.62% above control -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323553069_Chickpea_Cultivation_Governing_By_Phosphorus_Application_in_Calcareous_Soil
- Gujarat Gram 5: JAU's 2018-era variety list gives potential yield 3392 kg/ha and average 2510 kg/ha for the North Hill Zone entry; a separate entry gives 4306 and 2115 kg/ha for Saurashtra kharif -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 5: maturity recorded as 157-160 days (DPD); JAU's listing gives 176 days (medium group); a dealer listing gives 103 days (unreliable) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 8 (Seednet name): state trials 2019-20 to 2021-22 under irrigated and rainfed conditions; seed yield superior to checks -- https://asthafoundation.in/img/02-Gujarat%20Gram%208%20-%20A%20Chickpea%20Variety%20High%20Yielding%20and%20Suitable%20for%20Machine%20Harvest.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Gujarat Gram 5: JAU pedigree record gives parentage GJG 9707 x IPC 97-7 (pedigree JND 2001-02-02-01-05-01-5B), bred by hybridization followed by pedigree selection -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 5: DPD notes the variety as MABB (marker-assisted backcross) derived -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gujarat Gram 8 (Seednet name): parentage PG 07104 x WR315, per JAU's list -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
- No QTL or marker-trait association study for GG 5 found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Gujarat Gram 5: Indian Farming article authors are M S Pithia, R M Javia, V V Ramani and V P Andani, all at Pulses Research Station, JAU, Junagadh 362 001 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/view/84265
- Gujarat Gram 5: Vikram Singh and co-authors (JAU soil science) worked with GG 5 (GJG 0809), noting it was developed and evaluated by the Main Pulses Research Station, JAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323553069_Chickpea_Cultivation_Governing_By_Phosphorus_Application_in_Calcareous_Soil
- Gujarat Gram 8 (Seednet name): JAU's Pulses Research Station table lists GG 8 with notification year 2023 and parents PG 07104 x WR315 -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
- Institution: Pulses Research Station runs chickpea crop improvement, agronomy, entomology and pathology work, and produces nucleus and breeder seed of chickpea -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh

drought.details: Described as suited to conserved soil moisture in rainfed Gujarat and recommended for rainfed cultivation under conserved moisture (Javia et al. 2018). The digest reports no drought test data for this variety in the retrieved pages, so a drought tolerance level cannot be graded. Rainfed yield of 1867 kg/ha was 5.2-21.9% above checks Gujarat Gram 1, Gujarat Gram 2 and GJG 3 (Javia et al. 2018), which indicates adaptation to rainfed conditions but is not a direct drought stress test.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. No flood test data for this variety in the retrieved pages.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: described as wilt-resistant (Javia et al. 2018; the paper title also uses 'wilt resistant'), and as listed tolerant to wilt (DPD central/state list). The JAU variety document and the ICAR-AICRP chickpea report 2021-22 both rate it moderately resistant to wilt. The sources conflict; the JAU and ICAR ratings are the more specific official classifications. Stunt: good resistance (Javia et al. 2018); tolerant to stunt (DPD list); moderately resistant (JAU variety document and ICAR-AICRP 2021-22). Ascochyta blight: moderately resistant (JAU variety document). Fule Seeds (commercial source, not official) lists resistance to wilt and stunt.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod borer (Helicoverpa armigera): comparable pod borer damage to checks, with good resistance noted (Javia et al. 2018). The JAU variety document reports low Helicoverpa armigera infestation. Fule Seeds (commercial source, not official) lists low pod borer infestation. No other pest resistance data found for this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed grain yield 1867 kg/ha (Javia et al. 2018). JAU variety document: potential yield 4306 kg/ha, average 2115 kg/ha. DPD listing: 16-18 q/ha. Fule Seeds: 7.5-11 quintal/acre. KVK Porbandar frontline demonstrations: 18.10, 15.05 and 19.11 q/ha (2021-22 to 2023-24).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the three-year KVK Porbandar frontline demonstration results (18.10, 15.05 and 19.11 q/ha). No multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed conditions under conserved soil moisture in Gujarat (Javia et al. 2018). Normal sown in Gujarat (DPD listing). Sowing from the first fortnight of November at 45 x 10 cm spacing, seed rate 60 kg/ha, N:P:K 20:40:00 kg/ha (JAU variety document). Fule Seeds lists seed rate 24 kg/acre. Tested in Porbandar district by KVK frontline demonstrations. The JAU document describes the area as kharif in Saurashtra, which conflicts with the normal-sown rabi status given elsewhere.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110-112 days (Javia et al. 2018); 103 days, early group (JAU variety document); 120-130 days (DPD listing); 112 days (Fule Seeds). Sources differ.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Fule Seeds: semi-erect habit, dark brown seed, 100-seed weight 22.45 g. Javia et al. 2018: protein 19.9% and carbohydrate 67.84%, above checks. Morphological characteristics not otherwise specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Javia et al. 2018, rainfed trials: grain yield 1867 kg/ha, 5.2-21.9% above checks Gujarat Gram 1, Gujarat Gram 2 and GJG 3; maturity 110-112 days; protein 19.9% and carbohydrate 67.84%, above checks. (2) JAU variety document: potential yield 4306 kg/ha, average 2115 kg/ha, maturity 103 days. (3) KVK Porbandar frontline demonstrations, 2021-22 to 2023-24: 18.10, 15.05 and 19.11 q/ha, overall 12.70% above local varieties. (4) ICAR-AICRP Chickpea 2021-22 progress report: described as moderately resistant to wilt and stunt; no yield figures found in the digest. No peer-reviewed multi-location trial paper or KrishiKosh thesis naming this variety was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GJG 6 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Searches used "Gujarat Junagadh Gram 6" (variety_name) and "GJG 6" (seednet_variety_name). Most sources use "GJG 6" or "GJG-6" and match this variety. No seednet.gov.in page was retrieved, so the Seednet record itself is unverified. Some sources list GJG 6 under the earlier culture code GJG 1003 and the IC number IC:615013.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as wilt-resistant and tolerant of stunt, suited to conserved soil moisture in rainfed Gujarat -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330314101_GJG_6_A_high_yielding_wilt_resistant_chickpea_variety_for_conserved_moisture_condition_of_Gujarat ; https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8
Listed as tolerant to wilt and stunt, suitable for normal sowing (DPD central/state list) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
No flood, submergence, salinity, heat or drought test data found for this variety in the retrieved pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to wilt, with good resistance to stunt and comparable pod borer damage (Javia et al. 2018) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8
JAU variety document rates it moderately resistant to wilt, Ascochyta blight and stunt, with low Helicoverpa armigera infestation. This conflicts with the "resistant" wording above -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
ICAR-AICRP chickpea report 2021-22 describes it as moderately resistant to wilt and stunt -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Fule Seeds product page lists resistance to wilt and stunt and low pod borer infestation (commercial source, not official) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-junagadh-gram-6-gjg-6/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity 110-112 days; rainfed grain yield 1867 kg/ha, 5.2-21.9% above checks Gujarat Gram 1, Gujarat Gram 2 and GJG 3 (Javia et al. 2018) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8
Maturity 103 days (early group), sowing from the first fortnight of November at 45 x 10 cm, seed rate 60 kg/ha, N:P:K 20:40:00 kg/ha. Potential yield 4306 kg/ha, average 2115 kg/ha. The same document describes the area as kharif in Saurashtra, which conflicts with the normal-sown rabi status elsewhere -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
DPD listing: yield 16-18 q/ha, maturity 120-130 days, normal sown Gujarat -- https://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
KVK Porbandar frontline demonstrations 2021-22 to 2023-24: 18.10, 15.05 and 19.11 q/ha, overall 12.70% above local varieties -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/354%20IMPACT-OF-FRONTLINE-DEMONSTRATIONS-OF-CHICKPEA-(CICER-ARIETINUM-L.)-IMPROVED-VARIETY-GJG-6-ON-YIELD-IN-PORBANDAR-DISTRICT-OF-GUJARAT-INDIA.pdf
Fule Seeds page: 112 days, 7.5-11 quintal/acre, 100-seed weight 22.45 g, seed rate 24 kg/acre, semi-erect habit, dark brown seed -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-junagadh-gram-6-gjg-6/
Protein 19.9% and carbohydrate 67.84%, above checks (Javia et al. 2018) -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8

GENETICS AND QTL
Cross: GJG 0105 x FC 711 (pedigree JND 2002-01-01-05-02-01-SB), hybridization followed by pedigree selection (JAU variety document) -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/BPulsescropsVR.pdf
Javia et al. 2018 gives the cross as GJG 0105 x "FG 711", which conflicts with "FC 711" in the JAU document -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2018.00192.8

disease_resistance.summary: Fusarium wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ciceri): the HAU leaflet states the variety is resistant to wilt disease. The HC 6 paper reports about 8.3% wilt infection and describes this as high resistance. agronomic_details.yield: Record average yield: 3500.00 to 4000.00 Kg/Ha. HAU leaflet: average 10.67 q/acre, potential 16.67 q/acre. agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location trial: highest yield of 4167 kg/ha at Hisar, followed by 3327 kg/ha at Sriganganagar. agronomic_details.field_trials: Multi-location trial: highest yield 4167 kg/ha at Hisar and 3327 kg/ha at Sriganganagar; consistent yield above 2.5 t/ha over 13 years at Hisar and 5 years at RRS Bawal. seednet_fields.Parentage: ICCV 88506 x ICCV 90201	 ICCV 88506: Cold tolerant genotype ICCV 90201 (Himachal Channa II): High yielding, early maturing and Ascochyta blight resistant variety released for Himchal Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: It is proposed for cultivation Zone I i.e. Sub mountain low hills, sub tropical zone of Himchal Pradesh and Zone II mid hill conditions..
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Grain yield in variety DKG 986 is significantly affected by sowing dates. D1 (DOS= 7th Nov) recorded the highest yield of 2564 kg/ha which was statistically superior to yield at D2 (1898 kg/ha) and D3 (16.15q/ha 1615 kg/ha). Fertility levels also influenced the yield and F2 (100& RD) produced the highest yield of F3 (2064 kg/ha). The interaction of sowing dates x fertility levels disi not affected the yield.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: (i)Plant Height – 52.3 cm (ii)Flower colour – Pink (iii)	No. Of primary branches – 3.6 (iv)	No of pods.plant- 55.6 (v)	No of seeds/pod – 2 (vi)	100 seed wt.- 12.6 gm (vii)	Days to 50% flowering – 105.3 days (98 – 117 days) (viii)	Days to 75% maturity – 151 days (141 – 160 days).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: It is resistant to ascochyta blight and toerant to wilt and root rot, stem rot and rust. In coordinated trials, it showed 58.5% mean wilt incidence as compared with 81.1% in susceptible check, at hot spot locations. It was less at various locations in north India. It showed 27.1% incidence of dry root which is less than the susceptible check JG 62 (71.5%) and national varietal check GNG 1581 and at par with GNG 469. Similarly, it developed collar rot less than the susceptible. Based on the dats of various locations the variety developed the least Ascochyta blight (DR=4) and Botrytis grey mould (DR= 6.8) on 1-9 scale.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: It is early maturity variety and escpes the attack of pod borer. At KVK, Sundernagar, it showed pod borer infestation at par with the released varieties. Still prophylactic sprays of insecticides at 50% flowering stage are beneficial for managing pod borer attack.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Di – Ammonium Phosphate @ 100 kg per hectar at the time time of sowing. 20 kg Sulphur/ha ensures better crop yields.

agronomic_details.yield: 20-22 q/ha (approximately 2000-2200 kg/ha) per the ICAR-IIPR variety page.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to late-sown cultivation in the Central Zone. The DPD table lists the Central Zone as Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Bundelkhand UP. Protein content is above 24 percent.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium seed size (16.5 g per 100 seeds) and seed protein above 24 percent per the ICAR-IIPR variety page. The AICRP 2021-22 report (garbled in extraction, indicative only) describes medium plant height, spreading habit, good vegetative growth and small light-brown seed. The seed size descriptions conflict and should be checked against the primary source.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Heat-stress versus non-stress trial, 2017-19, 26 advanced lines: IPC 2006-77 was a check, reported as an above-average yielder with lower stability; the sowing-condition split was not clearly separable. (2) Herbicide-tolerance screening: among tolerant genotypes, IPC 06-77 showed the most consistent yield performance and more pods per plant. (3) Economic-impact study covering IPC 2006-77: adoption expected at 5 percent. No further trial results were found.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: IPC 2006-77 (chickpea)

STRESS TOLERANCE

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JG 36 (Jawahar Gram 36), chickpea

Name note: The searches used "JG 36" and "Jawahar Gram 36" (the CSC name). The Seednet name "JG-6" was not searched on its own, so no Seednet portal page was retrieved. Any JG-6 evidence below would need a separate check. Every finding below refers to JG 36 / Jawahar Gram 36.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant to wilt. Only wilt tolerance is named for this variety; drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance were not found for JG 36. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-jg-36-jawahar-gram-36/
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to JG 36. The search returned a Dhuria and Babbar heat-stress study, but it covers 68 kabuli lines, not JG 36, so it was discarded. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4064

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt tolerance is the only disease trait recorded for JG 36 (same source as above). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-jg-36-jawahar-gram-36/
- No evidence found for root rot, dry root rot, BGM, pod borer or other pest resistance specific to JG 36. -- searched under the general variety query; no JG 36 page carried this information.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release year 2016 (SVRC), originating centre JNKVV Jabalpur, yield 18-20 q/ha, 110-120 days to maturity, semi-spreading plant with dark brown seed, suitable for rainfed and irrigated conditions. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-jg-36-jawahar-gram-36/ ; also https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The ICAR-AICRP chickpea report 2021-22 lists JG 36 with the same release year, JNKVV origin, 18-20 q/ha, 110-120 days, and dark brown seed. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- JG 36 was one of the entries in a 30-line desi chickpea evaluation at the JNKVV seed breeding farm, Jabalpur, in rabi 2019-20 and 2020-21. The paper compares JG 36 with other lines for seed size and pod traits. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue12/PartAH/10-12-209-279.pdf
- JG 36 was a check variety in a 2007 characterisation of 40 advanced desi lines at the JNKVV seed breeding farm. -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/download/3320/6621/5786
- No evidence found for multi-location or AICRP yield trial results specific to JG 36. -- the trial and report pages retrieved did not give JG 36 multi-location data.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or pedigree study naming JG 36 was returned. The AICRP report shows a truncated parentage fragment, "JG 12 x JG ...", which is incomplete and not confirmed as JG 36's full parentage. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: JNKVV, Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh (originating centre). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-jg-36-jawahar-gram-36/
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. No page names the breeder of JG 36.
- Department: JNKVV Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics is the department that produced the 2019-20 and 2020-21 and 2007 evaluations above. This is an institute-level link, not a named breeder. -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/download/3320/6621/5786

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur. Website: https://www.jnkvv.org/ . The page retrieved gave no postal address, phone number or contact email for the Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics or the chickpea programme. -- https://www.jnkvv.org/
- Breeder name, email and phone for JG 36: No evidence found.
- Not attributed: An email (anitababbarjnkvv@gmail.com) appears on a 2014-15 kabuli-line paper by Dhuria and Babbar. It is an author contact for a different study and is not confirmed as a contact for JG 36, so it is excluded. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4064

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown (2021). "The exploration of varietal characterization of chickpea" (desi chickpea, 30 advanced lines, JNKVV seed breeding farm, rabi 2019-20 and 2020-21). The Pharma Innovation Journal, vol. 10, issue 12 -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue12/PartAH/10-12-209-279.pdf
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Characterisation of desi chickpea advanced genotypes with JG 12, JG 24 and JG 36 as checks (2007 material). Journal of IJPSS -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/download/3320/6621/5786
- ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2021-22). Annual progress report, with JG 36 variety listing. ICAR-IIPR -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis or DOI for JG 36 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing for JG 36 was returned. The AICRP report gives only national breeder seed totals, not variety-level availability. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Not searched: Seednet portal listing under "JG-6". Check https://seednet.gov.in directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Madhya Pradesh. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-jg-36-jawahar-gram-36/ ; https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The DPD table row for JG 36 also shows a region code of "CZ - MP" and a separate "NWPZ - UP" entry that sits next to it. The table layout is unclear, so Uttar Pradesh is not confirmed for JG 36. Check the official notification before recording any state beyond MP.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Gram Kabuli 6 (seednet name: Jawhar Gram Kabuli-1; code JGK 6 / JGK 2017-32), chickpea (Kabuli)

Searches run: 4 (variety and crop; breeder and institute; research; seed availability). No search returned a page that names this variety under either name. Every result was about another variety, another crop, or an unrelated product, and all were discarded under the strict relevance rule.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The variety search returned only a general chickpea variety list (dpd.gov.in) with a Kabuli entry for "Jawahar Gram-" (JNKVV, Madhya Pradesh). That is a different name and was not attributed to this variety. -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The same dpd.gov.in list mentions wilt and Botrytis grey mould resistance for a Kabuli entry, but the page does not name this variety, so it was discarded. -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Search returned no multi-location or agronomic data for JGK 6 or Jawhar Gram Kabuli-1.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Search returned no QTL or marker study naming this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The breeder search returned only ICRISAT's Kabuli variety ICCV 6, a different variety, which was discarded. No breeder name or developing station was found for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute, or contact page for this variety was returned. Note for verification: the variety record lists "Jawahar Lal Nehru Vishwavidyalaya". The chickpea breeding university commonly associated with the Jawahar Gram varieties is Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur. This is my own background knowledge, not a search finding, and the institution name should be checked against the CSC minutes before any contact is recorded.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The research search returned a 2020 Scientific Reports metabolomic study of desi and kabuli chickpea genotypes (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-020-70963-6). It does not name JGK 6 or Jawhar Gram Kabuli-1 in the retrieved text, so it was excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed search returned only a private dealer listing for Gujarat Kabuli Gram 1 (GKG 1), a different variety (https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/). It was excluded. No Seednet, NSC, state corporation, KVK or SAU listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found in the search results. The states in the variety record (Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jammu and Kashmir) are unverified; they come only from the input record.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet entry directly for JGK 6 / Jawhar Gram Kabuli-1 (seednet.gov.in), search the ICAR/AICRP chickpea annual reports and KrishiKosh by the code "JGK 2017-32", and confirm the developing institution against the CSC release notification.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kota Kabuli Chana 4 (RKGK 13-416), chickpea

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name fields are identical ("Kota Kabuli Chana 4 (RKGK 13-416)"). The Seednet portal itself was not reachable, so the evidence below refers to that name as it appears in secondary and institutional sources. Four searches were run (variety, breeder/institution, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- No stress-tolerance evidence specific to RKGK 13-416 was found. The only tolerance-related text in the results concerns other Kota varieties (Kota Kabuli Channa-2, Kota Desi Chana 4), which I did not attribute to this line. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638699219886341753.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST:
- No disease or pest resistance evidence specific to RKGK 13-416 was found. The DPD list shows resistance ratings for other Kota entries only. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- The ICAR-IIPR AICRP Chickpea 2021-22 report lists "RKG 13-416" in a Southern Zone kabuli trial: AVT-2 yield 1723 kg/ha (3 locations), AVT-1 1662 and 1497 kg/ha, IVT 1608 kg/ha, weighted mean 1621 kg/ha over 13 entries. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Maturity, plant height and seed size for RKGK 13-416 were not found. -- No evidence found in the results.
- Notification record: released as an open-pollinated kabuli chickpea by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties; notified 25 September 2023. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chickpea-variety-kota-kabuli-chana-4-rkgk-13-416/
- Release date mismatch: the input says 2023-05-02, the news item reports a notification date of 25 September 2023. Record both. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chickpea-variety-kota-kabuli-chana-4-rkgk-13-416/

GENETICS AND QTL:
- No QTL, marker, or genomic study on RKGK 13-416 was found. -- No evidence found in the results.
- Parentage: the input gives BG 1044 x BG 1110. The ICAR-IIPR report gives BG 1044 x BG 1111 for the sister line Kota Kabuli Chana 3 (RKGK 13-414), not for 13-416. Verify 13-416's parentage against the CSC minutes before using it. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- The developing institution is Agriculture University (AU), Kota, Agricultural Research Station (ARS), Kota, Rajasthan. A news item lists it among three chickpea releases from AU Kota (with Kota Desi Chana 2 (RKGM 20-1) and Kota Desi Chana 3 (RKGM 20-2)). -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638699219886341753.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist names: none found in the results. -- No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- No breeder names, emails, phone numbers, or postal address were found for AU Kota or its ARS. The only institutional reference was the AU Kota name in the release listings. -- No evidence found.
- Recommended next step: check the AU Kota website or the Kota ARS page directly (URL not confirmed by search).

PUBLICATIONS:
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, or conference paper on RKGK 13-416 was found. The results contained only unrelated chickpea papers from other countries. -- No evidence found.
- Institutional source (not a paper): ICAR-AICRP Chickpea Progress Report 2021-22, ICAR-IIPR. "Annual Progress Report, All India Coordinated Research Project on Chickpea, 2021-22." -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- No seed listing for RKGK 13-416 was found from the NSC, a State Seed Corporation, a KVK, SAU seed sales, or a private dealer. The results contained only consumer grain products (kabuli chana sold as food, not certified seed). -- No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka (for sale, per the CSC notification). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/chickpea-variety-kota-kabuli-chana-4-rkgk-13-416/
- Conflict: the AU Kota news item recommends the line for production in the Kota division (Zone V, Rajasthan), which differs from the three-state notification. The notified recommendation should be treated as authoritative. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638699219886341753.pdf

drought.details: No variety-specific drought data for Kripa were found. The only drought-tolerance mention in the central release list snippet appears next to a different entry (University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur) and cannot be attributed to Kripa. A general review notes chickpea has some tolerance to abiotic stress, including drought, but this is not specific to Kripa.

heat.details: No heat-tolerance data for Kripa were found. The heat-tolerant remark in the central release list refers to a different variety suited to late sowing in Madhya Pradesh. The kabuli ideotype review mentions Kripa only as a parent used in a study of flowering-time inheritance.

salinity.details: No evidence found.

flood.details: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.summary: The central release list records Kripa (Phule G 0517) as tolerant to Fusarium wilt and as an irrigated-condition variety. A journal article on Kripa (Phule G 0517) lists resistance and quality as keywords, but the specific diseases were not visible in the snippet.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance data specific to Kripa were found. A study used Kripa as one of four chickpea cultivars, with seed procured from the Pulses Improvement Project at Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth, in work on controlling Callosobruchus chinensis (a storage pest) with cold plasma. This does not establish resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Central release list gives 18-19 q/ha (average yield).
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability data found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released in 2009 by the Central Variety Release Committee for the Central Zone (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh) under irrigated conditions. One source also lists Karnataka. A parliamentary document lists Kripa among chickpea varieties for Gujarat.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110-115 days (central release list); this differs from the original data, which gives nan.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: SEMI SPREADING, BROAD LEAVES, EXTRA LARGE SEED SIZE (59.4G/100 SEEDS). Kabuli type. Reviews classify it among extra-large-seeded kabuli varieties (46-60 g per 100 seeds, or more than 50 g).
agronomic_details.field_trials: A journal article titled 'Kripa: An Extra Bold Kabuli Chickpea for Central and South Zone of India' describes Phule G 0517. The Rabi production plan lists Kripa and MNK 1 as extra-large kabuli varieties, with sowing from the first fortnight of November to the first fortnight of December.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No QTL, SNP or SSR information specific to Kripa was found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: None found. Kripa is mentioned as a parent in a cross used to study inheritance of flowering time (with ICC 17109), but no QTL details were available.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not reported. One abstract notes Kripa has high calcium content, and another reports a high value for a nutritional trait in Kripa (Phule G-0517). The underlying genes are not described.

agronomic_performance.adaptation: Released in 2009 by the Central Variety Release Committee for the Central Zone (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh) under irrigated conditions. One source also lists Karnataka. A parliamentary document lists Kripa among chickpea varieties for Gujarat.
agronomic_performance.maturity_days: 110-115 days (central release list); this differs from the original data, which gives nan.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: SEMI SPREADING, BROAD LEAVES, EXTRA LARGE SEED SIZE (59.4G/100 SEEDS). Kabuli type. Reviews classify it among extra-large-seeded kabuli varieties (46-60 g per 100 seeds, or more than 50 g).
agronomic_performance.field_trials: A journal article titled 'Kripa: An Extra Bold Kabuli Chickpea for Central and South Zone of India' describes Phule G 0517. The Rabi production plan lists Kripa and MNK 1 as extra-large kabuli varieties, with sowing from the first fortnight of November to the first fortnight of December.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance of L 558 itself. The PAU drought QTL paper concerns chickpea generally and does not name L 558 or L-550, so it cannot be used to rate this variety. No drought mechanisms were reported for L 558.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance of L 558 in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found under the CSC name L 558. Under the Seednet name L-550, a salinity study of seven desi and kabuli chickpea genotypes identified L550 (kabuli) and BG1053 as tolerant on the basis of physiological and biochemical parameters. The digest does not confirm that L-550 and L 558 are the same genotype, so this finding is not attributed to L 558 here. The level is therefore unknown.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources for wilt, Ascochyta blight or botrytis grey mould reaction of L 558. General PAU context only: 240 kabuli genotypes from different backgrounds and locations were screened under artificial epiphytotic conditions against Ascochyta blight during 2019-20 and 2020-21 at PAU, Ludhiana. The genotype list does not show L 558, so this screen provides no resistance rating for the variety.

agronomic_details.field_trials: Trial evidence in the digest does not directly test L 558. (1) Under the Seednet name L-550, the 2002-harvest quality study used L-550 as a kabuli reference, and L-550 (kabuli type) had the highest fat content among the chickpea cultivars tested. (2) Under the Seednet name L-550, L-550 flour differed significantly from all other chickpea flours in water and oil absorption, gelation capacity and emulsification properties. (3) A seed-rate trial at Ludhiana in Northern India used GLK 21143, GLK 21159 and BG 1053, not L 558. (4) A 2024 PAU paper titled 'New Kabuli Chickpea variety L 558' is listed in a ResearchGate reference list, but no yield or maturity data was visible. (5) The Ascochyta blight screen at PAU, Ludhiana (2019-20 and 2020-21) covered 240 kabuli genotypes, but L 558 is not in the genotype list.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under the Seednet name L-550, a salinity study on kabuli lines identified L550 as salt-tolerant, alongside BG1053, based on physiological and biochemical traits. Seven chickpea genotypes both desi and kabuli were evaluated for salinity tolerance, and on the basis of physiological and biochemical parameters, BG1053 and L550 from kabuli were identified as tolerant -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339343766_Desi_and_kabuli_chickpea_cultivars_had_differential_behaviour_towards_salinity_stress_tolerance
- Under the CSC name L 558: No evidence found. The drought QTL paper from PAU is about chickpea generally and does not name L 558 or L-550 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9437436/
- Under the CSC name L 558: No evidence found for heat, flood, submergence or drought tolerance of L 558 itself.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Under the CSC name L 558: No evidence found for wilt, Ascochyta blight, botrytis grey mould or pod borer reaction of L 558.
- General PAU context only: 240 kabuli genotypes from different backgrounds and locations were screened under artificial epiphytotic conditions against Ascochyta blight during 2019-20 and 2020-21 at PAU, Ludhiana -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393377730_Identification_of_Ascochyta_blight_resistant_sources_in_Kabuli_genotypes_of_chickpea_and_validation_of_identified_QTLs (the genotype list does not show L 558).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Under the Seednet name L-550: The 2002-harvest quality study used L-550 as a kabuli reference; L-550 (kabuli type) had the highest fat content among the chickpea cultivars tested -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0260877404004236
- Under the Seednet name L-550: L-550 flour differed significantly from all other chickpea flours with respect to its water and oil absorption, gelation capacity, and emulsification properties. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0308814604004650
- Under the CSC name L 558: No evidence found for yield, maturity or multi-location trial results. The seed-rate trial at Ludhiana used GLK 21143, GLK 21159 and BG 1053, not L 558 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318518201_Growth_Productivity_and_Economics_of_Kabuli_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_Genotypes_in_Response_to_Seed_Rate_in_Northern_India
- Under the CSC name L 558: The 2024 PAU paper title listed in a ResearchGate reference list reads "New Kabuli Chickpea variety L 558", but no yield or maturity data was visible -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369334660_Chickpea_Variety_PBG8

GENETICS AND QTL
- Under the CSC name L 558: No evidence found for parentage-linked markers or QTLs specific to L 558. The stated parentage (PB.7 x Rabat) was not confirmed by any search result.
- General PAU context: Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, Punjab, India is the source of the drought-QTL mapping work -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9437436/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

drought.details: The only MNK-1 drought-related evidence is farmer-preferred variety trial (FPVS) yields in Kurnool, Prakasam and Anantapur (mean 983 kg/ha) and a Karnataka FPVS note. Neither gives a drought-tolerance rating or mechanism, so no level is assigned. Release record states adaptation to normal sown rainfed as well as irrigated conditions, which is adaptation information, not a drought-tolerance rating.

heat.details: MNK-1 is listed as a heat-tolerant genotype in a field screening method study at ICAR-NIASM Pune (2023-25 seasons). This is a single listing without reported numeric heat-stress data or mechanisms, so the level is provisional.

salinity.details: In a salinity pot experiment (10 genotypes, three NaCl levels, College of Agriculture Vijayapur), MNK1 was described as less affected than several other genotypes on morpho-phenological and yield traits. The snippet gives no MNK1-specific numeric yield loss, so the level is provisional and relative only.

flood.details: No evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: moderately resistant, per the DPD central release table (2011 release, UAS Raichur). Fusarium wilt: moderately resistant, per a chickpea varieties slide summary. No other disease resistance is documented in the digest. The slide deck's 'tolerant to wilt, dry root rot and bgm' entry belongs to a different variety heading and was discarded.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Release record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: 12.80 q/ha under normal conditions (release record). DPD table gives 13-14 q/ha. FPVS mean in Kurnool, Prakasam and Anantapur: 983 kg/ha (about 9.83 q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources, apart from the multi-location AICRP entries noted under field_trials, whose values and units are not stated in the snippet.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Normal sown rainfed and irrigated conditions (release record). Recommended states per release record: Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu. DPD table lists irrigated conditions. Release record notes suitability for normal sowing conditions similar to other kabuli chickpea varieties, and tolerance to lodging and shattering.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Erect plants, broad compound leaves, milky-white seed, 51.9 g/100 seeds, 100-day maturity (slide summary). Release record: tolerant to lodging and shattering. Seed type: kabuli, extra-large-seeded (ICAR-IIPR AICRP 2021-22 report and PubMed source).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Karnataka FPVS 2017-18: MNK 1 was one of three elite entries; GBM 2 was the top yielder in Kalaburagi. (2) FPVS in Kurnool, Prakasam and Anantapur (Andhra Pradesh): mean yield 983 kg/ha. (3) ICAR-IIPR AICRP Chickpea 2021-22: MNK 1 listed among recent extra-large-seeded kabuli releases and in multi-location trial entries; values in brackets, unit not stated in snippet. (4) Salinity pot experiment (College of Agriculture Vijayapur): MNK1 less affected than several genotypes; no numeric loss given. (5) ICAR-NIASM Pune field screening (2023-25): listed as heat-tolerant; no numeric data in snippet.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Parentage per release record: GULBARGA LOCAL. Mapping population: F2:3 from MNK-1 x Annigeri 1 (188 F2 plants); 31,311 SNPs identified, of which 7,204 were polymorphic. Marker positions: Not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: 11 seed Fe QTLs and 8 seed Zn QTLs identified in the MNK-1 x Annigeri 1 population. MNK-1 alleles favoured Fe at all five CaLG04 loci. Individual QTL effect sizes: Not found in searched sources. Drought, heat or wilt QTL/marker work specific to MNK-1: not found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. Seed nutrient data: MNK-1 is an extra-large-seeded kabuli line with seed Fe 72.88 and Zn 30.98 mg/kg.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MNK-1 (chickpea)

Name note: the CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "MNK-1". Sources write it as "MNK 1" or "MNK-1", and all refer to the same kabuli line. Seednet's own portal page was not returned by any search, so the Seednet record itself is unverified. Release year: the Seednet record reads 2010-12-23, while the DPD table lists 2011 for UAS Raichur. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as a heat-tolerant genotype in a field screening method study at ICAR-NIASM Pune, 2023-25 seasons -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13311209/
- In a salinity pot experiment (10 genotypes, three NaCl levels, College of Agriculture Vijayapur), MNK1 was described as less affected than several others on morpho-phenological and yield traits; the paper gives no MNK1-specific numeric yield loss in the snippet -- https://journaloffarmsciences.in/index.php/JFM/article/download/190/211
- Drought: the only MNK-1 evidence is farmer-preferred variety trial (FPVS) yields in Kurnool, Prakasam and Anantapur (mean 983 kg/ha) and a Karnataka FPVS note, with no drought-tolerance rating -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
- Flood/submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to wilt, per the DPD central release table (2011 release, UAS Raichur) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Moderately resistant to Fusarium wilt, per a chickpea varieties slide summary -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/varieties-of-chickpea/87189800
- Pest resistance: No evidence found. The slide deck's "tolerant to wilt, dry root rot and bgm" entry is under a different variety heading (55.4 g/100 seeds, 110 days) and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Plant type and seed size: erect plants, broad compound leaves, milky-white seed, 51.9 g/100 seeds, 100-day maturity -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/varieties-of-chickpea/87189800
- Average yield 13-14 q/ha, maturity 100-105 days, Karnataka/AP/Odisha/TN, irrigated -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- ICAR-IIPR AICRP Chickpea 2021-22 report lists MNK 1 among recent extra-large-seeded kabuli releases, and in multi-location trial entries (values in brackets, unit not stated in snippet) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Karnataka FPVS 2017-18: MNK 1 was one of three elite entries; GBM 2 was the top yielder in Kalaburagi -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
- Seed germination testing protocol standardized on MNK-1 (2014-15 work) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327252161_An_improved_method_of_seed_germination_testing_in_Kabuli_chickpea

GENETICS AND QTL
- F2:3 mapping population (188 F2 plants) from MNK-1 × Annigeri 1; 31,311 SNPs found, 7,204 polymorphic; 11 Fe and 8 Zn QTLs; MNK-1 alleles favoured Fe at all five CaLG04 loci -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7588353
- Same study, Frontiers version (DOI 10.3389/fnut.2020.559120) -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2020.559120/pdf
- MNK-1 is a kabuli, extra-large-seeded line with seed Fe 72.88 and Zn 30.98 mg/kg -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33154975
- MNK-1 × GKB-10 derived green-seeded lines (cross relation, not the released variety itself) -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/49%20Multivariate-Analysis-for-Grain-Yield-and-Nutritional-Quality-Traits-of-Green-Seeded-Chickpea-(Cicer-arietinum-L.)-Genotypes-derived-from-Desi-and-Kabuli-(GKB-10-%C3%97-MNK-1)-Initial-Efforts-for-Green-S-Honnappa-M-49.pdf
- Drought, heat or wilt QTL/marker work specific to MNK-1: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (per the release record and DPD table): University of Agricultural Sciences, Raichur, Karnataka. Released 2011 per DPD -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist named for MNK-1 itself: No evidence found.
- Names that appear on UAS Raichur chickpea papers (Honnappa M, Hosamani M, Umesh Babu BS, D.M. Mannur) are linked to MNK-1-derived green-seeded lines, not to its release, so they are not attributed here -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2018/vol7issue6/PartAJ/7-6-125-743.pdf
- Development station context: ARS Kalaburagi, UAS Raichur, is named as the trial site in the derived-line work -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/49%20Multivariate-Analysis-for-Grain-Yield-and-Nutritional-Quality-Traits-of-Green-Seeded-Chickpea-(Cicer-arietinum-L.)-Genotypes-derived-from-Desi-and-Kabuli-(GKB-10-%C3%97-MNK-1)-Initial-Efforts-for-Green-S-Honnappa-M-49.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact for MNK-1: No evidence found.
- Institute-level email, phone, postal address or contact page for UAS Raichur: No evidence found in these results. Not guessed.

Search status: I ran four web_search calls, which is the maximum allowed. The first call returned the only relevant hit, and I saw only a truncated snippet of it. The tool limit then blocked my follow-up searches, so the digest is thin and several headings are empty for that reason. The CSC name and the Seednet name are identical ("PBG7 (GL 26054)"), so one set of evidence applies to both. The search pages mostly used "PBG7" without the GL number, so the GL number is not confirmed by any retrieved page.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The only pest-related text retrieved (H. armigera pod damage screening at BHU) concerns other genotypes, so I discarded it. The PAU ascochyta blight page concerns interspecific derivatives, not PBG7, so I discarded it too.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The ResearchGate paper titled "PBG7: A new high yielding variety of desi gram" presents PBG7 as a high-yielding variety. Its snippet gave no yield figures, trial sites or agronomy details -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276267978_PBG7_A_new_high_yielding_variety_of_desi_gram_Cicer_arietinum_L

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage or marker study for PBG7 was retrieved. The input record lists parentage as "Not specified".

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The ResearchGate paper lists Sarvjeet Singh as an author (dated May 2015). I could not confirm from the snippet whether he is the lead breeder or the release proposer. The title's "desi gram" matches Bengal gram, which is the Seednet crop name. Institution: the input record gives Punjab Agricultural University, and the search did not contradict it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276267978_PBG7_A_new_high_yielding_variety_of_desi_gram_Cicer_arietinum_L

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder email, phone, postal address or PAU institute contact page was retrieved. Follow-up was not possible because of the search limit. The PAU Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics is the logical place to look.

PUBLICATIONS
Singh, S. (2015). PBG7: A new high yielding variety of desi gram (Cicer arietinum L.). ResearchGate record of a PDF; journal and volume not confirmed by the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/276267978_PBG7_A_new_high_yielding_variety_of_desi_gram_Cicer_arietinum_L
Only the author name and the publication date (May 2015) were visible in the snippet, so the full author list and journal are unverified. No KrishiKosh, AICRP, ICAR or journal items were retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No NSC, Punjab state seed corporation, KVK, PAU seed sale or dealer listing for PBG7 was retrieved. The one seed-related result (a Pakistani AARI chickpea page) concerns other varieties and a different country, so I discarded it.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Punjab is recorded in the input record (CSC/variety record), but no search result confirmed it. This is unverified by the search.

Discarded results (not about PBG7): Frontiers ascochyta-blight paper (interspecific derivatives); Springer chickpea seed metabolomics paper (no variety named); AARI Faisalabad "Chickpea Desi" page (Pakistan, other varieties).

Recommended next steps: confirm the GL 26054 designation and the release notification in the CSC/ICAR minutes; check the PAU Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics and the PAU Pulses breeding pages for the lead breeder and contact details; search KrishiKosh and the AICRP on Chickpea annual reports for trial data; and check the Punjab Seed Corporation and PAU seed-sale listings for availability.

drought_tolerance.technical_details: The variety record states resistance to drought. The review 'Chickpea breeding and management' lists Pusa 212 as resistant to F. wilt and root rots, with moisture stress and low/high temperature tolerance. No quantitative drought-index data for Pusa 212 appeared in the snippets. It is used in drought-related physiology and breeding panels.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The review lists tolerance to low and high temperature, but this is a generic statement. The IARI Annual Report 2019-20 mentions a cross of ICC 14395 x Pusa 212 for heat stress screening (48 °C), but this does not show that Pusa 212 itself is heat tolerant. The variety is described as suitable for early and late sowing.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: Pusa-212 appears in a table in Flowers (2010) of germination and radicle-length salinity studies (Saxena & Rewari, 1991). The snippets give no result for this variety. The review notes that chickpea in general is salt sensitive. The accelerated-ageing and seawater study includes Pusa 212 but the snippets show no tolerance result.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No flood or waterlogging evidence for Pusa 212 was found. The CRIDA document only recommends surface drainage in high-rainfall, deep black soils for chickpea in general.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Fusarium wilt (resistant, supported by multiple sources); root rots (claimed in a review, but contradicted for dry root rot); dry root rot (susceptible)
disease_resistance.technical_details: Multiple sources list Pusa 212 as a wilt-resistant cultivar: the ICRISAT chapter 'Diseases of Chickpea', IARI technical options, course material and a review. A study of the chickpea wilt complex in western India found Pusa 212 showed the highest dry root rot incidence (31.7-100%) against the isolates tested. A 2023 abstract describes Pusa 212 as 'resistant and susceptible to DRR respectively' in a comparison, which is ambiguous in the snippet. The overall picture is wilt resistant but dry root rot susceptible. Wilt resistance may have eroded since 1982, as new races appear. The snippets do not report specific resistance genes.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: None documented. The record's 'resistant to gram wilt' is a disease trait, not a pest trait.
pest_resistance.technical_details: No insect pest resistance (e.g. Helicoverpa) evidence was found. Resistance to lodging and shattering are agronomic traits.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: Several citations (ICRISAT chapter, IARI publications, Flowers 2010, a review) support Fusarium wilt resistance, which is a stress trait. Drought, frost and low/high temperature claims come from the record and a review, with little independent verification. Yield is modest (16.8 Q/ha). The variety is documented as susceptible to dry root rot, and there is no Gujarat-specific evidence, no marker data and no flood or salinity evidence. This fits the 75 band (some research evidence, at least one stress trait and a citation) rather than 90-100.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: PUSA-212 is a 1982-released desi chickpea (P.340 x G.130, pedigree selection) with 130-150 days maturity and a yield of 16.8 Q/ha. Its Fusarium wilt resistance is supported by several sources, while its drought, frost and temperature tolerance rests mainly on the variety record and a review. It is susceptible to dry root rot, and no marker, flood, salinity or commercial-availability evidence was found.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Desi chickpea released in 1982 by the Central Varietal Release Committee, with small light-brown seeds, 130-150 days maturity and 16.8 Q/ha yield. It suits early and late sowing and is fertilizer responsive.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Fusarium wilt resistance is well supported, and drought, frost and lodging resistance are claimed with limited verification. Dry root rot susceptibility was documented, and flood, submergence, salinity, heat and pest evidence is absent or inconclusive.
