search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Gram-10 (CSC name) / Pant Gram-5. (Seednet name), chickpea, PG-265

Name check: The searches did not find any source for a 2024 CSC release of "Pant Gram-10" (PG-265). The only Pant G-10 record found is an older GBPUAT variety, WCG-10 (Pant G-10), released in 2001. The Seednet name "Pant Gram-5." matches a separate 2017 GBPUAT release, PG 035 (Pant Gram 5). Findings below are labelled by the name they refer to. The CSC 2024 identity of PG-265 remains unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): described as tolerant to Fusarium wilt and suited to late-sown conditions -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-pant-gram-5/
- Pant G-10 (2001 WCG-10 record, not confirmed as the CSC 2024 variety): listed as resistant to root rot, stunt virus, wilt and dry root rot -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to either name.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pant G-10 (2001 record): resistance to wilt, dry root rot and stunt virus is listed -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): wilt tolerance is listed; no other disease or pest data found -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for pod borer or other pest resistance for either name.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pant G-10 (2001 record): yield 21-25 q/ha, maturity about 147 days -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): yield 22.15 q/ha, maturity 126-140 days, brown seed of about 16.2 g/100 seeds -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-pant-gram-5/
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): 2017 AICRP listing gives a yield of 22-23 q/ha in the NWPZ, with late-sown suitability -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No multi-location trial data found for PG-265 (CSC name).

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): the AICRP report lists its cross as PG035 x HC 5 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Parentage for Pant Gram-10 (CSC name) is not specified in the input and was not found.
- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies on either name.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): originating centre is GBPUAT, Pantnagar, Uttarakhand -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-pant-gram-5/
- Pant G-10 (2001 record): originating centre is GBPUAT -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- No named lead breeder found for Pant Gram-10 or Pant Gram-5 (Seednet name).

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level, no breeder contact found)
- Dr. G.P. Dixit, Project Coordinator, AICRP on Chickpea, ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur 208 024. Phone (O) 0512-2580993; EPABX 0512-2580994, 2580995 Ext. 6108; mobile 09936149224; fax 0512-2580992; email aicrpciipr@yahoo.co.in -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Dr. A.K. Srivastava, Senior Scientist, Chickpea Coordination Unit, ICAR-IIPR Kanpur. Office 0512-2580993; EPABX 0512-2580994-95 Ext. 6109; mobile 08756995677; email bhu.avinash@gmail.com -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Dr. (Mrs.) Poonam Sharma, Principal Scientist (Microbiology), Pulses Section, PAU Ludhiana-141004. Office 0161-2401960; fax 0161-2400945; mobile 08146295100; email poonam1963in@yahoo.co.in -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Not verified for this variety: the IIPR varieties page lists Dr. Yogesh Kumar, chickpea breeder (mobile 9430139411; yogesh.kumar8@icar.gov.in), as developer of a different variety, IPC 2010-142 (Kuber). Use only as an IIPR breeding contact -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- No GBPUAT, Pantnagar breeder or station contact found in the searches.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper on Pant Gram-10 (CSC name) or Pant Gram-5 (Seednet name) found.
- ICAR-IIPR (2023). ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea Progress Report, 2021-22 (year inferred from the 2023 upload; authorship not stated in the snippet). ICAR-IIPR Kanpur -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, conference paper or DOI found for either name.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for seed availability of Pant Gram-10 (CSC name) or Pant Gram-5 (Seednet name) from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The searches were limited to general and national sources, so this heading is a search result, not a confirmed absence.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- CSC-listed states (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam) for Pant Gram-10: No evidence found in the searches.
- Pant G-10 (2001 WCG-10 record): listed for Maharashtra, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pant Gram 5 (Seednet name): listed for the North West Plain Zone (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, north-west UP, plus Uttarakhand, Rajasthan and J&K) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION
- The CSC release date (2024-08-02) and PG-265 code were not found in any source. The Seednet name "Pant Gram-5." is not corroborated as a PG-265 record.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as tolerant to BGM (botrytis grey mould), with irrigated-condition suitability; the AICRP table also describes it as late maturing -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found for this variety -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerance to BGM is the only disease/pest trait recorded for this variety; no wilt, root rot or Ascochyta ratings were found for it -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No other disease or pest evidence found -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- AICRP table entry (Pantnagar origin, Uttarakhand, irrigated): semi-spreading plant habit, medium height, large seed with a prominent beak, late maturing, about 125 days, and a value of 14.0 in the yield column (units not stated in the extracted text; presumably q/ha) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No multi-location trial data or farmer-field yield results found for this variety -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Name-confusion warning: "Vallabh Kabuli Chana-1 (WCGK 2000-16)" is a different variety (Modipuram, NWPZ) and must not be merged with this record -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/high-yielding-variety-of-green-gram-chickpea-vallabh-kabuli-chana-1-wcgk-2000-16/

GENETICS AND QTL
- The AICRP table gives the origin of this entry as "Selection", not the parentage PG 92-105 x PUSA 362 supplied in the record, so the parentage is unconfirmed -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No QTL, marker or genetic-study evidence specific to this variety found; the Agarwal et al. 2012 transcriptome paper uses ICCV2, not this variety -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3531472/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The AICRP table places the variety's origin at Pantnagar (Uttarakhand), which points to G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar; the table itself does not name a breeder -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No lead breeder name found in any search -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No Pant Kabuli Chana-1 breeder name, email, phone or postal address found. No institute contact page was retrieved in these searches (the Pantnagar origin is inferred from the AICRP table only) -- No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR-All India Coordinated Research Project on Chickpea (2022). Project Coordinator's report, chickpea 2021-22 (variety table includes Pant Kabuli Chana 1). ICAR-IIPR, PDF uploaded 2023 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh), conference paper or field-trial report specific to Pant Kabuli Chana-1 found -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No Seednet portal page was retrieved (the search did not target seednet.gov.in directly, so this is unverified) -- No evidence found
- No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Pant Kabuli Chana-1 found; the dealer listings returned are for generic kabuli chana or other varieties (e.g., Devansh Seeds lists DCP 92, Pusa 256, HC-5) -- https://www.exportersindia.com/devansh-seeds-corporation/white-chickpeas.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICRP table lists Uttarakhand as the state for this variety, consistent with the record -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

NAME AND RELEASE NOTES
- variety_name (CSC minutes) "Pant Kabuli Chana-1" and seednet_variety_name "Pant Kabuli Chana-1" are the same string. Evidence was found only under the AICRP report name "Pant Kabuli chana 1"; no Seednet record was retrieved, so the Seednet name is unverified.
- year_of_release: the AICRP table's year column reads 2010, but it is not confirmed as the notification year. The record's "NaT" stays unresolved -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Coverage gap: the four searches did not include seednet.gov.in, KrishiKosh, or the GBPUAT site directly. Those should be checked before the record is finalised.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Phule Vikrant (CSC release minutes) / Phule Vikram (Seednet portal), chickpea, Phule G 0405

Search budget: all 4 permitted web_search calls were used. A fifth call was refused by the tool limit, so the gaps below could not be filled.

Name note: The CSC name is "Phule Vikrant" and the Seednet name is "Phule Vikram." In the findings below, "Vikrant" refers to the CSC name and "Vikram" to the Seednet name. A 2025-era pulse-beetle study lists "Phule Vikram" and "Phule Vikrant" as two separate chickpea entries, so the two names may refer to different lines or be a naming error. This needs checking against the Seednet notification record before the two are treated as one variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched; no stress-tolerance data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) for Vikrant or Vikram surfaced.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Pulse beetle (Callosobruchus chinensis) biology was studied on several chickpea varieties, including Phule Vikram and Phule Vikrant, in a laboratory setting. This is a storage-pest study, not a field resistance assessment, and it reports no resistance rating for either name. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390658171_Biology_of_pulse_beetle_Callosobruchus_chinensis_L_on_different_varieties_of_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A 2021 impact-analysis paper in the Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry covers chickpea varieties released by the AICRP Pulses Improvement Project at MPKV Rahuri and names Phule Vikrant among them. It reports adoption trends and partial-budget economics, not yield or maturity values. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue1S/PartD/S-10-1-4-996.pdf
No yield, maturity, or multi-location trial data were found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No QTL, marker, or parentage information was located. Parentage is recorded as "Not specified" in the input record and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The institution is Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth (MPKV), Rahuri, Ahmednagar, Maharashtra. An Indian university directory describes MPKV's chickpea varieties as widely adopted by farmers. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/UniversityDetails.aspx?id=29
No lead breeder or scientist name was found for Vikrant or Vikram.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level address only, from the directory above: Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth, Rahuri, Dist. Ahmednagar, 413 722, Maharashtra. -- http://www.iauaindia.org/UniversityDetails.aspx?id=29
No email, phone, breeder contact, or institute contact-page URL was found. A MPKV official website should be checked directly for these.

PUBLICATIONS -- Only the following items were found. Authors and full bibliographic details were not extracted, so they are not listed.

ResearchGate, 2025 listing (year inferred from record ID; not verified) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390658171_Biology_of_pulse_beetle_Callosobruchus_chinensis_L_on_different_varieties_of_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L

This is a commercial listing, not an official seed-corporation or SAU record. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/phule-vikram-chickpea-chana-seeds-26526966812.html

drought.details: Phule Vikram is explicitly identified as drought tolerant and capable of performing under stress environmental conditions. Its adoption has been demonstrated by Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) as a stress/drought tolerant variety, contributing to increased productivity.

heat.details: The variety is described as heat tolerant and suitable for late sown situations, particularly in Madhya Pradesh. It is also explicitly mentioned among varieties tolerant to heat in ICAR reports.

salinity.details: While not explicitly stated as highly salt tolerant for Phule Vikram specifically, its adoption was demonstrated by KVK Buxar, which demonstrated 'stress/drought tolerant and short duration' varieties in conjunction with 'salt tolerant variety of paddy, wheat, mustard and chick pea'. Furthermore, Phule Vikram is listed among varieties released for cultivation in regions where QTLs responsible for salinity tolerance-related traits have been identified in chickpea breeding programs.

flood.details: Phule Vikram is explicitly listed among varieties tolerant to waterlogging conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Phule Vikram is noted for its resistance to wilt, specifically Fusarium wilt. It is also generally tolerant to biotic stresses.

pest_resistance.summary: While generally stated as tolerant to biotic stresses (which typically includes pests), no specific pest resistance details are provided for Phule Vikram.

agronomic_details.yield: Phule Vikram has demonstrated its ability to boost productivity and economic benefits, as evidenced by its adoption by farmers. In one study, the genotype Phule Vikram recorded a maximum yield per plant of 13.80 g, suggesting a high individual plant yield potential. However, a quantitative average yield in quintals per hectare (q/ha) is not specified.
agronomic_details.stability: While a formal stability analysis report is not detailed for Phule Vikram specifically, its recommendation for cultivation across multiple states and central/southern India suggests broad adaptation and stability across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: This variety is recommended for cultivation in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh, as well as broadly in central and southern India. It is particularly suitable for late sown situations in Madhya Pradesh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Phule Vikram exhibits a tall growth habit, making it suitable for mechanical harvesting. It produces medium-sized, yellowish-brown seeds. It has also been described as semi-erect.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Phule Vikram has been successfully demonstrated by KVKs (e.g., KVK Buxar) and adopted by farmers, leading to boosted productivity. Technology cluster frontline demonstrations have been conducted. Additionally, large-scale quality seed production (4827.36 quintals) of Phule Vikram has been implemented with seed growers in districts like Ahmednagar.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Phule Vikram was one of four chickpea varieties released in 2019, two of which were developed using marker-assisted breeding, strongly implying its development leveraged molecular markers. While specific markers (e.g., SNP, SSR) are not detailed, the use of genomics-assisted breeding for traits like heat and salinity tolerance is indicated.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTLs for heat stress and salinity tolerance-related traits have been identified in chickpea breeding programs that involve varieties such as Phule Vikram. However, specific QTLs and their effects unique to Phule Vikram are not explicitly quantified in the provided results.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Raj Vijay Gram 210 (RVG 210), chickpea

Name note: The evidence for this variety uses "Raj Vijay Gram 210 / RVG 210" (CSC name "variety_name"). Every search result for the Seednet name "RAJ VIJAY GRAM-202" concerns RVG 202 (Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 202, also called JSC 55), a separate variety. No Seednet page for either name was returned, so no finding below is attributed to the Seednet name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as resistant to Fusarium wilt in the central-varieties table for 2021 release, with tolerance to Helicoverpa pod borer -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Described as resistant to wilt and tolerant to pod borer, early maturing, bold seeded, with an average potential yield of about 1805 kg/ha -- https://www.rvskvv.net/images/Newsletter_Jul-Dec-2019_16.06.2020.pdf (text is jumbled; attribution to RVG 210 is the most likely reading, not confirmed)
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance specific to RVG 210: No evidence found. The searches returned drought-tolerance and heat-stability material for RVG 202, RVG 203 and other lines, which I did not attribute to RVG 210.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Fusarium wilt resistance and Helicoverpa pod borer tolerance (as above) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Dry root rot, Ascochyta, stunt, YMV and other disease reactions for RVG 210: No evidence found. Dry root rot resistance appeared only for other RVG lines.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity about 109 days and seed weight 26.7 g/100 seeds, per the RVG 210 entry -- https://www.rvskvv.net/images/Newsletter_Jul-Dec-2019_16.06.2020.pdf
- Central-varieties table entry for 2021 release, RVSKVV, AICRP RAK Sehore: duration and yield columns are not clearly labelled in the extracted text (readings of about 18-21 q/ha and 105-110 days) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- AICRP Project Coordinator's Report entry (No. 145, RVG 210, RVSKVV Sehore), with characteristics that appear to belong to a neighbouring row and need checking against the original PDF -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Multi-location or field trial results specific to RVG 210: No evidence found. The FPVS trial table covers RVG 202, 203, 204 and 205 only.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage for RVG 210: No evidence found. The DPD table gives a pedigree column for other lines, not for RVG 210. The CSC record says "Not specified".
- Marker-assisted or QTL work on RVG 210: No evidence found. Marker-assisted backcross and genomics results were reported for the consortium's introgression lines and for RVG 202, not RVG 210 -- https://doi.org/10.3390/plants10122583

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: RVSKVV (Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya), AICRP on Chickpea centre at RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore (MP) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (2022). All India Coordinated Research Project on Chickpea: Project Coordinator's Report 2021-22 (includes an RVG 210 entry, No. 145). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

- Seednet portal listing under either name: No evidence found (no Seednet page was returned by any search).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RAJ VIJAY GRAM 204 (RVG 204; RVSSG 8102; ICCV 08102) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST
Name note: the evidence below refers to "Raj Vijay Gram 204 / RVG 204 / RVSSG 8102". No evidence was found for the Seednet name "RAJ VIJAY GRAM-202". The Seednet crop name is not covered by any result. Every "RVG 202" page found refers to a different variety and is excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as tolerant to wilt, with timely-sown and machine-harvest suitability in the central release table -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Moderately resistant to wilt, tall semi-erect habit, seed size about 23.4 g/100 seeds in the ICAR-AICRP chickpea report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Heat stress (very-late sown, 5-44 °C test range): regression coefficient above 1 with above-grand-mean yield, recommended for very-late sown conditions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366836667_Stability_against_heat_stress_in_genotypes_of_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
Drought: listed in rainfed AMMI/GGE stability trial as a check variety; no specific drought score for RVG 204 was found -- https://oar.icrisat.org/12498/1/Legume%20Research-%20An%20International%20Journal_46_9_1105-1116_2023.pdf
Drought-tolerance selection (Tiwari et al. 2023) names PG205, not RVG 204 -- excluded as not this variety.
Salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
Wilt resistance/tolerance recorded in the central release table and ICAR report -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
"Reaction to major diseases and pests" on a trade listing claims wilt resistance and pod borer tolerance (dealer-sourced, not official) -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rvg-204-chickpea-chana-seeds-26527034255.html
Dry root rot, Ascochyta blight, Phytophthora or other disease ratings for RVG 204: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity: 111 days (ICAR-AICRP table); yield 22.32 q/ha in the same table -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Dealer listing gives 111 days, 7.5-8 q/acre, seed rate 25-30 kg/acre -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rvg-204-chickpea-chana-seeds-26527034255.html
Machine-harvestable, semi-erect, one of four varieties for central India -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf ; https://www.icrisat.org/crops/chickpea/overview
Farmer participatory varietal selection (FPVS) trials in MP (Indore, Sehore, Ujjain; RAK Sehore centre), 2017-2020 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
Multi-location trials at Jabalpur, Nandyal and Sehore (2016-2019), with RVG 204 among the entries as reported -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8703834/
Machine-harvestable varieties evaluated against NBeG 47, GBM 2, Phule Vikram and BG 3062 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344273491_Advances_in_Chickpea_Breeding_and_Genomics_for_Varietal_Development_and_Trait_Improvement_in_India

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (not in CSC minutes; ICAR table gives): ICCV10 x ICCL87322 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Used as a check in a rapid RIL generation advancement and Rhizobium study (SY, PH, DFF traits) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391019843_Rapid_generation_advancement_of_RIL_population_and_assessing_the_impact_of_Rhizobium_nodulation_on_crop_yields_in_Chickpea
QTL or marker mapping for RVG 204: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (RVSKVV), Gwalior -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rvg-204-chickpea-chana-seeds-26527034255.html
Station: AICRP on Chickpea (RAK), Sehore, MP -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The breeder-name search returned only pages on other varieties and non-breeder profiles.
ICRISAT lists ICCV 08102 (RVG 204) among varieties it released in India, indicating a joint parentage -- https://www.icrisat.org/crops/chickpea/overview

CONTACT DETAILS

Central zone (MP, CG, RJ, GJ, MH), timely sown, desi type, machine harvesting -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
Recorded as "Madhya Pradesh" in the input; the CZ listing is wider -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Web%20site.pdf

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: RVSKVV R.A.K. College of Agriculture, Sehore  (Madhya Pradesh)
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: 1.	Seed rate is 100 kg/ha for a row to row spacing of 30 x 10 cm. 2.	Responded well to 20:60:20:20 Kg NPKS/ha. 3.	Suitable for timely sown, semi-irrigated and irrigated conditions in both the zones. 4.	Good nodulation ability.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: 1.	Smooth surface, creamy colour and owl’s head shaped seeds. 2.	Medium tall semi spreading plants. 3.	White flowers with no anthocyanin content in plants.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress:
1.	It can sustain under as well as warm climatic conditions.
2.	Wider adaptability to sustain cool climatic condition at Punjab and adjoining areas as well as in worm climatic condition of Maharashtra during pod filling stage indicates the stress tolerance of variety.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The proposed variety RVSSG 30 showed resistant to moderately action against Fusarium wilt in four location and moderately resistant to Dry Root Rot at four locations. It was also found resistant against dyunt at 1 location. Against BGM the entry has got least incidence in three locations and under artificial conditions at ICRISAT.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to pod borer (Helicoverpa) and tolerant against pulse beetle under storage conditions.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 20 Kg N/ha, 60 kg P2O5/ha, 20 kg K2O/ha, 20 kg S/ha, Basal dose at sowing time.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under the 2019 Raj Vijay Kabuli row of the DPD central-release table, a timely-sown Madhya Pradesh kabuli line is noted for wilt tolerance, though the extracted row does not give the name RVKG 111 explicitly. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to RVKG 111 or RVKG 121.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The ICAR-AICRP chickpea report row for RVKG 111 lists a moderate-resistance code (MR), but the extracted text does not name the disease. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- A pod-borer (Helicoverpa) tolerance entry appears in the DPD table next to a "RVG 210" label. The layout is garbled, so I cannot confirm it belongs to RVKG 111. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Other pest and disease resistance statements in the search results (for example, Raj Vijay Kabuli 2021 for wilt and dry root rot) belong to other releases and are discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is listed as 117 days, with yield of 20-22 q/ha, in the AICRP report row for RVKG 111 (2019, Sehore, kabuli). The same row gives 100-seed weight as 26 g and describes medium-sized, smooth, creamy seed. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The same AICRP row gives the parentage as JG 130 x BG 8416. This conflicts with the parentage supplied in the request (Pusa 1088 x FG 711), and I have not resolved the conflict. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The DPD 2019 row gives 117 days maturity for a Raj Vijay Kabuli entry from RVSKVV, matching RVKG 111 but not naming it. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- In a thesis trial on black soils of Madhya Pradesh, RVKG-111 was among the kabuli genotypes recording higher plant height. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/76704337-bee8-408d-b420-c6fc351becc1/content

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The search returned no QTL, marker or genetic-study page naming RVKG 111 or RVKG 121. The TCGC genomics paper (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8703834/) is about chickpea breeding in general and does not name this variety in the retrieved text.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (RVSKVV), Gwalior, with the All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) centre at RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore (MP). -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The RAK College of Agriculture, Sehore is listed as part of RVSKVV in an author-affiliation block for a Translational Chickpea Genomics Consortium paper. That block names no lead breeder for RVKG 111. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8703834/
- Lead breeder or scientist name for RVKG 111: No evidence found. The breeder-name and "developed by" searches returned only other varieties, such as IPCK 2013-163 and IPCK 2009-145 from ICAR-IIPR, which are discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address: Race Course Road, Gwalior-474002, Madhya Pradesh. -- https://kvv.mponline.gov.in/Quick%20Links/Quick%20Links/Documents/RVSKVV%20PG%20and%20PH.D%20Final%20Seat%20metrix%202021-22%20with%20PH_12_10_2021.pdf
- Official website: www.rvskvv.net. -- https://www.rvskvv.net/
- Institute-level email vcrvsaugwa@mp.gov.in and phone 8989205805 come from a third-party college listing, not an official page. -- https://allegiance-educare.in/college/rajmata-vijayaraje-scindia-krishi-vishwa-vidyalaya-rvskvv
- A second institute email (pstovcrvskvv@gmail.com) and phone (07512970502) come from a third-party admissions page, not an official source. -- https://www.shiksha.com/university/rajmata-vijayaraje-scindia-krishi-vishwavidyalaya-gwalior-65557
- No breeder email or phone was found for RVKG 111 or RVKG 121.

PUBLICATIONS
- Nema, A. (n.d.). Evaluation of Nutrient Composition, Quality Traits and Nutrient Requirement of Major Dominating Chickpea Genotypes Grown in Black Soils of Madhya Pradesh. MSc thesis, RVSKVV, Gwalior (Soil Science and Agricultural Chemistry). Year not shown in the extracted text. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/76704337-bee8-408d-b420-c6fc351becc1/content
- ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2021-22). Project Coordinator's report, 2021-22. ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur (authors not listed in the extracted text). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No other peer-reviewed paper, conference paper or DOI naming RVKG 111 was found. The Tiwari and Tripathi (2020) Legume Research paper on desi and kabuli chickpea (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343942846_Evaluation_of_Physiological_and_Biochemical_Contents_in_Desi_and_Kabuli_Chickpea) is not shown to name this variety, so it is discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Seed-dealer and NSC pages returned only other varieties (PKV 2, Vijay, JAKI 9218, GUJ-2) and are discarded. No RVKG 111 or RVKG 121 listing by NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Madhya Pradesh. The DPD 2019 row lists the state, and the AICRP row gives Sehore (MP) as the centre. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

NAME NOTE
- Evidence refers to "Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 111 / RVKG 111" (CSC/AICRP naming). The Seednet name "Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 121 (RVKG 121)" returned no matching results in any search. Every finding above that refers to RVKG 111 is under that name only.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) RVSKVV newsletter (Jul-Dec 2019): notified entry with bold seeds of about 26.3 g per 100 seeds, maturity around 114 days, and average potential yield (no numeric value given). (2) Central release table (DPD): 18-20 q/ha yield, 99-123 days duration, Madhya Pradesh, timely sown. (3) ICAR-AICRP 2021 report: a Sehore row with parentage Pusa 1088 x FG 711 that matches the yield and duration in the Central release table; this is an inferred row match, as the page does not name RVKG 121 on that row. (4) Thesis-level comparison: RVKG-121 had the highest harvest index (41.23%) among 15 genotypes and was among the top for branches, pods per plant and seeds per pod. The same thesis gives a release year of 2012, which conflicts with the 2021 (DPD) and 2020-11-09 (user record) dates; the 2012 date is treated as unreliable. No peer-reviewed field-trial paper or DOI specific to RVKG 121 was found.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 2020 (variety_name) / Raj Vijay Kabuli gram 101 (JSC 42) (seednet_variety_name), chickpea (kabuli)

NAME NOTE: The CSC release table lists the 2020 entry under the code RVSSG 63 (also written RVSIG 63 in one garbled row). The Seednet name "Raj Vijay Kabuli gram 101 (JSC 42)" belongs to a separate, earlier release (listed as 2011 or 2012, code RVKG 101). Evidence about the 101 (JSC 42) entry is reported below only under the seednet name and is flagged. Nothing found names RVKG 2020 directly. The variety_code "RVKG 2020" does not appear in any source.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- CSC table lists the RVSSG 63 entry (2020 name, year cell reads 2021) as tolerant to pod borer (Helicoverpa) and to pulse beetle in storage, for semi-irrigated and irrigated timely-sown crops -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Heat-stress stability study lists RVSSG-63 with a regression coefficient below one and a lower-than-grand-mean yield, read as stable under normal and mid-late sowing but not high-yielding; no explicit heat tolerance claim -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366836667_Stability_against_heat_stress_in_genotypes_of_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
- Stability in phenology and yield under varied temperatures (25 genotypes) was reported, but the retrieved text does not confirm RVSSG 63 among the named genotypes -- No evidence found for RVSSG 63 specifically; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366614322_Stability_in_Phenology_Yield_and_Yield_Attributes_of_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_Genotypes_under_Various_Temperature_Conditions
- Drought, flood, submergence, salinity: No evidence found for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- RVSSG 63 entry (CSC table): moderately resistant to chickpea stunt -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- RVSSG 63 entry (CSC table): tolerant to pod borer and pulse beetle in storage -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Raj Vijay Kabuli gram 101 (JSC 42) entry (Seednet name, 2011/2012 release, NOT confirmed for 2020): moderately resistant to wilt; resistant to Fusarium wilt and moderately tolerant to pod borer -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Wilt, dry root rot, Botrytis grey mould, Ascochyta blight for RVSSG 63: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CSC table row for the RVSSG 63 entry gives 20-23 q/ha yield and 105-165 days maturity, but row alignment is garbled; treat as unverified -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 151 (variety code RVKG 151 / RVSSG 37), chickpea

Name handling: The sources I found name this variety as "Raj Vijay Kabuli Gram 151" (RVKG 151 or RVG 151) in the dpd.gov.in and ICAR-IIPR tables. The Seednet name "Raj Vijay Kabuli gram 101 (JSC 42)" refers to a different variety (Gram 101) in every source I found. Gram 101 findings appear below only under the Seednet heading and are labelled as Gram 101.

Mismatch to resolve: The parentage "ICCV2 X BG 256" in the input matches the ICAR-IIPR table entry for Gram 101, not Gram 151. For Gram 151, the same table lists "Dollar x Kripa." Please check the parentage against the CSC minutes before relying on either.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Gram 151 is listed as tolerant to wilt (Fusarium) in the dpd central-release table. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Gram 151 was found. The only stress-related wilt note for Gram 101 is "moderately resistant to wilt." -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Gram 151 is described as tolerant to wilt, with no other disease or pest resistance listed. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gram 101 (not 151): moderately resistant to wilt. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Gram 151 is an extra-large-seeded kabuli, sown timely under irrigated conditions, with a duration of about 113 days. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- The AICRP report gives 100-seed weight of 54.3 g, a 113-day duration, a yield of 20-21 q/ha, normal sowing, and medium-tall, spreading growth habit for RVKG 151. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The dpd central table lists yield 17-18 q/ha for Gram 151. This conflicts with the 20-21 q/ha in the AICRP report. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gram 101 (Seednet name): large-seeded kabuli, early maturing, about 110 days, yield about 20 q/ha, irrigated. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- No multi-location trial results specific to Gram 151 were found. The multi-location trial result in the search (Pakistani/Moroccan/Chinese kabuli germplasm) names other varieties and was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker or genetic study for Gram 151 was found.
- Parentage for Gram 151 in the AICRP table: Dollar x Kripa. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Parentage for Gram 101 in the AICRP table: ICCV 2 x BG 256. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Gram 151 was released by Rajmata Vijayaraje Scindia Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (RVSKVV) through its AICRP on Rabi Pulses (RAK) at Sehore, Madhya Pradesh. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No lead breeder or scientist name for Gram 151 was found in any search result. -- No evidence found (breeder name searched)
- Gram 101 was released by the same institution and centre. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone, postal address or institute contact page URL for Gram 151 or RVSKVV was found in the search results. -- No evidence found
- Institute-level identifiers available from the sources: "RVSKVV, AICRP RAK, Sehore (MP)." Use the RVSKVV and AICRP-RAK websites to find contact details; they were not in the results. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report entry beyond the 2021-22 report, thesis (KrishiKosh), or conference paper naming Gram 151 was found. The research search returned chickpea papers on other varieties and germplasm, which were discarded. -- No evidence found
- AICRP/ICAR Chickpea Project Coordinator's report (2021-22), which contains the Gram 151 variety entry: ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2023). Chickpea varietal table. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No seed source (NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or dealer) naming Gram 151 was found. The seed-related pages returned were for other varieties or other states and were discarded. -- No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gram 151 is listed for Madhya Pradesh, timely-sown and irrigated conditions. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Year of release: 2019 per the dpd and AICRP tables. -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Gram 101 (Seednet name): released 2011 or 2012 for Madhya Pradesh, with the release year differing between tables. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

drought.details: The IIAU entry describes GJGK 1617 as moderately tolerant to drought. No drought mechanism (root traits, osmotic adjustment, biomass or yield-under-stress data) was found in the digest. The ICAR-IIPR report describes the variety as suitable for timely-sown irrigated conditions in the North West Plain Zone and released for the West Central Zone including Gujarat; this is a irrigated-condition recommendation and does not itself establish drought tolerance. Seednet-name evidence for Sorath Kabuli 2 (GKG 2) describes irrigated recommendation and is a different variety, so it was not used for this rating.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to white rust and stag head; moderately resistant to downy mildew (IIAU entry). Good resistance to stunt disease (dealer listing, not a research source). pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to major insect pests as listed in the JAU/IIAU entry. Low pod borer damage reported in a dealer listing (not a research source). No further pest screening data found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Kabuli Gram 1 (Sorath Kabuli 1), chickpea, GJGk 1617

Searches run: 4 web_search queries (variety/release, breeder/institution, research/publications, seed availability). Name check: the CSC name "Gujarat Kabuli Gram 1 (Sorath Kabuli 1)" matches the GKG 1 sources below. The Seednet name "Sorath Kabuli 2 (Gujarat Kabuli Gram 2)" refers to GKG 2, a different variety per JAU's 2023 recommendations, so Seednet-name evidence is listed separately.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately tolerant to drought; GJGK 1617 is described as a kabuli variety with ~13.83 q/ha average seed yield and 139-144 days maturity -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- Source entry also states yield 5345 kg/ha, released for Gujarat (kharif, transplanted); this conflicts with the other sources and appears to be a mixed-crop brochure entry -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- Suitable for timely-sown irrigated conditions in the North West Plain Zone; released for the West Central Zone including Gujarat; 17-18 q/ha, 100-115 days -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Seednet-name evidence (GKG 2): recommended to farmers under irrigated conditions as an early-maturing kabuli variety -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//research_accomplishments_and_recommendations_2023_20251219_764.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to white rust and stag head; moderately resistant to downy mildew -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- Good resistance to stunt disease with low pod borer damage (dealer listing, not a research source) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/
- Moderately resistant to major insect pests (as listed in the JAU entry) -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- No peer-reviewed field disease screening for GJGK 1617 found (wilt/Ascochyta data appear only for other varieties) -- No evidence found beyond the above

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Plant height 89-107 cm, profuse branching, 17-23 sympodia, long staple (26.8 mm); 12-15 q/ha under recommended practices -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- Seed size 42.6 g/100 seeds (IIAU entry); 43.5 g/100 seeds (ICAR-IIPR report); 43.5 g test weight (dealer listing) -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf ; https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf ; https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/
- Dealer listing: 7.5-11 quintal/acre yield, dal recovery 67.45%, protein 23.60%, iron 63.78 ppm, zinc 35.40 ppm -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/
- Multi-location trial data (AICRP, Junagadh) not retrieved for this variety -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: cross ICC 14195P3 x ICCV 92337 (ICAR-IIPR report; the same report also prints ICCV93337) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Parentage in the CSC record is "Not specified"; the cross above is the only parentage found
- QTL or marker studies for this variety -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Pulses Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University (JAU), Junagadh, Gujarat -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
- Station established 1965-66 as a small research scheme; the station page lists GKG 1 among its chickpea varieties -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
- Lead breeder name(s) -- No evidence found. The IIAU entry mentions JAU officials (Research Director, PG Dean, Registrar) as acknowledgements only, not as breeders.
- Release year: 2022-10-26 in the input record; the dealer listing says 2023 -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder names, emails, phone numbers: No evidence found
- Institute-level contact: JAU Pulses Research Station page (no email, phone or postal address appeared in the retrieved text) -- https://www.jau.in/research-stations/research-stations/pulses-research-station-junagadh
- Recommend verifying contact details directly on the JAU site; I did not find an official email or phone for this station in the retrieved results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2023). Chickpea progress report 2021-22, ICAR-IIPR (AICRP chickpea) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (n.d.). Pulses/Field crop variety release brochure, Indian Agricultural Universities Association (IAUA) News -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (2023). Research Accomplishments and Recommendations 2023, Junagadh Agricultural University (covers GKG 2 recommendation) -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//research_accomplishments_and_recommendations_2023_20251219_764.pdf
- Peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) and conference papers specific to GJGK 1617 -- No evidence found
- Not used as variety evidence: Frontiers in Genetics 2022 (wilt pyramiding, 10.3389/fgene.2022.924287) and Poonia et al. FLD papers, which are not about this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Dealer listing for Sorath Kabuli 1 / GKG 1 (Fule Seeds) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gujarat-kabuli-gram-1-sorath-kabuli-1-gkg-1/
- Seednet (seednet.gov.in) listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation (GSSC), KVK or SAU seed-sales records for GKG 1 -- No evidence found
- Seednet-name variety (GKG 2 / Sorath Kabuli 2): seed production figures are in the allgujaratnews report -- https://allgujaratnews.in/en/amazing-discovery-of-new-varieties-of-gram-will-revolutionize-agriculture/

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Gujarat (CSC record; ICAR-IIPR report and IIPR zone text list Gujarat within the West Central Zone with Rajasthan, MP, UP Bundelkhand and Maharashtra) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Kharif transplanted recommendation in the IIAU entry conflicts with the rabi chickpea sources and should be treated as an error until verified -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf

drought.details: No search result reports drought tolerance for BL 44. Berseem is described only generally as a winter hardy, short-duration crop with high water requirement, which suggests limited drought tolerance for the crop overall. This is not variety-specific evidence.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance data found. Berseem is described as winter hardy. The Apni Kheti page gives a sowing temperature of 25-27°C and a harvesting temperature of 15-20°C for the crop in general.

salinity.details: A Scribd crop document says berseem can be grown in saline-sodic soils. This is a crop-level statement, and no BL 44-specific salinity evaluation was found.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data for BL 44 in the results.

disease_resistance.summary: No BL 44-specific disease reaction found. The Apni Kheti page reports resistance to stem rot and root rot, and immunity to downy mildew, for other listed berseem varieties; the snippets attribute these to the varieties described near BL 43 and Bundel Berseem 3, not clearly to BL 44. These findings should not be transferred to BL 44.

pest_resistance.summary: No BL 44-specific pest reaction found.

drought.details: Specific drought tolerance for BL-43 is not detailed. However, berseem (Egyptian clover) in general is recognized for its drought tolerance, with breeding programs aiming to select drought-tolerant genotypes under water stress conditions. It is described as being among the most drought-tolerant cover crops that produce significant biomass.

heat.details: Specific heat tolerance for BL-43 is not detailed. Berseem (Egyptian clover) breeding programs aim to select heat-tolerant and late-maturing lines. While it can show increased antioxidant activity under elevated temperatures as a coping mechanism, some reports indicate it is less heat-tolerant than certain other vetch varieties.

salinity.details: Specific salinity tolerance for BL-43 is not detailed. Berseem (Egyptian clover) can be cultivated in saline-sodic soils, and studies have identified ecotypes with salinity and alkalinity tolerance. Research has also evaluated the salt tolerance of various berseem cultivars and explored methods to enhance it.

flood.details: Specific flood tolerance for BL-43 is not detailed. While research mentions extreme climatic events like heavy rainfall threatening crops and studies on flood tolerance for other species, no direct information on berseem's flood tolerance is provided.

Some sources describe berseem as drought tolerant (ICRISAT field manual; a study-material PDF). The FAO Egyptian clover document mentions screening berseem accessions for drought tolerance. Another source (core.ac.uk crop production text) says Egyptian clover is less drought tolerant than alfalfa. The Tejveer Singh et al. review mentions drought-tolerant lines being identified. None of this can be attributed to this variety. Its tetraploid origin implies no specific drought advantage.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat data. The FAO document says a major objective of berseem breeding is to select heat-tolerant and late-maturing lines (crop-level objective only). Berseem is a winter-season crop.

VARIETY NAME CHECK

The parentage in the record (Chhindwara government dairy farm) matches the berseem JB-1 selection, not a barley line. The record mixes the two, so the barley entry needs checking against the CSC/Seednet records before use.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-resistance evidence was found for JB 07-15. The digest reports weed pressure (Cichorium intybus and Chenopodium album reducing green fodder and seed yield by roughly 25-35%), but this is not tied to any variety and is not pest resistance. No insect or other pest data were found.

(4) 2023-24 AICRP phosphorus trial at Urulikanchan (Pune) with four promising genotypes and two checks; genotype names not in retrieved text, so JB 07-15 is not confirmed. (5) JB 07-15: no yield, trial, or maturity data found under this name.

drought.details: The only ANANTHA-specific stress evidence is a drought hot-spot trial. ANANTHA was one of 30 drought-tolerant varieties tested without protective irrigation at Anantapur's natural drought hot spots during rainy seasons. Its AMMI row gives a mean pod yield of 223.7 g/m2 and rain-water-use efficiency of 45.28 g/m2/mm. The GGE biplot places 'Anantha' close to the centre of the concentric circle for pod yield, which the source reads as relatively stable performance. The paper's rank columns are ambiguous and their meaning could not be confirmed. The rating is medium because the evidence rests on a single multi-location study and no explicit tolerance rating is given in the source. Name note: the digest reports no evidence for a Seednet groundnut record named 'Ananth'; the Seednet crop field reads BHINDI (OKRA), which conflicts with groundnut and should be verified on seednet.gov.in. 'Anantha Jyoti' (ICGV 91114) and 'Kadiri' lines are different varieties and are excluded.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: ANANTHA (CSC name) / Ananth (Seednet name), groundnut, code H0704152, release 2010-10-10

Name note: Every groundnut result below refers to "ANANTHA" (CSC name). I found no evidence for "Ananth" as a Seednet groundnut record. The Seednet crop field says BHINDI (OKRA), which conflicts with groundnut. Verify that record on seednet.gov.in. Also, "Anantha Jyoti" (ICGV 91114) and "Kadiri" lines are different varieties and are excluded here.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The only ANANTHA-specific evidence is a drought hot-spot trial. ANANTHA was one of 30 drought-tolerant varieties tested without protective irrigation in Anantapur's natural drought hot spots during rainy seasons -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10404259 (also https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-38581-0)
Its AMMI table row gives mean pod yield of 223.7 g/m2 and rain-water-use efficiency of 45.28 g/m2/mm; the paper's rank columns are ambiguous and I could not confirm their meaning -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10404259
The GGE biplot places "Anantha" close to the centre of the concentric circle for pod yield, which the source reads as relatively stable performance -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-38581-0
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for ANANTHA. Searches returned only general groundnut resistance information (e.g., https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3580887/), not tied to this line.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The 2023 drought hot-spot multi-location study above is the only trial record found for ANANTHA -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10404259. Maturity duration, recommended sowing dates and fertiliser or spacing recommendations: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found specific to ANANTHA's parentage or markers. The parentage field in that study table is "--" (not recorded) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10404259. General ICRISAT/NARS genomic-tool reviews exist (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4794498/), but they do not mention ANANTHA.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder, developing institution and station: No evidence found. The 2010 release year and "Andhra Pradesh" adoption appear in the study table, but the source gives no developer -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10404259. The name "Ananth" in the Krishikosh results refers to a researcher author, not this variety -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/7ab871a2-058d-42e9-8452-1eb784453455/content

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder, institute, email, phone or postal contact for ANANTHA was found. I did not find an institute contact page for its developer, so I am not supplying one.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not captured in search results (2023). Integrating data from asymmetric multi-models can identify drought-resistant groundnut genotypes for drought hot-spot locations. Scientific Reports -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-38581-0 (mirror: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10404259; DOI not captured, likely 10.1038/s41598-023-38581-0 from the URL)
No other ANANTHA-specific peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, or KrishiKosh thesis was found. The KrishiKosh hits are unrelated theses on other groundnut genotypes -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/39f58bd7-d43c-42b0-9e58-d60604b39cc8/content

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for ANANTHA or Ananth from Seednet, NSC, a State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealers. The AP Seeds Corporation listings found cover K-6, TCGS 1694 and Kadiri Lepakshi, not ANANTHA -- https://www.deccanchronicle.com/news/groundnut-seed-distribution-in-anantapur-district-from-may-24-894786 and https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/seeds-corporation-to-distribute-subsidised-groundnut-seed/

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Andhra Pradesh, listed as the area of adoption in the drought hot-spot study table (the source spells it "Andhra Pradeh") -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10404259. The CSC field "Not specified" should be updated with this, but it is not an official notification.

Search budget: 4 web_search calls were used (the maximum allowed). The first call returned no ANANTHA-specific breeder or seed data, so the breeder, contact and seed-availability headings rest on no direct evidence.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Aparajita (Clitoria ternatea), JGCT-2013-3 (Titli)

Search note: 4 web_search queries were run, the maximum allowed. Results were dominated by herbal-medicine pages, and none of them documented this variety's release. Every heading below reports what was found or that nothing was found. Name note: "Aparajita" is the CSC release-minute name and "Aprajita" is the Seednet name. The evidence below refers to the plant species or to unrelated Aparajita material unless stated otherwise. No result mentioned JGCT-2013-3 or Titli.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for the cultivar. Only a tissue-culture study on acid stress in butterfly pea was returned, and it does not concern this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376057823_Tolerance_Level_of_Butterfly_Pea_Clitoria_ternatea_L_to_Stress_Acidity_Through_Tissue_Culture_Technique

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for multi-location or AICRP trials of this variety. The only related ICAR material is a DMAPR, Anand (Gujarat) report on flower-colour and petal-type polymorphism in Aparajita, which describes accession variation and does not report yield or trial performance. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JMAP/article/view/25996

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies of this variety. The flower-colour polymorphism paper above is the closest morphological-variation study. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JMAP/article/view/25996

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder name, developing scientist, or ICAR-IGFRI variety page was found. The input record names ICAR-IGFRI, Jhansi as the institution, but no search result confirmed that attribution. The results that mention Aparajita came from DMAPR Anand and ICAR-CTCRI Thiruvananthapuram, which are not the listed institution. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/61419

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, or postal address appeared in the results. The IGFRI contact page was not retrieved and should be checked directly before the record is finalised.

Open Access Journal of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants, 3, 212-214 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JMAP/article/view/25996 (The ICAR listing gives 2013 as the year and the citing paper gives 2012. The year needs verification.)

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No external source confirmed the list. The only support is the input record: Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, south Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat. This is unverified.

DATA-QUALITY FLAGS FOR REVIEWER
1. The Seednet record lists this variety under "BHINDI (OKRA)", which conflicts with the crop (Clitoria ternatea). This is probably a crop-mapping error on the portal and should be corrected or confirmed on seednet.gov.in.

heat.details: The 'Bhushan' genotype, alongside other walnut varieties (e.g., CITH-W-1, CITHW-6, CITH-W-8, CITH-W-10), has demonstrated a greater tolerance to heat stress. It is also noted for its ability to store water, a trait contributing to stress resilience.

flood.details: No specific evidence directly links 'Bhushan' walnut to flood tolerance or waterlogging tolerance. Information found relates to other crops like soybean or wheat, or general research by individuals named 'Bhushan'.

submergence.details: No specific evidence directly links 'Bhushan' walnut to submergence tolerance. Mentions of submergence tolerance in the search results pertain to rice or general anaerobic stress studies, not this walnut variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Yellow vein mosaic disease (YVMV): GAO-5 is described as resistant to YVMV compared with the checks GO 2 and Pusa Sawani. This is evidence for GAO-5 (the Seednet name), not confirmed for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52. The GAO-5 release area is described as the YVMV-prone area of Gujarat. No other disease data were found.

pest_resistance.summary: Sucking pests: GAO-5 is reported to have a low population of sucking pests compared with the checks GO 2 and Pusa Sawani. This is the only pest evidence found, it applies to GAO-5 rather than GAO 7 or AOL 12-52, and no data were found for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52.

agronomic_details.yield: Not available for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52. For GAO-5, the release notice reports an average yield of 141 q/ha, with green fruit yield 36% and 56% higher than the checks GO 2 and Pusa Sawani respectively.
agronomic_details.stability: AOL-12-52 x GJO-3 (a hybrid combination, not the variety itself) showed above-average stability in a multi-environment AMMI study. No stability data were found for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52 alone.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The GAO-5 release is for the YVMV-prone area of Gujarat. The input states (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Odisha) are not supported by any evidence in the digest for this variety. The Chhattisgarh, Orissa and Andhra Pradesh list found in the search belongs to Shitla Jayoti, a different variety.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) GAO-5 release trial: average yield of 141 q/ha reported in the release notice. (2) GAO-5 versus checks: 36% higher green fruit yield than GO 2 and 56% higher than Pusa Sawani. (3) AOL-12-52 general combining ability: significant and desirable GCA for yield per plant and related traits in a South Gujarat study. (4) Line x tester study: AOL-12-52 used as a parent, with significant general and specific combining ability effects. (5) AOL-12-52 x GJO-3 multi-environment AMMI trial: above-average stability. (6) Silicic acid foliar-spray field trial at the Main Vegetable Research Station, Anand, in which GAO-5 was used as a check cultivar. No trial was found that tests GAO 7 directly.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST**

**Name check:** I searched both names. The evidence covers Gujarat Anand Okra-5 (GAO-5), the Seednet name. I found no release record for "AOL 12-52 Gujarat Anand Okra 7 (GAO 7)" or its release year. AOL 12-52 appears only as a parent in hybrid studies. The input's year_of_release ("NaT") is not a valid date and could not be verified.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- GAO-5 is described as resistant to yellow vein mosaic disease (YVMV) compared with checks -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-okra-5-0
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for GAO-5 or AOL 12-52 were found. The heat-tolerance claims I found refer to the hybrid Anand Kranti, not this variety -- https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- GAO-5 is reported to have a low population of sucking pests and to be resistant to YVMV compared with the checks GO 2 and Pusa Sawani -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-okra-5-0
- For GAO-5 this is the only pest or disease evidence found. No data were found for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- GAO-5 reported an average yield of 141 q/ha in its release notice and gave 36% and 56% higher green fruit yield than the checks GO 2 and Pusa Sawani -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-okra-5-0
- AOL-12-52 showed significant and desirable general combining ability for yield per plant and related traits in a South Gujarat study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333508586_Combining_ability_studies_for_various_horticultural_traits_in_okra_Abelmoschus_esculentus_L_Moench_under_South-Gujarat_conditions
- AOL-12-52 x GJO-3 showed above-average stability in a multi-environment AMMI study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323937760_Genotype_x_Environment_Interaction_and_Stability_Analysis_for_Earliness_Seed_Yield_and_Fruit_Yield_in_Okra_Using_the_Additive_Main_Effect_and_Multiplicative_Interaction_AMMI
- GAO-5 was used as a check cultivar in a silicic acid foliar-spray field trial at the Main Vegetable Research Station, Anand -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue2/PartZ/8-2-306-538.pdf

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- AOL-12-52 is listed as a parent in a line x tester combining-ability study, with significant general and specific combining ability effects -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333508586_Combining_ability_studies_for_various_horticultural_traits_in_okra_Abelmoschus_esculentus_L_Moench_under_South-Gujarat_conditions
- A 2026-dated paper from AAU's Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding (Pravallika et al.) covers DNA markers and hybrid performance in okra. It does not name GAO 7 in the snippet, so its link to this variety is unconfirmed -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41798224/
- No QTL or marker study specific to GAO 7, AOL 12-52 or GAO-5 was found.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- The developing institution is Anand Agricultural University (AAU), Anand, Gujarat. The GAO-5 release entry is held by the Main Vegetable Research Station, Anand -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
- Scientists named in AAU okra work are V. I. Joshi and K. B. Kathiria. Their paper is on Anand Komal (GAO 8), not GAO 7 or AOL 12-52 -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/view/4901
- No lead breeder was named for GAO 7 or AOL 12-52.

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- Main Vegetable Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Anand 388110, Gujarat. The office phone number was truncated in the search result and could not be recovered -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
- Anand Agricultural University general site (institute-level contact): https://www.aau.in
- No breeder email or phone was found.

**PUBLICATIONS**
- Joshi, V. I., and Kathiria, K. B. et al. (2024). Assessing High-yielding Variety Anand Komal for Dual-season Cultivation of Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus L. Moench) in Middle Gujarat Agro Climatic Condition. International Journal of Plant & Soil Science -- https://doi.org/10.9734/ijpss/2024/v36i84901 (full author list not confirmed)
- Pravallika, P. L. N., Pandya, M. P., Sakure, A., Joshi, R., and Kumar, S. (year not shown). Integrating nutrient profiling, biochemical traits, and DNA markers for yield improvement in Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus). PubMed -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41798224/
- Combining ability studies for various horticultural traits in okra under South-Gujarat conditions (authors and year not confirmed). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333508586_Combining_ability_studies_for_various_horticultural_traits_in_okra_Abelmoschus_esculentus_L_Moench_under_South-Gujarat_conditions
- Genotype x Environment Interaction and Stability Analysis for Earliness, Seed Yield and Fruit Yield in Okra Using AMMI (authors and year not confirmed). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323937760_Genotype_x_Environment_Interaction_and_Stability_Analysis_for_Earliness_Seed_Yield_and_Fruit_Yield_in_Okra_Using_the_Additive_Main_Effect_and_Multiplicative_Interaction_AMMI
- Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 2019; 8(2): 1552-1558 (silicic acid trial using GAO 5). Phytojournal -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue2/PartZ/8-2-306-538.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP/ICAR report specific to GAO 7 was found.

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- Gujarat Farm Seeds Private Limited, 101 Jemsons House, Near Laxmi Cinema, Cross Roads, Anand 388001 (private dealer). Listed as a seller of okra seed; GAO-5 or GAO 7 is not named. Managing Director listed as Sagar Shah -- https://www.tradeindia.com/gujarat-farm-seeds-private-limited-35275535/
- The indiamart listing offers Komal Gold okra seed; it is not identified as GAO-5 or GAO 7 -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/okra-bhindi-seeds-komal-gold-21389526755.html
- AAU offers the hybrid Anand Kranti at a subsidised rate. This is not GAO 7 -- https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/
- No Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation or KVK listing for GAO-5 or GAO 7 was found. Seednet was not directly searched.

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- GAO-5 was released for the YVMV-prone area of Gujarat -- https://aau.in/gujarat-anand-okra-5-0
- The GAO-5 release list gives 2011 (42nd SSSC) -- https://aau.in/variety_released
- The AAU crop-variety list gives notification 421/2016 dated 29/12/2016 for GAO-5. This conflicts with the 2011 release year and needs checking -- https://aau.in/college-menu/251/236
- The states in the input (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Orissa) are not supported by any evidence for this variety. The Chhattisgarh/Orissa/Andhra Pradesh list I found is for Shitla Jayoti, a different variety -- https://www.vantikatech.com/2020/02/improved-varieties-of-okra-bhindi.html?m=1

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Okra / Gujarat Okra-2 (okra, Abelmoschus esculentus)

Search status: the search budget ran out after 4 queries, so several headings rest on thin evidence. The snippets I could read were short, and I did not open the full pages.

Name note: the CSC name is "Gujarat Okra" and the Seednet name is "Gujarat Okra-2". The only source I found calls the material "Gujarat Okra Hybrid-2 (GOH-2)", so it is unclear whether that refers to the same entry. Findings below are attributed to the name used in each source.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched, but no stress-tolerance data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) appeared for Gujarat Okra or Gujarat Okra-2.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Searched, but no disease or pest resistance data appeared.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Partial. A Junagadh University (JAU) characteristics document lists "Gujarat Okra Hybrid-2 (GOH-2)" and describes its pods as green, tender and attractive. No maturity, yield or trial data was found in the snippet. -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//vrs_imp_charactristics_of_varities_20260512_1553.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Searched, but no parentage, hybrid cross details or marker studies were found. The input record also gives parentage as "Not specified".

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial. The JAU Vegetable Research Station, Junagadh, is listed as a JAU research unit alongside the Research, Training & Testing Centre (RTTC) and Cotton Research Station, Khapat. No breeder or scientist name was found. -- http://www.jau.in/index.php/2-init-content/research/103-vegetable-research-station

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only. No breeder contact was found. The station page confirms the station's name and location (Junagadh) but no email, phone or postal address appeared in the snippet. Obtain these from the JAU contact page or the Vegetable Research Station page at the URL above.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Okra Hybrid 205 (okra)

Search budget note: the 4-search limit was reached. Searches 1 and 4 used the same query, so the topic 3 research query ran once and the seed query was not run separately. Topics with no hits are marked "No evidence found" below. The release-minutes name and the Seednet name were both checked. The Seednet name "Gujarat Okra Hybrid-2" appears only in a Junagadh (JAU) document, which describes a different hybrid (GOH 2), so no Seednet evidence for variety code 205 was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Plant is short-statured with short internodes, and the reduced height is described as making it less prone to wind damage -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-okra-hybrid-205-anand-kranti ; https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/
- Heat tolerance up to about 40 °C was reported by AAU scientists in controlled and field conditions. This comes from a news article, not an official AAU release -- https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/
- Drought, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Field prevalence of yellow vein mosaic disease and enation leaf curl disease was reported as lower than in the checks GJOH 4, GAO 5 and Pusa Sawani -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Jassid, whitefly and shoot and fruit borer damage was reported as lower than in the same checks -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Formal resistance rating for YVMV or OLCV: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Release year 2023; area of release Gujarat, kharif season, irrigated condition; average yield 140 q/ha; originating centre MVRS, Anand -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-okra-hybrid-205-anand-kranti ; https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Fruit yield was 20.00, 23.12 and 30.08 per cent higher than GJOH 4, GAO 5 and Pusa Sawani across Gujarat -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- In middle Gujarat, yield was 30.59, 38.02 and 55.70 per cent higher than the same checks, at a mean of 163 q/ha -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Fruits are dark green, tender and smooth with a narrow acute apex; leaf margins are strongly serrated -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-okra-hybrid-205-anand-kranti
- Higher mucilage (28.51 g/kg) and chlorophyll-a (0.400 mg/g) than the checks -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-detail/27577
- Maturity, sowing and seed rate for this hybrid: No evidence found
- Alternative names reported in news: "Anand Kranti" and "Gujarat Shankar Bhinda 205"; reported yield 16,500 kg/ha -- https://urbanacres.in/revolutionary-okra-variety-boosts-gujarat-yield/

GENETICS AND QTL:
- Parentage conflict: the parentage supplied in the record (JNDOH-02-2 from KS-404 x HRB-108-2) matches the JAU hybrid "Gujarat Okra Hybrid 2 (GOH 2)", not the AAU hybrid 205. Treat the parentage as unverified for variety 205 -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/FVegetableCropsVR.pdf

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Makhana / Maana (Bhindi, Okra)

Search status: the web_search tool returned "Server tool use limit exceeded" partway through my run, after the first query and some repeated calls. The digest below therefore rests on one usable result set, and the remaining topics were not searched successfully. Some of the headings below are unsupported for that reason.

Name check: "Makhana" is the common name for fox nut (Euryale ferox), an aquatic seed crop, not okra. The Seednet name "Maana" under BHINDI (OKRA) is the only name that fits the crop listed. The CSC name and the Seednet name may refer to different things, and I did not find evidence that resolves this.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The search returned okra pages for other varieties (Kashi Ageti, Shitla Jyoti, Kashi Satdhari) but nothing on "Maana" or "Makhana" stress traits. -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/varieties/okra

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The only okra variety page returned names other varieties (Kashi Ageti is tolerant to leaf miner and pod borer), which I am not attributing to Maana. -- https://iivr.icar.gov.in/varieties/okra

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Not searched successfully.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Not searched successfully.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The ICAR-IIVR okra page lists varieties but gives no breeder or institution entry for "Maana". A second query for breeder/institute was not returned.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder or institute contact was retrieved. The ICAR-IIVR page (https://iivr.icar.gov.in/varieties/okra) is the closest official source but gave no contact details in the content I saw.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. Not searched successfully.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Not searched successfully.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for "Maana". The ICAR-IIVR page lists recommended states only for other okra varieties, such as Kashi Ageti (Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Bihar, Jharkhand). Those are not attributed to Maana.

Next steps: rerun the Maana (okra) searches for the variety-release, breeder, research and seed-availability topics once the search tool is available again. Check seednet.gov.in and iivr.icar.gov.in for "Maana" directly, and check whether a fox nut (Makhana) variety record exists in the CSC minutes, which would be a separate crop.

disease_resistance.summary: NBH-180 is not reported as resistant to any disease. The SKUAST-J AICRP (Vegetable Crops) okra resistant trial evaluated eight entries, with Arka Anamika and NBH-180 as checks. The retrieved snippets do not give disease reaction scores for NBH-180. The ResearchGate review lists NBH-180 among 13 okra hybrids, but the 'moderately tolerant to YVMD and OELCD' note appears next to an IIVR germplasm entry, not NBH-180.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance data for NBH-180 found in the results.

agronomic_details.yield: In a 2019 varietal evaluation (Chemical Science/Chemi Journal), NBH-180 yielded 153.74 q/ha. This was statistically at par with the top hybrid NBH-225 (166.83 q/ha) and Mahabeej-333 (160.49 q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not assessed across environments in the retrieved material. NBH-180 is repeatedly used as a check or comparator, including in AICRP trials at SKUAST-J and evaluations at BUAT, which suggests it is a benchmark hybrid.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The recommended states span peninsular, central and eastern India (tropical and sub-tropical regions). No agro-climatic zone details found in the results.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: Used as a check with Arka Anamika in the AICRP okra resistant trial at SKUAST-J (2016-17). Evaluated alongside Mona-002, VNR-999 and DOV-1 in BUAT trials that recorded days to first flowering and related traits. Compared in a 2019 hybrid/variety evaluation, where it ranked among the top yielders.
