search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIANT NOTE: The record gives "SG 1 White Long" as the release-minutes name and "White long" as the Seednet name. The crop is blackgram in the record but BITTER GOURD on Seednet. None of the four searches returned a page naming this variety for either crop. The only "SG 1" hit is a snake gourd variety, which is a different crop. Under the strict-relevance rule, every heading below is "No evidence found" unless noted.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches for "SG 1 White Long" with blackgram or bitter gourd returned only other varieties (blackgram T 9, CO 5, MDU 1, VBN series; bitter gourd CO 1, Coimbatore Long White, MDU 1, Priyanka, Priya). None of these is this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Blackgram pages on yellow mosaic and pod borer resistance concern other releases (e.g., MDU 1, https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/2014/Blackgram.pdf). Those are not this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Nothing on duration, yield, or trials for SG 1 White Long. Bitter gourd yield tables list other varieties (https://subsistencefarming.in/en/bitter-gourd-farming/). Those are not this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The bitter gourd QTL and genome papers concern other lines or accessions (e.g., DBGy-201 × Pusa Do Mausami, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-021-83548-8). They do not name this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the breeder of SG 1 White Long. The record's institution is Vegetable Research Station, Palur (TNAU). TNAU's Palur station page lists released varieties, but the only "SG 1" entry is SNAKE GOURD – PLR (SG) 1, a pureline from Sathipattu local, released 2007 (https://tnau.ac.in/site/vrs-palur/varieties-released/). That is a different crop and year, so it is not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only, not a breeder contact, and the source does not name this variety. Vegetable Research Station, Naduveerpattu, Palur-607102, Cuddalore (Dt.); phone 04142-75222(O); email hrspalur@tnau.ac.in (https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/seedavailability12.03.2019.pdf). The same email and phone appear in https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf. No named breeder or scientist was found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. Theses and papers returned concern other bitter gourd or blackgram material (e.g., Devadas 1993 PhD thesis on bitter gourd F1 hybrids, TNAU, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373268467_Evaluation_of_F1_Hybrids_in_Bitter_Gourd_Momordica_charantia_L_for_Yield_and_Quality). None names SG 1 White Long.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for this variety. TNAU seed stock lists include snake gourd PLR (SG) 1 at VRS Palur and bitter gourd CO 1, but neither is this variety (https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/TNAU%20-%20Seed%20stock%20position%20as%20on%2002.09.2022%20-%20English.pdf). No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, or dealer listing was found for SG 1 White Long.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. "Not specified" in the record, and no source gave a recommended state for this variety.

Searches run: 4 (blackgram variety; bitter gourd variety/breeder; bitter gourd research; VRS Palur seed and contact). Verification needed: the TNAU Palur release list, the TNAU release notification for 2015, and the CSC minutes should be checked directly to confirm whether "SG 1 White Long" exists and which crop it belongs to.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Tarun (sesame; variety code CST 2001-3)

Search limit reached: the 4-search budget was used up, and a 5th call was refused by the tool. Results below come only from the four searches that ran. Where a heading has no supporting evidence, I say so.

Name note: variety_name is "Tarun" (CSC minutes) and seednet_variety_name is "tarun" (Seednet). None of the search results tied either name to a specific record, so I cannot say which name any evidence refers to. The Seednet crop field reads "BITTER GOURD", which conflicts with the sesame crop in the record. This needs checking on the portal before the record is finalised.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no Tarun-specific stress data.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no Tarun-specific resistance data.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The searches returned no Tarun-specific yield, maturity or trial data.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The one sesame breeding result (Springer chapter on sesame breeding) covers general sesame genetics and does not mention Tarun or CST 2001-3. Source: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23265-8_15

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. Parentage, developing institution, station and year of release are all unrecorded. Possible starting point (not confirmed to list Tarun): DOD sesame notification table, https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, institute email, phone or address appeared in the results. The DOD page above is an official ICAR-linked (Ministry of Agriculture) source that may carry a contact page, but I did not verify one. Recommend checking the DOD and Directorate of Oilseeds Research contact pages directly.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI mentioning Tarun or CST 2001-3 was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The NSC/SSC/KVK/SAU/dealer search returned only generic sesame production pages from outside India (for example NCSU, https://content.ces.ncsu.edu/sesame-production-fact-sheet), which are not relevant.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for Tarun. The DOD page (https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx) has a state-wise table of sesame varieties notified 2008–2019 and is the right place to check whether Tarun appears. I could not confirm this from the snippets returned.

Next steps: (1) Check the DOD state-wise notification table for "Tarun" and its release year and centre. (2) Confirm the Seednet crop mapping (sesame vs bitter gourd) on seednet.gov.in. (3) Search KrishiKosh and AICRP Sesame & Niger reports for "Tarun" or "CST 2001-3" in a later session.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I could not complete the evidence digest because the search tool failed. Here is what happened and what is still usable.

**What happened**
- My first code run issued four web_search calls (variety, breeder, research, seed availability). The script then crashed while printing the results, so I did not see any returned content.
- Every later search attempt returned "Server tool use limit exceeded," so I could not re-run or read them.
- I therefore have no sourced findings, and I have not checked any URL, DOI, contact, or seed dealer. I am not writing "No evidence found" for any heading, because the searches were run but their results were never read.

**Record data supplied in the request (unverified, not from search)**
- Variety name (CSC minutes): AAU SPC 101 (AAU SHN Motor 01)
- Seednet name: AAU SPC 101 (AAU SHN Motor 01) (Xeuti); Seednet lists the crop as BLACK GRAM (URD BEAN), which conflicts with the fieldpea crop in the request and needs checking on the portal.
- Variety code: AAU SHN Motor 01
- Institution: Assam Agricultural University, Shillongani
- Year of release: 2023 (2023-05-02 in the record)
- Recommended state: Assam
- Parentage: HUDP 15 × HFP 1016. HUDP 15 is attributed to BHU Varanasi (rabi field pea); HFP 1016 is attributed to CCS HAU Hisar.

**Still needed (to be filled once search works)**
- STRESS TOLERANCE, DISEASE AND PEST, AGRONOMY AND TRIALS, GENETICS AND QTL, PUBLICATIONS, SEED AVAILABILITY, RECOMMENDED STATES: all unsearched results.
- BREEDER AND INSTITUTION and CONTACT DETAILS: the breeder's name and AAU contact details are unknown. I have not invented any.

**Suggested manual checks**
- seednet.gov.in: confirm the crop label (fieldpea vs. black gram) and the notification details.
- AAU (Assam Agricultural University) and its Shillongani research station website, for breeder names and official contacts.
- ICAR/AICRP on Food Legumes reports, and KrishiKosh (krishikosh.egranth.ac.in), for trial data and theses.
- Assam state seed agencies, KVKs, and SAU seed sales counters for availability.

Once the search tool is available again, I can rerun the four searches (one per topic) and produce the full digest with cited findings.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: ADT 53 (rice)
Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed. The search tool returned no results for "ADT-5" or for the Seednet name, so every finding below refers to the name "ADT 53" (release-minute name, variety code AD07073/IET 23955).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to ADT 53. The only trait recorded is a non-lodging, compact plant type with well-exerted panicles -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1094

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to ADT 53. The Tamil Nadu advisory lists ADT 53 as a recommended kuruvai variety but gives no resistance data -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/tps-5-rice-variety?cat=tamilnadu-news

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Released 2019 by TNAU as a short-duration culture of 110-115 days (Pushpa et al., EJPB 2020) -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3314
-- Mean grain yield of 6334 kg/ha across 242 trials, 9.4% above ADT 43 (5788 kg/ha, 112 days) and 14.0% above CO 51 (5562 kg/ha, 112 days) -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3314
-- TNAU Aduthurai station page gives duration 105-110 days, yield 6334 kg/ha, and "alternate for ADT 43" -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-aduthurai/varieties-released/
-- Press summaries report milling 62% and head rice 65%, with zinc and iron content noted; the variety is described as suited to parboiling as an alternative to ADT 43 -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/new-paddy-variety ; https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/tps-5-rice-variety?cat=tamilnadu-news
-- Seed vigour study lists ADT 53 among 12 rice varieties with high seed vigour potential -- https://journalijecc.com/index.php/IJECC/article/view/3332
-- Tamil Nadu crop practice guide lists ADT 53 for Kuruvai (June-July) sowing in Tiruchirappalli and for Sornavari/Navarai seasons in northeastern districts -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/01_Rice.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- Pedigree-derived from the cross ADT 43 / JGL 384 (Pushpa et al., EJPB 2020) -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1094
-- CONFLICT: the supplied parentage ("pureline selection from Kanpur blackgram") is not supported by this source and appears to be wrong for a rice variety. No QTL or marker study was found -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1094

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Tamil Nadu Rice Research Institute (TRRI), Aduthurai, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-aduthurai/varieties-released/
-- Contributing authors (EJPB 2020): R. Pushpa, R. Saraswathi, D. Sassikumar, R. Chandirakala, R. Suresh, B. Meenakumari, K. Chozan, S. Suresh, A. Karthikeyan, V. Ravi. The paper does not state which of these is the lead breeder -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2020.1101.018
-- No evidence found for a named lead breeder in the institute's variety list -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/rrs-aduthurai/varieties-released/

CONTACT DETAILS -- Breeder contact: No evidence found.
-- Institute: No evidence found for a TRRI Aduthurai postal address, phone or email in the search results.
-- TNAU Seed Centre, Coimbatore: Director (Seeds), Seed Centre, TNAU, Coimbatore 641 003. Email rice@tnau.ac.in appears in the rice-section contact of the seed stock list (dated 31.07.2021) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
-- Seed-stock list also names: Agricultural Research Station, Paramakudi, 04564-222139; KVK Tindivanam, 04147-250001 / 90470 42517, kvktvm@tnau.ac.in; Rice Research Station, Tirur (phone not captured) -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
Pushpa, R., Saraswathi, R., Sassikumar, D., Chandirakala, R., Suresh, R., Meenakumari, B., Chozan, K., Suresh, S., Karthikeyan, A., & Ravi, V. (2020). ADT 53 - Short duration high yielding fine grain rice variety for Kuruvai/Kodai seasons of Tamil Nadu. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding, 11(1), 103-109 -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2020.1101.018 ; https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/EJPB/article/view/3314
Authors not confirmed (2024 or later, per file name) (n.d.). Characterization and Identification of Recent Rice varieties through Chemo-Taxonomical Test. Journal not confirmed -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/Characterization-and-Identification-of-Recent-Rice-varieties-through-Chemo-Taxonomical-Test-N-Aarthi-49.pdf (ADT-53 is one of ten rice varieties tested; authors not verified from the page text)
Authors not confirmed (n.d.). Assessing the Potential Seed Vigor of Rice Varieties. International Journal of Environment and Climate Change -- https://journalijecc.com/index.php/IJECC/article/view/3332
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report entry, or multi-location trial report naming ADT 53 was found in the results.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- TNAU Seed Centre stock position (31.07.2021, now outdated): ADT 53 listed at several locations, including 6,300 kg at Dept. of Seed Science & Technology, 2,430 at a KVK, 1,675 at KVK Tindivanam, 960 at Rice Research Station Tirur, 670 at ARS Paramakudi. Stock is subject to availability at enquiry -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
-- No evidence found for current NSC, State Seed Corporation or private dealer listings.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Tamil Nadu only. Kuruvai/Kodai in delta districts, and Sornavari/Navarai in other districts -- https://www.tnpscthervupettagam.com/currentaffairs-detail/new-paddy-variety ; https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/01_Rice.pdf

Note: Seednet name "ADT-5" was not searched separately. Under the Seednet name "ADT-5" (black gram, URD bean), no evidence was found for ADT 53 rice, and any black gram record should be treated as a different crop.

heat.details: No information on heat tolerance for ADT 56 rice is provided in the search results. Information on heat stress tolerance is present for other crops like moth bean and black gram, but not for this specific rice variety.

drought.details: Tolerant to moisture stress and considered drought tolerant. It can be suitable for dry land ecosystems, though protective life-saving irrigation may be required under severe stress. Morphological characterization indicates narrow leaves, which have been observed to be drought tolerant in most cases.

heat.details: While studies on the effect of temperature on urdbean phenological behavior involving ADT-6 exist, specific heat tolerance levels for ADT 6 are not detailed.

salinity.details: Tolerant to salt affected soils and salinity. ADT 6 has been included in studies investigating black gram genotypes under salinity stress at the vegetative stage.

flood.details: General information states urdbean has more tolerance to water logging conditions than mungbean, but specific flood tolerance for ADT 6 is not provided.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV/YMV), Urdbean Leaf Crinkle Virus (LCV), Leaf Curl Virus (LCV), and Stem Necrosis. Moderately resistant to Anthracnose and Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB). It is also known to be tolerant to root-knot nematode.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant to stem fly and shows moderate resistance to pod borer. It is also tolerant to root knot nematode.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield ranges from 655 kg/ha (6.55 q/ha) to 7-8 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Information on stability across diverse environments is not explicitly provided, but its suitability for rice fallow conditions across multiple states suggests adaptability within this specific cropping system.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Highly suitable for rice fallow conditions, particularly for the December-January season in the Cauvery Delta Zone of Tamil Nadu. It is also advised for sowing in the Chithiraipattam (Summer Irrigated) season in districts of Tamil Nadu including Thanjavur, Thiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Cuddalore, Villupuram, Tiruchirappalli, and Perambalur. It is also practiced in rice fallow systems in Odisha, West Bengal, and Chhattisgarh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Characterized by narrow leaves and pubescence.
agronomic_details.field_trials: ADT 6 has been included in various field trials and experiments, including those testing black gram varieties under different irrigation regimes and in FRBD design experiments for Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus resistance.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: ADT 6 was included in studies for morphological characterization and genetic diversity. It exhibits narrow leaves, which are associated with drought tolerance. It is also used in studies to investigate black gram genotypes under salinity stress.

disease_resistance.summary: DBGV-5 was used as a local check variety in field trials for Yellow Mosaic Disease (YMD) screening under natural conditions. It was not listed among the cultivars exhibiting resistance to YMD (Pratap urd-1, Uttara, PU-31, IPU-2-43), implying susceptibility or a lack of strong resistance (Result 5). DBGV-5 has also been utilized as a parent (LGB 752 × DBGV 5) in crosses to unravel the inheritance of Powdery Mildew Disease (PMD) resistance in blackgram, with F2 populations showing Mendelian segregation patterns for resistance (Result 7). However, its specific resistance level to PMD is not explicitly stated.

agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Erect and determinate growth habit, ovate leaf shape, black non-hairy smooth pods, and large seeds (Original Data). It is also resistant to lodging and shattering (Original Data). It has been identified as an early flowering type (Result 8).

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: The inheritance of Powdery Mildew Disease (PMD) resistance involving DBGV-5 as a parent (LGB 752 × DBGV 5) showed F1 resistance and F2 populations segregating in a 9:3:3:1 ratio, indicating significant Mendelian inheritance patterns for PMD resistance (Result 7). No specific QTLs are identified.

disease_resistance.summary: Powdery mildew (Erysiphe polygoni): BDU-12 was reported as moderately resistant in a natural epiphytotic screen and listed among the moderately resistant genotypes. Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): in a 2018 summer screen at ARS Bidar, a row showed a score of 2 and an MR (moderately resistant) rating; the snippet is partly garbled, so this rating is not fully reliable. A companion MYMV screen (ResearchGate listing) names BDU-12, but its category placement is unclear. Cercospora leaf spot: no BDU-12 evidence found. The DU-1 (UAS Dharwad, 2013) entry is susceptible to cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew, but this is a separate line of evidence and is not confirmed to be BDU-12.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. A study of sucking pests (aphids, jassids) on blackgram at ARS Bidar evaluated seed dressings (imidacloprid, thiamethoxam) but does not name BDU-12, so no pest resistance evidence for BDU-12 was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources for BDU-12 per-hectare yield in a multi-location trial. CSC record lists average yield as Not Available. A diversity study ranks BDU-12 highly for grain yield per plant and grain yield per hectare, but no numeric values were reported in the digest. DU-1 national table figures (about 14-15 q/ha) refer to the Dharwad DU-1 and are not attributed to BDU-12.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Not found in searched sources for BDU-12 varietal adaptation. The ARS Bidar station is in Zone-1 (north-eastern transition zone) of Karnataka with a blackgram mandate; this describes the station location, not confirmed varietal adaptation.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not found in searched sources. CSC record lists maturity_days as Not Available. The DU-1 duration (80-85 days) is for the Dharwad DU-1 and is not confirmed for BDU-12.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BDU-12 (CSC name) / DU-1 (Seednet name), blackgram

Search note: four web_search queries were run (BDU-12 variety; BDU-12 breeder/Bidar institute; BDU-12 research papers; DU-1 Seednet). The search snippets gave no release notification, maturity, yield, or parentage for BDU-12, and no breeder names or contact details.

Name note: The evidence below refers to BDU-12 unless marked DU-1. The DU-1 items are a separate line of evidence. A 2013 UAS Dharwad release is also called DU-1, and it is not confirmed to be the same material as BDU-12.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- BDU-12 was reported as moderately resistant to powdery mildew (Erysiphe polygoni) in a natural epiphytotic screen, and was listed among the moderately resistant genotypes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298342748_Screening_of_blackgram_genotypes_under_natural_epiphytotic_condition_for_powdery_mildew_disease_resistance_Erysiphae_polygoni_DC
- The DU-1 (UAS Dharwad, 2013) entry is described as susceptible to cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for BDU-12 were found in the results.

DISEASE AND PEST
- BDU-12 appeared in a 2018 summer MYMV screen at ARS Bidar, with a row showing a score of 2 and an MR (moderately resistant) rating. The snippet is partly garbled, so the rating is not fully reliable -- http://www.plantarchives.org/article/9-%20Screening%20of%20Blackgram%20genotypes%20against%20Mungbean%20Yellow%20Mosaic%20Virus%20(MYMV)%20disease.pdf
- A companion MYMV screen (ResearchGate listing) names BDU-12 among genotypes in the screen, but its category placement is unclear -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396464324_SCREENING_OF_BLACKGRAM_GENOTYPES_AGAINST_MUNGBEAN_YELLOW_MOSAIC_VIRUS_MYMV_DISEASE
- Sucking pests (aphids, jassids) on blackgram at ARS Bidar were studied with seed dressings (imidacloprid, thiamethoxam). BDU-12 is not named -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue4/PartAD/8-4-298-864.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A genetic diversity study of blackgram quantitative traits ranked BDU-12 highly for pods per plant, pod length, grain yield per plant and grain yield per hectare. Year and trial details are not clear from the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/315459088_Genetic_diversity_analysis_in_blackgram_L_Hepper_based_on_quantitative_traits
- No BDU-12 maturity duration or yield per hectare in a multi-location trial was found. DU-1 is listed in a national state-release table with 80-85 day duration and about 14-15 q/ha yield, but this is the Dharwad DU-1, not confirmed as the same variety -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- A Bidar-based study of 2016-17 and 2017-18 kharif trials is about pest control, not varietal agronomy -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue4/PartAD/8-4-298-864.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker, or genetic-mapping study on BDU-12 was found. The only genetic material found is the diversity analysis above -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/315459088_Genetic_diversity_analysis_in_blackgram_L_Hepper_based_on_quantitative_traits

- The station is in Zone-1 (north-eastern transition zone) of Karnataka, with a mandate covering blackgram -- https://uasraichur.karnataka.gov.in/new-page/About+ARS+Bidar/en

drought.details: No search result reports drought reaction for Gujarat Urd 2 (GJU 1509). The only related statements are generic: Result 4 (dpd.gov.in Annual Report 2015-16) states that a variety should be tolerant to water stress conditions, and Result 3 notes that the pathogen is favoured under water stress. These are general recommendations, not variety-specific evidence.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance data for Gujarat Urd 2 were found in the search results. Result 41 (Technologies for Enhancing Crop Productivity in Dryland Areas) describes dryland conditions with high summer day temperatures but does not link them to this variety.

salinity.details: No variety-specific salinity data for Gujarat Urd 2 were found. Result 23 (NFSM Status Paper on Pulses 2018) states that black gram cannot be grown on alkaline and saline soils, which is a crop-level constraint. Result 24 mentions a salinity tolerance breeding programme in black gram without naming Gujarat Urd 2.

flood.details: No flood tolerance evidence was found for Gujarat Urd 2 or for the related varieties in the search results.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease reaction data for Gujarat Urd 2 (GJU 1509) were found; the original record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'. Related evidence concerns Gujarat Urd-1 (SDAU, 2004), a different variety, and should not be attributed to Gujarat Urd 2. For Gujarat Urd-1, the JAU Research Booklet 2019 reports resistance to MYMV, leaf curl and powdery mildew. The CABI Compendium lists Gujarat Urd-1 and Barkha among varieties resistant to Urdbean leaf crinkle virus (ULCV). The DPD Pulses 2015-16 and Retrospect 2008 tables list Gujarat Urd-1 as moderately resistant to powdery mildew.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest reaction data for Gujarat Urd 2 were found; the original record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'. The CABI Compendium refers to varieties resistant to Bemisia (whitefly, vector of MYMV), and Gujarat Urd-1 appears in that list, but Gujarat Urd 2 is not named. Attribution to Gujarat Urd 2 is not supported.

agronomic_details.yield: Not available for Gujarat Urd 2 (original record null). For Gujarat Urd-1, the JAU Research Booklet 2019 reports 939 kg/ha, which is not applicable to Gujarat Urd 2.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability data for Gujarat Urd 2 were found.

disease_resistance.summary: Yellow mosaic disease (YMD): resistant under natural field conditions (AAU release notice; IAUA release notice; AAU/AGRESCO records; Pulse Research Station recommendation listing describing YMD resistance with better seed quality). The paper states the variety was developed for YMD resistance because local checks T-9 and GU-1 are highly susceptible to yellow mosaic in short-duration crops. Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): listed as resistant in one national listing (dpd.gov.in table entry GUJARAT 2022 ANAND URDBEAN 4). A seed vendor listing also states resistance against yellow mosaic virus disease. No other disease resistance found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Searches used "Gujarat Anand Urdbean 4" (release-minutes name, also written GAU 4 / Shyamal). The Seednet name "Gujarat Urdbean 3 (GU-3: Anjani)" returned only a different blackgram variety from NAU Navsari (released 2020), so no evidence was kept for that name, and it is not attributed to this variety below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Resistant to yellow mosaic disease under natural field conditions; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Described as resistant to yellow mosaic disease (YMD) in the AAU release notice; no other stress tolerance stated -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Developed for YMD resistance because local checks T-9 and GU-1 are highly susceptible to yellow mosaic in short-duration crops -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety
- [Seednet name GU-3 Anjani] No evidence found for this variety

DISEASE AND PEST
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] YMD resistance reported in multiple AAU and AGRESCO records; no specific pest resistance found -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal ; https://aau.in/college-menu/507
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Resistant to yellow mosaic in the Pulse Research Station recommendation listing (2021 release, YMD resistant with better seed quality) -- https://aau.in/college-menu/507
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Listed as resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV) in one national listing -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf (search result 23-9 item; the table entry labelled GUJARAT 2022 ANAND URDBEAN 4)
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Seed vendor listing states resistance against yellow mosaic virus disease -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gau-4-shyamal/
- [Seednet name GU-3 Anjani] No evidence found for this variety

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Kharif seed yield 1005 kg/ha, 19.08% above T-9 and 23.92% above GU-1 in middle Gujarat -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Summer seed yield 864 kg/ha, 22.21% above T-9 and 23.42% above GU-1 in middle Gujarat -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Average yield 961 kg/ha across seasons; tested as JAUG 2 in trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Agronomic traits: semi-erect habit, medium maturity, hairy pods with 6-7 seeds, dull black seed -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Maturity conflict: AAU/AGRESCO record medium maturity (not in days); a vendor page gives 95-100 days and seed rate 7.5-8 kg/acre, which conflicts with the 65-75 day figure in the IAUA notice -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/gau-4-shyamal/ ; https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638218771313581530.pdf
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Proposed for summer and kharif recommendation to farmers of middle Gujarat at the AGRESCO meeting -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Quality: 24.66% protein, 55.58% carbohydrate, Fe 49.97, Zn 29.28 mg/kg -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-urdbean-4-shayamal

GENETICS AND QTL
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] DNA fingerprinting with SRAP markers against T-9 and GU-1 checks; no QTL or marker-trait mapping found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Pedigree conflict: the supplied parentage (T-9 x NU-00-161, made rabi 2011-12) is not found in any source; the paper says the variety was selected from germplasm GP No. 6 at ARS Jabugam -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- [GAU 4 / Shyamal] Developed through selection by Pulse Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Vadodara; released by the state variety release committee in 2021 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354004319_Study_about_GAU_4_A_New_High_Yielding_Ymv_Resistant_Urdbean_Variety

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME NOTE: Evidence below uses "Indira Urd Pratham" (CSC/release-table name) and "INDIRA URD PRATHAM (RU 03-14)" (Seednet name). Searches did not reach the Seednet portal. Where a source uses the code RU 03-14, the Seednet name is implied. A Gurudev listing uses "RU 07 08", which conflicts with RU 03-14.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to powdery mildew up to the podding stage, per the central release table, which records 2015 release by IGKV Raipur for Chhattisgarh kharif and summer -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found in the searches.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Listed as resistant to yellow mosaic and powdery mildew in an IGKV publication table (IGKV/Pub./T.bl./2014/18), which reads as one row, so the YMV claim needs checking -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Girijesh-Sharma/publication/339134315_Improved_Cultivation_Practices_for_Dry_Land_Crops_in_Bastar_Plateau_Agroclimatic_Zone/links/5e3fe2b2a6fdccd965930ca7/Improved-Cultivation-Practices-for-Dry-Land-Crops-in-Bastar-Plateau-Agroclimatic-Zone.pdf
- Powdery mildew resistance is also reported in a Pulses review and a DPD summer-pulses table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348801694_Challenges_in_Pulses_Productivity_and_Agronomic_Opportunities_for_Enhancing_Growth_and_Yield_in_Blackgram_Vigna_mungo_L_Hepper_A_Review ; http://www.dpd.gov.in/2.%20Summer%20Pulses%20(English).pdf
- Resistance to MYMV, bruchids, or other pests specific to this variety: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release-table yield 12-13 q/ha, 70-75 days -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- A private seller's description gives 12-14 q/ha and 70-75 days, which is a non-official source -- https://www.vantikatech.com/2020/04/high-yield-uradblack-gram-variety.html
- Raipur planting-geometry trial (kharif 2013) found Indira Urd Pratham gave the highest seed yield, stover yield and harvest index among four genotypes -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/issues/article_abstract.php?aid=7538&iid=224&jid=3
- Bilaspur integrated nutrient management trial (kharif 2021) used this variety -- https://www.ijcmas.com/11-10-2022/Surabhi%20Patre,%20et%20al.pdf
- Chhattisgarh cluster demonstrations (Bemetara, Bhatapara, Janjgir-Champa and other districts) list "Indira urd 1", not confirmed as this variety -- https://dpd.gov.in/Annual%20Report%20%202023-24%2014.01.2025.pdf
- Multi-location trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Combining-ability study (2020) found this variety the best general combiner for most traits and reported best crosses with it -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-3-2020/Neeraj%20Ankur%20Toppo,%20et%20al.pdf
- Variety-specific QTL or marker studies: No evidence found. The 2022 GWAS on 100 blackgram genotypes (Punjab) does not name this variety in the retrieved text -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9310006/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released by Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur, Chhattisgarh -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- IGKV is an autonomous research and education body in Chhattisgarh -- https://www.dairyknowledge.in/dkp/link/indira-gandhi-krishi-vishwavidyalaya-igkv
- Lead breeder name(s) and station: No evidence found.

- Breeder names, roles, emails, phones: No evidence found.
- Institute-level postal address, phone, email, or contact page URL for IGKV: No evidence found in the searches. Institute website not retrieved.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Kharif season in entire Madhya Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Kharif season (I)	15 Kg N + 40 Kg P2O5 + 20 Kg S per ha. (II)	Timely sown conditions. (III)	Seed rate 12-15 Kg/ha. (IV)	30 X 10 cm inter and intra-row spacing. (V)	Tolerant to pod shattering.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: The variety has market and distinct characters like dark green canopy, prolific bearing, black pods on maturity and medium bold seeds.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to yellow mosaic virus, cercospora leaf spot, anthracnose, leaf crinklr, powdery mildew, bacterial leaf blight and web blight.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Tolerant to major insect-pest under field conditions.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 10-15 kg N + 40-45 kg P2O5 + 20 kg S as basal application. 20 kg Zn can also be applied.

drought.details: Tolerant to moisture stress and combined stress of drought and salinity. It has been tested for drought stress conditions at the seedling stage through PEG (Polyethylene glycol).

heat.details: While general abiotic stress (including heat) research is mentioned alongside IPU 13-1, specific heat tolerance for this variety is not explicitly stated in the provided results.

salinity.details: Tolerant to combined stress of drought and salinity.

flood.details: While urdbean generally has tolerance to waterlogging, specific tolerance for IPU 13-1 to flood or waterlogging conditions is not explicitly stated.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV). Moderately resistant to Leaf Crinkle Virus (LCV), anthracnose, and Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB). It is part of the development of disease-resistant urdbean cultivars.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance for IPU 13-1 is detailed, though it is a modern variety, and Integrated Crop Management (ICM) is practiced with it.

drought.details: No evidence found. The 2019 genetic divergence study at RARS Lam (LBG 752 used as a check) and the 2023 Krishna district adoption study do not report drought stress scores for this variety. The DPD source describes the variety as photo-insensitive for sowing across seasons, which is not a drought measure.

heat.details: No evidence found. The 2019 genetic divergence study and the 2023 Krishna district adoption study do not report heat stress scores for this variety. CSC record notes suitability for summer sowing after rabi paddy, which is an adaptation statement and not a tolerance measure.

salinity.details: No evidence found. The 2019 genetic divergence study and the 2023 Krishna district adoption study do not report salinity scores for this variety.

flood.details: No evidence found. The 2019 genetic divergence study and the 2023 Krishna district adoption study do not report flood tolerance for this variety. CSC record states suitability for rice fallows, which is an adaptation statement and not a flood tolerance measure.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: listed as resistant to wilt in the DPD variety listing (main disease tolerance on record). Yellow mosaic virus (YMV): reported as resistant in three sources, namely the DPD listing, a ResearchGate review (described as whitefly-transmitted disease) and an indiacustomercare-independent exam resource that lists LBG 752 among resistant varieties with Pant Urd-19 and KU-96-3. CONFLICT: a KVK Garikapadu demonstration sheet calls LBG-752 'YMV susceptible' in one treatment, while another entry in the same sheet calls PU31/LBG 752 'highly resistant to YMV'. The conflict is unresolved in the digest. Parent LBG 402 (Prabhava) is described as wilt-resistant, which the digest suggests may help explain wilt tolerance in the cross.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod borer, whitefly, aphids and thrips: Not found in searched sources. No evidence specific to LBG 752. Whitefly is mentioned only as the vector of YMV, not as a resistance trait of this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Conflicting figures: potential yield 18-20 q/ha and duration 75-80 days (DPD listing); yield of about 2000 kg/ha in 75-80 days (ResearchGate review). The digest notes the difference and does not resolve it. CSC average_yield field is recorded only as 'Kg/Ha' with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for LBG 752. Multi-location or AICRP yield trial data: No evidence found. LBG-20 (a parent) was stable across environments for branch number in a dual-season trial, which is not a yield stability measure for LBG 752.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: sole crop and intercrop during kharif and rabi seasons; suitable for uplands and rice fallows; suitable for summer including rice fallow after rabi paddy. DPD listing: 'All Seasons' in Andhra Pradesh. Photo-insensitivity (DPD) conflicts with the CSC morphology description of the plant as photosensitive; the digest does not resolve this.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PHOTOSENSITIVE WITH OVAL-LANCEOLATE DARK GREEN FOLIAGE ; PODS ARE LONG WITH AND SPARSELY HAIRY ; SEEDS ARE MEDIUM BOLD AND SHINING BLACK IN COLOUR.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Farmer-level demonstration on YMV tolerance and IPM at Garikapadu (KVK), with LBG 752 as the farmers' practice variety; the sheet contains the conflicting YMV susceptible/highly resistant entries described under disease_resistance. (2) 2019 genetic divergence study at RARS Lam, with LBG 752 used as a check; no stress or yield scores reported for this variety. (3) 2023 Krishna district adoption study: adoption constraints identified as lack of knowledge, extension and timely seed availability; no yield results reported. (4) Multi-location or AICRP yield trial: No evidence found. (5) Dual-season trial of parent LBG-20 for branch number only; not a trial of LBG 752.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. The RAPD paper found covers other black gram lines (PU-31 and accessions), not LBG 752.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL, marker or RAPD study on LBG 752 was found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. The digest notes that the parent LBG 402 (Prabhava) is photo-sensitive and wilt-resistant, which may help explain the wilt tolerance of the cross; this is an inference and not a molecular finding. Parentage: LBG 402 x LBG 20, bred by pedigree method.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to yellow mosaic virus (YMV), described as whitefly-transmitted -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348801694_Challenges_in_Pulses_Productivity_and_Agronomic_Opportunities_for_Enhancing_Growth_and_Yield_in_Blackgram_Vigna_mungo_L_Hepper_A_Review

Multi-location or AICRP yield trial data for LBG 752: No evidence found

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Mash 1190 (variety_name, CSC minutes) / Mash 114 (seednet_variety_name, Seednet portal)

Name note: The Mash 1190 (SUG 1190) entry comes from the DPD central-release table. The Mash 114 entries come from the review, press and farm-advisory pages. I did not reach the Seednet portal, so no Seednet record was verified. No source I found explicitly links Mash 1190 and Mash 114 as the same entry. The input's parentage (Mash 338 x RBI-1) matches the Mash 114 descriptions below, so treat that link as unconfirmed.

Release year: the input says 2022-10-26, but the DPD table lists Mash 1190 with year 2023 -- https://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Mash 1190: No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance -- http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Mash 114: No stress-tolerance findings specific to this variety were found in the sources reviewed. The review covers black gram stresses in general and says breeding needs more diverse material for stress resistance -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Mash 1190: The DPD table gives a days-to-maturity and region for this entry but its resistance column is blank. No disease or pest resistance evidence found -- http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Mash 114: A 2006-era news report says it is resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV) -- https://www.oneindia.com/2006/06/15/pau-launches-two-new-high-yielding-maize-varieties-1150360564.html
- Mash 114: The farm-advice page says yellow mosaic is spread by whitefly. This is general crop advice, not variety-specific -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/mash-urd
- General context: major black gram threats include MYMV, urdbean leaf crinkle virus, Cercospora leaf spot, powdery mildew, and whitefly, bruchids and others -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Mash 1190: Listed as a PAU Ludhiana variety with 70-80 days to maturity. Its yield cell is not legible in the extracted text, so no yield figure is recorded -- http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Mash 114: Described as a dwarf, short-duration kharif variety ready in about 85 days, with 6-7 bold black seeds per pod and average yield of 3.7 q/acre -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/mash-urd
- Mash 114: Kharif seed rate 7-8 kg/acre; summer seed rate 19-20 kg/acre; seed treatment with a fungicide then Rhizobium at 2 g/kg -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/mash-urd
- Mash 114: Across 14 multi-location trials it out-yielded the check Mash 338 by 39.45% -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
- Mash 114: In PAU breeding trials it gave 45.2% more yield than Mash 338, and 20% more in agronomic trials (press report) -- https://www.oneindia.com/2006/06/15/pau-launches-two-new-high-yielding-maize-varieties-1150360564.html
- Mash 114: Its breeding-trial figure (45.2%) differs from the 39.45% multi-location figure above. The sources do not reconcile the two.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Mash 114: Developed from an interspecific cross between black gram and rice bean -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
- Mash 114: Listed among genotypes with high Fe content (97.9 ppm, Singh et al. 2017) in the nutritional-quality table -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/
- General context: rice-bean traits (pod number, seed weight and MYMD resistance) have been introgressed into black gram -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/
- General QTL study: MYMV resistance QTLs were identified and validated in blackgram. It is not specific to Mash 1190 or Mash 114 -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4459
- Mash 1190: No QTL or marker study found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Mash 1190: Originating centre is listed as PAU Ludhiana, under the ICAR AICRP on MULLaRP source -- http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Mash 114: Described as released by Punjab Agricultural University -- https://blackgram.in/
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found for either name. No institute breeder page was found.
- AICRP on MULLaRP coordinating centre: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4459

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Punjab Agricultural University, Ferozepur Road, PAU Gate 2, Ludhiana, Punjab 140004 (address as listed by NDDB) -- https://nddb.coop/farmer/animal-nutrition/state-wise-list-of-seeds-producer-supplier
- Institute website: www.pau.edu -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Agricultural_University
- Director (Seeds) office phones, 2019 listing: 94640-37325, 98159-65404, 98724-28072. Dated; verify before use -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=4304
- Official email: No evidence found
- Breeder names, roles, phones and emails: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Singh et al. (2013). Mash 114 multi-location trial results (14 locations, 39.45% over Mash 338). Full title and journal not captured -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
- Authors not captured (2023). Genetics, genomics, and breeding of black gram [Vigna mungo (L.) Hepper]. Frontiers in Plant Science -- DOI 10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10822891/
- Vadivel K., Manivannan N., Mahalingam A., Satya V.K., Vanniarajan C., Ragul S. (2023). Identification and Validation of Quantitative Trait Loci of Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus Disease Resistance in Blackgram [Vigna mungo (L.) Hepper]. Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4459
- Press report (2006). PAU launches two new high-yielding maize varieties (Mash 114 reference). Newspaper item -- https://www.oneindia.com/2006/06/15/pau-launches-two-new-high-yielding-maize-varieties-1150360564.html
- Mash 1190: No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, AICRP report entry or trial result specific to Mash 1190 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Mash 1190: No evidence found from NSC, PSCL, KVK, PAU or dealer listings
- Mash 114: Mash 114 and Mash 338 were listed as seed on sale at a PAU Kisan Mela (undated) -- https://seedindustrynews.com/Seed-Industry-News/PAU-to-Sell-Improved-Seed-at-Kisan-Mela.html
- PAU seed channels: a Ludhiana campus seed counter open year-round, seed sold at KVKs, research stations and university seed farms, and an outlet at NDRI Karnal -- https://pau.edu/dirseeds/
- Seednet portal listing: not reached

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Mash 1190: Listed for NWPZ (Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand) -- http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Mash 114: Punjab-focused farm advice; no separate state recommendation found -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/mash-urd

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NOTE: Pant Urd 10 (CSC name) and Pant Urd 12 (Seednet name) are both black gram (Vigna mungo, urd bean), not chickpea. The "chickpea" field in the input appears to be wrong and I did not search chickpea. No evidence I found links Pant Urd 10 and Pant Urd 12 as the same variety, so the two names are reported separately below. The search budget ran out after 4 web_search calls, so breeder, contact and publication coverage is incomplete.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance under either name. The search returned general black gram pages and other varieties. (Searched under Pant Urd 10 and Pant Urd 12.)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pant Urd 10 (CSC table row): listed as resistant to MYMV and powdery mildew, with the note "(PU 10-23)" and LCV listed in the same row; the table layout makes the exact pairing ambiguous. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Urd 12: the 2021 Pantnagar newsletter describes it as disease resistant and reports reactions to important diseases and insect pests, but the snippet does not name the specific diseases. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/26.07.2021_Issue-13_COA_Pantnagar_Newsletter.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pant Urd 10 (CSC table row): 80-85 days duration and 12-13 q/ha yield, with the table noting Pant Urd 10 as kharif and released in 2019 by GBPUA&T. The 2019 year conflicts with the input release date of 2018-08-10. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Urd 12 (Pantnagar newsletter): reported 1427 kg/ha, against 1200 kg/ha for Uttara, 1193 kg/ha for PU-31 and 1153 kg/ha for KUG-479. Testing centres named include PAU Ludhiana, Hisar, and ARS Gurdaspur and Samba. Announced at the Annual Group Meet of Kharif Pulses, 27-28 May 2021. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/26.07.2021_Issue-13_COA_Pantnagar_Newsletter.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pant Urd 12: the newsletter says development began in 2010 with a cross between PU-31 and TU-942. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/26.07.2021_Issue-13_COA_Pantnagar_Newsletter.pdf
- Pant Urd 10: parentage is not specified in the input or in any source found. No QTL or marker study found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Pant Urd 12: developed by Pantnagar scientists of the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology. No individual breeder name was found. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/26.07.2021_Issue-13_COA_Pantnagar_Newsletter.pdf
- Pant Urd 10: the institution is GBPUA&T, Pantnagar, per the CSC table. No breeder name found. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute postal address as printed on the Pantnagar newsletter: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar 263145, Uttarakhand. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/26.07.2021_Issue-13_COA_Pantnagar_Newsletter.pdf
- No official email, phone or breeder contact found for either name. The search budget was exhausted before a contact-page search could run.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found that names Pant Urd 10 or Pant Urd 12. Results that mentioned Pantnagar urd work named other varieties (Pant Urd 7, 19, 30, 31), so I excluded them. Excluded example: Singh, D.P., Singh, B.B. and Pratap, A., "Genetic improvement of mungbean and urdbean..." -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/220/1989
- The Pant Urd 12 newsletter (2021) is an announcement, not a peer-reviewed paper, and is recorded under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS above.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Pant Urd 12: the ICAR-IIPR seed portal page is headed "Variety Name: Pant Urd 12, State: Uttarakhand, Seed Category: Certified Seed", but the visible centre rows in the snippet are for other varieties (e.g., AKU 10-1). Treat as unconfirmed. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php
- Pant Urd 10: no evidence found. The sources returned only general urd seed-chain data.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Pant Urd 10: NHZ (J&K, HP, TR, MN), consistent with the input. -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Urd 12: Uttarakhand, per the IIPR seed portal header. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Urd 11 / Pant Urd 12 (blackgram, PU 13-05, GBPUAT)

Search status: four web_search queries were run, which is the maximum allowed. A fifth query was refused by the tool limit. The first batch's full result objects were not kept in session state, so I could not re-read them. Nothing below is verified against a primary release notification, Seednet listing, or institute page for this variety.

Naming: "Pant Urd 11" (CSC release-minutes name) and "Pant Urd 12" (Seednet name) were both searched. No result tied either name to this variety, so no evidence is attributed to either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched under both names; no result described drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No result gave MYMV, anthracnose, or other disease or pest reaction for this variety. The only resistance-related hit concerned a different variety, VBN 11 -- http://www.researchgate.net/publication/375642257_Electronic_Journal_of_Plant_Breeding_VBN_11_-A_new_high_yielding_and_MYMV_disease_resistant_blackgram_variety (not a match; excluded).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for this variety. One unrelated Pantnagar spacing trial (kharif 2000-01 urd bean, wider spacing and pod numbers) was returned: https://saulibrary.edu.bd/daatj/public/uploads/Done%2019-10396.pdf (not about Pant Urd 11; excluded).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The MYMV inheritance study in the VBN 11 result is for a different variety and is excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No breeder name, developing station, or institute page for Pant Urd 11/12 was returned. The institution given in the input is G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology; this was not confirmed by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No name, email, phone, address or contact-page URL was retrieved for GBPUAT or for this variety's breeding programme.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, report, thesis or KrishiKosh record was retrieved that names Pant Urd 11 or Pant Urd 12.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The fourth search was not run as a seed-specific query. The Seednet name "Pant Urd 12" returned only a generic blackgram slideshow: https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/black-gram-ppt-black-gram-also-known-as-urad-or-urd-bean-is-an-important-pulse-crop-grown-in-india/271676749 (not a seed source; excluded).

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Only partial. The input lists Uttarakhand as the recommended state, but no search result confirmed this. The Department of Pulses central-release list was returned, with its visible entries including Pant U 8 (2020): http://dpd.gov.in/4.%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf. Its visible snippet did not show a Pant Urd 11 or Pant Urd 12 row, so the list should be checked directly for the entry and its notified zone.

Next steps for a complete record: open the dpd.gov.in list and find the Pant Urd 11 row; search seednet.gov.in for "Pant Urd 12"; check GBPUAT's Pantnagar pulses/breeding pages and KrishiKosh for the variety; and check the CSC or AICRP-MULLaRP annual reports for the 2023 release.

drought.details: Rainfed yield of 871 kg/ha is reported, with 23.2% and 25.9% gains over check varieties. No explicit drought-tolerance trial was found in peer-reviewed or institutional sources, so yield performance alone does not establish drought tolerance mechanisms.

heat.details: Only a non-authoritative blog claims heat and drought tolerance. This is not corroborated by ICAR or TNAU sources and is therefore not treated as evidence.

salinity.details: No evidence found.

flood.details: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.summary: Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): highly resistant, per the developers' release paper, together with synchronized maturity and determinate habit. Leaf crinkle: resistant, per the release paper. Powdery mildew: moderately resistant, per the release paper. Other diseases (YMV, leaf curl virus, stem necrosis, and a PM entry) appear in the national listing, but that row is garbled in extraction and is UNVERIFIED. Note that the evidence refers to blackgram, not chickpea.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found beyond the disease notes. The release paper states the culture was screened against major insect pests, but results were not retrieved, so no specific pest resistance can be confirmed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CROP MISMATCH: VBN 8 is a blackgram (urdbean, Vigna mungo) variety from TNAU, not a chickpea variety. The chickpea-specific fields in the request (variety code, 2018 release, states) appear to be carried over from a blackgram record, so none of the findings below are chickpea data. -- https://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
RELEASE YEAR CONFLICT: The TNAU Vamban variety list gives 2016, while the national pulses listing gives 2018. Parentage is also recorded differently across sources (VBN 3 x VBG 04-008 in the journal paper; Vamban 3 x VBN 04-008 on the TNAU page). -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/ ; https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360
DISEASE RESISTANCE (MYMV): Highly resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus, with synchronized maturity and determinate habit, per the developers' release paper. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360
DISEASE RESISTANCE (leaf crinkle and powdery mildew): Resistant to leaf crinkle; moderately resistant to powdery mildew, per the same release paper. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360
DISEASE RESISTANCE (other): The national listing row for VBN 8 is garbled in extraction but appears to mention YMV, leaf curl virus, and stem necrosis resistance, and a PM entry. Treat as unverified. -- https://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
DROUGHT: Rainfed yield of 871 kg/ha, versus 23.2% and 25.9% gains over check varieties; no explicit drought-tolerance trial found in peer-reviewed or institutional sources. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360
HEAT: Only a non-authoritative blog claims heat and drought tolerance; not corroborated by ICAR/TNAU sources. -- https://agri.bot/docs/duration-for-vbn-8-black-gram-variety/
SALINITY: No evidence found.
FLOOD / SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found.
PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found beyond the disease notes above. The release paper says the culture was screened against major insect pests, but results were not retrieved. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360
QTL / MARKERS: No evidence found.
YIELD AND TRIALS: Average yield of 900 kg/ha, 11.9% and 13.5% above checks VBN 6 and CO 6; irrigated yield of 988 kg/ha; trials included multilocation, adaptive research and on-farm trials. -- https://ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/1360 ; https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/
BREEDER / INSTITUTION: Developed at National Pulses Research Centre, Vamban, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU); released from the NPRC Vamban programme. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/
SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs): No evidence found.
RECOMMENDED STATES: Listed for the Southern Zone (Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Odisha), matching the request; TNAU separately describes suitability for all seasons in Tamil Nadu. -- https://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf ; https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/49th-Research-Highlights-2015-2017.pdf
MATURITY: 65–70 days, determinate with non-shattering pods. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/prs-vamban/varieties-released/

disease_resistance.summary: Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): listed as resistant in the TNAU profile for VBN 5. Urdbean leaf crinkle virus (ULCV): listed as resistant in the TNAU profile for VBN 5. Field evidence: in a farmer-field trial at Tiruppur (kharif 2020), VBN 5 showed the lowest MYMV incidence among the entries tested (4.1%), compared with 5.1% for LGG 630 and 5.3% for DGG 1. The trial measured incidence only; it did not establish resistance mechanisms or levels.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The input record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified', and no pest-resistance evidence for VBN 5 appeared in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of 878 kg/ha as listed by TNAU. In the Tiruppur farmer-field trial (kharif 2020), grain yield was 8.15 q/ha (815 kg/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Evidence comes from a single farmer-field trial location and season; no multi-environment stability data were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Per the input record, suitable for all seasons in both irrigated and rainfed conditions throughout Tamil Nadu except the Nilgiris and Kanyakumari districts. The digest does not independently confirm this adaptation statement.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: EARLY (input record). TNAU lists duration as 70-75 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PUBESCENT BLACK PODS; PODS COME OUT ABOVE THE CANOPY DURING PODDING STAGE UNDER NORMAL CONDITION; LANCEOLATE LEAVES IN NORMAL CONDITION AND OVATE LEAVES IN DRY CONDITION. TNAU also describes VBN 5 as high-yielding with multiple blooming and non-shattering pods, and 22.85% protein.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Tiruppur farmer-field trial (KVK, TNAU Tiruppur; 7 farms, 5 replications; kharif 2020): VBN 5 recorded 31.8 pods per plant and grain yield of 8.15 q/ha, the highest of the three improved entries. Comparators were LGG 630 at 7.90 q/ha and DGG 1 at 7.20 q/ha. VBN 5 also had the lowest MYMV incidence (4.1%) in this trial. No other trial results for VBN 5 were found.

seednet_fields.Parentage: VAMBAN 1 X VIGNA MUNGO VAR SILVESTRIS 1
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: SUITABLE FOR ALL SEASONS IN BOTH IRRIGATED AND RAINFED CONDITIONS. THROUGH OUT TAMIL NADU EXCEPT NILGIRIS AND KANYAKUMARI DISTRICTS.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: PUBESCENT BLACK PODS; PODS COME OUT ABOVE THE CANOPY DURING PODDING STAGE UNDER NORMAL CONDITION; LANCEOLATE LEAVES IN NORMAL CONDITION AND OVATE LEAVES IN DRY CONDITION.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PARENTAGE : VAMBAN 1 X VIGNA MUNGO VAR SILVESTRIS 1; DURATION : 65-70 DAYS; SEASON (IRRIGATED/RAINFED) : JUNE - JULY (ADI PATTAM) SEPTEMBER - OCTOBER (PURATTASI PATTAM) FEBRUARY - MARCH (THAI PATTAM); MEAN GRAIN YIELD : 871 KG/HA; IRRIGATED : 890 KG/HA; RAINFED : 850 KG/HA; GROWTH HABIT : ERECT AND DETERMINATE PLANT TYPE PINK WASH IN PETIOLE, STEM AND LEAVES MIDRIB; LEAVES : LANCEOLATE LEAVES IN NORMAL CONDITION AND OVATE LEAVES IN DRY CONDITION; STEM COLOUR : PINK WITH GREEN; BRANCHES : 2-4; INFLORESCENCE : RACEMOSE; FLOWER COLOUR : YELLOW; CALYX : YELLOW; POD COLOUR : BLACK; POD LENGTH : 4.0 CM; SEEDS/POD : 5-6; SEED COLOUR : DULL BLACK; 100 SEED WEIGHT : 3.5-4.0 G.

drought.details: VBN 6 is reported as tolerant to moisture stress and is listed among stress-tolerant blackgram genotypes. Some sources indicate it is 'moderately tolerant'. Cultivation strategies include growing VBN 6 under moisture stress conditions.

heat.details: No specific information on heat tolerance for VBN 6 was found.

salinity.details: While blackgram generally struggles with alkaline and saline soils, and VBN 6 is mentioned in the context of salinity tolerance breeding programs, there is no direct evidence stating VBN 6 itself is tolerant to salinity.

flood.details: General statements indicate urdbean has more tolerance to waterlogging than mungbean, but specific tolerance for VBN 6 is not mentioned.

disease_resistance.summary: VBN 6 exhibits resistance to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus (MYMV) and Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV). It is described as highly resistant to yellow mosaic virus disease.

pest_resistance.summary: No information on pest resistance was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield is reported between 800-900 kg/ha (8-9 quintals/hectare). Specific reported yields include 783 kg/ha and 804 kg/ha. Yield can vary significantly depending on conditions, with a reported 330 kg/ha under coconut plantation.
agronomic_details.stability: VBN 6 is mentioned as suitable for 'All Seasons' and 'Kharif/Rabi' in Tamil Nadu, suggesting broad seasonal adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation in Tamil Nadu. It is particularly suitable for rice fallow cultivation, including the January/Markazhi – Thaipattam (Winter Irrigated) seasons, as well as June-July/Sept 15-20 periods.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PUBESCENT BLACK PODS; PODS COME OUT ABOVE THE CANOPY DURING PODDING STAGE UNDER NORMAL CONDITION; LANCEOLATE LEAVES IN NORMAL CONDITION AND OVATE LEAVES IN DRY CONDITION. Seeds have a mean length of 3.94 mm.
agronomic_details.field_trials: VBN 6 has been part of various evaluations, including those for resistance to Urdbean Leaf Crinkle Virus (ULCV) where it served as a parent in crosses (e.g., with VBN 8). It has also been evaluated for boron efficiency (moderate B efficiency).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: VBN 6 is utilized in genetic studies, including genetic linkage mapping for MYMV resistance (against KKM 1) and single marker analysis in crosses (e.g., VBN 6 x TU 68). Specific QTLs, SNPs, or SSRs are not explicitly detailed in the provided results.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs or their effects are detailed.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No specific genes or pathways are detailed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CROSS-CHECK FLAG: The record lists crop as blackgram, but the Seednet crop name is BOTTLE GOURD, and every GH-22 source found describes a bottle gourd variety. No page tied GH-22 to blackgram. Under the strict relevance rule, the blackgram findings below are "No evidence found." The bottle gourd sources are listed separately at the end for record correction. Both names ("GH-22 (Ghiya Hisar 22)") were searched, and the evidence refers to the same name on both.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches for GH-22 blackgram returned no stress-tolerance data. The only GH-22 variety page found is for bottle gourd (see crop-mismatch section).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No blackgram GH-22 disease or pest data was returned. Generic blackgram pages (not GH-22) were excluded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for blackgram. The bottle gourd trial data are excluded (see crop-mismatch section).

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The only GH-22 genetics-related result was a generic blackgram GWAS (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9310006/), which does not name GH-22 and was excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a named GH-22 breeder. Institution-level link: a Haryana Kisan Ayog report lists "GH-22" among vegetable varieties released by CCS HAU, Hisar, Haryana, without naming the crop -- https://hkkp.org.in/Reports/Report_on_Horticulture.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No GH-22 breeder contact found. Institute-level contact (acceptable fallback): CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar - 125 004, INDIA; phone 1-800-1803001 -- https://translate.google.com/translate?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.hau.ac.in%2F&hl=hi&sl=en&tl=hi&client=srp (Google Translate proxy of hau.ac.in; the direct institute page was not returned by search). No email or station address was found for GH-22.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in Kanchan (IPCK 2009-145) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/

DISEASE AND PEST
- It is moderately resistant to wilt disease. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/
- Same wilt rating in the IIPR varieties page, which also records the gazette notification -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/ (index 4-6)
- No evidence found for stunt, dry root rot, Ascochyta blight, or insect resistance specific to Kanchan.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- It has large seed size (32.2g/100 seed weight) with seed creamy white colour. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/
- It matures in 130-135 days with yield of 18-20 q/ha and suitable for timely sown condition in Western and Central region of Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/
- No Kanchan-specific multi-location trial data found beyond the IIPR summary above.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for parentage, pedigree, marker-assisted work, or QTL studies on Kanchan. The parentage field "Not specified" is unresolved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur. Listed under Division of Crop Improvement -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/ (index 11-3)
- Lead breeder for Kanchan: No evidence found. The IIPR page gives a breeder only for the neighbouring line IPC 2004-01, and that is not Kanchan.
- Notification: This variety was released in 2022 (Gazette notification No. 1056 (E) dated 06.03.2023. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Name discrepancy: the IIPR pages describe the line as "Kabuli" in one entry (index 4-4, 20-4) and as "Desi" in another (index 1-3, 20-4). The crop type needs checking before the record is finalised.
- Release-date mismatch: the CSC field says 2022-10-26, but the gazette date is 06.03.2023. The CSC minutes were not located.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Division of Crop Improvement, ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur 208 024 -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/ (index 11-1)
- Breeder name, email, phone: No evidence found for Kanchan. The only breeder contact found is for IPC 2004-01 (Dr. SK Chaturvedi, Principal Scientist & Chickpea Breeder, Mob. 9336214977). The email on that page is truncated ("sushilk.c"), so it cannot be used as recorded -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/varieties/ (index 11-6, 11-7)
- Institute contact page URL: No evidence found in the search results.
- Full institute postal address beyond "Kanpur 208 024": No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No Kanchan-specific publication found. No paper, thesis, or conference item naming IPCK 2009-145 or Kanchan chickpea was retrieved.
- Context only: the ICAR-AICRP Chickpea Progress Report 2021-22 (AICRP chickpea report, ICAR-IIPR), which does not mention Kanchan in the retrieved text -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- KrishiKosh: not searched; no evidence retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Chickpea Kanchan (IPCK 2009-145): No evidence found on Seednet, NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, or SAU seed sales.
- Seednet crop "BOTTLE GOURD": the Seednet name "Kanchan" was searched under bottle gourd. The only Kanchan bottle gourd listings are private retail products, for example KANCHAN BOTTLE GOURD ( कंचन लौकी ) product -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/kanchan-bottle-gourd. These do not match the chickpea record, and no Seednet entry was found for chickpea Kanchan.
- Separate varieties not to be conflated with this record: Kashi Kanchan is a bottle gourd variety listed by a seed company -- https://www.vnrseeds.com/variety-list/?vdb=Bottle+Gourd (index 32-7). The ICAR-IIVR page under a bottle gourd URL describes a cowpea variety, Kashi Kanchan -- https://icariivr.org.in/product/bottle-gourd-kashi-kanchan/ (index 37-4). PDKV Kanchan is a Maharashtra chickpea variety released in 2019 -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf (index 16-8).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttar Pradesh only: the gazette-linked entry recommends timely sown conditions in the Western and Central region of Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/new-varieties/ (index 20-8). This matches the input field "Uttar Pradesh".

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME RESOLUTION
- "ALR 2" for coconut: no page uses this exact name for a coconut variety. The closest match is TNAU's "ALR (CN) 2" (coconut, Coconut Research Station, Aliyar Nagar), which the TNAU pages date to 2010, not the 2015-04-07 release date in the record. Treat the link as unverified.
- "ALR 2" as groundnut (ICRISAT PMD_72, TNAU groundnut pages, released 1994) is a different crop and was discarded.
- "PLR 2" (Seednet name, bottle gourd): one TNAU page lists PLR 2 among bottle gourd varieties. No page links it to the coconut release record, so the crop mismatch is unresolved.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- ALR (CN) 2 is described as drought tolerant -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/
- The same drought claim appears on the TNAU research-station profile page -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/about_us/abt_us_research_aliyar.html
- No flood, submergence, salinity or heat evidence found for ALR (CN) 2 -- searched via the search 1 and search 3 results; none returned.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for ALR (CN) 2 disease or pest resistance. The TNAU pages that mention resistance (leaf spot, leaf blight, basal stem rot, bud rot, eriophyid mite) refer to ALR (CN) 1 or ALR (CN) 3 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/ ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/coconut_varieties/coconut_tall_ALR-CN-1.html
- Bottle gourd PLR 2 disease or pest data: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- ALR (CN) 2: selection from Tiptur tall; average yield 109 nuts/palm/year after stabilisation; copra 136 g/nut; copra yield 14 kg/palm/year; oil 64.7% -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/ ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/about_us/abt_us_research_aliyar.html
- The TNAU page calls it a best substitute for Chowghat Orange Dwarf -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/contact-us/ (same varieties page; see https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/)
- ALR (CN) 2 trial data (multi-location, AICRP): No evidence found. The AICRP Palms centre page lists ALR (CN) 1, Kalpatharu and ALR (CN) 3 as the station's releases and omits ALR (CN) 2 -- http://www.aicrppalms.res.in/centres_aliya.html
- PLR 2 bottle gourd agronomy: No evidence found beyond the variety name in a TNAU list -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_bottlegourd.html
- Maturity for ALR (CN) 2: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for ALR 2 or ALR (CN) 2 genetic, marker or QTL work. The only genomic hits concerned unrelated bottle gourd or other crops.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution for ALR (CN) 2: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coconut Research Station, Aliyar Nagar (642 101, Coimbatore district) -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-aliyarnagar/varieties-released/ ; http://www.aicrppalms.res.in/centres_aliya.html
- Lead breeder name for ALR (CN) 2: No evidence found.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Punjab Barkat is a PAU-developed bottle gourd variety released in 2014 (the supplied record says 2022), with vigorous vines, long light-green cylindrical fruits, and a reported yield of about 226 q/acre. full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: PAU-bred bottle gourd (registered REG/2016/778) with vigorous, branched vines and long cylindrical light-green fruits. Reported yield is about 226 q/acre. Recommended in Punjab, with a high fruit count in Mohali farmer-field trials.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Moderately resistant to mosaic disease per secondary sources. It cannot be classed as stress tolerant on current evidence.

- Ruchi is listed as a dual-purpose linseed variety with rust and mildew resistance. Ruchi – All Uttar Pradesh. (Rust & Mildew Resistant) -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/research-article/scientific-cultivation-of-dual-purpose-crop-linseed

heat.details: Specific heat tolerance details for Vardan (IPL - 315) lentil are not available. A vegetable 'Vardan' is described as tolerant to heat (RESULT_16). 'Vardan' (brand name for bags) is generally associated with heat stress in a climate change context (RESULT_17).

salinity.details: 'Vardan' is identified as a salt tolerant cultivar within 'oilseed/legume' crops (RESULT_28). This Vardan variety is associated with Chandrashekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology (CSAUAT) and performs in partially reclaimed sodic soil (RESULT_28). Another 'Vardan' developed through heterosis breeding (likely a vegetable based on context) was also more tolerant to salt than bottle gourd rootstocks (RESULT_30). The 'Vardan-1' bio-care product also notes salt stress tolerance (RESULT_5, RESULT_19).
