drought.details: No drought-specific evidence was found for Varuna or Varuna-WRR2. The Haryana State Seeds listing describes T-59 (Varuna) as suitable for rainfed areas, which is a general suitability statement rather than a measured drought tolerance result. The same listing also describes T-59 as frost resistant and lodging resistant. Tractor Junction describes T-59 as suited to all climatic conditions. These statements refer to T-59 (the older open-pollinated Varuna), not confirmed for Varuna-WRR2. The digest notes that the research query found no drought-index evidence.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to Varuna or Varuna-WRR2 in the searched research query.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to Varuna or Varuna-WRR2 in the searched research query.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to Varuna or Varuna-WRR2 in the searched research query.

disease_resistance.summary: White rust (Albugo candida): Varuna is documented as susceptible. It was used as the susceptible host in white-rust transformation work and as the susceptible cultivar in a 2014-16 white-rust fungicide trial. Transgenic WRR-gene lines derived from Varuna were characterised as resistant, including resistance to a virulent Ac2V isolate. Varuna-WRR gene lines show higher constitutive defence metabolites and sustained transcriptomic and metabolomic defence responses against A. candida. Naming note: the digest uses both Varuna-WRR2 and Varuna_WRR for the white-rust-resistant derivative, and the source linking them to the variety code is not confirmed. No other disease resistance evidence was found.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for aphid, Alternaria, or other pest resistance in Varuna.

agronomic_details.yield: Haryana State Seeds: 8-10 quintals/acre (T-59 Varuna). Tractor Junction: about 6-8 quintals/acre (T-59 Varuna). Kisaan Helpline: average seed yield 18 quintals/ha. CSAUA&T Kanpur variety-characterisation table lists 1140 (2015-16) falling to 60 (2020-21), with unclear meaning. These figures are not consistent with each other and are not confirmed for Varuna-WRR2. DMH-11 is reported 28% above Varuna in ICAR-DRMR trials, but this figure comes from the promoter and the Biotech Consortium, not an independent multi-location trial.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location AICRP-RM yield data for Varuna-WRR2 was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended states: Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh (Northern Rajasthan standardised to Rajasthan). Haryana State Seeds describes T-59 as suitable for rainfed areas. Tractor Junction describes T-59 as suited to all climatic conditions. Kisaan Helpline describes irrigated conditions. Agro-climatic fit beyond these statements is not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Haryana State Seeds: 145-150 days. Tractor Junction: 145-150 days. Kisaan Helpline (Hindi): 110-115 days. Sources differ; variety identity for each figure should be checked.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Haryana State Seeds (T-59 Varuna): lodging resistant, non-shattering, frost resistant. Oil content about 39% (Haryana State Seeds and Tractor Junction) and 37% (Kisaan Helpline). Sowing 25 Sep-15 Oct; seed rate 2 kg/acre (Haryana State Seeds) and line sowing 7.5 kg/ha (Kisaan Helpline). Morphological characteristics are not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Haryana State Seeds and Tractor Junction report yield ranges for T-59 Varuna as listed above; these are listing values, not trial results. (2) CSAUA&T Kanpur variety-characterisation table: Varuna (T-59) yield 1140 (2015-16) to 60 (2020-21), meaning unclear. (3) DMH-11 reported 28% above Varuna in ICAR-DRMR trials, sourced from the promoter and Biotech Consortium, not independent. (4) A 2014-16 white-rust fungicide trial used Varuna as the susceptible cultivar. No multi-location AICRP-RM data for Varuna-WRR2 was found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Varuna x Heera doubled-haploid (VH) map with 833 markers. A chromosome-scale genome assembly of Varuna with 18 pseudochromosomes is reported. Marker positions are not available in the digest. Varuna bn 3.6 carries barnase, and barstar sits in EH-2 modbs 2.99 (a transgenic male-sterility system, not a stress marker).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Varuna x Tumida doubled-haploid population: 20 stable QTL for nine plant architecture traits, with candidate genes mapped to the Varuna and Tumida genome assemblies. No QTL specific to white-rust resistance in Varuna-WRR2 was found beyond the multi-omics study. QTL effect sizes are not available in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: BjuWRR1-mediated resistance to A. candida in Varuna_WRR, with higher constitutive defence metabolites and sustained transcriptomic and metabolomic defence responses (2026 multi-omics study). Candidate genes for plant architecture traits are mapped to the Varuna and Tumida assemblies. Barnase/barstar is a transgenic male-sterility system in bn 3.6.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Haryana State Seeds lists T-59 (Varuna), the older open-pollinated variety. No listing for Varuna-WRR2 was found. The Seednet portal could not be reached, and no Seednet listing was confirmed. The Seednet crop name (BOTTLE GOURD) is not supported by any source.
commercial_info.private_dealers: Tractor Junction and Kisaan Helpline pages reference Varuna varieties; no dealer details were found in the digest. Not found in searched sources for dealers.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY RECORD: Varuna (variety_name) / Varuna (seednet_variety_name), crop mustard (Brassica juncea). Seednet crop name is BOTTLE GOURD; no source supports that.

NAME NOTE: Searches on "Varuna" returned two different lines. Varuna T-59 is the older open-pollinated mustard variety. Varuna-WRR2 / Varuna_WRR is a white-rust-resistant derivative in CGMCP research. Varuna bn 3.6 is a barnase male-sterile GM line. No source linked the 2022-10-26 date to a CSC release of Varuna-WRR2. The date matches the 18-Oct-2022 GEAC release recommendation and the 25-Oct-2022 MoEFCC approval for GM mustard (DMH-11 and parental lines). I could not confirm a Seednet listing; the Seednet portal was not reachable by search.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. A Bayer page for the Arize hybrid line says Arize hybrids in general tolerate temporary drought, moderate salinity and flash floods, but it does not name 6129, so I discarded it. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.com.ph/en-ph/products/arize-hybrid-rice-seeds/about-arize.html

DISEASE AND PEST
Hybrid 6129 (IET 18815) is listed as resistant to blast, brown spot, brown plant hopper (BPH) and white backed plant hopper (WBPH) in an ICAR crop-improvement table (name given as "Hybrid 6129", variety name 6129 used, Seednet name 619 not found). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/CI-11.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Arize 6129 was one of the entries in a transplanting-date trial in which it was compared with the check HPR 2143; leaf area index was reported at 60 and 90 days after transplanting, and grain/straw yield was reported by treatment. The excerpt gives no absolute yield figure for 6129, and the authors and year are not shown. -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/download/6273/version/6998/6478/46787
Bayer's Arize 6129 Gold product page lists high yield, short duration and very high grain filling. No days-to-maturity or kg/ha figure is given. The product page is for "Arize 6129 Gold", so its identity with the 6129 hybrid is inferred from the name. -- https://www.bayercropscience.in/en/seed-products/arize-6129-gold/234489
No evidence found for numeric yield, maturity in days, or stress-screening data specific to 6129 in the search results.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Searches for 6129 with marker, QTL or parentage terms returned nothing relevant. Parentage is not specified in the release record.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Bayer Crop Science (the release record names Bayer Crop Science). The 2007 All-India notification lists the hybrid as "Hybrid-6129 (IET 18815)". The Haryana 2015 notification lists "6129 (BS 129, HRI152, IET 18815)". -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
Lead breeder name: No evidence found for a breeder of 6129. Bayer's global Head of Breeding (Mike Graham) appears in Bayer rice press material, but no source links him to 6129, so I have not attributed the variety to him. -- https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/bayer-introduces-agricultural-system-for-direct-seeded-rice-with-potential-to-reduce-greenhouse-gas-emissions-and-water-use-by-up-to-40-percent/

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for an email, phone or postal address for the 6129 breeding team. Institute-level page found: Bayer Crop Science India, product page for Arize 6129 Gold -- https://www.bayercropscience.in/en/seed-products/arize-6129-gold/234489
No institute contact details (email, phone, address) were found on that page.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not stated (year not stated). Field trial on transplanting dates with Arize 6129 and HPR 2143 check. Plant Science Today (ISSN 2348-1900) -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/download/6273/version/6998/6478/46787
Production Oriented Survey report (AICRIP, 2020-21). Lists Arize-6129 among hybrids prevalent in Haryana districts and in Ambala. Authors not stated. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/POS2020-21.pdf
No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, KrishiKosh record or DOI specific to 6129 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Bayer Crop Science India sells Arize 6129 Gold in 1 kg and 3 kg packs -- https://www.bayercropscience.in/en/seed-products/arize-6129-gold/234489
Seednet (619 or 6129): No evidence found. The Seednet-name search for "619" returned only brinjal pages, so the Seednet name 619 is not linked to this rice variety. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Haryana: 6129 (BS 129, HRI152, IET 18815) notified by S.O. 268(E) dated 28.01.2015 -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm
All India: Hybrid-6129 (IET 18815) notified by S.O. 1703(E) dated 05.10.2007 -- https://www.drdpat.bih.nic.in/Notified-Rice-Varieties.htm and https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/Licence/Document/Variety.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RECORD FLAG -- The input lists crop "potato" and Seednet crop "BRINJAL", but the only Arunima entry I found is a sweet potato line from the CTCRI tuber-crop release bulletin. The parentage (brinjal, Digras, Yeotmal) and the Seednet name ARUNA did not appear in any result. Treat the record as unverified until the CSC minutes and Seednet entry are checked. Searches used: (1) release/notification, (2) breeder/institute, (3) research papers, (4) identity check on ARUNA/brinjal. No seed-availability search was run, so that heading has no search behind it.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The only Arunima entry found is noted for a relatively low incidence of sweet potato weevil; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found for it. -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-11/technical-bulletin_tuber_crop_varieties_in_india.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- Weevil incidence is the only pest note for Arunima. The anthracnose resistance and scale/mealybug tolerance in the same bulletin belong to Bhu Arunima (Odisha), not Arunima. -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-11/technical-bulletin_tuber_crop_varieties_in_india.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The bulletin describes a semi-spreading plant, purplish-red-skinned elliptic tubers with orange flesh, beta-carotene content, and a 90-100 day duration. No yield data for Arunima was found. -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-11/technical-bulletin_tuber_crop_varieties_in_india.pdf
Name collision: "Sree Arunima" (sweet potato hybrid SPH-31, 26.06 t/ha, submitted for Odisha release) is a different entry. -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2023-02/annual-report-2023-icar-ctcri.pdf (URL as returned: https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-02/annual-report-2023-icar-ctcri.pdf)
Name collision: Co 14005 (Arunima) is a sugarcane variety notified in 2023. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/sugarcane-variety-co-14005-arunima/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Breeder name not found. The bulletin lists the entry under the AICRP on Tuber Crops with Andhra Pradesh as its state, and cites a 2024 Dr. YSRHU technical profile of the AICRP prepared at Kovvur. -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-11/technical-bulletin_tuber_crop_varieties_in_india.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. No email, phone or Dr. YSRHU address appeared in the results. Institute-level address from the bulletin's publisher line: ICAR-Central Tuber Crops Research Institute, Sreekariyam, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, India. -- https://www.ctcri.org/public/publications/2025-11/technical-bulletin_tuber_crop_varieties_in_india.pdf

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: The Scribd compilation mentions salinity classes of vegetables in general, but none specific to Arka Avinash.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence. The waterlogging and submergence text in the State of Indian Agriculture 2017 and the ICAR report concerns rice germplasm (EC881906, EC887557 from the Philippines), not brinjal.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: No brinjal-specific evidence. The submergence snippets refer to rice accessions.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: Bacterial wilt (Ralstonia solanacearum, formerly Pseudomonas solanacearum). It is widely listed as a bacterial wilt resistant variety. One ResearchGate-hosted paper (Mysore J. Agric. Sci.) lists Arka Avinash with a disease severity of 75.56% and a score of 4 in a sandalwood host-interaction study, which is not a brinjal disease assay. The snippet is ambiguous, so it is not counted as evidence of susceptibility or resistance.
disease_resistance.technical_details: Described as a hybrid derivative of Arka Kusumakar x IIHR-3 ('Long' in some sources). The resistance mechanism or gene is not described in the snippets. One consumer news site calls it 'bacterial scorch resistant', which is likely a mislabel of bacterial wilt.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: None documented. Shoot and fruit borer appears only in general pest-management slides, not as a trait of this variety.
pest_resistance.technical_details: No pest resistance evidence.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: One research-backed stress trait (bacterial wilt resistance) is supported by a review chapter on eggplant bacterial wilt breeding and by the ICAR report and the State of Indian Agriculture 2017, with yield data of 34-42 t/ha. This fits the 75 band (at least one stress trait and a citation). It falls short of 90+ because there is no abiotic stress evidence, no Gujarat-specific trial data, and no molecular or genetic detail. Bacterial wilt is also not a documented priority problem in Gujarat, and the variety's suitability to Gujarat's semi-arid and saline conditions is unverified.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Bacterial wilt resistant; long green fruits with a green calyx; 34-42 t/ha yield; ICAR-IIHR variety

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Arka Avinash is an ICAR-IIHR long green brinjal (Arka Kusumakar x IIHR-3) known for bacterial wilt resistance and yields of about 34-42 t/ha. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or pest resistance evidence was found, and the submergence results relate to rice. Evidence is moderate, drawn mostly from reviews, institutional reports and teaching slides, with no Gujarat trial data.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Tall, spreading, long green-fruited brinjal with a fleshy green calyx, yielding 34-42 t/ha. Maturity, adaptation and recommended states are not specified.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Resistance to bacterial wilt is consistently reported across sources. No abiotic stress tolerance or pest resistance is documented. Gujarat suitability is unverified.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is confirmed as an AAU release with institutional documentation (recommendations booklet, annual reports, JAM minutes) and a strong reported yield of 634.90 q/ha. However, no stress or climate-resilience trait can be attributed to it, and there are no peer-reviewed citations. Under the rubric this fits 'only yield info, no stress/citation' (40), nudged up to 50 for the credible institutional sources and the large yield advantage over checks. The score is not higher because disease, pest and salinity snippets cannot be reliably tied to this variety.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: AAU-released brinjal variety; high reported fruit yield of 634.90 q/ha, well above checks; stress traits not documented

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: GAb 6 (Anand Doli) is a brinjal variety from Anand Agricultural University, Gujarat, with a reported fruit yield of 634.90 q/ha that substantially exceeds the check varieties. No variety-specific evidence of abiotic stress tolerance or disease/pest resistance was found, and the sources are institutional reports rather than peer-reviewed research. Evidence quality is low to medium, and the release year differs between the supplied metadata (2022) and the sources (2019).
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Brinjal variety released by AAU, Anand (GJ), with a yield of 634.90 q/ha in AAU trials. Maturity, parentage, plant type and season are not available in the retrieved snippets.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No stress tolerance traits can be attributed to GAb 6; the salinity, disease and pest snippets relate to other items in the same documents. The variety is rated 'unclear' for stress tolerance, and full-text review of the AAU recommendation booklet and JAM minutes is advised.

drought.details: GNRB-1 is noted as tolerant to abiotic stresses, including drought. It is mentioned as a standard check in studies under drought conditions and hybrids involving GNRB-1 have shown excellent results in abiotic stresses like drought. Research involves assessing accessions highly tolerant to drought, along with submergence and anaerobic germination.

heat.details: GNRB-1 is generally tolerant to abiotic stresses including heat stress and high temperatures. It is identified as a brinjal variety useful for developing heat-tolerant varieties and is part of studies related to heat stress mitigation.

salinity.details: GNRB-1 is noted as tolerant to abiotic stresses, including salinity. Hybrids involving GNRB-1 show excellent results in abiotic stress such as salinity. It is mentioned in contexts of salt-resistant/tolerant rootstocks and studies involving salt media, indicating some level of tolerance or utility in breeding for salinity tolerance.

flood.details: No specific details regarding flood tolerance beyond general abiotic stress tolerance. However, submergence tolerance is mentioned.

disease_resistance.summary: GNRB-1 is tolerant to Phomopsis blight and exhibits low incidence of little leaf disease (3.90% reaction). It is generally tolerant to biotic stress.

pest_resistance.summary: GNRB-1 is tolerant to biotic stress and shows moderate resistance against stem borer. It is also mentioned in the context of pest management and resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields include 120-135 quintals per hectare (q/ha) and 301.74 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: GNRB-1 is recommended for general cultivation in brinjal growing areas of Gujarat state and has been evaluated in various agricultural university meetings (AGRESCO).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to brinjal growing areas, particularly recommended for South Gujarat farmers.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: GNRB-1 features anthocyanin on the stem and young purple-green leaves.
agronomic_details.field_trials: GNRB-1 has been part of numerous agricultural evaluations and recommendations. It served as a check variety in comparisons with other brinjal genotypes (e.g., GRB 5, Swarna Mani Black, GOB 1) and in line x tester mating designs. Trials include assessing its response to foliar application of Novel Organic Liquid Nutrients and its performance as seedlings under protected cultivation/polyhouse conditions. It has been recommended in AGRESCO meetings and annual reports of agricultural universities.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not specified
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: GNRB-1 is used as a standard check in line x tester mating designs for studying gene action. Hybrids involving GNRB-1, such as GNRB-1 × CH-215 and GNRB-1 × NBL-5, have been developed to increase fruit yield through heterosis and are also screened for tolerance to anaerobic germination, submergence, and drought. The presence of anthocyanin on the stem and young purple-green leaves is a distinguishing morphological characteristic.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety has biotic stress traits (lower little leaf disease, jassid, whitefly and fruit borer incidence than the check) and yield information. However, there is no peer-reviewed citation, only institutional listings (JAU page, notification list). That fits the 'some stress trait, no citation' tier (50) rather than the 75 tier. The listings confirm release and notification but give no stress evidence. Abiotic stress, markers and trial data are absent.

dashboard_data.stress_tolerance_yesno: Yes (biotic only: little leaf, jassid, whitefly, fruit borer; relative to check)
dashboard_data.key_attributes: Long-fruited; 70-75 days; 15-20 t/ha; green rough bifurcated calyx; lower pest and little leaf incidence than check

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Gujarat Brinjal Long-1 (released 2002 by GAU, Anand) is a long-fruited, 70-75 day variety yielding 15-20 t/ha, adapted to Gujarat brinjal areas. It showed lower little leaf disease and lower jassid, whitefly and fruit borer incidence than check Junagadh Long. Evidence is limited to institutional records, with no peer-reviewed citations or abiotic stress data.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Long-fruited brinjal, cross of Bt Pusa Purple x Pusa Kranti, maturing in 70-75 days with 15-20 t/ha yield. Suited to Gujarat; notified in 2003 (448(E)).
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Relative tolerance to little leaf disease, jassid, whitefly and fruit borer versus the check, based on institutional data only. No evidence for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. No molecular or published support.

disease_resistance.summary: Little leaf: low incidence at Anand compared with the checks GOB-1 and GJB-2 (AAU). This is a relative comparison, not a formal resistance rating. In a GRB-5 comparison trial, GAOB-2 used as a state check recorded little leaf incidence of 5.02%; the digest states this is a check value and not a GAOB-2 resistance rating. No other disease resistance evidence found.

pest_resistance.summary: Whitefly: low numbers per leaf at Anand compared with the checks GOB-1 and GJB-2 (AAU). This is a relative comparison, not a formal resistance rating. In the GRB-5 comparison trial, GAOB-2 as state check recorded 2.58 jassids per leaf, 3.22 whitefly per leaf and 3.28% fruit borer; the digest states these are check values and not resistance ratings. Bt-brinjal and fruit-and-shoot-borer material concerned other events and varieties and was discarded. No other pest resistance evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: AAU reports an average of 444 q/ha (about 44,400 kg/ha). The CSC record gives 15,000 to 20,000 kg/ha (150 to 200 q/ha). These values differ substantially and the digest does not resolve the discrepancy. In the GRB-5 comparison trials, GAOB-2 averaged 358.74 q/ha as a state check.
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location data exist from the GRB-5 comparison trials at Junagadh, Anand, Ladol and Navsari (see field_trials). No formal stability analysis across environments was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: suitable for cultivation under the brinjal growing area of Gujarat. AAU release page: irrigated Kharif-Rabi conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CALYX GREEN IN COLOUR WITH ROUGH SURFACE AND BIFURCATED ; WHITISH GREEN SMALL STAR LIKE STRUCTURE AT THE BOTTOM OF THE FRUITS. Fruit type (AAU): pinkish purple skin, obovate shape, medium size, prickles on pedicel and calyx. The MVRS parental table describes the same fruit traits (solitary, obovate, purple). Plant habit and spacing: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Anand: 36% and 29% higher fruit yield than GOB-1 and GJB-2, respectively (AAU). (2) Quality: higher vitamin C, anthocyanin and total soluble sugars than GOB-1 (AAU). (3) GRB-5 comparison trials at Junagadh, Anand, Ladol and Navsari: GAOB-2 as state check averaged 358.74 q/ha against 395.04 q/ha for GRB-5 (Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry, 2021). (4) Seed health: a 2018 seed-mycoflora study reported GAOB-2 germination and seedling-length values against GOB-1, Doli-5, GABH-3 and ABH-1; the digest gives no numeric values. (5) Release date: AAU lists a state release in 2013 (45th SSSC), which does not match the CSC year of 2015-04-07; the discrepancy is unresolved.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: SSR genetic distance of 0.30 between GAOB-2 and line AB 20-07 (MVRS parental diversity study). No other marker data found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL or marker-trait mapping study naming GAOB-2 was found. In MVRS hybrid studies, GAOB-2 was a good combiner for fruit weight, fruit girth and TSS when used as a parent or tester. Crosses with GAOB-2 showed heterobeltiosis for yield and yield components (e.g., AB 20-19 x GAOB 2).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: all findings below refer to "Gujarat Anand Oblong Brinjal-2" (GAOB-2), the CSC release name. No search result linked the Seednet name "GUJARAT BRINJAL LONG-1" to this variety, so that name has no evidence under any heading.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Searches were run on the variety name, and the only related material was the AAU release page (irrigated Kharif-Rabi conditions, no stress data). -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-oblong-brinjal-2

DISEASE AND PEST
Low incidence of little leaf disease and low whitefly numbers per leaf compared with the checks GOB-1 and GJB-2 at Anand. -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-oblong-brinjal-2
In a GRB-5 comparison trial, GAOB-2 used as a state check recorded little leaf 5.02%, jassids 2.58 per leaf, whitefly 3.22 per leaf and fruit borer 3.28%. These are check values, not GAOB-2 resistance ratings. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue4S/PartA/S-10-3-43-877.pdf
Bt-brinjal and fruit-and-shoot-borer pages discussed other events and varieties and were discarded. The mite-control recommendation on the MVRS page is crop-level, not variety-specific, and was discarded. -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/251/236/1000

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Release details: AAU lists the variety as a state release in 2013 (45th SSSC). The CSC/Seednet year of 2015-04-07 does not match this 2013 date; the discrepancy is unresolved. -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-released ; https://aau.in/variety_released
Yield: average 444 q/ha; at Anand it gave 36% and 29% higher fruit yield than GOB-1 and GJB-2. -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-oblong-brinjal-2
Quality: higher vitamin C, anthocyanin and total soluble sugars than GOB-1. -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-oblong-brinjal-2
Fruit type: pinkish purple skin, obovate shape, medium size, prickles on pedicel and calyx. -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-oblong-brinjal-2 ; the same traits (solitary, obovate, purple) appear in the MVRS parental table. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13503658/
Comparison trial: in GRB-5 trials at Junagadh, Anand, Ladol and Navsari, GAOB-2 averaged 358.74 q/ha as state check, against 395.04 q/ha for GRB-5. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue4S/PartA/S-10-3-43-877.pdf
Seed health: in a 2018 seed-mycoflora study, GAOB-2 showed seed germination and seedling-length values reported against GOB-1, Doli-5, GABH-3 and ABH-1. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-8-2019/G.J.%20Bhagora,%20et%20al.pdf
Maturity, plant habit and spacing: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No QTL or marker-trait mapping study naming GAOB-2 was found. -- searched; no evidence found.
GAOB-2 was used as a parent or tester in MVRS hybrid studies. It was a good combiner for fruit weight, fruit girth and TSS, and had a 0.30 SSR genetic distance from line AB 20-07. -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-56612-4 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13503658/
Crosses with GAOB-2 showed heterobeltiosis for yield and yield components, e.g. AB 20-19 × GAOB 2. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363541543_Genetics_of_growth_and_yield_attributing_traits_of_brinjal_Solanum_melongena_L_through_six_generation_mean_analysis
Parentage (Bt Pusa Purple × Pusa Kranti) as given in the record: no evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Anand Agricultural University (AAU), Anand, Gujarat, released as a state variety. -- https://www.aau.in/crop-varieties-released
Developing station: Main Vegetable Research Station (MVRS), Anand, which lists GAOB-2 among its releases. -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/251/236/1000
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): no evidence found. The MVRS scientists Rajesh R. Acharya and Mihir M. Pandya co-authored papers using GAOB 2 as a parent, but no source names them as its breeder, so they are not attributed here. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13503658/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-56612-4

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute: Main Vegetable Research Station, Anand Agricultural University, Anand 388110 (Gujarat). Office (02692)290251; Farm (02692)261817; Email rsmvrs@aau.in. -- https://www.aau.in/college-menu/251/236/1000 ; the same details appear at https://www.aau.in/achievements-1
Named breeder contact: no evidence found.

drought.details: No formal drought test was found. The digest reports a claimed suitability for areas with serious irrigation shortage, based on the variety's short (about 180-day) duration, not on a measured drought response. No mechanism data were found. Note: the digest's own contrast between the 180-day duration and the CSC maturity value of 45 to 60 days is unresolved (see agronomic_performance).

heat.details: No heat tolerance data were found for this variety in the digest. The CSC stress_reaction field states 'H 7 THRIVES WELL UNDER SUMMER CONDITIONS ALSO.' This statement refers to 'H 7', which does not match this variety's name or code, so it was not attributed to IISR Pragati.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance data were found for this variety.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data were found for this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne incognita): moderately resistant, per the screening and release report and the institute variety page. Rhizome rot: field trial in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, recorded 4.51% incidence in IISR Pragati versus 2.12% in CO2, so IISR Pragati showed higher rhizome rot than the comparison variety in that trial; no resistance is claimed for rhizome rot. Leaf blotch and leaf spot: less frequent in IISR Pragati than in CO2 in the same trial. Rhizome rot, leaf blotch and leaf spot were all recorded across the three varieties tested in that trial. No other disease resistance was found in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The CSC pest_reaction field is 'Not Specified' and the digest contains no pest resistance findings for this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Mean yield 38 t/ha fresh rhizome, with up to 52 t/ha under favourable conditions; 30% and 34% higher than national and local varieties, per the institute page and the ResearchGate record. Pooled yield over three years was 14.52 kg per 3 m2 plot for Acc. 48, the highest of the accessions tested. The CSC average_yield field gives 30000 to 40000 Kg/Ha, which is broadly consistent with the 38 t/ha mean.
agronomic_details.stability: The Kerala trial at AICRPS centres (2013-16), on-farm trials and yield stability were reported only as table captions in the source; no stability values were given in the digest. The three-year pooled yield is the only multi-season figure found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The CSC adaptation_ecology field recommends release and cultivation in Haryana, Punjab and Delhi under irrigated conditions. The digest does not corroborate this and reports trials in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The CSC recommended states (Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Chhattisgarh) are also not corroborated by digest findings. The CSC adaptation and recommended-state fields are therefore in conflict and unverified against the digest.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 45 To 60Days (CSC record). Conflict: digest sources report a crop duration of 180 days, and some extension sources give 180-200 days. This discrepancy is unresolved.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. The CSC morphological_characteristics field is 'Not specified'.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu on-farm trial: rhizome rot 4.51% in IISR Pragati versus 2.12% in CO2; leaf blotch and leaf spot less frequent in IISR Pragati than CO2; all three varieties showed rhizome rot, leaf blotch and leaf spot. (2) Kerala trial 2013-16 at AICRPS centres with on-farm trials and yield stability reported; results are given only as table captions, so no values were available. (3) Three-year pooled trial: 14.52 kg per 3 m2 plot for Acc. 48, the highest of the tested accessions. (4) Greenhouse and field trial of 21 genotypes (2021-23): IISR Pragati gave high fresh yield per clump and high curcuminoids in some seasons. (5) Genetic variation study on turmeric genotypes: highest fresh rhizome yield per clump for IISR Pragati. (6) Quality traits: curcumin 5.02%, oleoresin 15.29%, essential oil 6.3%, dry recovery 15.95%. CSC agronomic_features also report excellent colour, very good keeping quality (13 days at room temperature), and good yield at 60 x 60 cm spacing with 80-90 kg N + 60 kg P2O5, plus weed control with 1-1.5 kg a.i. Stomp/HAT applied 3-4 days after transplanting; these are CSC-recorded features, not digest trial results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No marker study specific to this variety was found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL study specific to this variety was found. A genetic variation and trait association study on turmeric genotypes reports IISR Pragati with the highest fresh rhizome yield per clump among the genotypes studied; this is a phenotypic finding, not a QTL result.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

commercial_info.private_dealers: BSS Agro Solutions, Sangareddy, Telangana: listed as out of stock at Rs 50/kg. BSS Agro Ltd, Hyderabad, Telangana: Rs 40/kg, MOQ 1000 kg. Seednet listing for HISAR PRAGATI (brinjal) was not found and is not linked to this turmeric variety.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: IISR PRAGATI (turmeric, Curcuma longa)

Name check: The CSC name is IISR PRAGATI. The Seednet name is HISAR PRAGATI, listed under BRINJAL. None of the four searches returned a Seednet page, and no page linked HISAR PRAGATI to turmeric or brinjal. Every finding below refers to the turmeric variety IISR Pragati (also written Pragathi, and known as Acc. 48). The Seednet listing remains unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Moderately resistant to root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne incognita) in the screening and release report, with the same status listed on the institute's variety page -- https://spices.res.in/bpd/node/19 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324585658_A_new_short_duration_turmeric_variety_IISR_Pragati_-_a_boon_to_Indian_farmers
Suitability for areas with serious irrigation shortage is claimed, based on its 180-day duration; no formal drought test was found -- https://spices.icar.gov.in/pages/iisr-pragatiturmeric ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311133690_IISR_Pragati_-_New_Turmeric_Variety_from_ICAR_-_Indian_Institute_of_Spices_Research_Kozhikode_Kerala
No heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance data found for this variety -- searched under STRESS TOLERANCE, none found beyond the nematode and irrigation statements above

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderate root-knot nematode resistance is reported in the release literature and extension material -- https://arowest.com/spices/turmeric/varieties/iisr-pragati/ ; https://indianspices.com/sites/default/files/185.%20Institute%20Publication-Turmeric%20Extension%20Pamphlet%20-%20March%202022.pdf
Field trial in Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu: rhizome rot incidence was 4.51% in IISR Pragati versus 2.12% in CO2, with leaf blotch and leaf spot less frequent in IISR Pragati than CO2 -- https://www.magazines.cornous.com/downloadpdf/86
Rhizome rot, leaf blotch and leaf spot were all recorded across the three varieties tested in that trial -- https://www.magazines.cornous.com/downloadpdf/86

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Mean yield 38 t/ha fresh rhizome, with up to 52 t/ha under favourable conditions; 30% and 34% higher than national and local varieties -- https://spices.res.in/bpd/node/19 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311133690_IISR_Pragati_-_New_Turmeric_Variety_from_ICAR_-_Indian_Institute_of_Spices_Research_Kozhikode_Kerala
Crop duration 180 days; some extension sources give 180-200 days -- https://spices.res.in/bpd/node/19 ; https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/view/87633
Quality traits: curcumin 5.02%, oleoresin 15.29%, essential oil 6.3%, dry recovery 15.95% -- https://spices.res.in/bpd/node/19 ; https://www.indianspices.com/sites/default/files/cultivation_practices-TURMERIC-1.pdf
Pooled yield over three years of 14.52 kg per 3 m2 plot for Acc. 48, highest of the tested accessions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311133690_IISR_Pragati_-_New_Turmeric_Variety_from_ICAR_-_Indian_Institute_of_Spices_Research_Kozhikode_Kerala
Kerala trial 2013-16 at AICRPS centres, on-farm trials and yield stability reported (table captions) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324585658_A_new_short_duration_turmeric_variety_IISR_Pragati_-_a_boon_to_Indian_farmers
Greenhouse and field trial of 21 genotypes (2021-23): IISR Pragati gave high fresh yield per clump, and high curcuminoids in some seasons -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2214786124000652 ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/horticulture/articles/10.3389/fhort.2026.1899925/full

GENETICS AND QTL
Origin is a clonal selection from germplasm (Acc. 48) at IISR; the pedigree "R-34 x SAL-26" supplied in the request was not found in any source -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324585658_A_new_short_duration_turmeric_variety_IISR_Pragati_-_a_boon_to_Indian_farmers ; https://spices.res.in/bpd/node/19
Genetic variation and trait association study on turmeric genotypes reports IISR Pragati with highest fresh rhizome yield per clump -- https://updatepublishing.com/journal/index.php/josac/article/view/8589
No QTL or marker study specific to this variety found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR), Kozhikode, Kerala, through clonal selection -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324585658_A_new_short_duration_turmeric_variety_IISR_Pragati_-_a_boon_to_Indian_farmers
Named breeding scientists: D. Prasath, Santhosh J. Eapen, B. Sasikumar, H. J. Akshitha, N. K. Leela (scientists, IISR); R. Chitra and B. Mahender are co-authors on the 2018 report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324585658_A_new_short_duration_turmeric_variety_IISR_Pragati_-_a_boon_to_Indian_farmers ; https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/view/87633
Release year conflicts: 2016 (identified at the 27th AICRP on Spices group meeting, NRC Seed Spices, Ajmer, 2016), 2017 (spices.res.in and the 2017 issue of Indian Horticulture), and CVRC notification on 16 January 2018 (secondary aggregator only) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311133690_IISR_Pragati_-_New_Turmeric_Variety_from_ICAR_-_Indian_Institute_of_Spices_Research_Kozhikode_Kerala ; https://spices.res.in/bpd/node/19 ; https://arowest.com/spices/turmeric/varieties/iisr-pragati/

Name check: The searches for "BJC 1" and "JC-1" returned no pages naming either variety. Every hit for those strings was an unrelated product (a Cambridge exam, a tumour-drug paper, a US mustard-type article, or a DMH-11 hybrid). The only pages that touch this variety use the code "PC 6". Those pages are noted below. The "JC-1" name was searched alongside "mustard" and "PAU", and the Seednet "BRINJAL" crop label is not supported by any result. That label conflicts with the mustard crop and was not used.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches for BJC 1 or JC-1 with stress terms returned nothing for this variety. The nearest page is a general chapter on rapeseed-mustard breeding for abiotic stress, which does not name this variety -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/75542

The PAU oilseed pages mention Alternaria and aphid work only in general project terms, not for this variety -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=297&intDepTitleID=0&intLinkID=9

Nothing in that extract gives maturity, yield figures, or a link to BJC 1 or JC-1 -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
PAU's College of Agriculture page lists "PC 6" as a 2016 release described as a determinate African Sarson variety suitable for mechanical harvesting. That description places PC 6 under African sarson rather than Indian mustard, so the crop identity needs checking before use -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=20&intLinkID=9

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance of Kanika. The searches returned only disease, yield and storage-pest material. A genomics review of mungbean abiotic stress mentions Kanika (IPM 302-2) as having wider adaptability, but the review is general and gives no Kanika-specific drought data.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance of Kanika. The searches returned only disease, yield and storage-pest material.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance of Kanika. The searches returned only disease, yield and storage-pest material.

disease_resistance.summary: Yellow mosaic disease (MYMV/MYMIV): (1) Rated highly resistant to yellow mosaic disease (MYMV) in the national central-varieties table for mungbean (DPD). (2) ICAR-IIPR's release note describes Kanika as highly resistant to yellow mosaic disease. (3) A 2026 Frontiers in Genetics study lists Kanika as moderately resistant to MYMIV (mungbean yellow mosaic India virus), among 13 moderately resistant mungbean genotypes. (4) Listed among mungbean varieties for yellow mosaic disease management in a biotic-stress review of pulses; that review gives no reaction score for Kanika. Cercospora leaf spot (CLS): Rated highly resistant to Cercospora leaf spot in the DPD national central-varieties table for mungbean. Other diseases: Named among varieties carrying host-plant resistance in a 2024 SATSA Mukhapatra review of greengram and blackgram diseases. This is a general list, not a Kanika-specific trial. No other disease reaction data found in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Cowpea weevil (Callosobruchus maculatus), a storage pest: Kanika (IPM-302-2) is among the most resistant greengram germplasm in a storage-pest screen, recording a low egg count per 100 seeds. No field pest reaction data (e.g., for sucking pests or pod borers) was found in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Potential yield of 10-12 q/ha (about 1000-1200 kg/ha) per the DPD varieties list. ICAR-IIPR reports a yield potential of 11-12 q/ha, with 27% yield superiority over the best check IPM 02-3. A general genomics review lists Kanika (IPM 302-2) among varieties yielding 1.2-1.4 t/ha, with no Kanika trial data given.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The genomics review describes wider adaptability in general terms only, with no environment-level stability data for Kanika.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for kharif and spring seasons in Uttar Pradesh (DPD state-wise list and DPD mungbean varieties document).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. The digest gives no morphological or agronomic feature details beyond yield and duration.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Kharif 2022 field trial at ITM University Gwalior: Kanika was one of ten genotypes tested for seed longevity after chemical seed-spray treatments to induce seed dormancy. It had the lowest EC value at two months after harvest. (2) ICAR-IIPR reports 27% yield superiority over the best check IPM 02-3, with yield potential of 11-12 q/ha. (3) The 2026 Frontiers study and the 2024 SATSA review contain no Kanika yield trial data. (4) The genomics review cites a 1.2-1.4 t/ha yield range for Kanika, but gives no trial design or site details. No further field trial results were found in the digest.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Kanika was used as a genotype in KASP marker development for MYMIV resistance genes (TMV gene and F-box/LRR gene) in mungbean and urdbean. The study's allele data for Kanika are consistent with moderate resistance. The F-box/LRR allele result differs between the two entries in the digest, so this result should be treated as unresolved. No marker positions were given in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL mapping study specific to Kanika was found in the searched sources.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: MYMIV resistance genes studied through KASP markers: TMV gene and F-box/LRR gene. Pedigree: PM 4 x EC 398897 (ICAR-IIPR and the Frontiers study record the same cross). No gene-level mechanism specific to Kanika was reported beyond these markers.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of Kanika. The four searches returned only disease, yield and storage-pest material. -- No URL (no matching page returned)
- Listed as moderately resistant to MYMIV (mungbean yellow mosaic India virus) in a 2026 Frontiers genetics study that scored Kanika among 13 moderately resistant mungbean genotypes. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/genetics/articles/10.3389/fgene.2026.1844678/xml

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rated highly resistant to yellow mosaic disease (MYMV) and to Cercospora leaf spot (CLS) in the national central-varieties table for mungbean. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- ICAR-IIPR's own release note describes Kanika as highly resistant to yellow mosaic disease. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Named among varieties carrying host-plant resistance in a 2024 SATSA Mukhapatra review of greengram and blackgram diseases. Note: this is a general list, not a Kanika-specific trial. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380395530_Major_Diseases_of_Green_Gram_Black_Gram_and_Their_Integrated_Management_Strategies
- Listed among mungbean varieties for yellow mosaic disease management in a biotic-stress review of pulses. Note: the review does not give a reaction score for Kanika. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378374030_BIOTIC_STRESS_OF_MAJOR_PULSES_AND_THEIR_MANAGEMENT
- Among the most resistant greengram germplasm to cowpea weevil (Callosobruchus maculatus) in a storage-pest screen, with IPM-302-2 (Kanika) recording a low egg count per 100 seeds. -- https://indianentomology.org/index.php/ije/article/view/2270

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Potential yield of 10-12 q/ha, duration about 70 days, suitable for kharif and spring seasons in Uttar Pradesh. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Yield potential of 11-12 q/ha, and 27% yield superiority over the best check IPM 02-3 as reported by ICAR-IIPR. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- A genomics review of mungbean abiotic stress lists Kanika (IPM 302-2) among varieties yielding 1.2-1.4 t/ha with wider adaptability. Note: the review is general; no Kanika trial data is given. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339418850_Genomic_Approaches_to_Abiotic_Stresses_in_Mungbean
- Seed longevity under storage after chemical seed-spray treatments: Kanika was among ten genotypes tested in a Kharif 2022 field trial at ITM University Gwalior, and had the lowest EC value at two months after harvest. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379044590_Impact_of_Chemical_Spray_on_Seed_Longevity_for_Induction_of_Seed_Dormancy_in_Mungbean_Vigna_radiata_L

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: PM 4 × EC 398897 (ICAR-IIPR states the cross; the Frontiers study records the same pedigree). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/ ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/genetics/articles/10.3389/fgene.2026.1844678/pdf
- Used as a genotype in KASP marker development for MYMIV resistance genes (TMV gene and F-box/LRR gene) in mungbean and urdbean. Note: the study's allele data for Kanika are moderately resistant, and the F-box/LRR allele result differs between the two entries. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/genetics/articles/10.3389/fgene.2026.1844678/full
- No QTL mapping study specific to Kanika was found. -- No URL

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research (IIPR), Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. The release was from the State Variety Release Committee (SVRC) of UP in 2018. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- IIPR's list of pulses varieties developed 2014-2025 includes Mungbean IPM 302-2 (Kanika), 2018. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/research-achievements/ (via translated page: https://www-icar--iipr-org-in.translate.goog/research-achievements/?_x_tr_sl=en&_x_tr_tl=hi&_x_tr_hl=hi&_x_tr_pto=tc)
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. No page named a breeder for Kanika.
- Institute head listed as Dr Bansa Singh, Director, on a government listing page for IIPR (the page is undated and may be out of date). -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/icar-indian-institute-pulses-research

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur 208 024, Uttar Pradesh, India (postal address as given on the IIPR varieties page). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/varieties/
- Institute website: iipr.icar.gov.in (given on a directory listing; the Wikipedia entry gives the same domain). -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Pulses_Research
- Director: Dr Bansa Singh (name only; no email or phone found). -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/organisations/ministry-and-departments/icar-indian-institute-pulses-research
- Breeder email and phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Sen Gupta et al. (2026). Development and validation of diagnostic KASP markers for MYMIV resistance in urdbean (Kanika included as a mungbean genotype). Frontiers in Genetics. -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fgene.2026.1844678
- Authors not confirmed (listed on a ResearchGate profile of ITM University Gwalior; the author order for the paper is not verified) (2023). Impact of Chemical Spray on Seed Longevity for Induction of Seed Dormancy in Mungbean (Vigna radiata L.). Journal/report not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379044590_Impact_of_Chemical_Spray_on_Seed_Longevity_for_Induction_of_Seed_Dormancy_in_Mungbean_Vigna_radiata_L
- Authors not confirmed (2024). Major Diseases of Green Gram, Black Gram and Their Integrated Management Strategies. SATSA Mukhapatra, Annual Technical Issue 28 (ISSN 0971-975X). Kanika is named only in a list of resistant varieties. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380395530_Major_Diseases_of_Green_Gram_Black_Gram_and_Their_Integrated_Management_Strategies
- Authors not confirmed (year not confirmed). Screening of Greengram Germplasm against Cowpea Weevil Callosobruchus maculatus (F). Indian Journal of Entomology. -- https://indianentomology.org/index.php/ije/article/view/2270
- No AICRP/ICAR annual report or KrishiKosh thesis specific to Kanika was returned by the searches. -- No URL

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Kanika seed sales from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU or private dealers. The only "Kanika" seed-sale page returned was for a different product (a fruit-type variety, not a pulse), which was discarded.
- Seednet listing: not returned by any search, so the Seednet record under the crop name "BRINJAL" was not verified. -- No URL

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttar Pradesh: Kanika is listed for kharif and spring in the state-wise pulses varieties list maintained by the Directorate of Pulses Development, GoI. -- https://dpd.gov.in/1.%20Final%20State-wise%20within%2010%20Yrs.%20Pulses%20(Compile).pdf ; https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Name and crop check: The seednet crop label "BRINJAL" conflicts with every source, which identifies Kanika (IPM 302-2) as a greengram/mungbean (Vigna radiata) variety. The "BRINJAL" label looks like a data error on the Seednet record and should be corrected before use. Release year 2018 is confirmed by ICAR-IIPR; the exact release date 2018-08-10 was not verified in any source.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Krati (KLB 2008-4), lentil. Seednet name checked: Kranti (listed under BRINJAL)

Searches run: 4 (release/traits; breeder/institute; research papers; Seednet "Kranti" brinjal). Evidence below refers to the lentil variety under "Krati" unless a line says otherwise.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Krati found in the searches. The only trait notes are wilt and rust resistance (see DISEASE AND PEST). -- No evidence found (searched: Krati release traits, 2 queries)

DISEASE AND PEST: Krati is listed as resistant to wilt in the central/state lentil variety tables. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
Krati is described as resistant to rust and wilt by the university. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/
Pest resistance (pod borer, aphid, etc.) for Krati: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Yield 18-20 q/ha and days to maturity 115-120 in the central/state release table (the table lists the variety as released in 2015 from CSAUA&T Kanpur, large seed). -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
University description: early maturity of about 125 days, light foliage, semi-erect plant habit, reddish-grey bold seed, profuse branching and many pods. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/ ; https://csauk.ac.in/director-aes/
Sowing window: suited to late-sown conditions across Uttar Pradesh. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/
Multi-location trial results for Krati: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage recorded as LG 362 x DPL 62 in the AICRP list (the institutional "Parentage: Not specified" field in the record is therefore incomplete). -- https://icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
QTL, marker or genomic studies specific to Krati: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Developing institution is Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology (CSAUA&T), Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/
The lead breeder of Krati is not named in any source found. The Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding at Kanpur is listed with Prof. Vijay Kumar Yadav as Professor and Head, but no source ties him to Krati. -- https://csauk.ac.in/genetics-plant-breeding/
Lentil research sits under the university's Legumes research section (mandate covers lentil improvement). -- https://csauk.ac.in/director-aes/
Krati is also listed among varieties released by the university's Directorate of Research. -- https://csauk.ac.in/director-aes/

CONTACT DETAILS:
Institute: Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. Official website: https://csauk.ac.in (department and director pages above). Official email, phone and full postal address of the university or the Genetics and Plant Breeding department: No evidence found in the searches.
Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, Kanpur: Prof. Vijay Kumar Yadav (Professor and Head); Prof. Rajendra Kumar Yadav (Professor); Prof. Mahak Singh (Professor, Oilseeds section). Their email and phone numbers: No evidence found. -- https://csauk.ac.in/genetics-plant-breeding/
A researcher profile lists a Dr. Shweta (Breeder, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, Kanpur) with no contact details. It does not establish a link to Krati. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Dr-3

PUBLICATIONS:
Parihar et al. (2025). Environmental adaptation of small-seeded lentils (Lens culinaris) in Indian climates: Insights into crop-environment interactions, mega-environments, and breeding approaches. Crop Science -- DOI 10.1002/csc2.70090 (https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/csc2.70090). Note: the result shows Manoj Katiyar (Genetics and Plant Breeding, CSAUA&T Kanpur) as a co-author; the full author list was not captured, and the visible text does not name Krati.
Singh, M. et al. (2022). Evaluation and identification of advanced lentil interspecific derivatives... Frontiers in Plant Science -- DOI 10.3389/fpls.2022.936572 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9499259/). Note: about other lines (Jammu Lentil 144 and 71); does not mention Krati.
No Krati-specific peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report entry or KrishiKosh thesis found.

SEED AVAILABILITY: A private seed-company product list includes KLB 2008-4 (Krati) among lentil varieties. -- https://www.indiaseeds.com/products.html (commercial listing, not verified).
NSC, UP State Seed Corporation, KVK or CSAUA&T seed-sale listings for Krati: No evidence found. The university says it produces breeder, foundation and certified seed of its crops. -- https://csauk.ac.in/achievments/

RECOMMENDED STATES: Whole Uttar Pradesh (state release). -- https://icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
Listed in the DPD state-wise recommendation for pulses (within 10 years, from 2011 onward) for lentil. -- https://dpd.gov.in/1.%20Final%20State-wise%20within%2010%20Yrs.%20Pulses%20(Compile).pdf

SEEDNET NAME "KRANTI" (CROP LISTED AS BRINJAL): No Seednet record was found for a lentil variety called Kranti. The brinjal results were unrelated varieties: Pusa Kranti (IARI, New Delhi) -- https://www.nhb.gov.in/pdf/vegetable/brinjal/bri012.pdf ; Azad Kranti (a brinjal variety listed in a CSAUA&T-linked characteristic table) -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/fbrinjal.pdf ; and commercial hybrids such as F1 Kranti -- https://www.indiamart.com/dev-seeds/brinjal-seeds.html. None of these is KLB 2008-4. The Seednet "Kranti" / BRINJAL entry therefore appears to be a mismatched record and should not be linked to Krati.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Lotus (variety_name = seednet_variety_name = "Lotus"; crop = BRINJAL / horticultural)

Name check: both the CSC release-minutes name and the Seednet name are "Lotus," so one set of searches covered both. Four searches were run: release and traits, breeder and institution, research papers, and seed availability. None returned a brinjal variety called Lotus.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The stress search returned lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) gene and salt-alkali studies, Lotus forage-legume (Lotus corniculatus/tenuis) submergence studies, and other brinjal genotypes (ICS-BR-1351, HBR-314-E, MHBJ 112, IIHR lines). None names a brinjal variety "Lotus." Discarded as other crops or varieties.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The results mentioned Arka Nidhi, Arka Harshitha, Arka Avinash, Pusa Oishiki and Bt brinjal (Mahyco EE-1, Janak, BSS 793). These name different varieties and were discarded. The NBRI "Namoh 108" resistance claim is for an ornamental lotus flower and was also discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. The trial results (Arka Nidhi insecticide trial, Fusarium bio-organic trial, AICRP genotype evaluations) concern other varieties or unnamed genotypes.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The genetics results covered Nelumbo gene-function work and brinjal heterosis in Utkal and Arka lines, none of which names a brinjal "Lotus."

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. No breeder, developing institute, or station was tied to a brinjal variety named Lotus. The Pusa Oishiki page is ICAR-IARI, but it names a different variety and was not attributed. The Arka varieties are IIHR and the Bt lines are Mahyco, and those were also not attributed.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No institute or breeder contact was located for this variety. The only contacts surfaced were for unrelated institutes and companies, which were not used.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Brinjal papers returned (salinity-tolerance genotype studies, AICRP-based genetic variability studies, and Bt-brinjal trial critiques) do not name the variety Lotus. None was listed.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed results were for lotus flower and rhizome seeds (Nelumbo), generic brinjal retailers, and brinjal seed packs under other names. None offered a brinjal variety called Lotus. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or Seednet listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. "Various states" in the record is not supported by any source found.

Summary for the record: the variety "Lotus" under BRINJAL could not be verified. Nothing in the four searches confirms its existence, release, parentage, or breeder. Before this record is used, check the Seednet entry directly (seednet.gov.in) and the CSC release notification for the 2015-04-07 date, and confirm the breeding institute with the relevant AICRP on Vegetable Crops centre or ICAR-IIHR.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Searches covered "Pant Brinjal Hybrid-1" (the Seednet name) and "PBH-4" (the variety code, which matches Punjab Agricultural University's hybrid naming). The evidence for the Pantnagar hybrid and the PAU PBH-4 hybrid is separate. The record's institution (PAU) and parentage (PB 129 x PB 225) do not match the Pantnagar sources, which give PB 121 x PB 225 and credit GBPUA&T Pantnagar. No source found links "Brinjal Hybrid" or the CSC release to either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Pant Brinjal Hybrid-1 is listed as tolerant to bacterial wilt, with no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found. To learnt to bacterial wilt. -- http://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/lec05.html (wording is garbled in source; read as "tolerant to bacterial wilt")

DISEASE AND PEST
Bacterial wilt tolerance for Pant Brinjal Hybrid-1 (single listing, see above) -- http://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/lec05.html
No pest-resistance evidence found for this hybrid. The only pest-resistance result was for Bt brinjal, which is a different product (Mahyco EE-1 event) -- https://www.isaaa.org/resources/publications/pocketk/35/ (discarded for relevance)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Fruit is described as long and borne in clusters -- http://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/lec05.html
Yield is given only as a category for all F1 brinjal hybrids (55-80 t/ha). It is not specific to this hybrid -- http://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/lec05.html
Parentage in the source is PB 121 x PB225, not PB 129 x PB 225 as in the record -- http://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/lec05.html ; also http://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/pdf/lec05.pdf
Maturity, trial results and multi-location data: No evidence found.
Release notification and 2015 release year: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Heterosis and combining-ability papers were returned, but none names Pant Brinjal Hybrid-1 or PBH-4 (e.g., https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/389/321 names only PBH-3, PBHR-41, PBH-5). Discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Pant Brinjal Hybrid-1 was developed at Pantnagar, with brinjal breeding using indigenous germplasm: Improved cultivars like Pant Samrat, Pant Rituraj, Pant Brinjal-4 and Pant Brinjal Hybrid-1 have been developed at Pantnagar utilizing the brinjal germplasm. -- https://ishs.org/ishs-article/752_114/
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.
PBH-4 (code in record): PAU released and lists PBH-4 among its brinjal hybrids, but no PAU breeder name was found -- https://www.pau.edu/content/banner/6297.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found for either name.
No institute contact details found for GBPUA&T Pantnagar or for PAU's brinjal programme in the retrieved text. Institute-level contact to be taken from https://www.pau.edu (PAU, Ludhiana) and https://pantnagar.ac.in (GBPUA&T) after verification; neither page was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
Only the ISHS conference-paper record for Pantnagar brinjal improvement was found. Authors and year were not shown in the retrieved text: Not shown (n.d.). Current status of brinjal improvement using indigenous germplasm at Pantnagar. ISHS -- https://ishs.org/ishs-article/752_114/
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI specifically on Pant Brinjal Hybrid-1 or PBH-4 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
PAU invites seed-production partners for PBH-4 (with PBH-3, PBH-6 and PBHR-41) for 2024-25 and 2025-26 in Maharashtra -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewBannerDetail&_act=manageBanner&intID=6297 ; https://www.pau.edu/content/banner/6297.pdf
Retail or NSC availability of Pant Brinjal Hybrid-1 from GBPUA&T: No evidence found. The listings returned (e.g., Pancha Ganga PBH-418, VNR-218, Sungro, Seminis) are other products and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found for either name. The state lists found belong to other hybrids (PB-67, PHBL-51) and were discarded -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/brinjal-hybrid-variety-pb-67/ (not this variety)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
IDENTITY NOTE: The evidence splits into two different varieties. HI 8737 (Pusa Anmol) is a durum wheat variety from IARI, and the release-year and state fields match it. The parentage (Pusa Purple Long x Hyderpur) and the Seednet crop (BRINJAL) match an IARI brinjal F1 hybrid also named Pusa Anmol. Each heading below says which one the evidence refers to. Do not merge the two records.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Wheat (HI 8737 / Pusa Anmol, variety_name): Released as rust and Karnal bunt resistant, for irrigated timely-sown high-fertility conditions; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found. A NEW RUST AND KARNAL BUNT RESISTANT, HIGH YIELDING DURUM WHEAT VARIETY FOR HIGH FERTILITY IRRIGATED TIMELY SOWN -- https://asthafoundation.in/img/SV%20Sai%20Prasad.pdf
- Wheat: Stem rust resistance is conferred by two dominant genes in HI 8737 (pathotype-specific Pgt test in central India). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432282_IARI_Indore_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Vol_62
- Brinjal (Seednet name PASA ANMOL, crop BRINJAL): No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wheat: Rust and Karnal bunt resistance (see above). Also described as resistant to stem and leaf rusts. -- https://asthafoundation.in/img/SV%20Sai%20Prasad.pdf
- Brinjal (Pusa Anmol): Listed among cultivars with appreciable resistance to shoot and fruit borer (Leucinodes orbonalis) in a BHU IPM study. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344164741_Parasitisation_of_brinjal_shoot_and_fruit_borer_Leucinodes_orbonalis_Guenee_by_Trathala_flavoorbitalis_Cameron
- Brinjal (Pusa Anmol): Grouped as susceptible to red spider mite in a 2014–2015 screening of 25 brinjal varieties. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349368115_Response_of_brinjal_Solanum_melongena_Guen_varieties_for_the_resistant_reaction_against_brinjal_shoot_and_fruit_borer_BSFB_and_red_spider_mites_RSM
- Brinjal: No bacterial wilt or Fusarium data for Pusa Anmol found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Wheat: Tested for three years at 39 trial locations across the Central Zone; under timely-sown conditions it averaged 51.07 q/ha against checks HI 8498 (48.32) and MPO 1215 (49.05). -- https://asthafoundation.in/img/SV%20Sai%20Prasad.pdf
- Wheat: Recommended by Madhya Bharat state for 2022-23, with yield potential 65.00 q/ha and average 53.04 q/ha. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/recommended-wheat-varieties-for-rabi-season-for-farmers-of-madhya-pradesh/
- Wheat: Bold grain with 1000-grain weight about 46 g, and average yield 51.42 q/ha across three sowing dates in the Indore trials. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348432282_IARI_Indore_Madhya_Bharat_Wheat_News_Vol_62
- Brinjal (Pusa Anmol): Reported about 80% more yield than Pusa Purple Long; yield potential 40–50 t/ha in one source and 62 t/ha in another. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/ta/aas/brinjal.html ; https://eagri.org/eagri50/HORT281/lec05.html
- Brinjal: No duration or multi-location trial data found specific to this hybrid.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Wheat pedigree: HI 8177/HI 8158//HI 8498. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344250282_Wheat_A_Reference_Guide_Highlighting_Special_Features_of_Varieties_Recommended_for_Cultivation_in_India
- Wheat: Rust resistance genes identified (two dominant genes in HI 8737); no QTL or marker mapping study found.
- Brinjal parentage: Pusa Purple Long x Hyderpur (F1 hybrid). -- https://www.horticultureguruji.in/cultivation-of-brinjal-2/
- Brinjal: No QTL or marker studies found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Wheat: Developed by ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Indore; the CSC approved release in 2014. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/IARI-News/Newsletter_October-December-2014.pdf
- Wheat: Released under the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release; notified via S.O. 196(E) dated 28.1.2015. -- https://asthafoundation.in/img/SV%20Sai%20Prasad.pdf
- Brinjal: Developed at IARI, New Delhi (F1 hybrid). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/ta/aas/brinjal.html
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found for either the wheat or the brinjal line in the search results.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone or postal address for HI 8737 or the brinjal Pusa Anmol was returned. The institute-level IARI newsletter contains no contact details.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: Citations exist (ICAR, PAU, NHB, ISAAA, IIVR) but they are descriptive and give no variety-specific stress tolerance. The drought-tolerance snippet comes from a different crop's variety that shares the name, so it is not credited. The only stress-related statements are crop-level cautions (waterlogging, low temperature). The score reflects limited yield information (475-500 q/ha), citations of moderate quality, and no confirmed stress trait. A score of 40-50 is defensible, and 50 is chosen because the variety is documented as a thornless, round, spring-season type. The Gujarat methodology's 60 requires at least one citation, which exists, so the score could be argued up to 60. No Gujarat-specific trials were found, so it stays at the conservative 50.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Punjab Bahar is a PAU-developed thornless, round, dark purple brinjal selected from local material and suited to spring cultivation, with a reported yield of 475-500 q/ha. No variety-specific stress, disease or pest tolerance is verified. The drought-tolerance text in the search results belongs to a same-named bottle gourd, so evidence quality is low.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Thornless, round, dark purple fruited brinjal from PAU, plant height about 93 cm, spring season, yield 475-500 q/ha. Maturity and Gujarat adaptation are not documented.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No verified drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, and no disease or pest resistance data. Drought-tolerance statements are confounded with the same-named bottle gourd variety. Brinjal in general is sensitive to waterlogging and cold.

agronomic_performance.yield_potential: 45000 to 55000 kg/ha (45-55 t/ha). Other sources: 51.6 t/ha (eAgri), 516 q/ha (krishisewa), 520-540 q/ha (ICAR Kharif advisory 2025), 40-50 t/ha (TNAU).
agronomic_performance.yield_stability: Not formally documented. The variety is still recommended in ICAR advisories (2021-2025), which suggests continued use across seasons, but no multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: RECOMMENDED FOR RELEASE AND CULTIVATION IN DELHI, UP, PUNJAB AND ANDHRA PRADESH. Autumn-winter and spring-summer crops of the Central Gangetic Plains; normal crop of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Notified for Zones IV, VII and VIII (ISAAA). Not recommended specifically for Gujarat.
agronomic_performance.maturity_days: 80 to 85 days from sowing to first picking
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Vigorous, non-spiny plants with semi-erect branches; long, glossy, dark purple fruits (TNAU, eAgri, MapMyCrop).
agronomic_performance.field_trial_results: No detailed multi-location trial data in the results. Only release-level yield figures and advisory recommendations. One ResearchGate/Academia item mentions a randomized complete block design with Pusa Hybrid-5, but the snippet is truncated and its crop is unclear.
agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: Listed repeatedly in ICAR Rabi and Kharif agro-advisories, the TNAU checklist, the NHRDF souvenir and the IARI technology options, which indicates sustained recommendation. No direct farmer feedback surveys were found.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: There are many citations and sources confirming the variety's identity, yield (45-55 t/ha) and recommendation by ICAR/IARI. However, no source gives variety-specific evidence of stress tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, flood, disease or pest). The official stress reaction is 'NOT APPLICABLE', and the drought and heat hits are ambiguous or generic. The 75 and 60 bands require at least one stress trait with a citation or a citation with weak stress traits. Citations exist for yield and adaptation, which would fit 60, but the lack of any stress trait and the absence of Gujarat in the recommended states led to a conservative score. Evidence of agronomic merit is moderate. Score band chosen: 50 (a defensible range is 40-60).

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Long glossy dark purple fruits; F1 hybrid; 45-55 t/ha; 80-85 days to first picking; fertility-responsive; poor in poor soils; no major disease or pest seen in release trials.
dashboard_data.state_acronyms: DL, UP, PB, AP, KL, TN, KA
dashboard_data.seasons: Autumn-winter and spring-summer (Central Gangetic Plains); normal season in southern states; ICAR advisory also mentions a Kharif sowing window of mid-April to end of May.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Hybrid-5 is an IARI long-fruited brinjal F1 hybrid released in 1992 with high yield (45-55 t/ha) and maturity in 80-85 days, and it is widely listed in ICAR and state advisories. No variety-specific evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood, disease or pest tolerance was found, and the official stress reaction is 'not applicable'. Evidence is strong for yield and adaptation but weak for stress traits, and the variety is not formally recommended for Gujarat.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Long-fruited, dark purple IARI F1 hybrid yielding 45-55 t/ha, maturing in 80-85 days, responsive to good soil fertility and poor in poor soils. Recommended for Delhi, UP, Punjab, AP and southern states across multiple seasons.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No documented stress tolerance. Release trials noted no major disease or pest problems, but there are no screening data or resistance genes. Generic brinjal waterlogging sensitivity applies. Genetic marker and QTL information is absent.
