search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ranga (CSC name, sugarcane) / Prangal (Seednet name, listed under BRINJAL)

Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed (release and notification; Prangal on Seednet; breeder; Co V 15-356 research). The seed availability search was not run because the search cap was reached. The Seednet and CSC records conflict on crop: Seednet lists brinjal, while the CSC record and the Co V code point to sugarcane.

STRESS TOLERANCE (Ranga: no evidence found; Prangal: no evidence found)
No page names Ranga or Prangal for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. A RARS Anakapalle waterlogging study tests 16 unnamed pre-release clones, so it is not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/Sugarcane-Clones-Suitable-for-Water-logged-Conditions-of-Andhra-Pradesh-PS-Rao-66.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST (Ranga: no evidence found; Prangal: no evidence found)
A 2025 news report on two new Anakapalle sugarcane varieties says one is red-rot resistant, but neither variety is named, so it is not attributed. -- https://www.etvbharat.com/amp/en/state/andhra-pradesh-anakapalle-agri-research-centre-releases-two-new-sugarcane-varieties-enn26061900957
The sugarcane borer review credits Co 356 with borer resistance. That is a different designation from Co V 15-356, so it is discarded. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10340-024-01750-9

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (Ranga: no evidence found; Prangal: no evidence found)
The same news report gives yield and jaggery figures for the two unnamed varieties, so they are not attributed. -- https://www.etvbharat.com/amp/en/state/andhra-pradesh-anakapalle-agri-research-centre-releases-two-new-sugarcane-varieties-enn26061900957
The AICRP sugarcane page for the Anakapalle station lists its released varieties. None is Ranga. The closest entry is CoA 14321 (Vasista, 2009A 107), released in 2020 with a yield of 135 t/ha. That designation differs from "2009 V 127" in the record, so it is not attributed. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/anakapalle.htm

GENETICS AND QTL (Ranga: no evidence found; Prangal: no evidence found)
No page on marker, QTL or DNA-fingerprinting work names this variety. The fingerprinting hits concern Swarnamukhi (Co T 10367), a different clone. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346126746_Swarnamukhi_Co_T_10367_-_A_New_Sugarcane_clone_for_Andhra_Pradesh

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (Ranga: no breeder found; Prangal: no evidence found)
The ANGRAU 2020-21 annual report says one sugarcane variety from the university was submitted to the State Variety Release Committee for identification and release. It does not name the variety, so this cannot be linked to Ranga. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/ANGRAU%20AR%20%202020-21.pdf
The developing station for ANGRAU's Anakapalle sugarcane work is the Regional Agricultural Research Station, Anakapalle. This is station-level context only. -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/anakapalle.htm
Ch Mukunda Rao (Associate Director of Research) and D Adilakshmi (Principal Scientist, Sugarcane) are named in a news report about two unnamed Anakapalle varieties. They are not attributed to Ranga. -- https://www.etvbharat.com/amp/en/state/andhra-pradesh-anakapalle-agri-research-centre-releases-two-new-sugarcane-varieties-enn26061900957

drought_tolerance.technical_details: Snippets mention drought only in generic contexts. One grafting snippet says a rootstock is 'resistant to wilt pathogens and tolerant to drought', which refers to the rootstock, not Pusa Hybrid-6. The IARI Annual Report 2022 drought snippet appears next to a bitter gourd entry, so it cannot be attributed to this brinjal hybrid. No direct drought trial of Pusa Hybrid-6 is evident.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The IARI 2018 annual report has a heat tolerance screening item next to the Pusa Hybrid-6 yield figure (44.25 t/ha), but the snippet does not link the two. Other heat-related snippets are generic. The release notes say it suits spring-summer crops only where summers are free of long hot dry winds, which suggests limited tolerance to hot dry conditions.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: A 2025 ScienceDirect study (Plant Physiology and Biochemistry, pii S0981942825001949) lists Pusa Hybrid-6 among genotypes classed as highly tolerant at the germination stage. This is a germination-stage screen only, and the snippets show no field-level salinity data. I rate it medium rather than high because the evidence covers one stage and the full text was not available. Grafting studies cite it as a scion on salt-tolerant rootstocks, which does not show intrinsic tolerance.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No direct evidence for this variety. Sources state that brinjal in general cannot tolerate waterlogging. The waterlogging items in IARI reports concern other crops and germplasm.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: The submergence snippets concern rice and other crops. The BAU Sabour document that mentions Pusa Hybrid-6 uses it as a yield check in a brinjal hybrid trial, not as a submergence-tolerant entry.

disease_resistance.specific_diseases: The official description reports no major disease problems in the field. A 2023 bacterial wilt screening snippet groups Pusa Hybrid-6 with entries other than the resistant Arka Nidhi, which implies it was not resistant (the snippet is truncated).
disease_resistance.technical_details: No resistance genes or mechanisms are documented. The observation of no major disease problems is a field observation, not a resistance claim.

pest_resistance.specific_pests: Fruit and shoot borer (FSB). The ISAAA brief reports Pusa Hybrid-6 as the national check in Bt brinjal trials, with higher damage (mean shoot damage 13.07% and higher fruit damage) than the Bt hybrids (1.51%) and non-Bt counterparts (7.06%).
pest_resistance.technical_details: The release notes recommend routine pest control, particularly in August to October, against FSB. These data show susceptibility to FSB, not resistance.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Hybrid-6 is an early, round-fruited IARI F1 brinjal hybrid (1991) with consistently reported yields of 40-50 t/ha and wide use as a check variety. The only research-backed stress trait is germination-stage salinity tolerance, while it is susceptible to fruit and shoot borer and no drought, heat, flood or submergence tolerance was found. Yield evidence is strong, stress evidence is weak, and no genetic marker or breeder contact data were located.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Early (85-90 days) round purple F1 hybrid from IARI, released in 1991, yielding 40-50 t/ha. Suited to fertile soils in autumn-winter and spring-summer seasons of northern and central India, and officially recommended for Maharashtra.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Evidence of stress tolerance is limited to germination-stage salinity tolerance in a 2025 screening study. It is susceptible to fruit and shoot borer, and the search results show no direct evidence for drought, heat, flood or submergence tolerance. Overall stress tolerance is unclear and not demonstrated.

pest_resistance.summary: No resistance to shoot and fruit borer (Leucinodes orbonalis) is supported by the evidence. Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1 and Hybrid-2 showed the highest shoot infestation (about 9.1 and 8.7 per cent) and fruit infestation (about 23.1 and 22.0 per cent) among the tested brinjal genotypes, and had higher total sugars and lower total phenols. These findings indicate relatively high infestation, not resistance. No other pest data found in the digest.

DISEASE AND PEST
Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1 and Hybrid-2 showed the highest shoot infestation (about 9.1 and 8.7 per cent) and fruit infestation (about 23.1 and 22.0 per cent) by shoot and fruit borer (Leucinodes orbonalis) among the tested brinjal genotypes, and had higher total sugars and lower total phenols. -- https://www.academia.edu/37770162/Biochemical_Basis_of_Resistance_in_Brinjal_Genotypes_Against_Shoot_and_Fruit_Borer_Leucinodes_Orbonalis_Guenee_
Bacterial wilt: no evidence found for this variety. The bacterial wilt tolerance results in the Scientific Reports and PMC papers refer to other hybrids (BBSR series crosses), not Shalimar. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12216501

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Shalimar Hybrid-1 was one of 30 pink brinjal genotypes tested at the Experimental Farm, Division of Vegetable Science, SKUAST-J (Jammu), in a genetic divergence study. It was classed as a public-sector hybrid from SKUAST-Kashmir, and was grouped in Cluster VI with Pink Long, Baramulla Local Sel-01 and Baramulla Local Sel-02. No yield values for this hybrid were found in the snippets. -- https://www.genresj.org/index.php/grj/article/download/genresj.FRFO5243/204?inline=1
No yield, maturity, spacing or multi-location trial data for Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1 found. -- https://www.genresj.org/index.php/grj/article/download/genresj.FRFO5243/204?inline=1

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found: no parentage, inbred parents, QTL, marker or combining-ability study for Shalimar Brinjal Hybrid-1 was found. Parentage remains "Not specified". EVIDENCE DIGEST: SHRESTHA (JRM-5)

Name check: "SHRESTHA" (CSC minutes) and "Shrestha" (Seednet) are the same string. Every match I found for JRM 5 (Shrestha) is for kenaf/mesta. No source links Shrestha to brinjal, so the Seednet crop label "BRINJAL" is unsupported. The brinjal results I found concern other varieties or companies. Treat the crop field as a probable data error, and check it against Seednet before filing.

The ICAR 2010-11 report describes it as recommended for rainfed conditions, which implies drought-prone tolerance, but it gives no measured drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SUBHRA / Shubhra (sesame), evidence digest

Name note: The CSC name is SUBHRA (OSC 207) and the Seednet name is Shubhra. The evidence below mostly uses the spellings "Subhra," "Shubra," and "SUBHRA (OSC 207)." Several official pages spell it differently, and some entries are ambiguous, so each line says which name the page uses.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for SUBHRA specifically. The DOD page's tolerance note (white seed; tolerant to leaf curl, phyllody, Macrophomina, Cercospora, capsule borer) sits in the row for Smarak, not Subhra. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Sesame.aspx
- The search returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or waterlogging data for Subhra.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for SUBHRA. The only Macrophomina tolerance statement in the DOD characters table is for Smarak (OSC 560), not Subhra. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A Rural Knowledge Bank table lists "Subhra (QSC 207)" with duration 85 days, average yield 9.0 q/ha, and oil content 52%. The name "QSC" appears to be a typo for OSC. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/oilseed-crops-in-odisha/sesame/
- The DOD characters table gives Subhra's yield potential as 800-900 kg/ha and oil content as 48-52%, with OUAT as the releasing centre. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx
- The DOD variety page describes "Shubra" (2012, OUAT, 48-52% oil, 800-900 kg/ha) as golden-yellow, bold-seeded, with delayed shattering, synchronous maturity, and suitability for kharif and summer seasons. The DOD seed-colour description conflicts with the white-seeded note for SUBHRA on another DOD page, so this entry is unresolved. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Sesame.aspx
- No multi-location or field-trial results for SUBHRA were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No pedigree, parentage, marker, or QTL data for SUBHRA or Shubhra appeared. The parentage field is "Not specified" in the record.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology (OUAT), Bhubaneswar, per the DOD release table. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx
- No breeder or scientist name linked to SUBHRA, Shubhra, or OSC 207 was found. -- No evidence found
- Name resemblance: the search surfaced a breeder profile for Dr. K. K. Panigrahi at OUAT (AICRN on Potential Crops; sunflower). That profile does not mention sesame or this variety, so it was excluded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Kaushik-Kumar-Panigrahi

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. Institute-level contact from the OUAT Department of Seed Science & Technology page (not confirmed as this variety's developing division): email registrar@ouat.ac.in; phones (0674)-2397970 and 2397818; postal address Odisha University of Agriculture & Technology, Bhubaneswar-751003, Odisha; website www.ouat.ac.in. -- https://ouat.ac.in/college-of-agriculture-bhubaneswar/department-of-seed-science-technology/

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The sesame papers from OUAT that appeared (repeated-mutagenesis study, F2M2 generation) and the rainfed Ghat-zone performance study do not name SUBHRA or Shubhra in the retrieved text, so they were excluded. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37561696 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328073756_Performance_of_sesamum_varieties_under_rainfed_upland_conditions_in_the_N-E_ghat_zone_of_Odisha
- No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Listed as a sesame variety in a quality seed production document: "SUBHRA (OSC 207)" alongside SMARAK (OSC 560). This confirms the variety appears in seed-production material; it does not confirm current stock. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/quality-seed-production-technology-of-groundnut-soyabean-and-sesame/259915221
- The Odisha seeds portal lists Subhra (OSC-207) under the Smarak (OSC-560) entry for OUAT sesame. -- https://odishaseedsportal.nic.in/ouatreport/dtls?cod=OUAT
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sale listing for SUBHRA was found. A commercial listing for generic "sesame seed" in Bhubaneswar was excluded because it names no variety. -- No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha. The DOD notified-varieties table lists Odisha as the state, with the Subhra/Shubra/Smarak group. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx
- Release-year discrepancy: the DOD characters table gives 2015 for SUBHRA (OSC 207), while the DOD variety page gives 2012 for "Shubra." The release date in the record is 2014-10-20. Verify against the CSC minutes.
- Registration: the PPV&FR extant-varieties compendium lists "SUBHRA (OSC 207)" by name. The applicant and registration number shown in the same extract are not tied to Subhra, so they were not recorded. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumforextantnotified-nov-2021.pdf

drought.details: No drought tolerance evidence found in the digest. The Odisha information sheet describes suitability for rainfed and irrigated shallow lowlands, which is an adaptation statement and not a drought-tolerance finding.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources.

salinity.details: Listed as tolerant to salinity in the Odisha information sheet. This rests on a single source and no mechanism or screening data were provided, so the level is provisional.

flood.details: Listed as tolerant to flood in the Odisha information sheet. The AP Seeds source lists submergence instead, and the wording differs between the two sources. Verify before citing. No mechanism data were provided.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB): listed as tolerant by AP Seeds and the IIRR newsletter (2015), and as moderately resistant by the Odisha information sheet. A 2017-18 Bengaluru trial recorded grain discolouration of 15.93% for Amara against 40.68% for NLR 34449 and 14.78% for MTU 1010 (lowest in that trial); this is a grain quality observation, not a disease-resistance rating. The 2009 release note in the IIRR source is cited for the BLB tolerance claim.

pest_resistance.summary: Brown planthopper (BPH): listed as tolerant by AP Seeds and the IIRR newsletter (2015), and as moderately resistant by the Odisha information sheet. Gall midge (GM): moderately resistant per the Odisha information sheet only.

agronomic_details.yield: Potential yield 6.5 t/ha (Odisha information sheet). The IIRR newsletter describes high yield without a figure. Average yield is not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources across environments. The IIRR newsletter describes the variety as high yielding and non-lodging.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to rainfed and irrigated shallow lowlands (Odisha information sheet). Grown across the Godavari zone of Andhra Pradesh, with more than 20,000 ha in each Godavari district in 2020-21 (AICRIP POS 2020-21). Odisha promotion is from a project sheet and is not a formal recommendation.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 115-120 days (Odisha information sheet). Described as long duration in the IIRR newsletter.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf, medium slender grain (Odisha information sheet). Non-lodging (IIRR newsletter).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Bengaluru 2017-18 trial: grain discolouration 15.93% for Amara, 40.68% for NLR 34449, 14.78% for MTU 1010 (lowest in trial). (2) Grown on more than 20,000 ha in each Godavari district in 2020-21 (AICRIP POS 2020-21). (3) Ranked among popular ANGRAU varieties at the 2021-22 Maruteru mega display. (4) Farmer preference in the Godavari zone: 38% of growers ranked it as most preferred. (5) Quality screening of 20 Andhra Pradesh varieties including Amara (Divya Prasanna Kumari et al., 2020); the digest does not report results from this study.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Amara (MTU 1064), rice. Seednet lookup under "Tamara" (BRINJAL).
Searches run: 4 of the 4 allowed. Seed availability had no dedicated search, so that heading rests on incidental hits only.

NAME NOTE: The release-minute name "Amara" (MTU 1064) matches rice sources. The Seednet name "Tamara" under BRINJAL matched no brinjal variety in any source found. The Seednet record itself was not reachable, so the crop mismatch is unresolved.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Evidence refers to Amara (MTU 1064).
Listed as tolerant to BPH, BLB and submergence -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx
Listed as tolerant to flood and salinity -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/amara-mtu-1064-english.pdf
Flood tolerance listed at Odisha sheet is "flood" and AP Seeds lists "submergence"; the two sources differ in wording, so verify before citing.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Evidence refers to Amara (MTU 1064).
Moderately resistant to BPH, BLB and gall midge (GM) -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/amara-mtu-1064-english.pdf
Described as tolerant to BPH and BLB, with a 2009 release note -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
Grain discolouration in one 2017-18 Bengaluru trial: Amara 15.93%, against 40.68% in NLR 34449 (lowest was MTU 1010 at 14.78%) -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/8d1eb20d-bad5-45e9-9dbf-20c0995da267/content

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Evidence refers to Amara (MTU 1064).
Semi-dwarf, medium slender grain, 115-120 days, suited to rainfed and irrigated shallow lowlands, potential yield 6.5 t/ha -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/amara-mtu-1064-english.pdf
High yield, non-lodging, long-duration variety -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
Grown on more than 20,000 ha in each Godavari district in 2020-21 -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/POS2020-21.pdf
Ranked among popular ANGRAU varieties at the 2021-22 Maruteru mega display -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382028084_Impact_Analysis_of_Angrau_Mega_Rice_Varietal_Display_Melas
Farmer preference in the Godavari zone: 38% of growers ranked it as most preferred -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391861761_Varietal_preference_of_rice_growers_millers_and_consumers_in_Godavari_zone_of_Andhra_Pradesh

GENETICS AND QTL -- Evidence refers to Amara (MTU 1064).
No Amara-specific QTL or marker study was found. The related MTU 1010 marker-assisted study (Xa21, Pi54, Pup1) is not about Amara -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8803164/
The genetic-parameters thesis refers to MTU 1061 and MTU 1001 as salinity-tolerance parents, not to Amara -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/644d31de-c0e9-42c7-b659-29c019c13bef/content

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Evidence refers to Amara (MTU 1064).
Developing institution: ANGRAU, through the Andhra Pradesh Rice Research Institute / RARS Maruteru, West Godavari -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
Named release year 2009 -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety has citable sources (TNAU documents, a journal manuscript, and a gazette notification for Tamil Nadu). However, no stress tolerance trait is documented for VMB-16-10 itself, since the drought, heat and salinity snippets belong to other crops or projects. The yield value is not visible, so the evidence is mainly about plant type (non-spiny, 118.6 cm height, 30.5 branches). It sits at the 'only yield/agronomic info, no stress' level. The citations might justify 60, but stress and yield evidence are too thin, so 40 is the conservative score. It is notified only for Tamil Nadu, with no Gujarat evaluation.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: VMB-16-10 is a non-spiny brinjal hybrid derivative, apparently from TNAU and notified for Tamil Nadu in 2022. It is described as 118.6 cm tall with 30.5 branches per plant. No variety-specific stress tolerance, genetic marker, or commercial availability evidence was found, and the evidence quality is low.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Non-spiny brinjal hybrid derivative, 118.6 cm plant height and 30.5 branches/plant, notified for Tamil Nadu in 2022. Yield, maturity, parentage and season are not specified in the available data.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No documented drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. The stress snippets in the search results concern other crops or separate projects. Disease and pest reaction tables exist in a yield performance paper, but their results were not retrieved. Its stress profile is therefore unconfirmed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VNR-218 (brinjal). Variety name and Seednet name are identical ("VNR-218"), so every search result below refers to both. Only four searches were allowed, so several headings have thin or no evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- none (searched within the four allowed queries; no source returned this)

DISEASE AND PEST
Described as resistant to bacterial wilt. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/brinjal-hybrid-variety-vnr-218/
Commercial listings claim superior disease resistance, but these are marketing claims without trial data. -- https://www.amazon.in/Hybrid-Brinjal-Gardeing-Germination-Vegetable/dp/B0DCTHZ2WD

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Small, long-fruited hybrid. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/brinjal-hybrid-variety-vnr-218/
Seed rate given as 150-200 g/ha; suitable for kharif and rabi sowing. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/brinjal-hybrid-variety-vnr-218/
Maturity, yield and multi-location trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found (no parentage, pedigree or marker study was returned; parentage is "Not specified" in the record).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Source given as VNR Seeds Pvt. Ltd., Raipur, with 2012 as the year. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/brinjal-hybrid-variety-vnr-218/
Commercial listings name VNR Seeds as manufacturer, country of origin India. -- https://www.amazon.in/Hybrid-Brinjal-Gardeing-Germination-Vegetable/dp/B0DCTHZ2WD
Lead breeder name and public-sector developing institute: No evidence found. The CSC record's "Not specified" institution is not contradicted, but it is also not confirmed. The product is presented as a private-sector F1 hybrid, so it may not have come through an ICAR or SAU programme.

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder name, role, email, phone or postal address: No evidence found. No VNR Seeds corporate or contact page was returned by the searches. No ICAR or institute contact page applies, since no public-sector developer was identified.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers were returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY

basic_info.institution: ICAR-CPCRI (Kasaragod, Kerala), with participating role of AICRP on Palms (Arsikere centre); the digest also credits 'CPCRI and TNAU' in a slide deck. Original record field 'Not specified' is filled from these sources.

drought.details: CPCRI lists Kalpatharu among varieties relatively tolerant to drought and describes it as a moisture-deficit-tolerant hybrid. The CPCRI page itself describes a tall variety. Indian Coconut Journal (2019) also groups Kalpatharu with relatively drought-tolerant varieties. No quantitative drought data (e.g., yield under water stress) was found. Note that the digest's transcriptomic study (2020) examined Kalpatharu seedlings under 25% soil-moisture water deficit, reporting about 7,300 differentially expressed genes; this is molecular evidence and does not quantify tolerance. The level is rated medium because the evidence is qualitative and from descriptive sources.

agronomic_details.yield: AICRP on Palms (2009-10 recommendation): 15,750 nuts/ha, copra 2.7 t/ha at 15.48 kg/palm/year, oil 67.2%. CPCRI (older page): about 116 nuts/palm/year under rainfed conditions, copra 176 g. CPCRI (newer page): 108-213 nuts/palm/year, tender nut water 351 ml, copra 187 g, oil 68%. ICAR-CPCRI 2022 article: 152-213 nuts/palm/year under irrigation and good management. Indian Coconut Journal (2019): 20,709 nuts/ha, copra 3.64 t/ha. The original record states that the proposed hybrid's performance is inferior to the check variety in copra and oil yield; this is retained as the CSC-preferred reference statement and is not contradicted by the digest's figures, which do not include a check comparison in the same units.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources, beyond the range of nut yields across sources (108-213 nuts/palm/year) and the 2009-10 AICRP multi-location recommendation.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for rainfed and irrigated coconut belts in interior Karnataka, Kerala and irrigated Tamil Nadu (AICRP on Palms). The CCARI table lists Kerala only. Recommended for ball copra by Indian Coconut Journal (2019) due to low spoilage (3.92%).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Flowering about 4 years after planting (CPCRI). Under rainfed conditions, 50% of palms flower at 59 months. Palm height about 6.5 m at 26 years under irrigation. Described by CPCRI as a tall variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP on Palms, 2009-10 recommendation: nut yield 15,750 nuts/ha, copra 2.7 t/ha at 15.48 kg/palm/year, oil 67.2%. (2) AICRP comparison table: Kalpatharu values 84.0 / 740.0 / 330.0 / 190.0 / 102.5 / 115.0; trait columns are not labelled in the extract. (3) CPCRI older page: about 116 nuts/palm/year under rainfed conditions, copra 176 g, flowering about 4 years after planting. (4) CPCRI newer page: 108-213 nuts/palm/year, tender nut water 351 ml, copra 187 g, oil 68%. (5) ICAR-CPCRI 2022 article: 152-213 nuts/palm/year under irrigation and good management. (6) Indian Coconut Journal (2019): 20,709 nuts/ha, copra 3.64 t/ha, spoilage 3.92%, 50% of palms flowering at 59 months under rainfed conditions, palm height about 6.5 m at 26 years under irrigation. (7) Set-II hybrid trial (1992, randomised block design, four replicates): Kalpatharu used as local check, with Chandra Sankara giving higher nut yield.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kalpatharu (coconut, IND 125S)**

**Name and crop check:** The variety_name "Kalpatharu" and the seednet_variety_name "kalpatharu" refer to the same coconut variety in every source found. The Seednet crop field "BRINJAL" conflicts with the coconut evidence. None of my four searches was filtered to brinjal, so I cannot confirm or rule out a brinjal entry on Seednet. Treat the crop field as a probable data-entry error. The 2013-06-04 year_of_release also conflicts with the sources, which give a 2009 recommendation (see RECOMMENDED STATES). "Not specified" for institution and parentage can be filled from the sources below: CPCRI is the developing institute, and the variety is a selection from Tiptur Tall.

**STRESS TOLERANCE:** CPCRI lists Kalpatharu among varieties relatively tolerant to drought, and calls it a moisture-deficit-tolerant hybrid, though the page itself describes a tall variety -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement ; https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties ; https://cpcri.icar.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
Indian Coconut Journal (2019) also groups Kalpatharu with the relatively drought-tolerant varieties -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

**DISEASE AND PEST:** No Kalpatharu-specific resistance to root (wilt) or other diseases was found in the sources. Root (wilt) resistance is reported for other varieties (e.g., Kalpa Sankara, Kalparaksha), not Kalpatharu -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement . The Amazon listing claims pest resistance, but it is a commercial plant listing with no supporting data, so I did not rely on it -- https://www.amazon.in/Green-view-Kalpatharu-Coconut-Hybrid/dp/B0BT214TVX . Pest and disease-specific evidence: No evidence found.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:**
- AICRP on Palms (2009-10 recommendation): nut yield 15,750 nuts/ha, copra 2.7 t/ha at 15.48 kg/palm/year, oil 67.2% -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS
- AICRP comparison table: Kalpatharu 84.0 / 740.0 / 330.0 / 190.0 / 102.5 / 115.0 (trait columns not labelled in the extract) -- same URL
- CPCRI: about 116 nuts/palm/year under rainfed conditions, copra 176 g, flowering about 4 years after planting -- https://cpcri.icar.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
- CPCRI newer page: 108-213 nuts/palm/year, tender nut water 351 ml, copra 187 g, oil 68% -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Coconut_Varieties
- ICAR-CPCRI 2022 article: 152-213 nuts/palm/year under irrigation and good management -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/129746/48480/472817
- Indian Coconut Journal (2019): 20,709 nuts/ha, copra 3.64 t/ha, recommended for ball copra due to low spoilage (3.92%) -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Under rainfed conditions, 50% of palms flower at 59 months; palm height about 6.5 m at 26 years under irrigation -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Set-II hybrid trial (1992, RBD, four replicates) used Kalpatharu as the local check, with Chandra Sankara giving higher nut yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS

**GENETICS AND QTL:** Kalpatharu is a selection from Tiptur Tall -- https://ccari.res.in/dss/coconute.html ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS . A 2020 CPCRI newsletter reports a transcriptomic study of two-year-old Kalpatharu and Kalpasree seedlings under 25% soil-moisture water deficit (about 7,300 differentially expressed genes) -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/news_letter/Kalpa_Oct-Dec-2020.pdf . QTL or marker-trait mapping for Kalpatharu: No evidence found.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:** Developing institute is ICAR-CPCRI (Kasaragod, Kerala), with a participating role for AICRP on Palms (Arsikere centre) -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement ; https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf . A slide deck credits Kalpatharu to "CPCRI and TNAU" -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/coconut-breeding/55986443 . The Indian Coconut Journal says the variety was proposed for release by AICRPP Arsikere -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf . Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.

**CONTACT DETAILS:**
- Professor & Head, Coconut Research Station, Aliyarnagar, Coimbatore Dist., Tamil Nadu; phone 04253-288722; email arsaliar@tnau.ac.in -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS (name of incumbent not stated)
- ICAR-CPCRI institute website (institute-level; no email or phone found in the results): https://cpcri.gov.in/page
- Kalpatharu Coconut Producer Company Limited, 9th Ward, Behind Old Bus Stand, Turuvekere Taluk, Tumkur-572227, Karnataka; CEO MB Siddhavasappa -- https://www.indiamart.com/kalpatharu-coconut-producer/aboutus.html . This is a private farmer company with no link to the variety; listed only to avoid confusion.
- Individual breeder email or phone: No evidence found.

**PUBLICATIONS:**
- Authors not stated (2009). All India Co-ordinated Research Project on Palms: recommendations approved for commercialization during 2009-10 (Kalpatharu, IND 125S). AICRP on Palms report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS
- Authors not stated (2019). Indian Coconut Journal, July 2019, 3C Index News 28. Coconut Development Board -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf
- Authors not stated (2022). ICAR-CPCRI article, Indian Horticulture, Nov-Dec 2022, pp. 31 ff. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/129746/48480/472817
- Authors not stated (2020). KALPA CPCRI Newsletter, Vol. 39, No. 4, Oct-Dec 2020 (water-deficit transcriptomics on Kalpasree and Kalpatharu). ICAR-CPCRI -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/news_letter/Kalpa_Oct-Dec-2020.pdf
- Peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) and conference papers specific to Kalpatharu: No evidence found in these searches.

**SEED AVAILABILITY:**
- ICAR-CPCRI supplies planting material and breeder seed, and runs community nurseries with Kerala's agriculture department -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/129746/48480/472817 ; https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement
- A private Kerala nursery (KJ Coconut Hybrid Nursery) sells hybrid seedlings, but it is not documented as selling Kalpatharu -- https://cpcri.gov.in/filemgr/webfs/publication/KJ_COCONUT_NURSERY_SUCCESS_STORY_by_Coconut_Development_Board.pdf
- A coconut farmer seedling supplier lists Kalpatharu (tall cultivar) as a certified CPCRI seedling; no dealer, address or price found -- https://coconutfarmers.in/seedlings/
- Kishan Coconut Nursery (Gujarat) sells CPCRI-trained hybrid seedlings, not Kalpatharu -- https://kishancoconutnursery.com/
- State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed-sale or NSC listings for Kalpatharu: No evidence found.

**RECOMMENDED STATES:** Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala, recommended by the XIX Biennial Workshop of AICRP on Palms in 2009 -- https://www.coconutboard.in/images/icj-2019-07.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS . The CCARI table lists Kerala only -- https://ccari.res.in/dss/coconute.html . Rainfed and irrigated coconut belts in interior Karnataka, Kerala and irrigated Tamil Nadu are the stated target regions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269876228_ALL_INDIA_CO-ORDINATED_RESEARCH_PROJECT_ON_PALMS . Note that the record's 2013 release year is not supported by these sources; the recommendation is 2009.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ganesh Broccoli (GK-2-5), broccoli, Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth (MPKV)

Name note: variety_name is "Ganesh Broccoli" and seednet_variety_name is "Ganesh Broccoli (GK-2-5)". All evidence below refers to "Ganesh Broccoli"; no result matched the GK-2-5 code or the Seednet portal. Searches run: 4 (release/traits, breeder/institute, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches on stress tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) returned nothing specific to Ganesh Broccoli.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for this variety appeared in the results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A field trial at Pune comparing Ganesh Broccoli with Pusa Broccoli KTS-1 across five spacings reported that Ganesh Broccoli performed better on several growth, yield and quality traits, including days to head appearance, days to first harvest, head diameter and average head weight, and was judged better suited to commercial cultivation under Pune conditions at 60 x 45 cm spacing -- https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/view/245
- The same trial report, in the PDF version, gives the mean head weight of Ganesh Broccoli as 154.80 g and the head diameter as 10.81 cm -- https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/245/228

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No QTL, marker, or genetic-study results for Ganesh Broccoli appeared. The GKO-1 and SA-5 patent records in the results are unrelated inbred lines from other breeders and were excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is listed among the improved and hybrid vegetable varieties developed by MPKV, Rahuri, under the AICRP on Vegetable Crops -- https://mpkv.ac.in/Uploads/Education/Horticulture.pdf
- A Studocu copy of an MPKV table lists "Broccoli - Ganesh Broccoli" with a release year of 2006, which conflicts with the 2014 CSC release date -- https://www.studocu.com/in/document/mahatma-phule-krishi-vidyapeeth/fundamentals-of-biochemistry/vegetable-variety-hhhfggg/72435476
- The Pune trial paper was credited to the AICRP on Vegetable Crops, Department of Horticulture, MPKV, Rahuri, with authors K.K. Bhangre and M.N. Bhalekar -- https://www.isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/view/245

drought.details: No drought tolerance evidence found. The digest notes suitability for rainfed cultivation, but this is a cultivation suitability statement, not a measured tolerance result.

heat.details: No heat tolerance data found for this variety.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance evidence found in searched sources.

flood.details: No flood tolerance evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust is reported for BSG 0912 / BSR 2. Both sources describe moderate resistance only. No other diseases were reported in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: No confirmed pest resistance. A ResearchGate figure titled 'Reaction of Groundnut culture BSG 0912 against insects under field' exists, but the retrieved text gives no result, so field insect reaction is not found in searched sources. A Legume Research paper states that both table-type forms (VRI 10 and BSR 2 are named) are vulnerable to storage insects, but it does not clearly attribute this to BSR 2 alone; this is treated as unconfirmed.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed average yield 2222 kg/ha. Irrigated average yield 2360 kg/ha. The CSC record gives an average yield of 1200.00 to 1500.00 Kg/Ha, which the digest does not address and which differs from the trial figures.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis was reported beyond rainfed and irrigated trial averages.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to rainfed and irrigated conditions (TNAU). The paper states suitability for all groundnut-growing districts of Tamil Nadu. A TNAU Scientific Workers Conference document lists BSR 2 (2019) among groundnut varieties with 105 days duration for Kharif and Rabi seasons. The TNAU page lists seasons from Chithiraipattam through Vaigasipattam (multiple seasons).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 115 To 120Days (CSC record). The TNAU page and the TNAU Scientific Workers Conference document give a duration of 105-110 days (105 days in the SWC document).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Spanish bunch growth habit. Table-purpose variety (Legume Research paper). Shelling outturn 70.2%, 100-kernel weight 41.0 g (rainfed trial data).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Rainfed trials: average yield 2222 kg/ha, about 5.9% above VRI 8 (2099 kg/ha), 18.3% above CO 7 and 19.1% above VRI(Gn) 6. Irrigated trials: average yield 2360 kg/ha, with gains of 15.5% over VRI 8, 14.5% over CO 7 and 22.9% over VRI(Gn) 6. Quality data: shelling outturn 70.2%, 100-kernel weight 41.0 g, oil content 45.01%. Thiruvarur evaluation (Legume Research): oil content 45% (lowest among table-purpose varieties tested) and 100-kernel weight 44 g. Sensory suitability reported for peanut butter, chutney powder and masala peanut.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No QTL, SNP or SSR marker data specific to BSR 2 were found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL or marker-assisted studies specific to BSR 2 were found. Two F2 populations derived from BSR 2 (BSR 2 x GPBD 4 and BSR 2 x TMV 2) were studied for variability and path analysis; no QTL effects were reported.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not found in searched sources (NSC and State Seed Corporation: no evidence for BSR 2). Seednet listing for 'BS-2' under BROWN SARSON: no evidence found; the retrieved Seednet page lists sarson types but not BS-2.
commercial_info.availability_status: limited. TNAU ARS Bhavanisagar produces BSR 2 planting material through an NHM model nursery. A Legume Research study notes that farmers often buy kernels from unregulated markets rather than certified seed for these varieties.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderate resistance to late leaf spot and rust is reported for BSG 0912 / BSR 2, not drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- https://www.academia.edu/142999069/A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2
- Suitability for both rainfed and irrigated cultivation is stated, but no drought or heat tolerance data were found for this variety. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd4e0ce2cede71d18e81
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to late leaf spot and rust. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20BSR%202.html
- Pest reaction: a ResearchGate figure titled "Reaction of Groundnut culture BSG 0912 against insects under field" exists, but the retrieved text gives no result. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Morphological-Description-of-Groundnut-culture-BSG-0912_tbl2_338773637
- Storage insect susceptibility: a Legume Research paper says both table-type forms (VRI 10 and BSR 2 are named) are vulnerable to storage insects, but it does not clearly attribute this to BSR 2 alone. Treat as unconfirmed. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5318
- Seednet / other names: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released 2019; Spanish bunch growth habit; duration 105-110 days; suited to rainfed and irrigated conditions. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20BSR%202.html
- Rainfed average yield 2222 kg/ha, about 5.9% above VRI 8 (2099 kg/ha), 18.3% above CO 7 and 19.1% above VRI(Gn) 6. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd4e0ce2cede71d18e81
- Irrigated average yield 2360 kg/ha, with 15.5%, 14.5% and 22.9% gains over VRI 8, CO 7 and VRI(Gn) 6. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338773637_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2
- Shelling outturn 70.2%, 100-kernel weight 41.0 g, oil content 45.01%. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd4e0ce2cede71d18e81
- Lowest oil content (45%) among table-purpose varieties tested in Thiruvarur, with 100-kernel weight of 44 g. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5318
- Sensory suitability for peanut butter, chutney powder and masala peanut. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5318
- Season list: Chithiraipattam through Vaigasipattam (multiple seasons). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20BSR%202.html

GENETICS AND QTL
- Cross derivative of VRI 2 × TVG 0004 (Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338773637_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2
- TNAU page gives parentage as VR12 × TVG 0004, which appears to be a typo for VRI 2. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20BSR%202.html
- Parentage conflict: the input record says "selection from a sample collected from Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh." Neither TNAU nor the journal paper supports this; it is probably a Brassica (brown sarson) record and does not describe this groundnut variety.
- F2 populations from BSR 2 × GPBD 4 and BSR 2 × TMV 2 were studied for variability and path analysis. -- https://horizonepublishing.com/journals/index.php/PST/article/view/5241
- QTL or marker-assisted studies specific to BSR 2: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338773637_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2
- Lead authors: K.N. Ganesan and Kulandaivelu Ganesamurthy, both at TNAU. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338773637_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2
- Full author list: K. N. Ganesan, B. Meena Kumari, P. Veerabadhiran, Ashish K. Binodh, P. S. Devanand, R. Pushpam, D. Punitha, S. Maruthachalam, Sheela Venugopal, N. K. Prabakaran and K. Ganesamurthy. -- https://agris.fao.org/search/en/providers/122436/records/675acd4e0ce2cede71d18e81
- Dr Vaithiyalingan M's TNAU profile lists a 2019 recognition award for groundnut BSR 2 and an AICRP groundnut role at Tindivanam. His exact role in the variety is not stated. -- https://tnau.irins.org/profile/151250
- Station: ARS Bhavanisagar (TNAU) runs NHM model nursery production of BSR 1 and BSR 2 planting material. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-bhavanisagar/establishment/
- The ARS Bhavanisagar page identifies the station but does not confirm it as the breeding station.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder email, phone and postal address: No evidence found.
- Institute-level contact: No contact details (email, phone or address) were in the retrieved text for TNAU, ARS Bhavanisagar or the breeders. Contact URL: https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-bhavanisagar/establishment/ (page found, contact fields not retrieved).
- Names and roles: K.N. Ganesan (lead author), Kulandaivelu Ganesamurthy (co-author), both TNAU. No contact details found for them.

PUBLICATIONS
- Ganesan, K.N., Meena Kumari, B., Veerabadhiran, P., Binodh, A.K., Devanand, P.S., Pushpam, R., Punitha, D., Maruthachalam, S., Venugopal, S., Prabakaran, N.K. and Ganesamurthy, K. (2019). A new high yielding Spanish bunch groundnut variety BSR 2. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding 10(4): 1495-1500 -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2019.00192.3
- Kamalasundari, S., Balasubramanian, P., Anuratha, A., Arulselvi, A., Babu, R. and Subbalakshmi, B. (2025). Genetic and Nutritional Secrets of Groundnut Varieties Unveiled for Enhancing Farmers Income by Groundnut Value Chain Process. Legume Research 48(4): 714-720 -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5318
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2024). Genetic variability and association studies in F2 populations of Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.). Plant Science Today -- https://doi.org/10.14719/pst.5241
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports with BSR 2 trial data: No evidence found in search results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- TNAU ARS Bhavanisagar produces BSR 2 planting material through an NHM model nursery. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ars-bhavanisagar/establishment/
- A Legume Research study notes farmers often buy kernels from unregulated markets rather than certified seed for these varieties. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5318
- Seednet listing for "BS-2" under BROWN SARSON: No evidence found. The Seednet notified-variety page retrieved lists sarson types but not BS-2. -- https://seednet.gov.in/material/Agriculture_Variety.htm
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers for BSR 2: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Tamil Nadu; the paper says it is suitable for all groundnut-growing districts of the state. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338773637_A_new_high_yielding_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_variety_BSR_2
- A TNAU Scientific Workers Conference document lists BSR 2 (2019) among groundnut varieties (105 days, Kharif/Rabi). -- http://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/swc/AGRICULTURE-ALL_ACTION_POINTS.pdf
- Brown sarson "BS-2" (Seednet name): no evidence found for any state recommendation.

NAME AND IDENTITY NOTES
- CSC name "BSR 2" (groundnut, TNAU, 2019) is supported by the evidence above. Seednet name "BS-2" under BROWN SARSON is not supported by any retrieved page. The Mathura parentage matches a Brassica sample, not this groundnut variety. Confirm the Seednet record before using it.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BS 279 (variety_name) / BS-2 (seednet_variety_name), crop recorded as cotton, Seednet crop "BROWN SARSON"

Searches run (4): "BS 279 cotton variety"; "BS 279 brown sarson variety OUAT"; "BS-2 brown sarson variety Odisha"; "OUAT Regional Research and Technology Transfer Station brown sarson BS 279 released 2020 Odisha".

Crop conflict: the only page that names BS 279 places it in cotton, not brown sarson. Nothing I found links BS 279 or BS-2 to brown sarson, so the Seednet crop label is unsupported by the evidence. Results for "brown sarson" pages describe the crop in general and were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for BS 279 or BS-2.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for BS 279 or BS-2 was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Brown sarson agronomy pages (e.g., The treatments comprising of 3 planting densities, 3 nitrogen levels and 2 phosphorus levels were replicated thrice using factorial randomized block design. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2020.v9.i5.12301/effect-of-planting-density-on-brown-sarson-brassica-campestris-var-brown-sarson-under-different-levels-of-nitrogen-and-phosphorus-in-mid-hills-of-himachal-pradesh) name no BS 279 or BS-2 and were discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No marker, QTL or genetic study names BS 279 or BS-2.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial. The OUAT research-stations page states that Cotton variety 'BS 279' has been released for Odisha by State Variety Release Committee during the year 2019-20. -- https://ouat.nic.in/research_stations. The page does not name the breeder or the station that developed the variety. The developing institution is therefore Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology (OUAT), station not confirmed. The record's "Regional Research and Technology Transfer Station" is not tied to a named station by any source found. No breeder name was found. The Mathura parentage claim was not found in any source.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. Institute-level contact found, not confirmed as the developing station: Associate Director of Research, RRTTS (CZ), OUAT, Bhubaneswar-751003, Odisha, India; Email: rrtts.bhubaneswar@ouat.ac.in; Mobile: 9437130700 -- https://ouat.ac.in/research_stations/regional-reaearch-and-technology-transfer-station-bhubaneswar-khordha/. Another OUAT station (Chiplima, Sambalpur) lists its own contact, which is not linked to this variety: https://ouat.ac.in/research_stations/regional-reaearch-and-technology-transfer-station-chipilima-sambalpur/

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, thesis, AICRP report or conference item names BS 279 or BS-2. The brown sarson papers returned (e.g., Rao, T.S. (1970). Heterosis for oil content in brown sarson (Brassica campestris var. Sarson). Euphytica -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01902929) do not mention BS 279 and were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The OUAT station page notes stations are involved in production and distribution of quality seeds (https://ouat.ac.in/research_stations/regional-reaearch-and-technology-transfer-station-bhubaneswar-khordha/), but no source confirms BS 279 seed is sold or where.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Odisha. Source: https://ouat.nic.in/research_stations (state release for Odisha, 2019-20, as cited above). This differs from the record's release date of 2020-11-09 and was issued by the State Variety Release Committee, not a Central (CSC) notification. No CSC notification was found.

Summary of gaps: the record's crop (brown sarson in Seednet vs. cotton in the release minutes), the BS-2 name, the Mathura origin, and the release year need verification against the State Variety Release Committee minutes and the Seednet portal entry.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: PLANT BREEDER, HP KRISHI VISHVAVIDYALAYA, OIL SEEDS RESEARCH STATION, KANGRA (HP).
seednet_fields.Parentage: It is a composite population developed from a cross between Pusa Kalyani and Yukina.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Suitable for general calculation in HP from 700 m to 1300 m above m.s.l.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: Very broad basal leaves with dark green colour, hairy on lower side and shining glabrous on upper side; branchings from base of the plant.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: plant height : 145 cm; the variety is medium tall (145 cm) with broad and dark green leaves, thick stem, profused branching, long siliquae with medium bold seed size. on an average it yields 1060 kg/ha. at Research Station, Kangra. At other research stations an average yield of 1234 kg/ha., was recorded an average yield of 1085 was recorded in coordinated yield ranged from 550-800 kg/ha. Nitrogen 60 kg, P2O5, 90 and a seed rate of 10 kg/ha. was recorded optimum in agronomical trials.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to white rust but susceptible to Alternaria blight.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Its reaction to pest is similar to the standard BSH1 i.e attacked by aphids.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Evidence refers to: Shalimar Sarsaon-2 / SS-2 (variety_name). No evidence found for Seednet name "Shalimar Sarson - 1" here; sources treat SS-1 as a separate variety.
- Tolerance to biotic and abiotic stresses is claimed for SS-2 in general terms, with no named stress, trial data, or method -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood, and submergence: No evidence found specific to this variety. The only drought data is a 19.2% rainfed yield gain for SS-2 in J&K, which is an AICRP yield figure, not a stress-tolerance rating -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest reaction for SS-2. The Shalimar Sarsaon-3 (KBS-3) row in the AICRP table is for a different variety and was excluded -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Seed yield about 12 to 15 quintals/ha, per a KVK-linked progressive farmer and a SKUAST-K statement in news coverage (SS2) -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/
- Yield potential of about 15 quintals/ha, with suitability for rice-based systems, cited for SS-2 by SKUAST-K -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/
- SS-1, SS-2 and SS-3 are grouped together at 16 to 17 quintals/ha, so this is a series figure, not SS-2 alone -- https://kashmirreader.com/2024/04/10/revolutionizing-oilseed-farming-in-jk-skuast-kashmirs-innovations-and-impact/
- AICRP-linked rainfed trial: 19.2% yield improvement from Shalimar sarson 2 in J&K over the check -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- Field use: front-line and cluster demonstrations in Pulwama, 2022-23 onward, about 150 ha reported under FLD/CFLD in one year -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/
- Maturity days: No evidence found.
- Parentage (Gulchin x NRCB 16): No evidence found. Gulchin appears only as KOS-101 in a history piece, not as SS-2's parent -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker, or genetic-stock study for SS-2 was returned. A ResearchGate result on yellow-seeded brown sarson lines involved Gulchin and KOS-1 but not SS-2, so it was excluded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318836621_Effect_of_planting_method_and_nutrient_management_practices_on_seed_yield_of_brown_sarson_Brassica_rapa_L

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology, Kashmir (SKUAST-K), Shalimar, Srinagar -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/
- Breeder or lead scientist names: No evidence found. The breeding programme is credited to SKUAST-K, with no named breeder for SS-2 -- https://kashmirreader.com/2024/04/10/revolutionizing-oilseed-farming-in-jk-skuast-kashmirs-innovations-and-impact/
- Station: Mountain Research Centre for Field Crops (MRCFC) is cited for SKUAST-K variety development, but SS-2 is not explicitly linked to it -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/business/skuast-ks-khudwani-centre-marks-sarson-day-pushes-oilseed-self-sufficiency-drive
- Dr Javeed Mugloo, Chief Scientist and Head, KVK Malangpora, is named for SS2 demonstrations, but not as breeder -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute page: https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/ (no email, phone, or postal address extracted from the search snippets)
- Dr Javeed Mugloo, Chief Scientist and Head, KVK Malangpora (name and role only; no email or phone found) -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/
- Official email, phone and postal address of the SKUAST-K Shalimar division: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated (2021). Project Coordinator's Report (2020-21), AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard, DRMR, Bharatpur. Report -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming SS-2 was found. Two ResearchGate papers were excluded because they concern SS-1 ("Shalimar brown sarson1") or other lines, not SS-2.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- SKUAST-K has seen rising demand for SS-2 from the rabi 2022-23 season -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/
- University seed chain: SKUAST-K with the J&K Department of Agriculture runs breeder-to-foundation-to-certified seed production -- https://www.greaterkashmir.com/opinion/revolutionising-oilseed-farming-in-jk/
- Free seed distribution through KVK Malangpora FLD/CFLD, with farmer-to-farmer seed multiplication -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, or private dealer listing for SS-2: No evidence found. A DesiKheti mustard page is generic and does not name SS-2, so it was excluded -- https://www.desikheti.com/pages/buy-mustard-seeds-in-jammu-and-kashmir-online

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Jammu and Kashmir. Confirmed by the AICRP report row for "Shalimar Sarsaon-2 ... Jammu and Kashmir" -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- Consistent with SS2 cultivation in Pulwama district, J&K -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuasts-high-yield-mustard-variety-ss2-profitable-farmers/

Notes on names and gaps:
- The release-year value (2019-06-01) is not confirmed by any search result. The AICRP table gives the notification entry as 5.9.19 for Shalimar Sarsaon-2 (KBS-49) -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- The Seednet name "Shalimar Sarson - 1" conflicts with the SS-2 evidence. Kashmir sources list SS-1 and SS-2 as separate varieties, so the Seednet record should be checked against the portal before use.
- The Gulchin x NRCB 16 parentage remains unverified.

drought.details: Shalimar Sarson-1 appears in Brown sarson lists in AICRP Rapeseed-Mustard Annual Group Meeting proceedings alongside a statement that 'these genotypes highly tolerant to drought' with seed yield reduction of 20% or less. The snippet does not explicitly confirm that Shalimar Sarson-1 is one of those tolerant genotypes, so the drought rating cannot be verified from the search results. Brown sarson is also listed among varieties in a 2014 Rajya Sabha document that calls for short-duration and drought-tolerant varieties, but this does not attribute drought tolerance to the variety.

heat.details: Search results report heat tolerance for other entries (for example, Vijay Mustard 2 rated highly tolerant to terminal heat stress). No result links terminal heat tolerance to Shalimar Sarson-1 directly. The DRMR Project Coordinator's Report lists Shalimar Sarson-1 among released varieties in its 2020-21 summary, which does not establish heat tolerance.

salinity.details: The 2021 AGM proceedings recommend that insect and disease resistance be weighted alongside salinity considerations. No result provides salinity tolerance data for Shalimar Sarson-1.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease reaction data specific to Shalimar Sarson-1 were found in the search results. pest_resistance.summary: No pest reaction data specific to Shalimar Sarson-1 were found in the search results. Proceedings discuss insect-pest population monitoring and the need for insect and disease resistance in varietal evaluation, without variety-specific results for this cultivar.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GK 3150 (maize, Ganga Kaveri, A0202011)

RELEASE/NOTIFICATION: Listed as a private-sector maize entry notified 27.03.2018 under notification 1379(E), recommended for Rajasthan, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh, rabi season, normal maturity. The notification number and date match the release date in the input record. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

BREEDER/INSTITUTION CONFLICT: The same IIMR cultivar page lists GK 3150 under JKAgrigenetics Limited, Hyderabad, rather than Ganga Kaveri. A second entry on the same page lists "GK 3150" under Ganga Kaveri Seeds Pvt Limited with a 30-03-2017 date, notification 1007 E, recommended for Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh, rabi, normal. This points to either two different entries under the same name or a data error, and needs checking against the official notification before the breeder field is relied on. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ (same page, 2017 entry)

RECOMMENDED STATES: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh (matches input). The company's own product page instead lists Andhra Pradesh as the suitable state for GK-3150, which conflicts with the notified recommendation. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/ ; https://gangakaveri-website.webflow.io/

COMPANY DESCRIPTION (unverified marketing claims): The company describes GK-3150 as over 12 feet tall with strong stalks, no lodging, and high grain and green fodder yield. These are not independent trial results. -- https://gangakaveri-website.webflow.io/

DROUGHT: No evidence found specific to GK 3150.

HEAT: No evidence found specific to GK 3150.

SALINITY: No evidence found specific to GK 3150.

FLOOD/SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found specific to GK 3150.

ABIOTIC STRESS (portfolio level only): The company says its maize breeding aims at single-cross hybrids tolerant to biotic and abiotic stresses. This is a general company statement, not a GK 3150 trial result. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/maize-seeds-10565569848.html

DISEASE RESISTANCE (portfolio level only): The company's maize listings describe some hybrids as tolerant to leaf blights and PFSR (pink/purple-type stalk rot wording as given in the source). The listing does not name GK 3150 as one of them. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/maize-seeds-10565569848.html

PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found specific to GK 3150.

QTL/MARKERS: No evidence found.

YIELD AND TRIALS: No evidence found from AICRP or peer-reviewed trials. The IIMR cultivar table shows a numeric value of 9.145 beside the GK 3150 entry, but the page does not label its unit or meaning, so it should not be read as a yield figure. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/

BREEDER/INSTITUTION (company background): Ganga Kaveri describes itself as having started seed production with the Rockefeller Foundation and National Seeds Corporation, and as having built a germplasm bank of inbreds from national and international institutes. This is general company background, not GK 3150 breeding records. -- https://gangakaveri-website.webflow.io/ ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/paddy-seeds-10565600873.html

SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs): No evidence found for GK 3150. Only retailer listings for a different hybrid, GK 3122, were found. -- https://agroshopy.com/index.php?route=product%2Fmanufacturer%2Finfo&manufacturer_id=14

seednet_fields.Parentage: Fodder Bajra CO 7 x Napier FD 459.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Under irrigated condition in garden lands for the states of NWZ & CZ (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Maharhtra, Gujarat, UP, MP and Chhattisgarh).
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for growing under irrigated conditions in garden lands. 1.	Spacing: 60 x 50 cm 2.	Set rate: 33,333 two budded sets/ha. 3.	Highly responsive to fertilizers Fertilizer requirement: 1.	FYM: 25
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Pink pigmenatation in the wall of leaf sheath. Profusely tillering (30 – 35 tillers/clump), high leafy (380 – 400 leaves/clump) long and broad leaves (90 – 100 cm long and 4.0 – 4.5 cm width) with high leaf stem ratio (0.7 – 0.8). Medium green soft leaves and stem serration on leaf margin.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to leaf blight and MR to leaf spot diseases.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Resistant to major pests in University trials.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): FYM: 25 t/ha 100:50:40 NPK/ha as basal + 50% N (50 kg N/ha) after each cut.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: BAIF Bajra-5 (CSC minutes name "BAIF Bajra- 5"; Seednet name "BAIF BAJRA-5"; the evidence below refers to the same pearl millet fodder variety under both names. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search.)

EVIDENCE DIGEST: NDFB-3 (CSC variety name) / NDFB-3 (Seednet name); variety code Narendra Chara Bajra-3; crop: pearl millet (bajra) fodder

Name note: The CSC name and the Seednet name are both NDFB-3, so every finding below refers to the same name. The variety code Narendra Chara Bajra-3 also appears in the sources and was treated as the same variety.

Search scope: Four searches were run. Two of them returned mostly unrelated results, so several headings below are "No evidence found."

STRESS TOLERANCE

EVIDENCE DIGEST: PCB 166 (bajra/pearl millet, Seednet name PCB 164, code FBL 4), Punjab Agricultural University

Search budget: 4 web_search queries were run (PCB 166 variety; PCB 164 bajra fodder variety; PCB 166 breeder; PCB 164 bajra FBL 4 research). The fourth returned unrelated results, and no query was run for seed availability because the 4-search limit was reached.

Name note: The evidence below refers to PCB 166 unless stated otherwise. The Seednet name PCB 164 belongs to an older PAU composite, released in 2003 (80-day maturity, about 15 q/acre grain, tolerant to downy mildew). It is not the same variety as PCB 166, so no PCB 164 trait data is attributed to PCB 166 here. Release-date note: the input gives 2022-10-26, but the PAU announcement is dated 08-03-2022 and lists PCB 166 among eight varieties recommended for Punjab. The 26 October date could not be verified.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found for PCB 166. The PAU kharif package listing describes it as tolerant to all major pearl millet diseases, which is a disease statement, not a stress statement. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf

drought.details: The variety is resistant to moisture stresses and tolerant to drought, requiring minimal water. It withstands adverse agroclimatic conditions.

heat.details: Tolerant to high temperatures.

salinity.details: Tolerant to salt stress.

flood.details: Bajra, as a crop, does not tolerate water-logging; therefore, standing rainwater should be avoided.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to downy mildew and other biotic stresses. It exhibits moderate resistance to smut, red leaf spot, and zonate leaf spot disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to shoot fly and less susceptible to top borer.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported fodder yields include 585.2 q/ha, 234 q green fodder, and 31197.2 kg/ha (311.972 q/ha). Grain yields reported are 12.8 q and 32.1 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Suitable for all bajra growing areas of Punjab and is noted for its ability to withstand adverse agroclimatic conditions, indicating good stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: A quick-growing, dual-purpose composite variety suitable for grain and fodder production. It is adapted to all bajra growing areas of Punjab, and can also be cultivated in regions like Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu due to its stress tolerance. Conflicting reports describe it as both 'early maturing' and 'late maturing'.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: A dual-purpose composite variety known for good quality stover and fodder, and very good popping quality. It is tolerant to lodging and is considered a hardy fodder crop.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Yield performance has been compared against check varieties, with PCB 165 showing a fodder yield of 585.2 q/ha compared to 535.4 q/ha for a check. Another variety, PCB 166, showed superiority over PCB 165 in green fodder yield by 12.3%.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Parentage involves chain crossing of 8 elite phenotypically superior lines. No specific genetic markers (e.g., SNP, SSR) directly associated with PCB 165 were specified in the provided results.

No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for TSFB 17-7 or Telangana Fodder Bajra 1. -- none

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The CGIAR leaf-spot and blight resistance statement refers to the 2020 TSFB 15-4 and TSFB 15-8 releases, not TSFB 17-7, so I did not attribute it here. -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/rising-fodder-shortage-prompts-release-of-two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-and-higher-forage-in-south-india/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Performance of TSFB 17-7 and TSFB 18-1 against national and zonal checks (2019-2021) is charted in an ICRISAT press release, but the retrieved text gives no yield values. -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-forage-yields-released-in-india
TSFB 17-7 is described as a single-cut pearl millet variety for the rainy season (maturity and yield figures not stated). -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-forage-yields-released-in-india
Single-cut listing for TSFB 17-7, released 2021 by PJTSAU, Hyderabad, with recommended states Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka (release year conflicts with the 2022 CVRC date). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382887644_Fodder_Crops_Technologies_A_Five_Years_2019-2023_Journey_of_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization

GENETICS AND QTL
Developed from ICRISAT pearl millet breeding material in collaboration with PJTSAU (this is the only origin statement found; parentage is not specified). -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-forage-yields-released-in-india
No QTL, marker or genomic study for TSFB 17-7 was found. Recurrent-selection and SSR studies returned in the search concern TSFB 15-4, TSFB 15-8 or unrelated germplasm and were discarded. -- none

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University (PJTSAU), Hyderabad, in collaboration with ICRISAT. -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-forage-yields-released-in-india
Release listing: "Telangana Fodder Bajra 1 (TSFB 17-7)", released 2022, CVRC, in the Fodder Bajra table, with no station name given. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/
Breeder name: No named breeder for TSFB 17-7 was found. Dr T Shashikala (PJTSAU Forage Breeder) and Dr SK Gupta (ICRISAT Pearl Millet Breeder) are named only for TSFB 15-4 and TSFB 15-8, so they are not attributed to this variety. -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/rising-fodder-shortage-prompts-release-of-two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-and-higher-forage-in-south-india/
Institution naming: the PJTSAU page spells it "Professor Jayashankar Telangana Agricultural University". -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute website: www.pjtsau.edu.in (https://pjtsau.edu.in/index.html), as listed on the FAO AGRIS record. -- https://www.fao.org/agris/zh/node/124619
Headquarters location: Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, Telangana (institute-level; no postal address or PIN for the forage programme was found). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professor_Jayashankar_Telangana_State_Agricultural_University
Official email and phone: not found in any retrieved page. No breeder-level contact found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not stated in retrieved text (2023). Fodder Crops Technologies: A Five Years (2019-2023) Journey of AICRP on Forage Crops and Utilization. AICRP on Forage Crops and Utilization report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382887644_Fodder_Crops_Technologies_A_Five_Years_2019-2023_Journey_of_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specifically on TSFB 17-7 was found. The Pharma Innovation Journal 2021 forage pearl millet trial and the Shashikala forage-resources paper do not name this variety, so they were discarded.

None of these were attributed to this variety. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/fodder-bajra-vitagraze-seed-17507828312.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Telangana, as stated for TSFB 17-7 in the ICRISAT release. -- https://pressroom.icrisat.org/two-pearl-millet-varieties-with-superior-forage-yields-released-in-india
The AICRP listing adds Andhra Pradesh, which conflicts with the three-state input. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382887644_Fodder_Crops_Technologies_A_Five_Years_2019-2023_Journey_of_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization

**EVIDENCE DIGEST: Telangana Multicut Bajra (TSFB 18-1), pearl millet fodder**

Name check: the release-minutes name you supplied is "Telangana Multicut Bajra". The PJTAU page spells it "Telangana Multi Cut Bajra (TSFB 18-1)". The Seednet name is "TELANGANA MULTICUT BAJRA (TSFB 18-1)". The findings below refer to the same variety under the code TSFB 18-1 and the names above. Four searches were run.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
No evidence found. Searches returned only general pearl millet or other-variety drought claims (for example, Bajra (Pearl Millet) is a drought-resistant fodder crop suited for arid regions.). These are from a private seed company's page about generic bajra, not this variety. -- https://shaktivardhakhspl.com/crops/forage-crops/bajra-fodder/ (discarded, generic)

**DISEASE AND PEST**
No evidence found. The only disease-resistance statements found concern other products, such as Nitya Vikas, Nutrifeed and Green Gold Bajra Multicut, and were discarded. -- https://agroshopy.com/index.php?route=product%2Fproduct&product_id=595 (discarded, other variety)

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- TSFB 18-1 appears in the AICRP on Forage Crops national group meet souvenir (Kharif and Rabi 2024), in a list entry titled as a multicut variety for summer 2021-22 from PJTSAU, Hyderabad. The entry gives no yield or agronomic data. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384978222_Souvenir_National_Group_Meet_Kharif_and_Rabi_2024_Published_by_BAU_Ranchi_and_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
- No yield, maturity, cutting-number or agronomy data for TSFB 18-1 were found. A 2021 AICRP Rajendranagar field trial was found, but it tested TSFB 15-4, TSFB 15-8 and Moti bajra, not TSFB 18-1, so it was discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/337210042_GREEN_FODDER_YIELD_AND_QUALITY_OF_DUAL_PURPOSE_PEARL_MILLET_MILLET_PENNISETUM_GLAUCUM_L_VARIETIES_AS_INFLUENCED_BY_CUTTING_AND_NITROGEN_MANAGEMENT (discarded, other varieties)

**GENETICS AND QTL**
No evidence found. Genomic and heterosis studies found name other hybrids or composites, not TSFB 18-1. -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41788218/ (discarded)

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Institution: the PJTAU Director of Research page lists the variety under fodder bajra with release year 2022 and the release committee CVRC. -- https://pjtau.edu.in/director-of-research-2/

Notified for awareness generation among farmers.
