search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CROP CONFLICT: the record lists crop "jatropha" (variety_name BALAJI) but the Seednet crop is "CABBAGE" (seednet_variety_name Balaji). The searches found no official BALAJI variety under either crop. Each heading below states which name its evidence refers to.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- BALAJI (jatropha): No evidence found. Results covered only Jatropha curcas as a species, which is generally described as drought-adapted and able to grow on marginal soils, not this variety -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/bio-fuels/Biofuel_jatropa.html
- Balaji (CABBAGE, Seednet name): No evidence found. The only related page is a commercial F1 listing that describes vigorous plants but gives no stress data -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/welcome-balaji-cabbage-seeds

DISEASE AND PEST
- BALAJI (jatropha): No evidence found.
- Balaji (CABBAGE): No evidence found. Listing gives no resistance information -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/welcome-balaji-cabbage-seeds

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- BALAJI (jatropha): No evidence found for a variety-level trial. Species-level agronomy only -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/bio-fuels/Biofuel_jatropa.html
- Balaji (CABBAGE): Commercial seed-company listing gives maturity of 75-80 days, head weight of 2.0-2.5 kg, semi-flat bluish-green heads, and says it is an F1 hybrid. This is marketing data, not trial data -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/welcome-balaji-cabbage-seeds

GENETICS AND QTL
- BALAJI (jatropha): No evidence found. The Jatropha breeding study returned concerns CJH backcross clones from TNAU, not BALAJI -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9449966/
- Balaji (CABBAGE): No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- BALAJI (jatropha): No breeder or developing institute found. Balaji Plantations of Shahjahanpur is a commercial nursery business, not a breeding programme -- https://www.indiamart.com/balaji-plantations/
- Balaji (CABBAGE): No ICAR, SAU or institute breeder found. Balaji Seeds (a private company) states that it releases cultivars, but names no breeder for a cabbage variety -- https://www.balajiseeds.in/ ; Balaji Agribiotech is a private hybrid-seed company -- http://www.balajiagribiotech.com/
- Note: the researcher "G Darshan Balaji" in a 2023 vegetable-breeding book chapter is unrelated to this variety and is not evidence for it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376828391_Advances_in_VEGETABLE_BREEDING

CONTACT DETAILS
- BALAJI (jatropha): Balaji Plantations, Shahjahanpur - 242306, Uttar Pradesh, India; listed owner "R Gupta (Owner)". A second listing names the seller "Ramesh". This is a commercial nursery, not a variety contact -- https://www.indiamart.com/balaji-plantations/ ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/jatropha-ratanjot-biodiesel-nurseries-4786222833.html
- Balaji (CABBAGE): Balaji Seeds website: no email, phone or postal address captured in the results -- https://www.balajiseeds.in/ . Balaji Agribiotech website: no email, phone or address captured -- http://www.balajiagribiotech.com/
- No ICAR, institute or SAU contact found.

PUBLICATIONS
- BALAJI (jatropha): No evidence found.
- Balaji (CABBAGE): No evidence found. Returned papers were on unrelated topics or authors with the same surname.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- BALAJI (jatropha): No evidence found.
- Balaji (CABBAGE): No evidence found. The 56th Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards minutes (27-28 June 2010) are online at https://www.yumpu.com/en/document/view/6732910/minutes-of-the-56th-meeting-of-central-sub-seednet-india. The retrieved text does not mention Balaji, so the 2010 release cannot be confirmed from it.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- BALAJI (jatropha): Balaji Plantations sells Jatropha ratanjot nursery plants (listed as out of stock on the page). This is planting material, not a notified variety -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/jatropha-ratanjot-biodiesel-nurseries-4786222833.html
- Balaji (CABBAGE): Balaji cabbage F1 seed is sold by DesiKheti at Rs 249, with Welcome Seeds as vendor -- https://www.desikheti.com/collections/buy-cabbage-seeds-online-at-best-price
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS (BALAJI, jatropha and Balaji, CABBAGE, combined)
- No evidence found.

GAPS
- Four searches were run. The fourth covered cabbage research, not seed. Seed evidence came from incidental results. No KrishiKosh, AICRP or Seednet variety page was retrieved for either name, so the variety code H0302103 and the 2010-10-10 release date remain unverified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Arka Krishna (CSC name) / Hare Krishna (Seednet name), Dolichos bean (Lablab purpureus)

Name note: The evidence below refers to Arka Krishna, the dolichos bean variety from ICAR-IIHR. Under the Seednet name "Hare Krishna" with crop "CABBAGE", the only hit was a private F1 cabbage hybrid, so it is not evidence for this variety. The Seednet portal produced no dolichos record for this name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Only the general pole-type description is given; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance is recorded for Arka Krishna. Low-moisture tolerance is attributed to other IIHR dolichos varieties (Arka Jay, Arka Vijay) -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
- No evidence found for Arka Krishna-specific terminal moisture stress tolerance. The 2023 Legume Research paper refers to a released variety only in general terms, without naming Arka Krishna -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4418

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to Arka Krishna. Rust resistance is recorded for Arka Prasidhi, not Arka Krishna -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Arka Krishna is described as a pole type, photo-insensitive and early variety, with pods borne in clusters that are dark green, per the IIHR variety page -- https://www.iihr.res.in/dolichos-bean-arka-krishna
- Pod yield is reported at 30.0 t/ha over a 120-day duration. The "early" description and the 120-day duration are inconsistent and should be checked against the release notification -- https://www.iihr.res.in/dolichos-bean-arka-krishna
- No Arka Krishna-specific multi-location trial results found. The Telangana and Dharmapuri trial papers concern Arka Amogh and Arka Sambhram, not Arka Krishna -- https://www.academia.edu/164908507/Performance_Evaluation_of_Dolichos_Bean_Lablab_purpureus_L_Variety_Arka_Amogh_for_Growth_Yield_and_Economic_Traits_under_Semi_Arid_Agro_Ecosystems_of_Telangana ; http://www.plantarchives.org/SPL%20ISSUE%2020-2/611__3762-3765_.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree: developed by pedigree selection from F7 generation of the cross IIHR 178 x Arka Swagath -- https://www.iihr.res.in/dolichos-bean-arka-krishna
- The PPV&FRA DUS guideline uses Arka Krishna as a reference for several descriptors (e.g., fresh seed colour, seed shape, pod pubescence). The per-character attributions in the extracted table are ambiguous -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/dolichosbeanguideline.pdf
- No QTL or marker study found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru -- https://www.iihr.res.in/dolichos-bean-arka-krishna ; https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-15/
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The IIHR page does not name the breeder.
- Division: Division of Vegetable Crops, IIHR (per a Plant Breeding scientist's slide deck on dolichos seed production; not confirmed as the Arka Krishna breeder) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/dolichos-seed-production/151052854

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. B.R. Raghu, Scientist (Plant Breeding), Division of Vegetable Crops, IIHR, Bangalore; email raghubr@iihr.res.in. Source is a slide deck, not an official directory, and he is not confirmed as the variety's breeder -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/dolichos-seed-production/151052854
- Institute website: iihr.res.in -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-15/
- Postal address, phone and official institute contact page: No evidence found in search results.

PUBLICATIONS
- No Arka Krishna-specific peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper was found in the searches.
- Related but not about Arka Krishna: Balaraju, S. & Ramesh, S. (2023). Identification of Indices for Empirical Selection of Dolichos Bean [Lablab purpureus (L.) Var. Lignosus] Genotypes for Tolerance to Terminal Moisture Stress. Legume Research 46(6): 695-699 -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4418
- Related but not about Arka Krishna: Mahesh, R.O. et al. (2019). Evaluation of dolichos bean genotypes. Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 8(4): 1729-1732 -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue4/PartAC/8-4-269-407.pdf
- Related but not about Arka Krishna: Sharma, V.K. et al. (2025). Performance Evaluation of Dolichos Bean Variety 'Arka Amogh' under Semi-Arid Telangana. Journal of Scientific Research and Reports -- https://doi.org/10.9734/JSRR/2025/V31I123852

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Arka Krishna seed from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or private dealers.
- Seednet search under "Hare Krishna" returned only a private Tokita F1 cabbage hybrid and unrelated items -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/tokita-hare-krishna-cabbage-seeds
- The IIHR portal has an online seed portal entry for related varieties (Arka Vijay, Arka Jay), not confirmed for Arka Krishna -- https://www.iihr.res.in/indian-beandolichos-bean-lab-lab-purpureus-l-arka-vijay-0

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Karnataka, per IIHR (suitable for Karnataka) -- https://www.iihr.res.in/dolichos-bean-arka-krishna

dashboard_data.key_attributes: CMS-based F1 hybrid (Pusa Hybrid-82). Dark green, waxy leaves. Flat, compact heads. Matures in 70-75 days. Trial yield about 47.9 t/ha.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: KTCBH-822 (Pusa Hybrid-82) is a CMS-based white cabbage F1 hybrid from ICAR-IARI Katrain. It has dark green, waxy leaves and compact flat heads, and it matures in 70-75 days with trial yields of about 47.9 t/ha. Institutional sources document its release and yield, but no stress tolerance, disease or pest resistance, or Gujarat suitability is confirmed for this hybrid.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: A CMS-based cabbage hybrid from IARI Katrain, with flat, compact heads and dark green waxy leaves. It matures in 70-75 days and yielded 47.92 t/ha in 2015-16 trials, above the check Pusa Cabbage Hybrid 1 (41.54 t/ha).
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No stress tolerance has been documented for this hybrid. The drought, heat, salt and submergence snippets refer to other genotypes or crops. No disease or pest data were found, and no genetic marker or QTL information exists.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Karan 5 (CSC name "Karan 5"; Co 0124; Seednet name "Karan"; crop sugarcane)

Searches run: 4 (within the 3–4 limit). Name note: the evidence below refers to "Karan 5 (Co 0124)" from the ICAR-SBI and PPVFRA lists. No search returned a Seednet portal record for "Karan" under sugarcane or cabbage, so the Seednet name and the CABBAGE crop label remain unverified. Results for "Karan" also matched other Karan-named varieties (Karan 1, 2, 4, 13), which I excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Co 0124 specifically. A 2010–11 ICAR report mentions drought and salinity tolerance for unnamed lines, and the snippet does not clearly link that to Co 0124 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Co 0124 specifically. A ChiniMandi article describes an unnamed 2009 North West Zone variety with moderately resistant reaction to pathotypes cf7 and cf8, but it does not name Karan 5, so I did not attribute it -- https://www.chinimandi.com/icar-sbi-readies-to-release-three-disease-resistant-high-yield-sugarcane-varieties-in-2026-director/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No Co 0124-specific yield, maturity, or trial data found. The only mention is a truncated listing of "Co 0124 (Karan 5)" in a 2010–11 ICAR crop-improvement annual report -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The QTL papers retrieved concern other populations, such as Brazilian cultivars, CP clones, and Indian bi-parental crosses that do not include Co 0124 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00122-011-1748-8

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Co 0124 is listed among CVRC-released and notified varieties of ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (SBI), Coimbatore -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/from-the-director-s-desk?id=363
  -- The ICAR-SBI Regional Centre Karnal states it developed Co 0124 among its recent early varieties -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=5563
  -- Breeder names for Co 0124: No evidence found. Dr. P. Govindaraj is named as ICAR-SBI institute director, not as a breeder of this variety -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/ag-tech-research-news/icar-sbi-breeds-three-disease-resistant-sugarcane-varieties-for-indias-cane-belt/
  -- Parentage: No evidence found. Year of release: No evidence found. Release year is blank in the input and was not found in the search results.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. No email, phone, or postal address for SBI or the Karnal centre appeared in the results. Institute-level pages: ICAR-SBI site -- https://sugarcane.res.in/ (also listed as sugarcane.icar.gov.in). Karnal Regional Centre page -- https://sugarcane.res.in/?page_id=5563. drought.details: Co 0237 (Karan-8) is listed among sugarcane varieties suited to drought conditions and is described as an early maturity clone. The digest does not grade the level of drought tolerance and reports no drought trial data or physiological mechanism.

heat.details: No heat trial evidence for Co 0237 was found in the digest. Leaf-tip drying is reported as common in summer, but this is not attributed as a heat-tolerance result for the variety.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. No salinity evidence for Co 0237 was found. The only salinity-related hit was a generic paper on the variety list in the CO 11015 study, which concerns a different variety and is excluded.

flood.details: Co 0237 is reported as tolerant of waterlogging. The digest does not describe a flood trial or mechanism, and waterlogging tolerance is used here only as the closest available evidence for flood conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Red rot: Co 0237 is rated moderately resistant to red rot, with the prevalent races noted (one source). The second source repeats the moderately resistant rating to the red rot pathogen. No evidence was found for smut, wilt or other diseases specific to Co 0237.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence was found for top borer or insect resistance specific to Co 0237.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield under normal condition is 71.33 ton/ha (cane). In AICRP trials in the North Western Zone, Co 0237 averaged 71.33 t/ha cane and 9.34 t/ha sugar.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The digest gives zone-level trial means only, with no multi-environment stability analysis.
agronomic_details.adaptation: North Western Zone (AICRP trials and ICAR-SBI North-West recommendation). Recommended for Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh (western and central). Release year note: the record lists 2011-06-28, but the sources say the clone was identified in 2010 by the AICRP varietal identification committee. No notification number was found. The release date needs checking against CVRC notifications.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified in digest. The digest describes Co 0237 as an early-maturing clone but gives no day count.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Free of spines and splits (per digest). Jaggery quality is rated A1 with a light yellow colour, and fibre is about 12.98%. Morphological details beyond these are Not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: AICRP North Western Zone trials: Co 0237 averaged 71.33 t/ha cane, 9.34 t/ha sugar and 18.78% juice sucrose. Checks were CoJ 64 (67.59 t/ha cane) and CoPant 84211 (66.84 t/ha cane). Within the zone, the clone ranked first for juice sucrose, fourth for sugar yield and fifth for cane yield. The AICRP varietal development table reports the same cane yield (71.33) and sucrose (18.78) figures and lists the clone as early-maturing, identified in 2010 for the North West Zone. No stress-specific trial results were found.

- Co 0237 is reported as tolerant of waterlogging. -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- Co 0237 is described as free of spines and splits, and leaf-tip drying is common in summer. -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- No salinity, flood or heat trial evidence for Co 0237 was found in these results. The only salinity-related hit was a generic paper on the variety list in the CO 11015 study (see PUBLICATIONS).

DISEASE AND PEST
- Co 0237 is rated moderately resistant to red rot, with the prevalent races noted. -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
- Co 0237 is rated moderately resistant to the red rot pathogen. -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/
- No evidence found for smut, top borer, wilt or insect resistance specific to Co 0237.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In AICRP trials in the North Western Zone, Co 0237 averaged 71.33 t/ha cane, 9.34 t/ha sugar and 18.78% juice sucrose, against checks CoJ 64 (67.59 t/ha) and CoPant 84211 (66.84 t/ha). -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
- Within the zone, the clone ranked first for juice sucrose, fourth for sugar yield and fifth for cane yield. -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
- The AICRP varietal development table lists Co 0237 as an early-maturing variety with the same cane yield (71.33) and sucrose (18.78) figures, identified in 2010 for the North West Zone. -- https://www.iisr.nic.in/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
- Jaggery quality is rated A1 with a light yellow colour, and fibre is about 12.98%. -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/
- Release year: the record lists 2011-06-28, but the sources say the clone was identified in 2010 by the AICRP varietal identification committee. No notification number was found. The release date needs checking against CVRC notifications.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Co 0237 was selected from the progeny of the cross Co 93016 GC. -- https://krishijagran.com/featured/sugarcane-varieties-suitable-under-abiotic-stress-conditions/ (also https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/)
- This is a selection source, not a full pedigree. The record's parentage field ("Not specified") should be reviewed against the official notification. No QTL or marker study on Co 0237 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Co 0237 was bred at the Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Regional Centre, Karnal (Haryana), part of ICAR-Sugarcane Breeding Institute (Coimbatore). -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/ ; https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/component/content/article?id=171
- The ICAR-SBI Coimbatore recent-releases page lists Co 0237 (Karan-8) under varieties for North-West India. -- https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/index.php/en/component/content/article?id=171
- No individual breeder or lead scientist name was found for Co 0237. The Karnal scientist names in results (Dr M.R. Meena, Dr Bakshi Ram) appear only in connection with Karna-18 and Co 12029, so they are not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact was found. No official email, phone or postal address for the ICAR-SBI Regional Centre, Karnal, was found in these results. Institute-level pages found: https://sugarcane.icar.gov.in/ (ICAR-SBI, Coimbatore) and https://sugarcane.res.in/ (ICAR-SBI research page). Neither contact page was checked for details.
- Note: the sugarcane.icar.gov.in page was only seen in search snippets. Confirm the Karnal Regional Centre address and phone on the institute's contact page before use.

PUBLICATIONS
- Shukla, S.K.; Sharma, Lalan; Awasthi, S.K.; Pathak, A.D. (2017). Sugarcane in India: Package of Practices for Different Agro-climatic Zones. AICRP(S) Technical Bulletin No. 1, ICAR-IISR, Lucknow -- https://www.nitiforstates.gov.in/public-assets/Policy/policy_files/TNG1660A000065.pdf (Co 0237 is listed among varieties for Rajasthan, central and western UP.)
- Authors not identified (2018). Co 0237 (Karan 8) variety note, blog post, not peer-reviewed -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/ (cited for trial data; secondary source)
- Authors not identified. CO 11015 (ATULYA): A recently notified sugarcane variety for Tamil Nadu. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342173736_CO_11015_ATULYA_A_RECENTLY_NOTIFIED_SUGARCANE_VARIETY_FOR_TAMIL_NADU (Co 0237 appears only in a list of 17 clones in the abstract. This paper is about Co 11015, so the mention is incidental, not a study of Karan 8.)
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis, KrishiKosh record or DOI specifically on Co 0237 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Co 0237 (Karan 8) seed sales from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU or private dealers. The search returned general seed pages and an ICAR-SBI note about demand for Co 0238, which is a different variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICRP technical bulletin lists Co 0237 for Rajasthan, central and western Uttar Pradesh. -- https://www.nitiforstates.gov.in/public-assets/Policy/policy_files/TNG1660A000065.pdf
- An ICAR-SBI North-West recommendation covers Haryana, Punjab, western and central UP, Uttarakhand and Rajasthan. -- https://sugarprocessqulitycontrol.blogspot.com/2018/ (secondary; matches the record's list)
- The record's list (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Western and Central UP) matches the NWZ recommendation; Punjab and Haryana are not named in the bulletin excerpt.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Prachi (HI 1563), wheat

NAME NOTE: The evidence below refers to "Pusa Prachi" / "HI 1563" (variety_name and variety_code). The Seednet name "Pusa Pakchoi-1" (listed under CABBAGE) returned no evidence. The only results were pak choi retailers in the UK and US, which were discarded.

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION (supporting line, no heading assigned)
Pusa Prachi (HI-1563) is listed in a Bihar notified-variety list with a date of 25/03/2011 and S.O. 632(E); the input release date is 2010-12-23, and the list's date column is not labelled -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
HI 1563 is listed among wheat varieties notified in India since 1965 by the CVRC sub-committee -- https://www.aicrpwheatbarleyicar.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/wheat-varieties-notified-in-india.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of HI 1563 / Pusa Prachi. The search returned only general IARI pages and other varieties (Pusa Basmati 1121, HD 3386, Pusa Malvi), which were discarded.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is documented as officially notified (2022) and as the first indigenous Pakchoi for the North Indian Plains. However, no stress or climate traits, no yield figures and no peer-reviewed citations were found. The sources are institutional reports, so the score falls between the 'minimal info' and 'only yield info' tiers. No Gujarat-specific adaptation evidence exists, and the variety is notified only for Delhi. It is not recommended for Gujarat without local trials.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: First indigenous Pakchoi variety (IARI); for North Indian Plains; notified for NCT of Delhi; suited to drip irrigation studies

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Pakchoi-1 is an IARI-developed Pakchoi variety, the first indigenous one for the North Indian Plains, and it was notified in 2022 for NCT of Delhi. No stress tolerance, disease or pest resistance, yield, maturity or molecular data were found, and the evidence consists only of institutional reports and a gazette notification. Evidence quality is low and Gujarat suitability is untested.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: IARI-bred Pakchoi (a non-heading Chinese cabbage type) notified in 2022 for Delhi and the North Indian Plains. Yield, maturity, parentage and morphology are not specified in the sources.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: No variety-specific evidence of abiotic stress tolerance or biotic resistance was found. Drought, disease and resistance snippets in the results refer to other crops. The only related work is a drip irrigation and soil matric potential study.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I'll start with the first three searches in parallel, since they don't depend on each other.STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant to drought and waterlogging, as listed for CoOr 03151 (Sabita) in the SRS Nayagarh row of an abiotic-stress variety table -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7501393/
Rated moderately tolerant to drought in a sugarcane chapter table, but the table layout makes it unclear whether this descriptor belongs to CoOr 03151 or the neighbouring Co 86249 row -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to red rot and smut in the same chapter table; the same row-attribution caveat applies -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane
Red rot and smut reaction for CoOr 03151 (Sabita) is therefore not confirmed from a clean source; no AICRP entry for this variety was retrieved.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Identified in 2009 as an early-maturing selection; AICRP table lists CoOr 03151 with cane yield 105.28 (units as given in table) and release years 2009-2011 -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/varietaldevelopment.htm
Described in an AICRP-linked review as spreading fast in the East Coast Zone -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
Odisha table lists CoOr 03151 (SABITA) with value 110.0 and code R; column headings are not in the retrieved text, so the meaning of these figures is unverified -- https://magazines.odisha.gov.in/Orissareview/2015/Jan/engpdf/104-107.pdf
Share of area reported as 18% in Odisha (AICRP-based review) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9012054/

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: a selection from the progeny of CoC 671 x Co 1148 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
No QTL or marker study for CoOr 03151 (Sabita) was found. The stress-responsive miRNA table in PMC7501393 names miRNAs for stress tolerance but does not link them to this variety's genotype; treat as no evidence.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing station: Sugarcane Research Station, Nayagarh (OUAT, Panipoila), an AICRP centre since 1983 -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/nayagarh.htm and https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/regularcentres.htm
Station-level linkage: the Tables page for stress tolerance attributes the CoOr 03151 (Sabita) entry to SRS Nayagarh -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7501393/
Named breeder for CoOr 03151 (Sabita): No evidence found. The station page names a sugarcane breeder and officer-in-charge, but does not tie him to this variety (see CONTACT DETAILS).
The "Co" prefix is the ICAR Sugarcane Breeding Institute naming convention, but no retrieved source names SBI Coimbatore as the developer of Sabita; do not assume it.

CONTACT DETAILS
Station contacts from the SRS Nayagarh page (station-level, not variety-specific) -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/nayagarh.htm
  Dr. Pramod Kumar Nayak, Sugarcane Breeder and Officer-In-Charge, Mob: 09937140810, pknpbg@gmail.com
  Dr. Jyoti Rekha Patnaik, Jr. Scientist (Agronomy), Mob: 08895351855, jrp_ouat@yahoo.com
  Ms. Swagatika Mohanty, Assistant Plant Pathologist, Mob: 09438639301, swagat.saroj@gmail.com
Station postal location: Sugarcane Research Station, Panipoila, 12 km from Nayagarh district headquarters, Odisha -- https://iisr.icar.gov.in/iisr/aicrp/pages/nayagarh.htm
University-level contact (not station): Odisha University of Agriculture & Technology, Bhubaneswar-751003, Odisha; (0674)-2397970/2397818; registrar@ouat.ac.in; www.ouat.ac.in -- https://ouat.ac.in/commodity/seed-research-nayagarh-sugarcane/

PUBLICATIONS
Dutta, D., & Ghosh, K. (2024). Sugarcane. In Modern Crop Production Technology of Kharif Crops (Vol. I, Ch. 14, pp. 160-177). JAYA Publishing House. Lists CoOr 03151 (Sabita, 2011) for the East Coast Zone -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane
Shukla, S. K., Zubair, A., Awasthi, S. K., & Pathak, A. D. (2018). AICRP technical publication-II: Sugarcane varieties identified by AICRP (S) in India. Lucknow: ICAR-IISR. Cited in a review that gives CoOr 03151 an 18% share in Odisha -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9012054/
Authors not shown (2020 or thereabouts, not confirmed). Forty Five Years of All India Coordinated Research Project on Sugarcane. Report, AICRP on Sugarcane, ICAR-IISR -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343442512_Forty_Five_Years_of_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sugarcane
Authors not shown. Current breeding and genomic approaches to enhance cane and sugar productivity under abiotic stress conditions (review, PMC7501393). Journal not shown in retrieved text -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7501393/
Note: the Co 15002 paper (Durai et al., 2021, J. Sugarcane Research, DOI 10.37580/JSR.2021.1.11.83-90) concerns a different clone and is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No seed source for CoOr 03151 (Sabita) was retrieved from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer pages. The seed-availability search was not run; the fourth search was used for contact details instead.

RECOMMENDED STATES
East Coast Zone; Odisha is named in the AICRP-based review and the chapter table -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9012054/ and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_Sugarcane
The chapter table places CoOr 03151 (Sabita, 2011) in the East Coast Zone, listing Odisha, coastal Andhra Pradesh and coastal Tamil Nadu as its states -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381880091_S

Arka Basant (capsicum): technicalkisan reports nursery seed rate of 400-500 g/ha and spacing of 60-75 cm by 45-60 cm. Arka Basant (capsicum): older release summary reports fruit weight of 50-80 g. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Arka Prasan / ARKA BASANT

NAME AND CROP MISMATCH (read first)
Blackgram: no evidence found. The "Arka Prasan" name in the CSC minutes appears only for ridge gourd, not blackgram. -- https://kvkariyalur.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/KVK-Ariyalur-TN-Annual-Report-2024.pdf (KVK Ariyalur, ridge gourd OFT); https://www.iihr.res.in/field-day-ridge-gourd-var-arka-prasan-organized-icar-iihr-panasachowdanahalli-village
The Arka Prasan ridge gourd variety is credited to IIHR Bengaluru, with a 2013 or 2016 release year given inconsistently in the KVK report. -- https://kvkariyalur.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/KVK-Ariyalur-Action-Plan-Detailed-Report-2024-25.pdf
The Seednet name ARKA BASANT refers to capsicum, and the evidence below for it is a different crop from the blackgram in the record. The evidence below refers to Arka Basant (capsicum), not to any blackgram variety. Parentage matches the capsicum record: "Improvement over IHR 225-1-1 (Var. Soroksan) followed by mass selection." -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
Year of release: not found for Arka Basant in any source retrieved. The "NaT" value is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Field tolerance of common leaf diseases is claimed for Arka Basant, with no quantified drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found. -- https://technicalkisan.com/seeds/capsicum/arka-basant (secondary commercial site)
A possible "triple resistance" to powdery mildew, downy mildew and anthracnose appears on the IIHR variety list, but the text sits beside other entries and may belong to a different capsicum variety, so treat it as unconfirmed for Arka Basant. -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
No evidence found for abiotic stress tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence).

DISEASE AND PEST
Field tolerance to common leaf diseases is the only disease claim found (see above). -- https://technicalkisan.com/seeds/capsicum/arka-basant
No evidence found for pest resistance, virus resistance or nematode resistance specific to Arka Basant.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity and yield figures conflict across sources:
- Harvest about 158-160 days from pruning; average bunch 410 g; TSS 20-21 °B; yield potential 40 t/ha and 36 kg/vine (IIHR bunch-type description). -- https://iihr.res.in/crop-wise
- Yield 15 t/ha in 180 days (older slideshare summary). -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/capsicum-varietal-wealth/193187274
- Yield 15-18 t/ha, rabi season, about 150-160 days, nursery seed rate 400-500 g/ha, spacing 60-75 cm by 45-60 cm. -- https://technicalkisan.com/seeds/capsicum/arka-basant
- Fruit weight 50-80 g, fruit erect, cream turning orange-red at maturity; yield potential 16 t/ha in 150 days (older release summary). -- https://www.slideshare.net/THANKLORD/varieties-of-capsicum
- Field-trial evidence: Arka Basant x IIHR-4096 showed good fruit length and earliness in a shadenet bell pepper hybrid study at IIHR. -- https://www.academia.edu/29284617/Evaluation_of_Varities_and_Hybrids_for_Yield_Attributes_in_Bell_Pepper_Capsicum_annuum_L_Under_Insect_Proof_Net_Cum_Shadenet
No blackgram agronomy or trial evidence found. Ridge gourd Arka Prasan OFT yielded 152.2 q/ha in Ariyalur (not the record's crop). -- https://kvkariyalur.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/KVK-Ariyalur-TN-Annual-Report-2024.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Ccs (capsanthin-capsorubin synthase) gene-specific marker polymorphism for red fruit colour, with Arka Basant among red-fruited lines at IIHR Bengaluru, 2013. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/314455223_Validation_of_Candidate_Gene_Specific_Markers_for_Ripe_Fruit_Colour_in_Bell_Pepper_Capsicum_annuumvar_grossum
No blackgram QTL or marker study linked to this variety found. The blackgram GWAS found (Punjab Agricultural University, 2022) covers a different panel and does not name this variety. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9310006/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru, Hesaraghatta Lake Post. -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
Origin: selection from Hungarian 'Soroksari' via IIHR 225-1-1, released by IIHR Bengaluru. -- https://www.slideshare.net/THANKLORD/varieties-of-capsicum

Arka Kamini (China aster): In a 2024-25 Nagpur trial of Arka-series varieties, Arka Aadya gave the highest flower count; Kamini's rank was not reported in the excerpt. -- https://zenodo.org/records/18400962
ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): IIHR gives indeterminate-type plant descriptions with a 16 t/ha yield in 150 days on one page, and determinate-type with 20 t/ha in 160 days on another. -- https://iihr.res.in/capsicum-arka-mohini-1 ; https://iihr.res.in/variety/arka-mohini
ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): Fruit weight and habit descriptions conflict across IIHR and third-party pages (130-150 g, 150-180 g, 180-200 g). -- https://iihr.res.in/variety/arka-mohini ; https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/commercial-varieties-of-capsicum.html
ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): Seed yield of about 150 kg/ha is listed. -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/03/commercial-varieties-of-capsicum.html

GENETICS AND QTL
Arka Kamini (China aster): No evidence found for QTL, marker or molecular studies.
ARKA MOHINI (capsicum): Its parentage (selection from Titan, and improvement over IIHR-214-1 followed by mass selection) is recorded, but no QTL or marker study was found. The combining-ability study is a crossing study, not a QTL study. -- https://www.slideshare.net/THANKLORD/varieties-of-capsicum ; https://jhs.iihr.res.in/index.php/jhs/article/download/1080/908/7389

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Arka Kamini (China aster): Developed by ICAR-IIHR, Bengaluru. Scientists named as advising the Bhoo-Samrudhi farmer: Dr R. Senthil Kumar, Dr Rajeev Kumar, Dr A.K. Nair, Dr J. Sathisha, and Dr P.C. Tripathi. No explicit breeder-of-record statement was found. -- https://www.iihr.res.in/performance-china-aster-cv-arka-kamini-chikkaballapur-under-icrisat-iihr-bhoo-samrudhi-project

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Shalimar Capsicum Hybrid-2 (searched under both names; the variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical, so no split was needed). DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for this variety. The same SKUAST-K article only mentions disease resistance as a general research focus of the vegetable division. -- https://kashmirreader.com/2026/07/17/skuast-k-advances-climate-resilient-vegetable-breeding/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Chilli genotype trials were run at SKUAST-K Shalimar, KVK Pulwama and KVK Budgam in kharif 2021-22. The trial materials were 78 entries (66 crosses and 12 parents), but the source does not name Shalimar Capsicum Hybrid-2. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372133109_Comparative_performance_of_chilli_Capsicum_annuum_L_genotypes_for_quantitative_and_qualitative_traits_under_temperate_conditions_of_Kashmir
Separately, an earlier Shalimar study evaluated 30 chilli genotypes at three Kashmir locations (Shalimar, Shuhama and Haran). This also does not name the variety. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/skuastjr-15-2-007

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage field is "Not specified", and no source gave pedigree, male-sterility system, or marker data for this hybrid.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The developing institution is most likely SKUAST-K (Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir), per the release record. The Division of Vegetable Science at the Shalimar campus runs the vegetable hybrid breeding, and its head is Prof. Ishfaq Abidi. No source ties Prof. Abidi or any named scientist to this specific hybrid, so this is institution-level only. -- https://kashmirreader.com/2026/07/17/skuast-k-advances-climate-resilient-vegetable-breeding/
No lead breeder name was found for this variety.

Search limit note: the search tool hit its usage limit after the first batch of four queries. Those four queries returned only truncated snippets, so the findings below are limited. Several headings have no usable evidence, and the gaps need follow-up.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for either name.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Appangala-2 is listed in a cardamom disease-resistance table as resistant to cardamom mosaic disease (row labelled "Appangala -2", with "Malabar" as the listed type). Attribution to this variety rests on that table entry; the page is a general cardamom cultivation review. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354638072_Cultivation_harvesting_processing_and_products_of_cardamom

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No trial, yield or maturity data for either name was retrieved.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The searches returned no QTL, marker or parentage record for either name. Parentage is listed as "Not specified" in the input.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution is named in the input as the Indian Institute of Spices Research (ICAR-IISR, Kozhikode). The IISR varieties page lists "Appangala 2" among cardamom varieties, which places it in IISR's variety listing. No breeder name was found. -- https://www.spices.res.in/pages/cardamom-varieties

CONTACT DETAILS -- The only institute address retrieved is for ICAR-IISR, Kozhikode, Kerala, PIN 673 012, from an IISR-branded PDF. No breeder email or phone was found. No institute email or phone was retrieved from the snippets. -- https://www.indianspices.com/sites/default/files/cultivation_practices-Cardamom.pdf

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming either variety was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for seed sales by NSC, a state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer. A cardamom cultivation PDF lists "Appangala 1" and "Appangala 2" in a table titled as important farmers' varieties in cardamom, not as released varieties with seed sources. -- https://www.indianspices.com/sites/default/files/cultivation_practices-Cardamom.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found confirming Karnataka and Kerala from a source. The input record gives "Karnataka & Kerala". Nothing retrieved verified it.

Flags for the record:
- The IISR and cultivation-practice pages list these names as cardamom varieties or farmers' varieties. Neither page confirms the 2017 CSC release, the NHY 35 code, or the recommended states.
- The Seednet name APPANGALA-1 and the CSC name Appangala-2 are not clearly the same entry. The evidence does not establish that the two names refer to one variety.
- The Appangala-1 search returned no page naming that variety. The Appangala-2 entries were the only ones that named the variety.
- The Seednet portal was not retrieved, so the Seednet record itself is unverified.

flood.details: No evidence found. The digest reports valley planting suitability and rhizome rot resistance, but no flood or waterlogging tolerance trial for this variety. Rhizome rot is a soil-borne disease, not a flood tolerance measure.

disease_resistance.summary: Rhizome rot (clump rot) caused by soil pathogens: resistant. Selected through clonal selection for this resistance together with high yield. Described as tolerant to rhizome rot and suited to valley planting; named as a rhizome-rot-resistant variety for valleys and rot-prone areas. Causal organisms named in one source as Pythium vexans and Rhizoctonia solani. Recommended for cultivation in areas prone to rhizome rot, in the context of chlorotic streak management. Not the katte/CMV-resistant variety; IISR Vijetha is the one recommended for mosaic areas, so no mosaic/katte resistance is attributed to IISR Avinash. Isolates of Colletotrichum gloeosporioides and Fusarium/Rhizoctonia/Pythium antagonists were tested on Avinash, but these results are not a resistance rating.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance rating found for IISR Avinash. Leaf blight and thrips reactions specific to this variety: no evidence found; the leaf blight and thrips results in the sources do not name it.

agronomic_details.yield: Conflicting figures in sources. (1) 2006 paper: average 643 kg/ha dry capsules, potential 979 kg/ha, dark green quality capsules. (2) IISR variety table and Krishi Jagran: 847 kg/ha dry capsules, potential 1483 kg/ha. The IISR table also reports essential oil 6.7%.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Yield recorded for 3 years at the original location only; multi-environment stability not reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to valley planting and rot-prone areas (rhizome rot). Yields well at 2.5 x 2 m spacing (IISR variety table). Recommended for Karnataka and Kerala.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 228.6 cm and 46 tillers per clump (Krishi Jagran). Dark green quality capsules (2006 paper). Essential oil 6.7% and extended flowering period (IISR variety table).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Selection trial: 4 plants selected from a population of over 51,000 plants for non-susceptibility to natural infection over 4-5 years and for high yield; yield recorded for 3 years at the original location. (2) Yield trials: 643 kg/ha average and 979 kg/ha potential (2006 paper); 847 kg/ha average and 1483 kg/ha potential (IISR table and Krishi Jagran). (3) Hybrid trial: in a preliminary evaluation trial (PET III) of 23 F1 hybrids, Mudigere 2 x IISR Avinash showed the highest plant height. (4) Breeding use: used as a female parent in hybridization with Appangala-1, Njallani green gold and Clone 893. Dry recovery figures (6-9%, 30.4/34.6 comparison values) appear in the digest without explicit attribution to this variety and are excluded.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: IISR (Avinash), cardamom (Elettaria cardamomum)

Name check: The variety_name ("IISR (Avinash)") and seednet_variety_name ("IISR (Avinash)") are identical. Sources use "IISR Avinash", "IISR-Avinash (RR1)" and "IISR Avinash (RR-1)". All findings below refer to this variety. The "Avinash-I" in one ISSR marker study is a different accession from Kozhikode and is excluded. The variety code H020216707 does not appear in any source found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to rhizome rot (clump rot) caused by soil pathogens; selected through clonal selection for this resistance and high yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264348817_IISR_Avinash_-_a_rhizome_rot_resistant_and_high_yielding_variety_of_cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton
- Described as tolerant to rhizome rot and suited to valley planting -- https://spices.res.in/itm-abi/page/spice-varieties
- Named as a rhizome-rot-resistant variety for valleys and rot-prone areas -- https://www.celkau.in/Crops/spices/cardamom/varieties.php (http://www.celkau.in/Crops/spices/cardamom/varieties.php)
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The moisture-stress trial in the Annual Report snippet does not name Avinash in the retrieved text -- https://spices.res.in/storage/app/public/publications/english/pdf/jN5n8KJzaRRuSEYMFdzuatH3A3HiOxp18YHPTmhm.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rhizome rot resistance, with the causal organisms named as Pythium vexans and Rhizoctonia solani -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-these-cardamom-varieties-for-higher-profitability-and-better-yields/
- Recommended for cultivation in areas prone to rhizome rot, in the context of chlorotic streak management -- https://www.indianspices.com/sites/default/files/cultivation_practices-Cardamom.pdf
- Not the katte/CMV-resistant variety; IISR Vijetha is the one recommended for mosaic areas -- https://pop.kau.in/spices&condiments.htm
- Leaf blight and thrips reaction specific to Avinash: No evidence found (leaf blight and thrips results in the sources do not name it) -- https://spices.res.in/mail/upload/202112272.pdf
- Isolates of Colletotrichum gloeosporioides and Fusarium/Rhizoctonia/Pythium antagonists were tested on Avinash, but the results are not a resistance rating -- https://spices.res.in/storage/app/public/publications/english/pdf/d6JJPi7unKVF2N6DLfJEQOwocCxXiKIEA2k4zhfK.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average yield 643 kg/ha (dry capsules), potential 979 kg/ha, dark green quality capsules (2006 paper) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264348817_IISR_Avinash_-_a_rhizome_rot_resistant_and_high_yielding_variety_of_cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton
- Conflicting figures: 847 kg/ha dry capsules with potential 1483 kg/ha, essential oil 6.7%, extended flowering period, yields well at 2.5 x 2 m spacing (IISR variety table) -- https://spices.res.in/itm-abi/page/spice-varieties
- Same 847 / 1483 figures, plant height 228.6 cm, 46 tillers per clump -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-these-cardamom-varieties-for-higher-profitability-and-better-yields/
- Selection trial details: 4 plants selected from a population of over 51,000 plants for non-susceptibility to natural infection for 4-5 years and high yield; yield recorded for 3 years at the original location -- https://spices.res.in/mail/upload/202112272.pdf (see also the 2006 paper: https://www.researchgate.net/profile/D-Prasath-2/publication/264348817_IISR_Avinash_-_a_rhizome_rot_resistant_and_high_yielding_variety_of_cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton/links/53d9cb610cf2a19eee880790/IISR-Avinash-a-rhizome-rot-resistant-and-high-yielding-variety-of-cardamom-Elettaria-cardamomum-Maton.pdf?origin=publication_list)
- Dry recovery of 6-9% in the medium class, and 30.4 / 34.6 values in a comparison table -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/smallcardemom.pdf and https://www.resurgentagric.com/img/resurgentagric_cardamom.pdf
- Breeding use as a parent: used as a female parent in hybridization with Appangala-1, Njallani green gold and Clone 893 -- https://spices.res.in/mail/upload/202112272.pdf
- Hybrid trial: Mudigere 2 x IISR Avinash showed the highest plant height in a preliminary evaluation trial (PET III) of 23 F1 hybrids -- https://spices.res.in/storage/app/public/publications/english/pdf/jN5n8KJzaRRuSEYMFdzuatH3A3HiOxp18YHPTmhm.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Developed by clonal selection, so no parentage is recorded in the sources. The "parentage: Not specified" entry is consistent with this. The sources conflict on origin: the IISR table says it is a selection from open-pollinated progeny of Appangala 1, while Krishi Jagran says it is derived from CCS-1 -- https://spices.res.in/itm-abi/page/spice-varieties ; https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-these-cardamom-varieties-for-higher-profitability-and-better-yields/
- Used as a reference entry in a PPV&FRA small cardamom descriptor table (DUS traits, e.g. panicle number and dry recovery) -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/smallcardemom.pdf
- QTL or marker-assisted studies specific to Avinash: No evidence found. The ISSR study names "Avinash-I" from Kozhikode, which is not this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/386098757_Advancements_in_Cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton_Breeding_Genetic_Diversity_Biotech_Strategies_and_Future_Directions

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeders named in the 2006 paper: M N Venugopal, D Prasath, Ravindra Mulge -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264348817_IISR_Avinash_-_a_rhizome_rot_resistant_and_high_yielding_variety_of_cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research, Cardamom Research Centre, Appangala, Madikeri, Karnataka (later a Regional Station, from November 2014) -- https://spices.res.in/storage/app/public/publications/english/pdf/d6JJPi7unKVF2N6DLfJEQOwocCxXiKIEA2k4zhfK.pdf
- Institute history (NRCS 1986, IISR 1995), Kozhikode headquarters -- https://spices.res.in/storage/app/public/publications/english/pdf/d6JJPi7unKVF2N6DLfJEQOwocCxXiKIEA2k4zhfK.pdf
- Release date: The CSC record gives 2017-09-18. The search found 1999 as the year of selection in the IISR table and "2000s" elsewhere. No CSC notification document was found -- https://spices.res.in/itm-abi/page/spice-varieties

CONTACT DETAILS
- M N Venugopal (breeder, Cardamom Research Centre); email as printed in the PDF: venugopal@iisr.or g (line-broken; probably venugopal@iisr.org, not verified) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264348817_IISR_Avinash_-_a_rhizome_rot_resistant_and_high_yielding_variety_of_cardamom_Elettaria_cardamomum_Maton
- Address (Cardamom

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The four searches returned nothing on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for GDC-1. The only carrot pages that came up were about Madhuban Gajar, a different variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page linked GDC-1 to disease or pest resistance. The Alternaria and nematode material in the search results concerns other carrot genotypes and lines, not GDC-1.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The study was run at the Horticulture farm, College of Horticulture, S. D. Agricultural University, Jagudan, Mehsana, Gujarat, comparing yield, quality and chemical composition under varying sowing times during rabi 2017-18, with four varieties (Patan Local, Pusa Vasuda, Pusa Rudhira and "Gujarat Dantiwada Carrot 1 (GDC 1)") in a split-plot design with three replications. The paper spells the name "Gujarat Dantiwada Carrot 1," not "Dantewada." The extracted table for GDC 1 gives a root yield of 18.07 t/ha in one row, but the table is garbled in the extraction, so the column alignment should be checked against the full paper before use. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=15935&vol=9-2-2020&SNo=15 ; https://www.ycjournal.net/Multilogicinscience/ResearchDocuments/PERFORMANC637160849317438161.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The Kalia carrot breeding review lists Indian carrot cultivars in a table, but the retrieved text does not show a GDC-1 entry, so I have not attributed anything to it. -- https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/371/317

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a named breeder or lead scientist for GDC-1. The only institutional link is the 2020 trial paper, which places the trial at SD Agricultural University's College of Horticulture, Jagudan, Mehsana, but does not name the breeder. Pages about Madhuban Gajar (Vallabhbhai Marvaniya, Junagadh; NIF/DST) are a different variety and are excluded. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=15935&vol=9-2-2020&SNo=15

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No SDAU, College of Horticulture or Jagudan email, phone, postal address or contact page was retrieved. I have not filled this in from memory. The institute contact page should be checked directly on the SDAU website.

PUBLICATIONS -- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2020). Performance of Different Varieties of Carrot (Daucus carota L.) with Respect to Yield, Quality and Chemical Compositions under Varying Sowing Times. Original Research Article, Volume 9, Issue 2, February 2020 (IJCMAS) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=15935&vol=9-2-2020&SNo=15 ; the same study also appears as a PDF on Multilogic in Science -- https://www.ycjournal.net/Multilogicinscience/ResearchDocuments/PERFORMANC637160849317438161.pdf
No other GDC-1 publications were found. AICRP, KrishiKosh and thesis searches were not run separately; the fourth search slot was used for seed availability.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for GDC-1 seed. Gujarat State Seed Corporation pages describe general seed supply through dealers but do not name GDC-1 -- https://www.newkerala.com/news/o/quality-certified-seeds-seed-corporation-driving-gujarats-agricultural-growth-197 . An ICAR-NHRDF availability PDF lists "Gujrat Dantewada Leafy," which is a coriander or methi variety, not carrot, so it is excluded -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Availability%20of%20Vegetable%20Seed%20with%20NHRDF%20in%202023-2024.pdf . Commercial carrot seed listings (Desikheti, TradeIndia, Naatigrains) do not mention GDC-1 and are excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The only location associated with GDC-1 is the Jagudan trial in Gujarat, which is a trial site and not a notified recommendation. The release year (2015), the release notification and the parentage are also unconfirmed. Seednet and CSC notification pages were not retrieved, so the variety name on the Seednet portal could not be checked against the release minutes.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety is officially notified and explicitly recommended for Gujarat (Zone VI), so it is relevant to the state. However, the sources are only an institutional annual report and a gazette notification. They contain no stress or climate traits, no yield data and no peer-reviewed research. The rubric's 50 band is for some stress or climate trait with no citation, and 60 is for at least one citation but weak stress traits. The variety has no stress trait and only institutional citations, so the score falls between these bands. It is set at 50 as a conservative, evidence-only choice, and it could be raised to about 60 if the official sources are accepted as citations.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Pusa Prateek (IPC-3) is a carrot variety from ICAR-IARI, notified in 2022 and recommended for Zone VI (RJ, GJ, HR, DL) and Zone VIII (KA, TN, etc.). The available sources are an institutional report and a gazette notification, and they give no data on stress tolerance, disease or pest reaction, yield, maturity or genetics. Evidence quality is low, so stress tolerance cannot be confirmed.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Vashda hybrid (IPC HC1) / carrot

Search log: four web_search queries were run ("Pusa Vashda hybrid carrot variety"; "Pusa Vashda hybrid carrot breeder developed by IARI"; "Pusa Vashda carrot research paper"; "Pusa Vashda hybrid carrot seed availability"). A fifth query ("Pusa Vashda" and "IPC HC1 carrot hybrid seednet") was blocked by the tool-call limit, so it was not run. I checked every result for "Vashda", "IPC HC1" and "HC1/HCI" and found no match for this variety. Names used in searching: "Pusa Vashda hybrid" (CSC minutes name) and "Pusa Vashda hybrid (IPC HCI)" (Seednet name). Neither name appeared in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no page naming this variety or its code.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page names this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The only carrot-related results were general varieties checklists and other carrot varieties, which I discarded under the relevance rule.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage was returned, and the record's parentage field is "Not specified."

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a breeder or lead scientist. Results only mentioned IARI in general terms in a national checklist of vegetable varieties (https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/pdf/tech_bulletin/national/Checklist-of-Commercial-Varieties-of-Vegetables.pdf). That page does not name this hybrid, so I have not attributed it to this variety. The institution listed in the CSC record (Indian Agricultural Research Institute) is taken from the input record only, not from search evidence.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No IARI division, station, email, phone or address was retrieved for this variety. Official IARI contacts should be checked directly at iari.res.in.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The carrot paper returned (Economic Impact of Vegetable Variety in Haryana: A Case of Pusa Rudhira of Carrot, https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Economic-Impact-of-Vegetable-Variety-in-Haryana:-A/b3228999089e1f0aee5ed120dc44bf8ed0299afc) concerns a different variety, Pusa Rudhira, so it is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed listings returned were for other Pusa-branded products (for example, a Pusa Yamdagini carrot listing on Amazon.in), which are different varieties and were excluded. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing for this hybrid was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found in search results. The input record gives "NCT of Delhi" as the recommended state, which is not confirmed by any retrieved source.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet portal entry for "Pusa Vashda hybrid (IPC HCI)" directly, search the CSC release minutes of 2015, and check IARI's vegetable science division and KrishiKosh for records of this hybrid.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot, per the ICAR-IIOR variety entry, JAU's release list and the Vikaspedia listing. The 2018 conference paper title also describes the hybrid as wilt and root rot resistant. No quantitative disease scoring was found in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to sucking pests and thrips, per the JAU new-variety release sheet. The JAU variety-13-years proceedings report lower leafhopper and fruit borer incidence than hybrid checks. These are field-level observations, not a formal resistance rating.

agronomic_details.yield: Mean seed yield 3820 kg/ha under irrigation (ICAR-IIOR entry). Station-level figure 3781 kg/ha with 48.30% oil (JAU station page). JAU release sheet gives potential yield 3500-4000 kg/ha and average 2340 kg/ha. Trial yield 3820 kg/ha, 9.0% above check GCH-7 (3503 kg/ha), in irrigated Gujarat (JAU proceedings).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The only multi-location evidence is the Assam and ARS Mandor trial mentions under field_trials, which are not established as stability data.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for irrigated areas of Gujarat (JAU). A listing under a GCH-9 (2018) heading claims rainfed recommendation for Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Odisha. This contradicts the irrigated-only Gujarat recommendation and is unverified, so it is not adopted here.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 105-110 cm; 100-seed weight 29.64 g; profuse branching; primary spike 100-104 days; seed-to-seed 210 days; first picking at 110-120 days after sowing; medium duration. Oil content is reported as 49.67% in the JAU release sheet and 48.3% in the JAU proceedings and station page. The digest flags this conflict and it is not resolved.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) ICAR-IIOR entry: mean seed yield 3820 kg/ha under irrigation. (2) JAU station page: station-level 3781 kg/ha with 48.30% oil. (3) JAU release sheet: potential 3500-4000 kg/ha, average 2340 kg/ha, oil 49.67%. (4) JAU proceedings: trial yield 3820 kg/ha, 9.0% above check GCH-7 (3503 kg/ha), irrigated Gujarat, 48.3% oil. (5) Kharif 2017 field experiment at Castor-Mustard Research Station, Sardarkrushinagar: eight hybrids tested, including JHB 1018 (the variety code); the paper's main focus is GCH 8, so results for this variety were not separately reported in the digest. (6) Assam (Jorhat) 2023-24 trial of Gujarat-bred genotypes: GCH 09 ranked among the most promising. The attribution to this variety is assumed from the name 'GCH 09' and is not confirmed. (7) ARS Mandor (Jodhpur) kharif 2022 trial: JHB 1018 among hybrids, recording the highest effective branches per plant (18.8).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME NOTE: CSC release minutes name this variety "Gujarat Castor Hybrid-9" (GCH-9, JHB-1018). The Seednet name "GCH-2 (GUJARAT CASTOR HYBRID-2)" refers to a different hybrid released around 1985-86 (VP-1 x JI-35). No search result linked the Seednet GCH-2 entry to GCH-9, so no GCH-2 evidence is attributed to this variety below. Release year differs by source: 2016-17 (JAU), 2018 (ICAR-IIOR, Vikaspedia). The input gives 2018-08-10. Gazette notification is S.O. 6318(E), dated 26-12-2018.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot, per the variety entry -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/386
Resistant to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot, per JAU's release list -- https://www.jau.in/castor-research-station-junagadh
Tolerant to sucking pests; thrips tolerance also noted in the JAU notification sheet -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/AOilseedsCrops.pdf
Tolerant to sucking pests; lower leafhopper and fruit borer incidence than hybrid checks -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf
Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. Searches returned nothing for these stresses on GCH-9.

DISEASE AND PEST
Wilt and root rot resistance, as above -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/386 ; https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/high-yielding-hybrids-and-varieties-of-castor-ricinus-communis-l
Tolerant to thrips and sucking pests (JAU notification sheet) -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/AOilseedsCrops.pdf
Lower leafhopper and fruit borer incidence than hybrid checks; field-level, not a formal resistance rating -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Mean seed yield 3820 kg/ha under irrigation; medium duration; first picking at 110-120 days after sowing -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/386
Station-level figure of 3781 kg/ha, with 48.30% oil -- https://www.jau.in/castor-research-station-junagadh
Potential yield 3500-4000 kg/ha, average 2340 kg/ha; plant height 105-110 cm; 100-seed weight 29.64 g; oil 49.67%; primary spike 100-104 days, seed-to-seed 210 days (note: the oil figure conflicts with the 48.30% above) -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/AOilseedsCrops.pdf
Trial yield 3820 kg/ha, 9.0% above check GCH-7 (3503 kg/ha), irrigated Gujarat; profuse branching, 48.3% oil -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf
Kharif 2017 field experiment at Castor-Mustard Research Station, Sardarkrushinagar, with eight hybrids including JHB 1018 (the variety code); the paper's main focus is GCH 8 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344162198_A_high_yielding_and_wilt_resistant_castor_Ricinus_communis_hybrid_for_India
Assam (Jorhat) 2023-24 trial of Gujarat-bred genotypes; GCH 09 ranked among the most promising (name "GCH 09", assumed to be this variety) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344162198_A_high_yielding_and_wilt_resistant_castor_Ricinus_communis_hybrid_for_India
ARS Mandor (Jodhpur) kharif 2022 trial with JHB 1018 among hybrids; JHB 1018 recorded the highest effective branches per plant (18.8) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344162198_A_high_yielding_and_wilt_resistant_castor_Ricinus_communis_hybrid_for_India
Conflicting claim: a listing under a "GCH-9 (2018)" heading says it is recommended for rainfed regions of AP, Telangana, Karnataka, TN and Odisha, which contradicts the irrigated-only Gujarat recommendation; unverified -- https://www.agrifarming.in/varieties-of-castor-in-india-boost-the-profit-with-high-yielding-hybrids-of-castor

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed. Variety name and Seednet name are both "ICH-66", so every finding below refers to ICH-66 under that single name. No Seednet portal page for ICH-66 was retrieved, and no CSC release-minute text was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE

The hybrid showed resistance to Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
It was also found resistant to leafhopper, with hopper burn grade 0 to 1 on a 0-4 scale at multilocations in all screening years. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Drought/rainfed suitability: recommended for rainfed areas, and the release is framed around rainfed Peninsular India (kharif). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

DISEASE AND PEST

Fusarium wilt, Macrophomina root rot, and leafhopper resistance, as listed above. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Salient-features table describes the hybrid as resistant to Fusarium wilt, Macrophomina root rot and leafhopper. -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/high-yielding-hybrids-and-varieties-of-castor-ricinus-communis-l
Botrytis: the 2019 IIOR field-day item describes the companion experimental hybrid ICH-538 as botrytis-tolerant, not ICH-66. Not attributed to ICH-66. -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/11101

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

Station trials at ICAR-IIOR in 2013-14 and 2014-15, then AICRP (Castor) MLTs in 2015-16 to 2017-18 against checks DCH-519 and DCH-177. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Mean seed yield 1566 kg/ha, 14.9% above DCH-519 (1324 kg/ha) and 18.3% above DCH-177 (1363 kg/ha). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Mean oil content 48.6%, versus 47.6% for DCH-519 and 47.0% for DCH-177. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Primary spike length 45 cm and 100-seed weight 29.0 g under rainfed conditions, versus the checks. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Maturity 100-130 days to primary spike maturity; non-lodging and non-shattering. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Vikaspedia table lists average yield 1560 kg/ha for the 2019 release. -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/high-yielding-hybrids-and-varieties-of-castor-ricinus-communis-l
Field-level performance: IIOR rabi-castor field day (22/02/2022, Nagarkurnool) reported ICH-66 grown on a farmer plot at 90 x 60 cm spacing, with a farmer expecting 10-12 q per acre. -- https://icar-iior.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-02/castor-rabi-fd.pdf
Discarded: a ResearchGate snippet cites 1574 kg/ha rainfed and 3375 kg/ha irrigated for the hybrid, but the same snippet's parentage and text appear to mix other entries, so it is unverified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378522773_ICH-66_a_new_high_yielding_and_biotic_stress-resistant_castor_hybrid_suitable_for_rainfed_conditions_of_Peninsular_India_ICH-66_A_NEW_CASTOR_HYBRID_SUITABLE_FOR_RAINFED_CONDITIONS_OF_PENINSULAR_INDIA

GENETICS AND QTL

Parentage SKP-84 x ICS-164, as stated in the JOR paper. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Parentage conflict: a ResearchGate snippet gives SKP-84 x PMC-14, and an Agrifarming page gives "High Oil Mutant x Mauthner's Dwarf". Both conflict with the JOR paper and with Vikaspedia, so they are not used. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378522773_ICH-66_a_new_high_yielding_and_biotic_stress-resistant_castor_hybrid_suitable_for_rainfed_conditions_of_Peninsular_India_ICH-66_A_NEW_CASTOR_HYBRID_SUITABLE_FOR_RAINFED_CONDITIONS_OF_PENINSULAR_INDIA ; https://www.agrifarming.in/varieties-of-castor-in-india-boost-the-profit-with-high-yielding-hybrids-of-castor
QTL/marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

Developed at ICAR-Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research (IIOR), Hyderabad, and identified by the Combined Varietal Identification Committee of Oilseed Crops in 2018. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Authors of the JOR paper: P. Duraimurugan and M. Santha Lakshmi Prasad, both ICAR-IIOR, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad-500 030. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Institution-level leadership: R.K. Mathur named as IIOR Director in a 2025-era news item (not a breeder of ICH-66). -- https://newsmeter.in/whats-new/hyderabad-how-iior-s-biopolymer-technology-will-revolutionize-indian-farming-739783
Vikaspedia lists ICAR-IIOR, Hyderabad, Telangana-500030 as the source institute. -- https://vikaspedia.in/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/high-yielding-hybrids-and-varieties-of-castor-ricinus-communis-l
Breeder attribution: the Duraimurugan and Santha Lakshmi Prasad authorship is the only breeder-level link found for this variety; other IIOR scientists in the results (R.D. Prasad, G. Suresh) appear in extension and field-day roles, not as ICH-66 breeders.

CONTACT DETAILS

Institute-level (AICRP Information System page, IIOR): Director, Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- 500 030; Phone 040-24598444, 24016141; Fax 040-24017969; E-mail director.iior@icar.org.in. -- https://icar-iior.org.in/aicrp-information-system
Named scientists with breeder-level link: P. Duraimurugan and M. Santha Lakshmi Prasad, ICAR-IIOR, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad-500 030, Telangana (no individual email or phone found). -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137537
Caution: a Google Play app listing for IIOR castor gives iior.developer@gmail.com, p.madhuri@icar.gov.in and 5-6-155, Rajendranagar, Premavathi Pet, Hyderabad 500030. These are app-developer details, not verified institute contacts; use with care. -- https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=in.org.icar_iior.icariiorcastor2&hl=en_US

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Castor-26 (JC-26), castor (Ricinus communis)

Search scope: 4 web_search queries were run: variety/release, breeder/institute, research publications, and seed availability. Both names were searched ("Jawahar Castor-26" and "JC-26"). Nothing returned by any query named Jawahar Castor-26 or JC-26 as a castor variety, so most headings below have no evidence.

Input record (not verified by search): release 2020-11-09, recommended state Madhya Pradesh, parentage DCS-105 x JC-8, developed by Zonal Agricultural Research Station, Jawaharlal Nehru Viswa Vidyalaya (name as given in the input). No search result confirmed any of these fields.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found for JC-26. Searches returned only a JNKVV page for Jawahar Castor-4 (JC-4), which lists Fusarium wilt and Macrophomina root rot tolerance. JC-4 is a different variety and is excluded. -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/451

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found for JC-26. A sucking-pest screening paper covers 33 advanced breeding lines (none named JC-26), so it is excluded. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/145998

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found for JC-26. The only yield and agronomy data for a JNKVV castor variety are for JC-4, which is excluded. -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/451

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found for JC-26. Pedigree (DCS-105 x JC-8) appears only in the input record; no search result confirmed it. -- (input record only; no URL)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found for JC-26. The JNKVV page for JC-4 names Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya, Jabalpur, as developer of JC-4 only. The input record names "Zonal Agricultural Research Station, Jawaharlal Nehru Viswa Vidyalaya" for JC-26, but no search result confirmed this. Scientist profile pages for castor (e.g., Jawahar Lal Jatothu, ICAR-IIOR) do not mention JC-26, so they are not attributed to it. -- https://icar-iior.org.in/node/451 ; https://icar-iior.org.in/dr-jawahar-lal-jatothu

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone, or address was found for JC-26. Institute-level contact for JNKVV was not returned by any search.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found for JC-26. Castor papers returned (e.g., on value chains, harvesting, castor breeding reviews) do not name JC-26, so they are excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for JC-26. Results were mandi (market) price pages and private oil or seed sellers, which do not name JC-26 and are not seed sources for it. -- https://mandibhavindia.in/en/commodity/castor-seed

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found for JC-26 from search. Madhya Pradesh appears only in the input record. The JNKVV JC-4 page lists Madhya Pradesh for JC-4, which is excluded. -- (input record only); https://icar-iior.org.in/node/451

drought.details: No direct evidence found for drought tolerance specific to PCH-111 (searched; none in results). The OUAT AICRP listing places PCH-111 under rainfed upland conditions in Odisha during kharif alongside DCH-177, but this is a suitability listing and does not establish drought tolerance or its mechanisms. Released yield range of about 1500 kg/ha under rainfed conditions versus 2000 kg/ha under irrigated conditions is reported, but no drought-specific trial data is provided.

heat.details: No direct evidence found for heat tolerance specific to PCH-111 (searched; none in results).

salinity.details: No direct evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to PCH-111 (searched; none in results).

flood.details: No direct evidence found for flood tolerance specific to PCH-111 (searched; none in results).

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to Fusarium wilt, per the PCH-111 salient-features entry in the Vikaspedia high-yielding hybrids and varieties of castor package. No other disease resistance evidence was found in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately tolerant to sucking pests, semilooper and spodoptera, per the Vikaspedia salient-features entry. Leafhopper (Empoasca flavescens) study reports hopper-burn score of 2 (11-25% injury) at early sowing on PCH-111 among other entries, and score 4 (over 50% injury) at late sowing. The same review notes zero wax-bloom (green-bloom) expression on PCH-111, linked to antixenosis resistance; this is indicative only. A biology study of Amrasca (jassid) on six castor varieties reports a shorter nymphal and adult-stage profile for PCH-111 than some entries, with larval durations reported; this is a biology observation and not a resistance rating.

agronomic_details.yield: Released as a hybrid with a yield range of about 1500 kg/ha (rainfed) to 2000 kg/ha (irrigated). The CSC average_yield field records only the unit 'Kg/Ha' with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Identified as superior and relatively stable for seed yield in a multi-genotype AMMI and GGE biplot study of eight genotypes including PCH-111 (Nature Scientific Reports). Specific stability statistics were not captured in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to rainfed upland conditions in Odisha during kharif (OUAT AICRP listing). Recommended for Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in rainfed and irrigated areas (Vikaspedia). Trials were conducted under AICRP Zonal coordination unit V (Hyderabad) and spread from RARS Palem. Row spacing of 90 cm and plant spacing of 60 cm are recommended for rainfed upland under the general AICRP castor package; these are not PCH-111-specific.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Vikaspedia: released hybrid with yield of about 1500 kg/ha rainfed and 2000 kg/ha irrigated. (2) Nature Scientific Reports AMMI/GGE study: PCH-111 among eight genotypes, identified as superior and relatively stable for seed yield. (3) AICRP Zonal coordination unit V (Hyderabad) trials, spread from RARS Palem; no yield values captured. (4) Farmer-level problem study in Mahabubnagar district (ResearchGate): reports shortages of adequate hybrid seed quantities for PCH-111; no yield values captured. (5) Leafhopper (Empoasca flavescens) review: hopper-burn score 2 (11-25% injury) at early sowing and score 4 (over 50% injury) at late sowing on PCH-111 among other entries. (6) Amrasca (jassid) biology study on six castor varieties: shorter nymphal and adult-stage profile for PCH-111 than some entries, with larval durations reported; numeric values not captured.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt resistance is the only disease claim tied to PCH-222 by name. PCH-222 is described as a wilt-resistant castor hybrid from RARS Palem, and farmers were advised toward wilt-resistant, high-yielding hybrids including PCH-111 and PCH-222. No PCH-222-specific disease screening scores were found. Palem's broader breeding goals include wilt complex and botrytis resistance, but these are programme goals, not PCH-222 test results.

pest_resistance.summary: No PCH-222-specific pest resistance evidence found.
