CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano) -- evidence name: "CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano)", which matches the Seednet name "CICR-H COTTON 54 (NANO)". Only one source names this variety, and it is a breeder profile page, so most headings below have no evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The four searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The four searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The breeder profile lists the variety as a compact type, released in 2022, for irrigated and rainfed conditions in the Central and South Zones. CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano) · Compact variety · 2022 · Central and South Zone · Irrigated& rainfed -- https://cicr.org.in/manickam/
No maturity, yield, or multi-location trial results were found for this variety. The AICRP and CICR snippets that mention compact or trial work do not name this variety, so I discarded them. (Source: https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage or QTL/marker data for this variety was returned. The parentage field "Not specified" was not resolved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Dr. S. Manickam is listed as a Principal Scientist in Plant Breeding at CICR, and his profile lists CICR-H Cotton 54 (Nano) among the varieties he developed. -- https://cicr.org.in/manickam/
The institution is ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research, Nagpur, headquartered in Nagpur with regional units at Coimbatore and Sirsa. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research (secondary source; verify on cicr.org.in)
Co-breeders were not identified. The "(Breeder)" entry in the AICRP 2024-25 report is for another line, so I did not attribute it to this variety. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- Dr. S. Manickam, Principal Scientist (Plant Breeding), CICR; no email or phone was found for him. -- https://cicr.org.in/manickam/
Institute-level: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research, Nagpur, NH 44 (Nagpur-Wardha Road), Nagpur; Sirsa campus on NH9, Sirsa, Haryana. No email or phone was found in the search results. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
Official website: https://cicr.org.in (the domain of the breeder profile page; no contact page was retrieved).

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for a paper on this variety. The breeder profile lists "Madhu, B., Sivakumar, S., Manickam, S., Murugan, M., Rajeswari, S. and Boopathi, N. M. (2023)" but the title, journal, and link are not shown, and nothing ties it to this variety, so I did not list it. -- https://cicr.org.in/manickam/

drought.details: CPD-1652 was identified as a drought tolerant cotton genotype (G. hirustum) with significantly higher mean seed yield.

disease_resistance.summary: No specific disease resistance for the plant variety CPD-1652 is mentioned in the provided results. While one result mentions resistance to Bacterial Leaf Blight, this was in reference to a different cotton genotype (AKH-09-5). Another source mentions 'bacteria and viruses' in the context of textile fibers, not plant resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: No information on pest resistance for CPD-1652 is available.

agronomic_details.yield: CPD-1652 was found to be superior for seed cotton yield (SCY) and lint yield compared to other varieties like NH-615 and RAH-1071. It also exhibits high GCA for SCY, indicating its ability to transmit high yield traits to its offspring.
agronomic_details.stability: No specific information on yield stability across diverse environments is provided.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The variety is recommended for cultivation in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Orissa. Its drought tolerance suggests suitability for rainfed conditions or areas prone to water scarcity.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CPD-1652 exhibits desirable traits such as high Number of Bolls per Plant (NBP) and high Boll Weight (BW), which contribute to its superior yield.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Screening of cotton genotypes, including CPD-1652, for stress tolerance was conducted. Diallel and biplot analyses for genetic insights and hybrid evaluation imply extensive field trials.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (SNP, SSR) or QTL positions are identified.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: CPD-1652 exhibits high General Combining Ability (GCA) for Seed Cotton Yield (SCY), Number of Bolls per Plant (NBP), and Boll Weight (BW). This insight was derived from integrated biplot and numerical diallel analyses, indicating its potential as a parent for hybrid development. Hybrids involving CPD-1652, such as GBHV-200 × CPD-1652, have been identified.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No specific molecular mechanisms or genes are described.

disease_resistance.summary: No resistance rating for CSH-3129 was found. The only disease-related evidence is a 2017-18 and 2018-19 treatment trial for root rot and wilt management using biocontrol agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas, arbuscular mycorrhiza) and fungicides; this is a treatment trial, not a resistance rating. A separate seed-treatment assay on CSH-3129 and CICR-3 measured germination, seed rot and vigour; the combined treatment gave the highest vigour index in CSH-3129. Seed-rot or vigour results are not a resistance rating.

pest_resistance.summary: No resistance rating for CSH-3129 against bollworm or sucking pests was found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Not found in searched sources. CSH-3129 yield values were not extracted from the ICAC Subiksha presentation, and no yield data specific to CSH-3129 was found in any retrieved text. The supplied record's average_yield field gives units only (Kg/Ha) with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Not found in searched sources as an agro-climatic fit. The North zone evaluation (ICAR-CICR Regional Station, Sirsa) places CSH-3129 under irrigated conditions; this is context for the trial, not a stated adaptation. The supplied recommended states (Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) are unverified in the digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified. No plant-type or morphological data specific to CSH-3129 were found in any retrieved text.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) North zone evaluation of G. hirsutum advanced populations (ICAR-CICR Regional Station, Sirsa; ICAC presentation, Ahuja 2024): CSH-3129 appears as a check or entry for ginning out-turn (GOT) above 40% and high yield under irrigated conditions; the slides show a field view of CSH-3129 and list it among donor lines with high GOT. (2) ICAC presentation on the Subiksha long-staple variety (Manikam 2024): CSH 3129 is listed among genotypes consolidated for yield and fibre-quality evaluation; yield values were not extracted. (3) Disease-management treatment trial, 2017-18 and 2018-19: CSH-3129 tested for root rot and wilt management with biocontrol agents and fungicides; no resistance outcome reported. (4) Seed-treatment assays: CSH-3129 and CICR-3 tested for germination, seed rot and vigour; the combined treatment gave the highest vigour index in CSH-3129. No quantitative yield results were found.

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "CSH-3129", so every search used that name. I did not reach the Seednet portal itself, and no search result came from it. Crop was matched as cotton (G. hirsutum, Sirsa/CICR context) in every retained item.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of CSH-3129. Searches returned only unrelated cotton pages. Searched: "CSH-3129 cotton variety", "CSH-3129 cotton research".

DISEASE AND PEST
- CSH-3129 was tested in 2017-18 and 2018-19 for root rot and wilt management using biocontrol agents (Trichoderma, Pseudomonas, arbuscular mycorrhiza) and fungicides. This is a treatment trial, not a resistance rating. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41938-023-00739-3
- Seed-treatment assays on CSH-3129 and CICR-3 measured germination, seed rot and vigour; the combined treatment gave the highest vigour index in CSH-3129. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s41938-023-00739-3
- No resistance rating for CSH-3129 against bollworm or sucking pests was found. -- searched via "CSH-3129 cotton variety"

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CSH-3129 appears as a check or entry in a North zone evaluation of G. hirsutum advanced populations for ginning out-turn (GOT) above 40% and high yield under irrigated conditions (ICAR-CICR Regional Station, Sirsa). The slides show a field view of CSH-3129 and list it among donor lines with high GOT. -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/1-Ahuja-4B.pdf
- In an ICAC presentation on the Subiksha long-staple variety, CSH 3129 is listed among genotypes consolidated for yield and fibre-quality evaluation. Yield values for CSH-3129 were not extracted. -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/04SManikam-7C.pdf
- No maturity, plant-type or yield data specific to CSH-3129 were found in any retrieved text. The CICR crop-improvement page and the AICRP 2024-25 report did not name this variety. -- https://cicr.org.in/crop-improvement/ ; https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- CSH 3129 was used as a female parent in a male-sterility/hybrid breeding table (GMS 26 x CSH 3129). This is a breeding use, not a QTL or marker study. Authors and year were not shown. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/male-sterility-in-cotton/146290655
- No QTL, marker or DNA-fingerprinting study specifically for CSH-3129 was found. -- searched via "CSH-3129 cotton research"

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No lead breeder name for CSH-3129 was found in any retrieved source. The S.K. Verma profile page was discarded because it does not mention CSH-3129; it is a CICR staff profile only. -- http://www.cicr.org.in/profiles/Verma_SK.html (discarded, not attributed)
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Regional Station, Sirsa, Haryana, which the institute's own materials associate with the North zone cotton breeding work. -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/1-Ahuja-4B.pdf ; https://cicr.org.in/crop-improvement/
- A Tribune article reports a new cotton variety from CICR Sirsa, but the variety name in that article was not confirmed as CSH-3129, so it is not attributed here. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/features/new-cotton-variety-to-boost-productivity-cicr-397467

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. Institute-level contacts only:
- Institute: ICAR-CICR, Regional Station, Sirsa 125 055, Haryana, India (address as shown on the CICR site). -- http://www.cicr.org.in/profiles/Verma_SK.html
- Institute headquarters: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research, Nagpur (Nagpur-Wardha Road, NH 44). Email and phone not retrieved. -- https://cicr.org.in/crop-improvement/
- Crop Improvement Division, Sirsa (institute contact page): https://cicr.org.in/crop-improvement/
- No official email or phone for the Sirsa station was found in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not retrieved (2023). Combined application of effective Trichoderma, Pseudomonas and arbuscular mycorrhiza spp. reduced soil-borne diseases and boosted growth in cotton. Journal not confirmed in retrieved text -- https://doi.org/10.1186/s41938-023-00739-3
- Ahuja (2024). Evaluation of Advance Generation Populations of G. hirsutum cotton for High GOT% and High yield under North zone irrigated conditions. ICAC conference presentation -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/1-Ahuja-4B.pdf
- Manikam S. et al. (2024, first author Manikam per filename; full author list not retrieved). Subiksha, the Compact Long Staple Cotton Variety with High ... ICAC presentation. CSH 3129 appears only as a listed genotype -- https://icac.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/04SManikam-7C.pdf
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Institutional Structure of Cotton Research in India. Book chapter (IntechOpen), listing CSH-3129 among G. hirsutum varieties -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140
- Authors and year not retrieved. Male sterility in cotton. Slide presentation citing CSH 3129 as a cross parent -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/male-sterility-in-cotton/146290655
- No KrishiKosh thesis or peer-reviewed release-notification paper for CSH-3129 was found in the searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales or official Seednet listings. The seed-availability search returned only unrelated seed shops (e.g., ornamental cotton seed sellers) and general pages; none were kept.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No search evidence found for Haryana, Punjab or Rajasthan as recommended states. The states come from the supplied record only (recommended_states_raw) and are unverified here.

RELEASE (supplementary)
- Release year 2016-08-12 is from the supplied record only; no CSC release notification or Seednet release record was found in the searches.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CSHG 1862 (cotton, Gossypium hirsutum)

Name note: The release-minutes name and the Seednet name are both "CSHG 1862", so one set of evidence covers both headings. I found no separate Seednet portal page, so Seednet-specific fields (variety code A0501309, release date 2013-01-18, parentage) are unverified. Searches 3 and 4 returned mostly unrelated 19th-century and US patent material, so those headings rest on little evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf (searched; the report mentions only the irrigated north zone)

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance. -- searched across the first two searches; no CSHG 1862 resistance data appeared

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- CSHG 1862, a GMS-based hirsutum hybrid released for the irrigated north zone, recorded an overall mean seed-cotton yield of 2.1 tonnes/ha. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- The same report says the hybrid is capable of spinning at 40s counts, and has been found superior (text cut off in the source; comparator not visible). -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Maturity, plant type, fibre length and multi-location trial data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- CSHG 1862 is a GMS (genetic male sterility) based intra-hirsutum hybrid, as listed in the CICR list of intra-hirsutum hybrids alongside Savitha, Suguna, Surya, Kirthi and Omshankar. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf ; https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/51140
- Parentage: not found (Seednet also lists "Not specified").
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), which was established at Nagpur, in 1976. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf
- Regional stations: its headquarters at Nagpur and its Regional Stations at Coimbatore and Sirsa. The Sirsa station is the north-zone station relevant to this hybrid, though the source does not explicitly tie CSHG 1862 to Sirsa. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf
- Lead developer name(s): The CICR At-a-Glance document has a table headed "Name | Lead developer | Species | Year", but the names did not appear in the retrieved text. Needs manual check of that PDF. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ICAR-CICR-At-Glance-with-coverpages.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder name, email or phone found.
- Institute-level: ICAR-CICR, Nagpur (headquarters, NH 44 Nagpur-Wardha Road) and Sirsa campus (NH9, Sirsa, Haryana). Postal codes and phone numbers not in the retrieved text. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research
- Institute website: cicr.org.in (cited in the CICR technical bulletin and the At-a-Glance PDF, though no contact page was retrieved). -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf
- Director named on Wikipedia: Dr. V. N. Waghmare (date of listing not confirmed). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Institute_for_Cotton_Research

PUBLICATIONS
- ICAR (2012?). Crop Improvement, Annual Report 2011-12 (section on CSHG 1862 release). ICAR Annual Report -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf (author and year not confirmed in the retrieved text)
- Authors not stated in retrieved text. CICR varieties and hybrids, Technical Bulletin No. 13. Central Institute for Cotton Research, Nagpur -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cotton-varieties-hybrids.pdf (CSHG 1862 not confirmed in the retrieved excerpt)
- No peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers on CSHG 1862 found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU or private dealers. The search returned no seed-sales results for CSHG 1862.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The ICAR report places the hybrid in the irrigated north zone. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- The state list "Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan" from the record was not confirmed by any retrieved source.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: DAMAK MC5459 BGII / DAMAK MC5459 BG II (cotton, Rallis India Ltd.)

Searches run: 4 web_search queries (variety overview, breeder/institution, research/trials, seed availability). No result named either "DAMAK MC5459 BGII" or "DAMAK MC5459 BG II". Both names are therefore unconfirmed for every heading below. The search did not reach seednet.gov.in, the CSC minutes, or any Rallis variety page.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The variety-name search returned only unrelated US cotton cultivar patents (DP 570 BGII, DP 576 BGII, and others) and a Nigerian seed-portal entry for MAHYCO C571 BGII. None names this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. The searches returned only general Bt cotton material, including a 2022 Genes paper on Cry-gene segregation in Indian Bt hybrids (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9859209/). That paper does not name this variety, so it was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. A Cotton Association of India bulletin reporting AICRP BG II hybrid trials for 2022-23 and 2023-24 (https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__05_29-04-2025.pdf) lists other hybrids such as Rasi Max 003 BG II and ARH 2020 BG II, not this variety. Discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The only marker or QTL hit was a 2022 Uzbek upland cotton study (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9168987/) on different cultivars. Discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The Rallis seeds page (https://www.rallis.com/innovation/seeds) describes the company's cotton programme generally, but does not name this variety or any breeder. Discarded under the strict-relevance rule. The Rallis Dhaanya seeds page (https://www.rallis.com/business/seeds-cn) likewise does not name it.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute contact or address for this variety was returned. The only Rallis-linked results were company and product pages.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. No paper, AICRP/ICAR report, thesis or KrishiKosh record names this variety. The KrishiKosh search was not run as a separate query, so this result reflects the four searches only.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. The closest result was a KisanShop listing for "Tata Pravir (MC5403) BG II" by TATA Rallis (https://www.kisanshop.in/product/tata-pravir-mc5403-bg-ii-hybrid-cotton-seeds). It is a different variety (MC5403, not MC5459) and was discarded. No NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for MC5459 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found. The states Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat appear only in the input record and were not verified by any search result.

NOTES FOR THE RECORD
- Name check: "variety_name" (DAMAK MC5459 BGII) and "seednet_variety_name" (DAMAK MC5459 BG II) gave the same null results, so the evidence applies to neither name.
- Parentage: "Not specified" in the input. No search result supplied it.
- Suggested next steps: search seednet.gov.in directly for "DAMAK MC5459 BG II" under COTTON (KAPAS) and check the CSC release minutes for the exact name. Also check KrishiKosh and the AICRP cotton annual reports for the 2022–2024 seasons.

drought.details: DHH 11 is mostly cultivated in rainfed cotton areas and is considered abiotic tolerant, showing tolerance under drought/water stress conditions. Its drought tolerance may be linked to the role of PI and relative water contents (with NAU2 54). It is listed among varieties for which discovery of novel genes for drought tolerance is a focus for transgenic development.

heat.details: DHH 11 shows tolerance to heat stress. It is mentioned in the context of research on heat tolerance in cotton and adaptation to warm weather conditions.

salinity.details: DHH 11 is categorized as abiotic tolerant, including salinity/sodicity. Efforts have been made for the development of salt tolerant cotton varieties, with DHH 11 being among those considered.

flood.details: Cotton, including DHH 11, generally does not tolerate excess water or waterlogging conditions. Drainage is essential, and waterlogging is a reported challenge.

disease_resistance.summary: Specific resistance levels for DHH 11 are not detailed, but genetic engineering efforts for varieties including DHH 11 focus on developing resistance to leaf-curl virus.

pest_resistance.summary: Specific resistance levels for DHH 11 are not detailed, but genetic engineering efforts for varieties including DHH 11 focus on developing resistance to insect pests. DHH 11 is also associated with discussions of weed resistant transgenic cotton.

agronomic_details.yield: Application of mepiquat at 90 DAS (Days After Sowing) improved boll weight, seed cotton yield, and total dry matter in cotton cv. DHH 11. No specific quantitative yield (kg/ha) is provided for DHH 11, though it is referenced in comparative yield contexts.
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified.
agronomic_details.adaptation: DHH 11 is primarily cultivated in rainfed cotton areas, particularly in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, where it is subject to water stress. It is adapted to red soil, coastal black cotton soil, black, and light red soil types. Optimal soil temperature for sowing cotton (including DHH 11) is 12-14 degrees Celsius.

F2228 was the non-Bt zonal check in the two-year, five-location North Zone AICRP cotton evaluation of PAU Bt 2 and PAU Bt 3, where it averaged 2,409 kg/ha seed cotton yield. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=4977
The same trial result, reported separately, gives the same 2,409 kg/ha check yield for F 2228. -- https://smartagripost.com/pau/
In the PAU Bt 5 AICRP evaluation (2019–2022, five North Zone locations), F 2228 was one of the comparators; PAU Bt 5 averaged 2,572 kg/ha, and the report cites a 0.25% margin over F 2228. These are PAU Bt 5 results, not F2228 results. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z ; https://bioengineer.org/new-bt-cotton-variety-pau-bt-5-delivers-higher-yields-for-north-india/
Yield context: a 2015 state approval report says F-2228 was approved by the State Varietal Approval Committee with a yield of 7.4 quintals per acre. The page's URL suggests a March 2015 date, which does not match the 2016-08-12 release date in the record. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/punjab-agri-dept-releases-9-new-varieties-of-crops-115031701010_1.html

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, pedigree or marker data for F2228 was returned. The PAU Bt 5 paper's pedigree (LH 2298 × PAU Bt 1) belongs to that variety, not F2228. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found for F2228 breeder names, developing scientists or station. The developing institution named in the record is Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana. That institution is confirmed by the state approval report, which lists F-2228 among PAU-developed cotton varieties. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/punjab-agri-dept-releases-9-new-varieties-of-crops-115031701010_1.html
Breeder names from the PAU Bt 5 paper (Dharminder Pathak and Harish Kumar, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, PAU; Paramjit Singh, Vineet Kumar, Gomti Grover, PAU-RRS Bathinda; Pankaj Rathore, PAU-RRS Faridkot) belong to PAU Bt 5 and are not attributed to F2228. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z

CONTACT DETAILS
No F2228-specific contact found. Institute-level only: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, Punjab, India; website www.pau.edu (cited in the Wikipedia entry for PAU, which gives the institute's location as Ludhiana and the URL as www.pau.edu). No official email, phone or postal address was returned in the search results. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Agricultural_University

PUBLICATIONS
Singh, P., Kumar, V., Grover, G., Rathore, P., Pathak, D., & Kumar, H. (2026). American Cotton Bt Variety- PAU Bt 5 (PBH Bt 21). Springer journal (publication details as listed on the article page; F 2228 appears only as a comparator) -- DOI 10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z
No other peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper on F2228 was found. The search returned unrelated cotton papers that do not name F2228.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No Seednet, NSC, PSC, KVK, PAU seed sales or private dealer listing for F2228 was returned. A Tribune article notes that subsidies apply to PAU-approved seed varieties, but it does not name F2228. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/punjab-announces-33-subsidy-on-cotton-seeds-to-revive-shrinking-acreage/

RECOMMENDED STATES
Punjab (state-level approval). The 2015 State Varietal Approval Committee report approved F-2228 for Punjab. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/punjab-agri-dept-releases-9-new-varieties-of-crops-115031701010_1.html
F2228 was used as a zonal (North Zone) check, which indicates it was a Punjab-region reference variety in the AICRP trials, not a North Zone recommendation. -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=4977

NAME CHECK
Variety name and Seednet name are both "F2228." No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so the Seednet record and variety code A0501475 could not be verified. The record's 2016 release year is not confirmed; the approval report found is from 2015.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
F2383 (cotton) evidence digest

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "F2383", so every search used both. No page used a different name for this variety. Crop: cotton. Searches run: (1) variety/release/traits, (2) breeder/institution, (3) research papers and trials, (4) seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The variety search returned only unrelated USPTO cotton patents for other varieties (19R238NRB3XF, 16R232B2XF, etc.), which were discarded. No page reports drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for F2383.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page links F2383 to resistance or susceptibility to leaf curl, bacterial blight, leaf spot, nematodes or pink bollworm. The PAU pages on leaf curl and virus-resistant breeding lines (https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/pau-unveils-virus-resistant-cotton-breeding-lines/ and https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&dataE=datae&intID=9404) and the PAU Bt 5 paper (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z) concern other varieties or lines, so I excluded them.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
- Plant height of F2383 is recorded as 73.60 cm, versus 56.40 cm for MRC6301, 98.10 cm for MRC6304 and 149.0 cm for LH2076, in a handheld picker field evaluation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318307499_Field_evaluation_of_portable_handheld_type_cotton_picking_machines_for_different_cotton_varieties
- The same paper records roller-type picker labour on F2383 at 868 man-h/ha, the highest of the four varieties tested -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318307499_Field_evaluation_of_portable_handheld_type_cotton_picking_machines_for_different_cotton_varieties
- A spacing/density study lists F2383 among three varieties (with RCH773 and Suraj) at three locations, including PAU Ludhiana; it reports the most sympods (40) for F2383 at 67.5 x 30 cm spacing at PAU, and the lowest yield (595 kg/acre) for F2383 at 45 x 30 cm at PAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/339412999_Response_of_desi_cotton_Gossypium_arboreum_L_hybrids_to_spacing_and_fertilizer_levels_under_irrigated_conditions. Caveat: the page title refers to desi cotton hybrids, but the abstract is about F2383 as a G. hirsutum-type entry; treat the crop label as unconfirmed.
- F2383 is listed among semi-compact genotypes suitable for high-density planting systems, with an average yield gain of around 30% under high-density planting across the genotypes studied (this is a group average, not F2383-specific) -- https://www.ojs.pphouse.org/index.php/IJEP/article/download/4891/2397/4839

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No pedigree, parentage or marker/QTL study for F2383 was returned. Parentage is "Not specified" in the release record and the search did not resolve it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found naming a breeder for F2383. The search returned PAU cotton breeding staff pages (Dr Dharminder Pathak, Principal Cotton Breeder, https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?DO=viewFacultyData&_act=manageDepartments&intDepTitleID=0&intFacultyID=36&intLinkID=9&strDepTitle=; Dr Pankaj Rathore, Principal Cotton Breeder, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/pau-unveils-virus-resistant-cotton-breeding-lines/). These pages do not mention F2383 and are not attributed to it. Institution from the release record: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana; the PAU Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics handles cotton breeding (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z).

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for cultivation cotton growing regions of North zone comprising Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Growth habit of plants of FBt 16-4 indeterminate. The plants are tall and its stem has no pigmentation with sparse hairiness. The leaves of FBt 16-4 are palmate in shape with medium hairiness and presence of nectarines and gossypol glands. The bracts of FBt 16-4 are normal. It has cream flower and open, medium size ovate shaped bolls with pitted surface. Seed fuzz of FBt 16-4 is medium and white in colour.

The compendium and Tribune pages describe reduced flower drop compared with other desi varieties, but they do not link this to drought or any other stress, so it is not treated as drought evidence.

disease_resistance.summary: Cotton leaf curl virus (CLCV): a 2011 press report says PAU expected FDK-124 to be highly resistant to CLCV. This is a pre-release expectation, not a field-validated result, and no peer-reviewed or trial confirmation was found. No other disease resistance was found; CSC disease reaction is 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: Whitefly and jassid: pages describe FDK 124 as tolerant to jassid and whitefly (compendium, Tribune) and list resistance to whitefly and jassid (Apnikheti). Evidence is descriptive; no trial data were found. CSC pest reaction is 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 20 to 21.00 q/ha (under normal condition). Compendium: 23.2 q/ha. Apnikheti: about 9.3 quintals/acre (approximately 23 q/ha by conversion). AICRP 2024-25 (indicative, ambiguous table layout): mean seed cotton yield about 2873 kg/ha and mean lint yield about 1086 kg/ha. The compendium describes FDK 124 as a high-yielding desi variety.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis was found; AICRP 2024-25 multi-location data are indicative only.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC adaptation_ecology: irrigated conditions. Trial locations in the AICRP 2024-25 report: Sriganga Nagar, Faridkot, Bathinda and Sirsa. Sowing guidance (first April to 15 May for desi cotton in Punjab) is a general desi-cotton statement, not FDK 124 specific, and is kept as context only.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Morphological characteristics: Not specified in CSC record. CSC agronomic feature: spacing of 67.5 x 45.0 cm and 100% dose of N, i.e. 75 kg N/ha, recommended. Apnikheti and croplibrary pages report fibre length 21 mm and ginning outturn 36.4%. AICRP 2024-25 gives GOT about 37.8% (indicative).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP-Cotton 2024-25 annual report: FDK 124 (ZC) used as a zonal check at Sriganga Nagar, Faridkot, Bathinda and Sirsa; mean seed cotton yield about 2873 kg/ha, mean lint yield about 1086 kg/ha, GOT about 37.8%; table layout ambiguous, values indicative. (2) PAU compendium: yield 23.2 q/ha and early maturity noted. No other trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: FDK 124 (cotton, desi/Gossypium arboreum)

Name note: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "FDK 124" in the input, and I found no separate Seednet portal record. All evidence below refers to the name "FDK 124" (also written FDK-124 or FDK124). Several pages discuss other PAU cotton varieties (LD 327, LD 694, FDK 331, PAU Bt 1), and I excluded those.

Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pages describe FDK 124 as tolerant to jassid and whitefly, and as producing less flower drop than other desi varieties. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf ; https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/bathinda/demand-for-native-cotton-varieties-on-the-rise-231086
- A 2011 press report says PAU expected FDK-124 to be highly resistant to cotton leaf curl virus (CLCV); this is a pre-release expectation, not a field-validated result. -- https://agrisalsa.wordpress.com/2011/08/27/pbw-621for-wheat-and-fdk-124-desi-cotton-new-varieties-from-pau-ludhiana/
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to FDK 124. Searches returned only general statements about desi cotton.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistance to whitefly and jassid is listed for FDK 124. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/fibre-crops/cotton
- CLCV resistance is claimed in the 2011 press release (see above). No peer-reviewed or trial confirmation was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity about 160 days; average yield about 9.3 quintals/acre; fibre length 21 mm; ginning outturn 36.4%. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/fibre-crops/cotton ; https://croplibrary.com/cotton-farming-profit-per-acre/
- Compendium gives yield 23.2 q/ha and states that FDK 124 is a high-yielding desi variety with early maturity in the desi-cotton list. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
- The 2024-25 AICRP-Cotton annual report lists FDK 124 (ZC) as a zonal check in trials at Sriganga Nagar, Faridkot, Bathinda and Sirsa. The table gives a mean seed cotton yield of about 2873 kg/ha and mean lint yield of about 1086 kg/ha, with GOT about 37.8%. The table layout is ambiguous, so treat these values as indicative. -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf
- Sowing: first April to 15 May for desi cotton in Punjab. -- http://ekapas.com/punjab/ (this is a general desi-cotton statement, not FDK 124 specific; keep only as context)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: selection from LD 830. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
- No QTL, marker or mapping study naming FDK 124 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released by Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf ; https://agrisalsa.wordpress.com/2011/08/27/pbw-621for-wheat-and-fdk-124-desi-cotton-new-varieties-from-pau-ludhiana/
- The press item quotes PAU Director of Research S S Gosal on the variety's development. -- https://agrisalsa.wordpress.com/2011/08/27/pbw-621for-wheat-and-fdk-124-desi-cotton-new-varieties-from-pau-ludhiana/
- No page names the individual breeder who developed FDK 124. The PAU Plant Breeding department page lists Dr Dharminder Pathak as Principal Cotton Breeder, and the AICRP report names Dr Paramjit Singh as Principal Cotton Breeder at RRS Bathinda. Neither page links them to FDK 124 as developers, so they are not attributed here. -- https://pau.cyberframe.in/pau-new/public/college/coa/departments/Plant ; https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or direct contact for FDK 124 was found.
- Institute-level: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana. No PAU contact page with phone or email was retrieved in these searches. Please check the PAU website directly.
- Email addresses that appear in a symposium volume (ashokkumar@pau.edu, vineet2906@pau.edu) belong to other papers' authors and are not attributed to this variety, so I have not listed them as contacts. -- https://www.crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n5ed776da939b5.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Gosal SS (ed.) (year not shown). A Saga of Progress: Compendium of 50 Years of Achievements. Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf
- AICRP on Cotton (2025). Annual Report 2024-25 (FDK 124 as zonal check, multi-location trial data). Central Institute for Cotton Research -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Comparative studies on seed protein characteristics in eight lines of two Gossypium species. Journal of Cotton Research -- https://jcottonres.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s42397-019-0024-3 . Caution: this uses an "FDK-124" line of G. arboreum, and the page does not confirm it is the PAU variety.
- Excluded: an ResearchGate entry on Bt cotton under Khanewal conditions (Pakistan) mentions "FDK124", but the page does not establish it is the PAU variety, so I have not listed it.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- A 2011 press item stated that sufficient seed was available for multiplication. -- https://agrisalsa.wordpress.com/2011/08/27/pbw-621for-wheat-and-fdk-124-desi-cotton-new-varieties-from-pau-ludhiana/
- A Tribune article (roughly ten years old) reports strong farmer demand for FDK-124 seed in the Bathinda cotton belt, with desi seed sold out early in the season. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/bathinda/demand-for-native-cotton-varieties-on-the-rise-231086
- Ekapas lists FDK 124 as a recommended desi variety for Punjab. -- http://ekapas.com/punjab/
- No Seednet listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales page for FDK 124 was found. Bharat Beej result did not mention FDK 124 and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Punjab: confirmed by the PAU compendium and press items. -- https://pau.edu/content/downloads/compendium.pdf ; https://agrisalsa.wordpress.com/2011/08/27/pbw-621for-wheat-and-fdk-124-desi-cotton-new-varieties-from-pau-ludhiana/
- Haryana and Rajasthan: No evidence found in the searched pages. These states appear only in the input record and are unverified here.
- Release year: the input gives 2010-12-23 (CSC minutes), but the PAU compendium and 2011 press report give 2011. This discrepancy should be checked against the CSC notification.

drought.details: No evidence found of drought tolerance ratings for F 2228. A kharif 2017 sowing-date trial at Faridkot and Bathinda reported that seed cotton yield fell with each delay in sowing across all tested cultivars. This is a general trend for the trial and not a tolerance rating for F 2228, and it does not describe drought mechanisms.

heat.details: No evidence found of heat tolerance ratings or mechanisms for F 2228 in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found of salinity tolerance ratings or mechanisms for F 2228 in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found of flood tolerance ratings or mechanisms for F 2228 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: No evidence found that F 2228 itself is rated resistant or susceptible to cotton leaf curl disease (CLCuD) or other diseases. The researchgate source reports yield only. A search at ncbi PMC9442625 returned only unrelated Texas cotton work and was not used as evidence for F 2228. F 2228 was one of the American genotypes used as a parent, crossed with three wild or synthetic donors, to transfer CLCuD resistance. This is parentage evidence, not a resistance rating. The krishikosh.egranth.ac.in source was not directly retrieved and is not cited. The source actually retrieved for this statement is the crdaindia PDF.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found that F 2228 is rated resistant or susceptible to bollworms or other pests. The ncbi PMC9442625 search returned only unrelated Texas cotton work.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield of 7.4 quintal per acre at approval in 2015. Two-year AICRP North Zone trial at five locations: F 2228 was the non-Bt zonal check at 2,409 kg/ha seed cotton yield. Kharif 2017 Faridkot/Bathinda trial: 2,295 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the multi-location AICRP North Zone trial results summarised under field trials. The digest reports no stability analysis for F 2228.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Punjab. Listed among PAU-developed American cotton varieties released in 2015. Tested at Faridkot and Bathinda in south-western Punjab under kharif 2017 sowing-date conditions. No further agro-climatic adaptation data found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Kharif 2017 Faridkot/Bathinda trial reported a plant height in the 153-155 cm range group. Other morphological characteristics: Not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Two-year AICRP North Zone trial at five locations: F 2228 served as non-Bt zonal check at 2,409 kg/ha seed cotton yield; PAU Bt 2 and PAU Bt 3 were 20.6% and 17.9% higher. (2) Kharif 2017 Faridkot/Bathinda trial: F 2228 yielded 2,295 kg/ha, below the Bt hybrids NCS 855 BGII (2,997 kg/ha) and RCH 650 BGII (2,884 kg/ha); plant height 153-155 cm range group. (3) AICRP 2019-2022 North Zone trial: the newer PAU Bt 5 exceeded F 2228 by a marginal 0.25%. F 2228 is only the comparator in this result, which concerns PAU Bt 5.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE (name: F 2228; variety and Seednet names are identical)
- No evidence found of drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance ratings for F 2228. A kharif 2017 sowing-date trial at Faridkot and Bathinda reported that seed cotton yield fell with each delay in sowing across all tested cultivars, which is a general trend and not a tolerance rating -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330037095_Performance_of_Bt_and_non_Bt_cotton_cultivars_under_different_sowing_environment_of_south_western_Punjab

DISEASE AND PEST (name: F 2228)
- No evidence found that F 2228 itself is rated resistant or susceptible to cotton leaf curl disease, bollworms or other pests. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330037095_Performance_of_Bt_and_non_Bt_cotton_cultivars_under_different_sowing_environment_of_south_western_Punjab (the page reports yield only); https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9442625/ returned only unrelated Texas cotton work
- F 2228 was one of the American genotypes used as a parent, crossed with three wild or synthetic donors, to transfer cotton leaf curl disease resistance. This is parentage evidence, not a resistance rating -- https://www.krishikosh.egranth.ac.in (not directly retrieved); source actually found: https://www.crdaindia.com/downloads/files/n5ed776da939b5.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (name: F 2228)
- Approved by the Punjab State Varietal Approval Committee in 2015 alongside F-2383, with a reported yield of 7.4 quintal per acre -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/punjab-agri-dept-releases-9-new-varieties-of-crops-115031701010_1.html
- Listed among PAU-developed American cotton varieties released in 2015 -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/features/a-year-of-highs-and-lows-for-farm-varsity-175053
- Two-year AICRP North Zone trial at five locations: F 2228 served as the non-Bt zonal check at 2,409 kg/ha seed cotton yield; PAU Bt 2 and PAU Bt 3 were 20.6% and 17.9% higher -- https://www.pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intEventID=4977
- Kharif 2017 Faridkot/Bathinda trial: F 2228 yielded 2,295 kg/ha, below the Bt hybrids NCS 855 BGII (2,997 kg/ha) and RCH 650 BGII (2,884 kg/ha); its plant height was 153-155 cm range group -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/330037095_Performance_of_Bt_and_non_Bt_cotton_cultivars_under_different_sowing_environment_of_south_western_Punjab
- AICRP 2019-2022 North Zone trial: the newer PAU Bt 5 exceeded F 2228 by a marginal 0.25% -- https://bioengineer.org/new-bt-cotton-variety-pau-bt-5-delivers-higher-yields-for-north-india/ (F 2228 is only the comparator here) and https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00034-z

GENETICS AND QTL (name: F 2228)
- No evidence found of QTL, marker or pedigree studies on F 2228. Its only genetic role found is as a parent in CLCuD introgression work

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for GN.Cot.-29 (also searched as GN.Cot.22, GBab 106) returned no page naming this variety for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance. The returned pages were about other cotton varieties, such as a variety with a yield potential of 1640kg/ha that is not this one. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/top-varieties-of-cotton-in-gujarat/

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found under either name. The only pest or disease mention in the results is for a different G. herbaceum variety, GADC 3 (Wagad Gaurav), which is moderate tolerant to major disease and pests. That is a different variety and is not attributed here. -- https://www.aau.in/gujarat-anand-desi-cotton-3-wagad-gaurav

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found under either name. No multi-location, maturity, or yield trial for GN.Cot.-29 or GN.Cot.22 appeared. The Gujarat cotton pages returned were about G.Cot 17 and other varieties.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, marker, or QTL study names GN.Cot.-29, GN.Cot.22, or GBab 106.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution (from the release record): Navsari Agricultural University (NAU). Developing station: the NAU cotton programme is based at the Main Cotton Research Station, Surat. No lead breeder or scientist is named for this variety in any result. Searches on names of NAU cotton scientists returned people working on other varieties or hybrids, so none is attributed here. -- https://nau.in/pages/about-navsari-agricultural-university-1548127676 ; https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/533b4-aboutus_cottonhighlight.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No variety-specific breeder contact found. Institute-level contacts found for NAU's cotton research (not verified as contacts for this variety):
- Email: cottonist@nau.in
- Address: Main Cotton Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University, Athwa Farm, Surat 395007
- Source: https://www.nau.in/assets/uploads/533b4-aboutus_cottonhighlight.pdf
No phone number was found. The NAU site home page is https://nau.in/index.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The NAU Surat cotton page lists 2021 items on Multi-tier Cropping System in Bt Cotton Hybrid and standardizing geometry for Bt cotton varieties. Neither names GN.Cot.-29 or GN.Cot.22, so they are excluded. -- http://www.aiccip.cicr.org.in/CZ-GJ-NAUSurat.html
Also excluded: a NAU thesis list (https://old.nau.in/alloprtitle.php) and a ResearchGate paper on Bt cotton BG I (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389542204_HETEROSIS_AND_GENE_ACTION_STUDIES_IN_BT_COTTON_BG_I_GOSSYPIUM_HIRSUTUM_L). Neither names this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found under either name. The seller listings returned (TradeIndia, DesiKheti, ExportersIndia) sell generic or hybrid cotton seed, not GN.Cot.-29 or GN.Cot.22. No NSC, Gujarat State Seed Corporation, KVK, or NAU seed-sales listing was found. Seednet (seednet.gov.in) was not reached by the search tool.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Gujarat, as stated in the release record only. No search result confirmed the recommendation. The NAU page says Gujarat contributes substantially to the national cotton area (24%) and productions (37%), which is background and not evidence for this variety. -- https://nau.in/nauvariety

Search note: four searches were run in one batch: "GN.Cot.-29 cotton variety", "GN.Cot.22 cotton breeder Navsari Agricultural University", "GN.Cot.-29 GBab 106 cotton research paper", and "GN.Cot.22 cotton seed availability Gujarat". Stress, trial, and QTL topics were covered only through these broader queries. A narrower follow-up on seednet.gov.in and krishikosh.egranth.ac.in would be needed to close the gaps.

drought.details: The provided search results indicate that water stress significantly affects cotton production and highlight the growing need for drought-tolerant varieties (RESULT_2, RESULT_5, RESULT_19, RESULT_27, RESULT_33, RESULT_36). drought.details: The variety is suitable for both irrigated conditions in Junagarh District and rainfed conditions in Saurashtra Agro-climatic Zone VI and VII. It demonstrated a seed cotton yield of 1566 kg/ha under rainfed conditions in Agro-climatic Zone-IV. While specifically marked as 'NOT TESTED' for drought resistance in the original data, its documented suitability and performance under rainfed conditions suggest practical tolerance to water scarcity. Cotton, particularly G. hirsutum varieties (to which G.Cot-38 likely belongs), is generally considered moderately drought-tolerant once established and known for excellent drought tolerance in water-limited environments. Other G.Cot varieties (e.g., G cot-11) are noted for abiotic tolerance including drought/water stress.

heat.details: Heat stress tolerance has not been specifically tested or documented for G.Cot-38 in the provided data. General cotton germplasm resilience against heat stress involves measuring plant phenological traits, flowering, and boll retention capacity.

salinity.details: G.Cot-38 is explicitly stated to be tolerant to salinity. Cotton in general demonstrates considerable tolerance to high salinity compared to other crops like corn. flood.details: G.Cot-38 is resistant to lodging. However, cotton as a crop generally cannot tolerate excess water, necessitating good drainage. Water logging is a known stress condition for cotton production.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Gujarat Cotton-46 (G.Cot-46: Sorath Swet Hem)

Name note: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are the same string in the input, and no separate Seednet page was retrieved. All evidence below refers to the name "Gujarat Cotton-46 (G.Cot-46: Sorath Swet Hem)" as it appears in the sources. One JAU page uses "G.Cot.Hy-46", which conflicts with the open-pollinated type recorded in the release list (see PUBLICATIONS and BREEDER AND INSTITUTION).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No variety-specific evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of G.Cot-46. A salinity-trial report mentions salt-tolerant cotton cultivars in coastal Gujarat, but it does not name G.Cot-46 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311739945_Prospects_and_impact_of_cultivating_salt_tolerant_varieties_of_cotton_and_wheat_in_coastal_saline_soils_of_Gujarat

DISEASE AND PEST
- No variety-specific resistance data found for G.Cot-46. Zone-level data from the AICRP 2024-25 report give grey mildew, bacterial leaf blight and Alternaria incidence for Gujarat in the Central Zone, but these are not tied to this variety -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf
- A general Gujarat variety review says the top-ranked variety shows moderate tolerance to diseases and pests, but the page does not name G.Cot-46 -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/top-varieties-of-cotton-in-gujarat/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A JAU release file has a cotton entry for a variety whose name is not legible in the extract, listing potential yield of 2538 kg/ha seed cotton and 820 kg/ha lint, and average yield of 2215 kg/ha seed cotton and 769 kg/ha lint. It also lists sowing from 15 June to 10 July at 120 x 45 cm, and N:P:K 160:0:120 kg/ha. Whether this entry is G.Cot-46 is unverified -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/DCashCrops.pdf
- The same JAU entry recommends the variety for irrigated kharif cotton in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh (Central Zone) -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/DCashCrops.pdf
- No multi-location or AICRP trial results for G.Cot-46 found -- https://cicr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/AICRP-2024-25-final-1.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found (no parentage, marker or QTL data; parentage is "Not specified" in the input and was not found elsewhere).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The Cotton Research Station at Junagadh was set up in 1962 and works on breeding tetraploid G. hirsutum cotton -- https://www.jau.in/cotton-research-station-junagadh
- The JAU station page lists "G.Cot.Hy-46" among varieties released, which conflicts with the OPV classification in the release list -- https://jau.in/index.php?Itemid=39&catid=2&id=100%3Acotton-research-station&option=com_content&view=article
- Dr. M. G. Valu is named as Research Scientist (Cotton) and Unit Head at the Junagadh station (Genetics and Plant Breeding). He is not confirmed as the developer of G.Cot-46 -- https://www.jau.in/cotton-research-station-junagadh
- The station was strengthened to produce nucleus, breeder and foundation seed of cotton -- https://www.jau.in/cotton-research-station-junagadh
- Institution as given in the input: Cotton Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University. The JAU Cotton station has a 2008 GM cotton project and an AICRP cotton centre -- https://www.aiccip.cicr.org.in/Junagadh.html
- No lead breeder for G.Cot-46 named in any source found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. M. G. Valu, Research Scientist (Cotton) and Unit Head, Cotton Research Station, JAU -- phone (0285) 2674150; PBX 2672080-90 Ext. -- https://www.jau.in/cotton-research-station-junagadh
- Address: Cotton Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University, Junagadh - 362001 (Gujarat) -- https://www.jau.in/cotton-research-station-junagadh
- Institute-level contact: Junagadh Agricultural University, Junagadh 362 001, Gujarat (INDIA). No email found -- https://www.jau.in/new-varieties-released
- No email address for the breeder or the station was found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specific to G.Cot-46 was found. Searches returned only general cotton reports and one 2025 JAU conference proceedings that does not mention the variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found that G.Cot-46 seed is sold by NSC, the Gujarat State Seed Corporation, a KVK, SAU seed sales or a named dealer. Private dealers in Junagadh that list cotton seed were found, but none name G.Cot-46 -- https://www.justdial.com/Junagadh/Cotton-Seed-Distributors/nct-10140820
- A Junagadh seed firm lists cotton seeds among its products, but the variety is not named -- https://www.gascoseeds.com/
- Seednet portal was not searched directly; no Seednet record was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The release list recommends G.Cot-46 for Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Odisha, as an open-pollinated variety -- https://krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/indian-government-released-2-new-varieties-of-cotton-for-farmers/

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for GJ.Cot-102 or GJHV-516. -- https://www.jau.in/cotton-research-station-junagadh (searched; no variety-specific stress data on this page)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The searches returned only a generic root-rot seed-treatment and crop-rotation note in a package-of-practices document, which does not name this variety. -- https://www.studocu.com/in/document/vivekananda-global-university/hi-tech-horticulture/package-of-practices-for-cotton-cultivation-in-gujarat-gj-agri-101/127649071

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Potential yield for GJ Cotton 102 (kharif, irrigated) is listed as 2538 kg/ha seed cotton and 820 kg/ha lint; average yield is listed as 2215 kg/ha seed cotton and 769 kg/ha lint. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/DCashCrops.pdf
Recommended agronomy for the GJ Cotton 102 entry: sowing 15 June to 10 July, spacing 120 x 45 cm, seed rate 5-7 kg/ha, fertilizer N:P:K 160:0:120 kg/ha. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/DCashCrops.pdf
Maturity is given as 170-200 days, and yield as 1955 kg/ha, in a JAU Cotton Research Station variety table that lists GJ.Cot-102 with release year 2017 (this conflicts with the 2018-08-10 release date in the record). -- https://www.jau.in/index.php/component/content/article/2-init-content/research/100-cotton-research-station (the table is in Gujarati; the figures were read from it)
Trial-result note: no multi-location trial results specific to this variety were found; the AICRP/state-trial material returned was generic institute text. -- https://www.jau.in/cotton-research-station-khapat

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage for GJ Cotton 102 is given as JGP-25 x GJHV-14, with breeding by hybridization followed by pedigree selection; this conflicts with "Not specified" in the record. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/DCashCrops.pdf
No QTL or marker study specific to this variety was found. -- searched; none returned

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Cotton Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University, Junagadh 362001, Gujarat (the originating-source line for the GJ Cotton 102 entry). -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/DCashCrops.pdf
Station page lists a Research Scientist (Cotton) and Unit Head, Dr. M. G. Valu (Ph.D., Genetics and Plant Breeding). The page does not state that he bred this variety, so this is station-level only. -- https://www.jau.in/cotton-research-station-junagadh
Station background: the station is the cotton unit of JAU, established under Gujarat Act No. 5 of 2004; the station page gives its establishment year as 1962. -- https://www.jau.in/index.php/component/content/article/2-init-content/research/100-cotton-research-station
No named lead breeder for GJ.Cot-102 or GJHV-516 was found. The C.T. Patel (H-4 hybrid) result was discarded as an unrelated variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level (station, not confirmed as breeder contact): Dr. M. G. Valu, Research Scientist (Cotton) and Unit Head, Cotton Research Station, JAU; phone (0285) 2674150; PBX 2672080-90 Ext. -- https://www.jau.in/cotton-research-station-junagadh
Postal address: Cotton Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University, Junagadh 362001 (Gujarat). -- https://www.jau.in/cotton-research-station-junagadh
University contact: Junagadh Agricultural University, Junagadh 362 001, Gujarat (India); no email found. -- https://www.jau.in/new-varieties-released
Breeder email, personal phone, and institute contact page for this variety: none found.

PUBLICATIONS
Chapara, Rani; Madugula, Sudharani (year not given in the snippet). Heterosis for Seed Fibre Quality Traits in Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum L.). Journal/report not stated -- https://zenodo.org/records/11125775
Note: this paper uses GJHV 516, one of the codes in this record, as a parent in a cross, so it is attributed here on the basis of that code only. The journal and year are not visible in the snippet.
No other peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, thesis (KrishiKosh), or conference paper naming this variety was found. The GHB614/COT102 and other GM-event papers were discarded because they concern a different event.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The searches did not return a Seednet listing, NSC or Gujarat State Seeds Corporation listing, KVK, or SAU seed-sales page for this variety. The results were private cotton-seed traders and mandi price pages, none naming GJ.Cot-102 or GJHV-516, which were discarded. -- https://www.tradeindia.com/junagadh/cotton-seeds-city-198325.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
Recommended for irrigated cotton in Gujarat state (kharif), and also for release in the Central Zone states of Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh under irrigated conditions. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/DCashCrops.pdf
The Gujarat-recommended list in a JAU package-of-practices document also includes an abbreviated "G. Cot - 102" entry. -- https://www.studocu.com/in/document/vivekananda-global-university/hi-tech-horticulture/package-of-practices-for-cotton-cultivation-in-gujarat-gj-agri-101/127649071

drought.details: H-1300 is tolerant to moisture stress and water stress. It is listed among drought-tolerant varieties recommended to states.

heat.details: The variety is tolerant to terminal heat stress.

salinity.details: H-1300 is tolerant to salt and saline irrigation. In studies on tolerance to saline irrigation under drip systems, it showed the least reduction in stomatal conductance with increased salinity and exhibited an increase in certain performance metrics up to 2.5 dS/m.

flood.details: No direct information found regarding specific tolerance to flood or waterlogging for H-1300.

disease_resistance.summary: H-1300 is tolerant to Fusarium Wilt and moderately resistant to Leaf Blight disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Specific pest resistance for H-1300 is not explicitly detailed in the provided search results.

agronomic_details.yield: H-1300 typically yields 22 to 23 quintal/ha under normal conditions. It was part of studies evaluating seed cotton yield under various irrigation methods and salinity levels. Another variety, Su-flum, was reported to be 80.92% better than H-1300, indicating H-1300 serves as a known performance benchmark.
agronomic_details.stability: Recommended for normal sown and irrigated conditions, H-1300 is suitable for cultivation in the North Zone (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh). It is consistently listed as a recommended variety in ICAR Kharif Agro-Advisories.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to normal sown and irrigated conditions. Recommended for the North Zone (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height ranges from 120-150 cm. It is a bold seeded variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: H-1300 has been evaluated in various field trials, including the All India Coordinated Research Project on Management of Salt Affected Soils and Use of Saline Water in Agriculture, specifically for its tolerance to saline irrigation under drip systems in Agra and Bikaner. It has also been evaluated in the All India Coordinated Research Project on cotton.

drought.details: The CCSHAU varieties document lists 'Tolerant to water stress has been observed, tolerant to salinity' in the section that follows the HD 432 heading. The snippet is truncated, so attribution to HD 432 is probable but not fully confirmed. The CSC record gives only 'FIELD TOLERANT'. No drought physiology, mechanism or quantitative data were found. Level is a cautious estimate.

heat.details: The 'Tolerant to terminal heat stress' line in the CCSHAU document appears in a wheat entry, not under HD 432. No heat tolerance evidence for HD 432 was found.

salinity.details: The CCSHAU document states 'Tolerant to salt' near the HD 432 entry, which is also described as released for cultivation in Haryana. In the AICRP Salt Affected Soils biennial report (2008-10), HD-123 and HD-432 were tested under saline irrigation. HD-432 was described as the second most sensitive genotype in one trial, but its mean seed cotton yield (77.3 g/m2) was higher than that of HD-123 (40.3 g/m2). HD-432 had the maximum sympod number (41) at 2.5 dS/m. Overall, tolerance appears moderate, with some conflicting statements.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data found for HD 432. The AICRP 2025 proceedings mention waterlogging studies in cotton, but no result for HD 432 is shown.

disease_resistance.summary: A breeder CV describes HD 432 as tolerant to Fusarium wilt. A slide deck lists HD 432 among disease-resistant varieties, a secondary and non-specific source. The 'Moderately resistant to Leaf Blight' line in the CCSHAU document belongs to a different crop entry. Cotton leaf curl disease is a concern for upland cotton, but no HD 432 reaction was confirmed.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance was documented. HD 432 was used as the test variety in a CCSHAU MSc entomology study of seasonal bollworm incidence (sown 18.04.2020, spacing 67.5 x 30 cm), which indicates it is susceptible to bollworm attack and was not selected for resistance. The stem borer line in the CCSHAU document relates to another crop.

agronomic_details.yield: No quantitative yield in the CSC record. A breeder CV describes it as a high yielder. In the saline irrigation trial, mean seed cotton yield was 77.3 g/m2 (HD-432) versus 40.3 g/m2 (HD-123). Fibre: 2.5% span length 21.2 mm, micronaire 7.0, strength 17.0 g/tex (CSC record).
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-environment stability data not found. It is recommended in ICAR Kharif Agro-Advisories 2025 alongside HD-123 and HD-324 for desi cotton, indicating continued use. Desi cotton hybrid AAH-1 is flagged for yield reduction in the same advisory.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released for cultivation in Haryana. Suited to normal planting in the north Indian desi cotton zone. Tolerant of saline conditions to a moderate degree. Plant height is 170-180 cm.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: 1. GREEN PLANT BODY WITH DEEP CUT LOBE LEAVES 2. WHITE PETAL WITH YELLOW POLLEN COLOUR WITH RED SPOT AT THE INNER BASE OF THE PETAL. 3. SEMI ERECT PLANT HABIT.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Tested in AICRP salinity trials (2008-10) including drip irrigation and saline water studies. A sowing-date study used HD 432 sown in the first fortnight of May 2017. Included in the AICRP Cotton AGM 2025 proceedings as a check at Sirsa (listed alongside CISA 310). Recommended seed rate is 8-10 kg/ha at 67.5 x 30 cm spacing.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No QTL, SNP or SSR information for HD 432 was found. Parentage is HD 167 x DS 5 (CSC record).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: None found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: None found. The strong stem that confers lodging resistance and low kapas shedding is a morphological trait with no molecular characterization in the sources.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: No specific seed corporation listing found. The variety is registered or listed in PPV&FR Authority annual reports (2020-21 and 2021-22) in the DUS cotton context.

(3) AICPMIP seed-requirement table (2016-17 trial proceedings): HHB 223 listed at 2 kg per trial entry; this is a seed requirement, not a performance result.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- HHB 223 (MH 1468) is listed as having dwarf stature, early maturity and synchronous tillering in the AICPMIP release table, but no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence test of HHB 223 itself was found. The AICPMIP table also gives it compact, cylindrical earheads and a 2010 notification. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Indirect only: HBL 11, the male parent of HHB 223, is the basis of marker-assisted terminal drought work at CCS HAU, and the authors suggest HHB 223 could be improved for terminal drought tolerance through improved HBL 11 lines. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336428571_Introgression_of_terminal_drought_stress_tolerance_in_advance_lines_of_popular_pearl_millet_hybrid_through_molecular_breeding ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353750645_Development_of_advance_pearl_millet_lines_tolerant_to_terminal_drought_stress_using_marker-assisted_selection
- Salinity: the ICAR 2010-11 annual report salt-tolerance passage describes a different entry (amber grain, 11% protein), not HHB 223, so it is not attributed here. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- The AICPMIP/millets.res.in list describes HHB 223 as resistant to downy mildew and blast. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- No pest-resistance data for HHB 223 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Medium maturity, conical earheads with long purple bristles, dual-purpose use. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Hisar irrigated/rainfed trial (Journal of Applied and Natural Science, DOI 10.31018/JANS.V6I2.431): HHB 223 recorded the highest earhead girth (2.6 cm) and test weight (11.16 g) among HHB 67 Improved, HHB 197, HHB 223 and HHB 234. -- https://www.academia.edu/77167338/Performance_of_pearl_millet_genotypes_under_irrigated_and_rainfed_conditions_at_Hisar_India
- Six-hybrid trial at CCS HAU, Hisar (kharif 2016 and 2017): HHB 223 showed higher tillering under irrigation; yield values in the extracted table are garbled, so no yield figure is cited. -- https://www.ijpab.com/form/2018%20Volume%206,%20issue%203/IJPAB-2018-6-3-346-351.pdf
- AICPMIP seed-requirement table lists HHB 223 at 2 kg per trial entry (2016-17 trial proceedings). -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2017.pdf
- Yield potential claims from AICPMIP/ICAR sources for HHB 223 specifically were not found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage per AICPMIP/millets.res.in: ICMA 94555 x HBL 11. This conflicts with the input record (female H-1157, male H-1220). Flagged for verification, not overwritten. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- HBL 11 is the male parent of HHB 223, and the improved HBL 11 MAS work is linked to LG2 and LG5 foreground markers for terminal drought. -- https://www.ias.ac.in/article/fulltext/jgen/100/0088 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353750645_Development_of_advance_pearl_millet_lines_tolerant_to_terminal_drought_stress_using_marker-assisted_selection
- No QTL or marker study specific to HHB 223 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Name variety_name "HHB 223 (MH 1468)": evidence refers to this name. Notification S.O.211(E), dated 29.01.2010 (one source gives 29.1.2010), breeder institution CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar, through AICPMIP. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Seednet name "HHH-223" (crop listed as cotton/kapas): no search targeted this name, so no evidence was found for it. The cotton crop label appears to be a portal error; the evidence supports pearl millet only.
- The institution field "Not explicitly stated" is resolved by the AICPMIP table to CCS HAU, Hisar.
- Breeder personal names for HHB 223 were not found in any source.
- Institution: CCS HAU's Hisar pages cover the university and its Plant Breeding department. -- https://hau.ac.in/page/faculty-list-of-genetics-plant-breeding

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar - 125 004, India; general phone 1-800-1803001 (listed on the university faculty page). -- https://hau.ac.in/page/faculty-list-of-genetics-plant-breeding
- Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding (CCS HAU), Head-cum-Dean COA: Dr. S. K. Pahuja, Prof. & Head, gpbhau@hau.ac.in, +91 9416270318. These are departmental contacts, not confirmed as the HHB 223 breeder. -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1689650060.pdf
- Directorate of Human Resource Management (CCS HAU): dhrm@hau.ac.in, +91-1662-284316/255414 (not a breeding contact; listed for institute reference). -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1616403188.pdf
- Breeder-level contacts for HHB 223: No evidence found. Names associated with CCS HAU pearl millet molecular work (Neelam R. Yadav, nryadav58@gmail.com; Ram C. Yadav, rcyadavbiotech@yahoo.com) are from HBL 11 / drought papers, not confirmed as HHB 223 breeders. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336428571_Introgression_of_terminal_drought_stress_tolerance_in_advance_lines_of_popular_pearl_millet_hybrid_through_molecular_breeding ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353750645_Development_of_advance_pearl_millet_lines_tolerant_to_terminal_drought_stress_using_marker-assisted_selection

- Singh S et al. (2014). Hybrid breeding in pearl millet: past and present status. CCS HAU, Hisar (table of released hybrids includes HHB 223 (MH 1468)). -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status (author list partly shown; "Sumerpal Singh" named in the page)

- AICPMIP/millets.res.in list: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HS 292 (cotton, Gossypium; CSC name and Seednet name both "HS 292", so one set of evidence covers both)
Searches run: 4 of 4 allowed. Only one institutional source (the CCS HAU Cotton Research Station, Sirsa) was found, so most headings are thin.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to lodging and drought; early maturity lets it escape bollworm -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf
- Highly resistant to leafhopper and bacterial blight; "basic tolerance" to pests and diseases is claimed -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Leafhopper resistance and bacterial blight resistance (as above) -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf
- Bollworm: escape via early maturity, not resistance -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Tall growing, 150-190 cm, taller in humid and fertile soils -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf
- Average yield 22.4 q/ha; few pickings needed, which lowers picking cost -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf
- Combines high yield potential, high boll weight and better ginning outturn; fibre is coarse and short, unsuitable for mill spinning, suited to domestic, medical dressing and non-spinning uses -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf
- Multi-location or coordinated trial data specific to HS 292: No evidence found (a sister line, HS 298, ranked first for seed cotton yield in the South Zone coordinated trials; HS 296, HS 300 and HS 304 were also tested in coordinated trials) -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage listed as "Not specified" in the input; no pedigree found in the search results -- No evidence found
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar, through its Cotton Research Station, Sirsa -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20
- Station history: established April 1956 as a fodder research station, transferred to CCS HAU in 1976 under the Integrated Cotton Development Project; about 53.5 acres of farm -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found in the retrieved pages
- Release record discrepancy: the Sirsa PDF says HS 292 "was released in 1985" but also that it was notified in the Gazette of India on 26.12.2018 (No. 5077). The input's 2018-08-10 release date does not match the 2018 gazette notification; the 1985 date and the gazette date need checking against the CSC minutes -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute site: https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20 (Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar)
- Station: Cotton Research Station, Sirsa, Western Haryana -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20
- Official email, phone and postal address of the station or the breeder: No evidence found in retrieved content (check the HAU contact page directly)

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specific to HS 292 was found in the search results. The Sirsa station achievements PDF is the only HS 292 document retrieved: Cotton Research Station Sirsa (n.d.). Significant achievements of Cotton Research Station, Sirsa. CCS Haryana Agricultural University -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The Sirsa station reports breeder, foundation and TFL seed production for cotton -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf
- Current seed sellers (NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, dealers) and the Seednet listing: No evidence found. The searches returned only unrelated retail seed pages, and no Seednet page was retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified for the South Zone in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-20 (also https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1567662228.pdf)
