drought.details: The CCSHAU varieties document includes text on tolerance to water stress, but the snippet does not clearly tie it to H 1236, so it cannot be attributed to this variety. No drought-specific trial data for H 1236 were found.

heat.details: The only heat tolerance statement in the CCSHAU document (terminal heat stress) appears to refer to a wheat variety. No heat tolerance data for H 1236 were found.

salinity.details: The CCSHAU document lists 'Tolerant to salt' near the H 1236 entry, though the snippet attribution is not fully certain. In the AICRP saline water trials (2008-10), the seed cotton yields of H-1117 and H-1236 were significantly higher than other genotypes. The number of monopods decreased under saline conditions in all genotypes except H-1236 at a water salinity of 2.5 dS/m. This suggests relatively good performance under moderate salinity. The level is rated medium because no quantitative tolerance index was available.

flood.details: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.summary: H-1236 is listed among resistant or tolerant varieties for North India in the NIPHM IPM package, in a disease management review, and in a Cotton Production in India chapter. The chapter context is cotton leaf curl virus disease management (resistant varieties, whitefly suppression, weed host eradication). The specific disease is not stated in every snippet, so resistance to cotton leaf curl virus is probable but not confirmed for H-1236 specifically. The slide deck lists H-1236 among varieties to grow as part of disease management strategies.

pest_resistance.summary: H-1236 is listed with resistant/tolerant varieties in the NIPHM IPM package for cotton. No specific insect pest resistance was documented for it. The 'tolerant to top borer and shoot borer' text in the CCSHAU document refers to sugarcane.

agronomic_details.yield: No quantitative yield for H 1236 was found. It is among the higher-yielding genotypes (with H-1117) under saline irrigation in AICRP trials.
agronomic_details.stability: Not documented across environments, beyond performance under saline water irrigation.
agronomic_details.adaptation: American cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) variety released for cultivation in Haryana. It is recommended in ICAR Kharif agro-advisories 2025 among varieties for north Indian cotton regions (with HS-6, H-1117, H-1126, H-1098 Improved, H-1300).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: American cotton variety; plant height 130-150 cm; maturity 165-170 days.
agronomic_details.field_trials: AICRP on Management of Salt Affected Soils and Use of Saline Water in Agriculture (2008-10) evaluated H-1236 under saline irrigation, including drip trials, where it gave significantly higher seed cotton yield. A 2015 ISSS abstract reports cotton genotypes including H-1236 and desi HD-123 in a cotton-wheat root water uptake study. The variety was also among entries at the PPV&FRA DUS cotton center (2020-21).

agronomic_performance.field_trials: AICRP on Management of Salt Affected Soils and Use of Saline Water in Agriculture (2008-10) evaluated H-1236 under saline irrigation, including drip trials, where it gave significantly higher seed cotton yield. A 2015 ISSS abstract reports cotton genotypes including H-1236 and desi HD-123 in a cotton-wheat root water uptake study. The variety was also among entries at the PPV&FRA DUS cotton center (2020-21).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Oat (variety_name) / JAWAHAR TAPTI (seednet_variety_name), forage oat, JO 07-310
Searches run: 4. Only one result names this variety. Evidence for the Seednet name JAWAHAR TAPTI was not found, so the findings below refer to "Jawahar Oat- JO 07-310" as printed in the ICAR report.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming this variety with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Results were about other oat varieties or other crops.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Jawahar Oat- JO 07-310 is listed as moderately resistant to leaf spot and blight in the ICAR annual report for 2024-25 -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
No pest-resistance evidence was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The ICAR 2024-25 report lists the variety with an average green fodder yield of 575-600 q/ha and a maturity of 130-140 days -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
No multi-location trial or AICRP trial data specific to this variety was found. The JNKVV Jabalpur nitrogen-level studies in the search results name other oat entries (for example JHO-822 and OS-6), not Jawahar Oat, so they were discarded -- https://archive.dbskkv.org/collection/292/document/1319

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage (Maljari x NA 39, NA 48, NA 32, G-27) was not confirmed by any retrieved page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The ICAR 2024-25 report credits the variety to Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya, Jabalpur, under the ICAR-AICRP on Forage Crops listing -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf
No breeder or scientist name for this variety was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RVK-11 (Raj Vijay Kapas-11, IH 11) -- DIGEST

Name note: the evidence below refers to RVK-11 (variety_name). No page was found under the Seednet name K-11 for this variety. Every "K 11" hit describes a different Tamil Nadu Karunganni cotton (TKA-188, G. arboreum), so those hits were excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for RVK-11.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for RVK-11 resistance traits. The Khandwa centre profile lists RVK-11 among its non-Bt varieties, but it gives no resistance claim: Desi cotton (G. arboreum) varieties Khandwa-2, JK-4, Jawahar Tapti, American cotton variety Sarbottam, JK-4, Jk-35, RVK-11 and RVK-67 are the famous non Bt varieties released by this Centre. -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/CZ-MP-Khandwa.html
Conflict on species: the same profile also describes RVK-11 as G hirsutum Non Bt variety released for Madhya Pradesh by MP state Variety Release Committee, Bhopal in 2016 -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/CZ-MP-Khandwa.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- RVK-11 was released as a G hirsutum non-Bt variety for Madhya Pradesh by the MP state variety release committee in 2016. -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/CZ-MP-Khandwa.html
- The Khandwa centre reports nucleus seed production of RVK 11 under its 2020-21 research achievements. -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/CZ-MP-Khandwa.html
- The RVSKVV newsletter says Cotton variety RVK 11 has been Notified vide No. SO 3220 (E) 06.09.2019 for south Zone (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and -- the text is cut off before the state list. -- http://www.rvskvv.net/images/Newsletter_Jul-Dec-2019_16.06.2020.pdf
- Yield, maturity and trial data for RVK-11: No evidence found. The yield (2000-2100 kg/ha) and 113-day maturity in the same newsletter passage belong to a legume variety described before the RVK 11 notice, so they were excluded. -- http://www.rvskvv.net/images/Newsletter_Jul-Dec-2019_16.06.2020.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for RVK-11 QTL, marker or genetic studies. The parentage supplied in the record (07940-1-D x 11876 x 07794-1-D x H450) matches a different variety, TNAU's K 11 (TKA-188), so it cannot be attributed to RVK-11. -- https://masujournal.org/view_archive_journal.php?id=2466

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder name for RVK-11: No evidence found.
- Developing institution: the RVSKVV cotton centre at Khandwa is named as the centre that released RVK-11 (RVK-11 and RVK-67 are the famous non Bt varieties released by this Centre.) -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/CZ-MP-Khandwa.html
- Dr. Dinesh Kumar Paliwal appears as a Scientist on the Khandwa centre page, but the page does not link him to RVK-11, so he is not attributed as breeder. -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/CZ-MP-Khandwa.html

drought.details: Drought tolerance is claimed in several sources, but most are secondary or vendor claims. A vendor listing describes stable yields under severe drought (about 6-8 quintal/acre). A testbook summary (not a primary source) describes it as drought tolerant and suited to dry, semi-arid regions. An Anantapuramu on-farm study describes it as resistant to drought, with rainfed potential of 20-25 q/ha and irrigated potential of 45-50 q/ha. Minikit demonstrations (2015-2018) recorded drought resistance. The digest contains no physiological mechanism data. Digest trials in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. The digest does not confirm Telangana or Tamil Nadu adaptation from trial data.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Vendor listing: maturity 112 days, 51% oil, 70% shelling, kharif season, seed rate 75 kg/acre, spacing 12-20 inches. Protein about 28% and oil 51%, compared with 48% oil in Kadiri-6 (Anantapuramu study). Minikit demonstrations noted dark foliage. The notification-derived description of a high-yielding Spanish bunch type is recorded in the abstract. Maturity conflicts exist between the input (135-140 days) and the vendor listing (112 days).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Chittoor district on-farm test, rabi 2020-21 and kharif 2021-22: pod yield 28.0% and 13.5% above farmer practice. (2) Kurnool on-farm test, kharif 2020 and 2021: seed yield 3375 kg/ha, 28.5% above Nitya Haritha and 35.1% above K-6. (3) Karnataka north transitional zone trial: dry pod yield 2745 kg/ha, statistically on par with Dh-256; stem rot 3.8% versus 8.1% for JL-24. (4) Anantapuramu on-farm study: rainfed potential 20-25 q/ha, irrigated 45-50 q/ha. (5) Minikit demonstrations, 15 farmer fields, 2015-2018: 1187 kg/ha versus 980 kg/ha for Kadiri-6. (6) Published abstract trial/notification yield: 3840 kg/ha dry pod, 2666 kg/ha kernel, about 31.9% above TAG 24.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: K 1812 / Kadiri Lepakshi (groundnut)

Name note: the evidence refers to "Kadiri Lepakshi (K 1812)", the CSC/release name "K 1812". No search result mentioned "K-12" in connection with this groundnut variety. The Seednet listing under "COTTON (KAPAS)" was not reached, so the Seednet record is unverified and its crop label conflicts with the groundnut evidence.

Search coverage: four web_search queries were run: (1) release and notification, (2) breeder and station (the query was phrased "breeder Agricultural Research Station Kadiri"), (3) research papers and trials, (4) seed availability, which also tried "K-12". No seednet.gov.in page was returned.

Conflicts with the input record:
- Parentage: the input says K 11 x K 9. The ICAR-JOR notification abstract says it is a derivative of the complex cross ((ICGV 92069 x ICGV 93184)SIL4 x ICGV 98300). The input parentage is not supported by any result.
- Recommended states: the input lists Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. The JOR notification says it was notified for All India Summer Zone IIIa, covering Karnataka and Maharashtra. No result confirmed Telangana or Tamil Nadu.
- Release date: the input gives 9 Nov 2020. Secondary sources give only "2020" with no day.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as drought tolerant, with stable yields under severe drought (about 6-8 quintal/acre per the vendor listing) -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/kadiri-lepakshi-k-1812/
- Described as drought tolerant and suited to dry, semi-arid regions (testbook summary, not a primary source) -- https://testbook.com/question-answer/new-variety-of-crop-kadiri-lepakshi-181239--67ac8476ae8a4ebecf726ae7
- Described as resistant to pests, diseases and drought in a Anantapuramu on-farm study; rainfed potential 20-25 q/ha and irrigated 45-50 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375506325_Performance_of_Kadiri_Lepakshi_K-1812_groundnut_in_Anantapuram_district_of_Andhra_Pradesh_India
- Minikit demonstrations (2015-2018) recorded drought resistance and resistance to sucking pests, with dark foliage noted -- https://aatcc.peerjournals.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Impact-of-Minikit-Demonstrations-on-Productivity-and-Profitability-of-Groundnut-in-Anantapuramu-district-of-Andhra-Pradesh.pdf
- Heat and salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Notification abstract: described as multiple-resistant, with a high-yield Spanish bunch type -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/145280
- Specific diseases and pests named in the notification: not visible in the retrieved abstract; "Multiple resistant" is stated only in summary form.
- Stem rot incidence in a Karnataka trial was 3.8% for K-1812, lower than JL-24 (8.1%) -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/view/4682
- Thrips and jassid resistance is claimed in a testbook summary, not a primary source -- https://testbook.com/question-answer/new-variety-of-crop-kadiri-lepakshi-181239--67ac8476ae8a4ebecf726ae7
- Listed among ICAR-DGR AICRP groundnut varieties described as tolerant to drought and resistant to multiple diseases and pests (2020 AICRP report, cited in a 2025 paper) -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue10/PartF/8-10-40-464.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Notification: average dry pod yield 3840 kg/ha and kernel yield 2666 kg/ha, about 31.9% above national check TAG 24 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/145280
- Maturity 112 days; 51% oil; 70% shelling; kharif season; seed rate 75 kg/acre; spacing 12-20 inches -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/kadiri-lepakshi-k-1812/
- Protein about 28% and oil 51%, compared with 48% oil in Kadiri-6 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375506325_Performance_of_Kadiri_Lepakshi_K-1812_groundnut_in_Anantapuram_district_of_Andhra_Pradesh_India
- Chittoor district on-farm test (rabi 2020-21, kharif 2021-22): pod yield 28.0% and 13.5% above farmer practice -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/TJRA/article/view/138819
- Kurnool on-farm test (kharif 2020 and 2021): seed yield 3375 kg/ha, 28.5% above Nitya Haritha and 35.1% above K-6 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/178148
- Karnataka north transitional zone trial: dry pod yield 2745 kg/ha, statistically on par with Dh-256 -- https://journalijpss.com/index.php/IJPSS/article/view/4682
- Minikit demonstrations (15 farmer fields, 2015-2018): 1187 kg/ha versus 980 kg/ha for Kadiri-6 -- https://aatcc.peerjournals.net/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Impact-of-Minikit-Demonstrations

EVIDENCE DIGEST: KCH 305 BG II (cotton)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "KCH 305 BG II", so one name was searched. No result named this variety under either name.

No evidence found. Searches returned nothing on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for KCH 305 BG II. Results covered other Kaveri BG II hybrids: KCH-144 (high-yield, high-ginning, 160-170 day claims) -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-kaveri-seeds-kch-144-cotton-seeds.php ; KCH-36 (sturdy plant, 29-30 mm staple) -- https://kisancenter.com/product/kaveri-kch-36-cotton-seeds-bg2/217977 . These name different varieties and are not evidence for KCH 305 BG II.

DISEASE AND PEST

EVIDENCE DIGEST: KCH 9333 BG II (cotton)
Names searched: variety_name "KCH 9333 BG II" and seednet_variety_name "KCH 9333 BG II" are identical. The only page naming this variety writes it "KCH 9333 BGII". I treated that spelling as the same variety and flag it here.
Searches run: 4 (variety/release; breeder; research papers; seed availability). The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. None of the four searches returned a page naming KCH 9333 BG II with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. The results were about other Kaveri or Bt cotton hybrids (KCH-100, KCH-36, KCH-14K59, KCH-144).

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page links KCH 9333 BG II to a pest or disease reaction. The "BG II" in the name is not verified by any retrieved page. The Bollgard II pages returned describe KCH-100 and KCH-36, not this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Listed among "Promising products developed in 2019-2020" in Kaveri Seed Company's 33rd Annual Report 2019-20, alongside KCH 307 BG II, KCH 9323 BG II and KCH 9292 BGII -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/sept20/Annual_Report_2019-20.pdf
- The same report lists KCH 9333 BGII as a "Products with a prospect" item under the heading "Suitable for North Zone Cotton Wheat"; the PDF layout does not make it fully clear whether that zone tag applies to this entry alone or to the group -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/sept20/Annual_Report_2019-20.pdf
- No field-trial yield, maturity or agronomy data for this variety were found. The KCH-100 and KCH-36 pages describe different varieties and were discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No marker, QTL or parentage information was retrieved. Parentage in the input is "Not specified", and no page filled that gap.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The developing institution is Kaveri Seed Company Ltd. (from the input record). The annual report names Kaveri as the company that developed the promising product list, with an in-house R&D programme -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/sept20/Annual_Report_2019-20.pdf
- No lead breeder or scientist name was found for KCH 9333 BG II. Names from other results (for example, Kaderbad Ravindranath, ANGRAU, NHH 44 trial authors) belong to other varieties or institutions and were excluded.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder contact, Kaveri email, phone or postal address was retrieved for this variety. The only Kaveri URL found is the annual report PDF above, which is not a contact page. An institute-level contact search was not part of the four searches.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference item names KCH 9333 BG II. The AICRP-related result (Cotton Association bulletin, 2025) covers private-sector compact BG II hybrids in general and does not name this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for KCH 9333 BG II was retrieved. Dealer pages returned were for KCH-100, KCH-36 and other varieties, and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The input record states Haryana, Punjab and Rajasthan. No retrieved page confirms this state list.
- The 2019-20 annual report points only to North Zone suitability for the KCH 9333 BGII entry -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/sept20/Annual_Report_2019-20.pdf

RECORD FLAGS
- The input release year is 2022-06-17, but the only retrieved source describes this variety as a 2019-20 promising product. Both may be correct (development versus notification), but the release date needs checking against the CSC minutes or Seednet.
- The Seednet portal and the variety code A050117794 were not searched directly. A Seednet or GEAC check is the next step.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: LAHB Cotton - 1 (CSC name) / LAHB Cotton - 1 (Seednet name)

Name note: The CSC and Seednet names are identical in the input, and no separate Seednet portal page turned up. All evidence below refers to "LAHB Cotton-1" as written in the ANGRAU crop-variety PDF and the CAI bulletin.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for LAHB Cotton - 1. The "tolerant to jassids" and "resistant to BLB and grey mildew" statements in the ANGRAU PDF belong to the separate LHDP Cotton-1 entry, so I discarded them. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for LAHB Cotton - 1. The only pest and disease statements located were for LHDP Cotton-1, which I discarded. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The ANGRAU PDF gives a crop duration of 180-195 days (medium to late) for LAHB Cotton-1 in kharif, with a potential yield of 20-22 q/ha under irrigated conditions in the South Zone. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf
- Fibre quality as listed by ANGRAU: ginning out turn 30.1%, extra-long staple length 37.1 mm, fineness 3.2 micronaire, tenacity 35.9 g/tex. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf
- The CAI bulletin lists LAHB Cotton-1 (ANGRAU, 2021) in a hirsutum x barbadense hybrid table with the same fibre values (37.1, 3.2, 35.9) and an 80s count, and gives its zone as "South Zone States". -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__48_25-02-2025.pdf
- No multi-location trial results found for LAHB Cotton - 1. -- (no URL; searched)

GENETICS AND QTL
- The ANGRAU PDF describes LAHB Cotton-1 as an inter-specific hybrid of G. hirsutum x G. barbadense, bred by heterosis breeding. Parentage is not given, so the input "Not specified" stands. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf
- No QTL or marker studies found for LAHB Cotton - 1. -- (no URL; searched)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The CAI bulletin attributes LAHB Cotton-1 to ANGRAU. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__48_25-02-2025.pdf
- The ANGRAU PDF lists it under CVRC release. It does not name a breeder or a station. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf
- Release year conflicts across sources: the ANGRAU PDF says 2019, the CAI bulletin says 2021, and the input says 2020-11-09. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf ; https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__48_25-02-2025.pdf
- No lead breeder name is attributed to LAHB Cotton - 1 in any result. The ANGRAU cotton breeder profile (Kaderbad Ravindranath, Wikipedia) and the ANGRAU scientist Satish Yadlapalli appeared in results, but neither page names LAHB Cotton - 1, so I did not attribute them. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaderbad_Ravindranath ; https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=EV9PbaAAAAAJ&hl=en
- The ANGRAU Regional Agricultural Research Station named in the input is not mentioned in the LAHB evidence. -- (no URL; searched)

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found: no breeder email, phone or postal address for LAHB Cotton - 1 was located.
- No institute-level contact page for ANGRAU's cotton division or the Regional Agricultural Research Station was located. The only ANGRAU URL found is the variety-list PDF: https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for LAHB Cotton - 1. The results that mention ANGRAU cotton papers (Yadlapalli, 2009) concern genetic diversity and stability in other cotton material, so I did not list them. -- https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=EV9PbaAAAAAJ&hl=en

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for LAHB Cotton - 1. The single seed search returned only unrelated seed sellers (garden, heirloom and game-item results).
- The CAI bulletin contains a general sentence about National Seed Corporation and State Seed Corporation supplying breeder and foundation seed. It does not tie that sentence to LAHB Cotton-1, so I did not treat it as availability evidence. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__48_25-02-2025.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The ANGRAU PDF gives the recommended area as the South Zone of India under irrigated conditions. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf
- The CAI bulletin gives "South Zone States" for LAHB Cotton-1. -- https://caionline.in/uploads/publications/doc/ISSUE_NO__48_25-02-2025.pdf
- Neither source lists Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu by name. The input list is therefore not independently confirmed; it matches the South Zone wording only in general terms.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: LAXMI (variety_name) / LAXMI (seednet_variety_name), code 3636 (LTH-22)**

Searches run: 4 (release/traits; breeder/institution; research papers; institution contact). Naming: the only evidence for this variety is the PPV&FRA registration for "Laxmi 3636 (LTH-22)", listed under **maize**, not cotton. Nothing I found links LAXMI to the Seednet "COTTON (KAPAS)" entry.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
No evidence found. Searches on drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence returned only general maize or unrelated hybrid studies, none naming Laxmi 3636 or LTH-22.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
No evidence found. No page named this variety with disease or pest reaction data.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
No evidence found. No yield, maturity or multi-location trial record names Laxmi 3636 or LTH-22.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
No evidence found. The parentage given in the record ("Gadag-1 x Co. 2") was not confirmed by any source. The one parentage line I saw, for a different maize hybrid, did not match this variety.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- The PPV&FRA registration lists the applicant as Yaaganti Seeds Pvt. Ltd., a private applicant, and gives the variety as "Extant (Notified)" under registration number 462 of 2018 -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compediumforallcategoryuptonov-2021.pdf
- No breeder or scientist name is linked to this variety in any source. The company's founder and manager names appear only as company background, so I have not attributed them to the variety -- https://www.indiamart.com/company/1127004/aboutus.html
- Release year 2015 from the CSC minutes was not verified. The PPV&FRA entry carries a 2018 registration number, not a release date.

**CONTACT DETAILS** (institute-level only; no breeder contact found)
- Company: Yaaganti Seeds Pvt. Ltd. Website http://www.yaagantiseeds.com, email yaaganti[at]gmail[dot]com, address No. 8-2-277/45, UBI Colony Road No. 3, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad-500034, Telangana; phone +91-11-26562122/25/33/44, 26567373, 26962819 -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/allstinstitutions/yaaganti-seeds-pvt-ltd-0?language=en
- Address on Indiamart: 3rd Floor, No. 8-2-277/45, U.B.I Colony, Road No. 3, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad-500034; manager listed as Venkateswarlu Yaganti -- https://www.indiamart.com/company/1127004/
- Phone 040-23540745 (directory listing for Yaaganti Seeds Pvt Ltd, Hyderabad) -- https://www.vcsdata.com/company/Yaaganti-Seeds-Pvt-Ltd/424.html
- Registered applicant address in PPV&FRA: Survey No. 69, Gundlapochampally (Vill. & Panchayat), Medchal-Mandal, Rangareddy-501401, Telangana, with a second address at 18 Barakhamba Road, New Delhi-110001 -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compediumforallcategoryuptonov-2021.pdf
- Discarded: the email bhavani.b@nuziveeduseeds.com (a different company's domain), Yaaganti Agrotech Pvt. Ltd. (a separate firm), and Laxmi Seeds / Asha Agrisciences (Secunderabad).

**PUBLICATIONS**
No evidence found. Searches of journals, KrishiKosh and AICRP reports returned no paper, thesis or report on Laxmi 3636 or LTH-22.

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- No evidence found for seed sales of Laxmi 3636 specifically. The Yaaganti retailer listing names hybrid maize "Laxmi Sagar", a different product -- https://www.indiamart.com/company/1127004/
- Seednet's producer/marketer page lists "Laxmi" only under soybean, sunflower and chilli entries, not cotton or maize for this variety -- https://seednet.gov.in/material/Seed_Producers_Marketers.htm

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- Not verified. The states in the input record (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu) did not appear in any source I found. The PPV&FRA entry gives no state-wise recommendation.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant to jassids (pest tolerance, listed here because the source groups it with resistance traits) -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The ANGRAU sheet only describes irrigated conditions, and the HDPS trial page did not report stress responses.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to bacterial leaf blight (BLB) and grey mildew -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf
Tolerant to jassids (leafhopper) -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Crop duration 145-155 days, kharif season, potential yield 25-28 q/ha, irrigated South Zone, short compact plant type (100-110 cm) with synchronous maturity, recommended for high-density planting at 60 cm x 15 cm -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf
Ginning out turn 38.6% and upper half mean length 28 mm -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf
Release year listed as 2018 on the ANGRAU sheet, which conflicts with the 2020-11-09 date in the input. A UAS Raichur AICRP profile says it was approved at the CVRC meeting at the AICRP on Cotton Annual Group Meeting, 30-31 May 2019 -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html
Seed cotton yield 28-30 q/ha, GOT 37-38%, span length 27-28 mm, duration 145-150 days, reported for "LHDP 1" (a name variant; the page does not state the full name) -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html
Plant growth regulator trial under high-density planting of LHDP-1 (pre-release) at Lam, with mepiquat chloride 50 ppm at 45 and 75 DAS improving growth and yield; a related trial was run at RARS Warangal in kharif 2022 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354528102_Influence_of_plant_growth_regulators_in_cotton_under_HDPS
Note: the ANGRAU sheet's entry also contains LAHB Cotton-1 data (an interspecific hybrid). Those data were excluded because they refer to a different variety.

GENETICS AND QTL
Pedigree: L 762 x G Cot 100 (conflicts with "Not specified" in the input), breeding method listed as pedigree method -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf
No evidence found for QTL, marker or molecular studies on this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ANGRAU, Regional Agricultural Research Station, Lam (Guntur), as the input states. The ANGRAU sheet and the AICRP profile both place the variety in the ANGRAU/Lam programme -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Cotton.pdf ; https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html
No evidence found naming the lead breeder or scientist for LHDP Cotton-1. The UAS Raichur profile (Dr. Shivanand Hanchinal, Entomology) says he contributed to the variety's approval and publications, but he is a pathology/entomology scientist and no breeder role is stated, so he is not recorded here as breeder -- https://aiccip.cicr.org.in/SZ-KA-UASraichur.html
Other cotton-breeding results retrieved (Kaderbad Ravindranath's ANGRAU varieties) name other varieties and were excluded.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder contact, institute contact page or Lam station email/phone was returned for this variety. An unrelated Bt-cotton paper from RARS Lam, Guntur gives the address "Guntur, 522034" but does not name LHDP Cotton-1, so it is not attributed here -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/apps-18-2-006

PUBLICATIONS

Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Influence of plant growth regulators in cotton under high density planting system. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354528102_Influence_of_plant_growth_regulators_in_cotton_under_HDPS

disease_resistance.summary: No Mahanandi-specific disease resistance found. RARS Nandyal screened 17 foxtail millet genotypes for leaf blast and rust over two years; Mahanandi/SiA 3159 is not confirmed among the entries in the abstract. Resistance status for this variety is unknown.

(2) RARS Nandyal 40-accession study: SiA 3159 was the best standard check (superior traits listed above). (3) 2019 Rewa (JNKVV) multi-location trial: SiA-3159 reported highest ear length and grain yield per plant among 22 genotypes; this was a multi-location check, not a Mahanandi-specific release trial. (4) Mahanandi-specific national multi-location yield data beyond these: Not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CROSS-CHECK WARNING: The variety record conflicts with itself. The release minutes say crop "millet", but the Seednet crop field says "COTTON (KAPAS)". The evidence below shows Mahanandi (SiA 3159) is a foxtail millet (Setaria italica) line from ANGRAU's RARS Nandyal, not cotton. Treat the Seednet crop entry as probably wrong until it is verified.

NAME MAPPING: Both "Mahanandi" (variety_name) and "MAHANANDI" (seednet_variety_name) are used. All evidence below refers to Mahanandi, also written SiA 3159, a foxtail millet variety. No search returned a cotton variety called Mahanandi. The cotton hits (ANGRAU cotton breeders, Narasimha, BT cotton) are unrelated.

Search budget note: all four searches were used. Searches 1 to 3 were partly wasted on the "Mahanandi" name collision (the Mahanandi village, a recipe blog, and a retail product page). Seed availability was not searched.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Foxtail millet is described as drought tolerant at crop level, with no Mahanandi-specific data (heat, salinity, flood, submergence not found) -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/foxtail-millet?lgn=en
Mahanandi-specific stress tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- RARS Nandyal screened 17 foxtail millet genotypes for leaf blast and rust over two years. Mahanandi/SiA 3159 is not confirmed among the entries in the abstract -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363579924_Evaluation_of_foxtail_millet_genotypes_for_blast_and_rust_diseases_under_field_conditions
Mahanandi-specific disease or pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- SiA 3159 was advanced to All India Coordinated Trials in 2018-19, with a yield of 4.66 t/ha in the entry report -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/Annual%20Report%20%20-%202018-2019%20(1).pdf
SiA 3159 was the best standard check in a 40-accession study at RARS Nandyal (superior in productive tillers, panicle length, photosynthesis, transpiration, chlorophyll fluorescence, harvest index) -- https://sasapjas.org/studies-on-genetic-variability-and-genetic-parameters-for-grain-yield-and-its-components-in-foxtail-millet-setaria-italica-l-p-beauv/
A 2019 Rewa (JNKVV) trial reported SiA-3159 with the highest ear length and grain yield per plant among 22 genotypes. This was a multi-location check, not a Mahanandi-specific release trial -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370843713_Cultivation_of_Foxtail_Millet_in_India
Mahanandi-specific national multi-location yield data beyond the above: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- A 2023 Frontiers study characterised 20 foxtail millet landraces with SSD-derived lines and four released cultivars obtained from RARS Nandyal. The paper's abstract does not confirm whether Mahanandi is one of the four -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/genetics/articles/10.3389/fgene.2023.1052575/full
Parentage, pedigree, QTL and marker data specific to Mahanandi: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), with the Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Nandyal, Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh. This is the station the evidence points to for SiA 3159 -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Foxtail-millet-Seed-varieties-from-RARS-Nandyal-Andhra-Pradesh_tbl2_334480467
Named lead breeder for Mahanandi/SiA 3159: No evidence found. Scientists named in the foxtail millet paper (Sai Ram, Naik, Narasimhulu, Venkatesh Babu, Reddi Sekhar) and in the blast/rust paper (Munirathnam, Venkataramanamma, Anusha) are associated with RARS Nandyal but are not confirmed as breeders of Mahanandi -- https://sasapjas.org/studies-on-genetic-variability-and-genetic-parameters-for-grain-yield-and-its-components-in-foxtail-millet-setaria-italica-l-p-beauv/ ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363579924_Evaluation_of_foxtail_millet_genotypes_for_blast_and_rust_diseases_under_field_conditions
Release/notification details for the 2022-10-26 date: No evidence found. The 2019-20 ANGRAU report lists foxtail millet releases SiA 3222 and SiA 3223 but does not name SiA 3159 as a release -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/ANGRAU-AR-2019-20-Final_pdf.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found.
Institute contact (RARS Nandyal): Regional Agricultural Research Station, Nandyal -- 518 502 (Annual Report 2018-19). A different source gives "Nandyal-518 503, Kurnool District". Postal code conflict unresolved. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/Annual%20Report%20%20-%202018-2019%20(1).pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Foxtail-millet-Seed-varieties-from-RARS-Nandyal-Andhra-Pradesh_tbl2_334480467
University headquarters: village Lam, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh (Wikipedia summary). Official email and phone: No evidence found. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acharya_N._G._Ranga_Agricultural_University
Agricultural College, Mahanandi (a separate college, Nandyal district, 518 502) is not the breeding station: No direct evidence it breeds SiA 3159 -- https://www.agcmnd.in/

Karnataka recommendation for Mahanandi: not listed in that source.

drought.details: MR-786 is identified as a good general combiner for days to 50% flowering and days to 50% boll bursting within discussions on biotic and abiotic stress management. Its direct drought tolerance level is not specified.

heat.details: MR-786 is identified as a good general combiner for days to 50% flowering and days to 50% boll bursting. It is mentioned in the context of identifying temperature stress/heat tolerant donors as parents in breeding programs, implying its potential utility in developing heat-tolerant lines, but its direct heat tolerance level is not specified.

salinity.details: MR-786 is identified as a good general combiner for days to 50% flowering and days to 50% boll bursting in discussions that include salt tolerance evaluations of other lines (e.g., FL 478). Its direct salinity tolerance level is not specified.

flood.details: MR-786 is identified as a good general combiner for days to 50% flowering and days to 50% boll bursting in the context of studies on field performance of genotypes under natural flash flood conditions. Its direct flood tolerance level is not specified.

disease_resistance.summary: MR-786 is stated to possess robust disease-resistant traits. It is also recognized as a good general combiner for traits related to multiple disease resistance and for identifying resistant sources.

pest_resistance.summary: MR-786 is commercially marketed as 'अमेरिकन नॉन बीटी नरमा' (American Non-Bt cotton), indicating it does not carry Bt-mediated insect resistance. While general discussions about insect resistance in cotton (including a novel cry2AX1 gene) are present in the search results, no inherent pest resistance mechanisms are explicitly attributed to MR-786.

agronomic_details.yield: MR-786 is described as a good general combiner for cotton yield per plant, indicating its genetic potential for contributing to high yields. It is also mentioned in the context of genetic improvement for kapas yield. Quantitative yield for MR-786 specifically is not provided, however, a hybrid cross involving MR-786 (MCU 13 x MR 786) recorded a yield of 2138 (units not specified).
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly specified in the provided search results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for cultivation in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Uttar Pradesh. Its performance in crosses has been evaluated in various trials.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not available in image. A hybrid cross involving MR-786 (MCU 13 x MR 786) has a maturity duration of 140-150 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: MR-786 is identified as a good general combiner for early flowering (days to 50% flowering) and boll development (days to 50% boll bursting). For the hybrid MCU 13 x MR 786, desirable characteristics include a high Ginning outturn (36.2%), high boll number (39.0), and long staple length (UHML – 29.5 mm).
agronomic_details.field_trials: MR-786 has been utilized in breeding programs, with its performance as a parent in crosses (e.g., MCU 13 x MR 786) discussed in proceedings from Tamil Nadu Agricultural University. It was also part of discussions regarding the field performance of genotypes under natural flash flood conditions.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not specified for MR-786 specifically.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs linked to MR-786 were identified.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Molecular breeding is generally mentioned in the context of achieving submergence tolerance in cotton. Discussions also include a novel cry2AX1 gene for insect resistance in cotton, but this is not applicable to MR-786 as it is a non-Bt variety. No specific molecular mechanisms are detailed for MR-786 itself.
